requirements.text: An ArchiveRecord stores the end-of-life of one listing: kind of end, reason, optional reference, restoreUntil and purgeAt.
References to deals or trades are owner assertions labelled unverified unless the referenced module provides a signed completion.

ArchiveRecords are P1 vault data; a record whose listing is cited by an Offer, Negotiation or Deal is kept for RET-EVIDENCE after the listing purge and pseudonymized on privacy.deletion.completed, and every other record is purged with the listing.
Each command validates the listing status, the owner and the 90-day restore window before any change.

Close requires a reason and never silently releases inventory holds: the hold of the Deal named in closedWithRef is converted, other Deal-linked holds are released only together with commerce.deal.cancel and a signed reservation release, and cycle holds are never released here.
Every violation maps to a stable error code.

The expiry sweep applies the same clock sanity rule as F01.S01.M03: it compares with the median of the latest receipts from at least 2 distinct relays, ignores receipts more than 24 h ahead of that median, and with fewer than 2 relays uses the device clock with a warning.
ArchiveRecord follows the declared machine; the pseudo-state live means the listing has no record yet.
Every transition runs together with the matching Listing.apply_status call and, where a publication is active, with bazaar.publication.end, in one transaction.
Restored listings return as unpublished and must go through publication checks again; restore never republishes automatically.

The expiry sweep never expires a listing with active Deal-linked or cycle holds: it requests bazaar.publication.renew (requestedBy expiry_deferral) while the 120-day cap of F01.S01.M03 allows and the publication is not in policy_attention, and otherwise defers the local expiry and records the deferral until the holds end; a deferral never signs a statement.
An expired listing can be closed directly by the owner, and an expired listing that is published again closes its record as superseded.

close, archive, restore and expire are vault commands; none produces a signed statement itself; the tombstone is produced by bazaar.publication.end in F01.S01.M03 when a publication is active, and a reservation release by F01.S03.M01 when a Deal-linked hold is released with its Deal.
Events expired, archived, restored and closed are emitted in the same transaction as the status change.
Expiry also depends on the owner's own clock; other vaults apply the expiresAt inside the signed projection and treat relay receipt times as claims.

The expire command ends the active publication through bazaar.publication.end {reason expired} of F01.S01.M03 in its own transaction, which issues the tombstone through F11.S01.M02 federation.tombstone.issue (idempotent per target), and bazaar.listing.expired carries that tombstoneCid, so F11.S01.M02 links it instead of issuing a second tombstone; when no publication was active the field is absent.
Vault policy: only the local principal who owns the listing may close, archive, restore; expire runs from the vault scheduler.
No relay role participates; relays remove content only when they receive the signed tombstone or by their own hosting policy.
Reading archive records is limited to the owner.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and sweeps are safe to run twice.

Ending a publication, converting or releasing holds, cancelling Deals, changing the Listing status and writing the ArchiveRecord commit together; the tombstone and release transport is a separate retried step.
Offline use is complete locally; nothing here claims relay delivery.
Close references and reasons are P1 vault data and are never put in public events beyond the reason enum.

Archived listings keep content for 90 days; unreferenced content is then purged at purgeAt = min(restoreUntil, deletionRequestedAt + 30 d) and replaced by a tombstone kept 180 days (CTR-PRV-001), while records cited by an Offer, Negotiation or Deal keep their evidence fields until evidenceUntil.
A sold marking is an owner assertion; the UI never presents it as verified payment or delivery.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.archive_records), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every ArchiveRecord field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and pseudonymizes retained records on privacy.deletion.completed.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); sweep results are local diagnostics.
Sweeps stay within battery-friendly time budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Overdue expiry lag is visible to the user in diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate events against the schema registry; payloads must match what F01.S04.M01 and F06.S01.M01 consume.
Sweeps are tested with an injected clock.
The user export contains all ArchiveRecords of own listings.
Import keeps restoreUntil and purgeAt as exported and immediately purges records already past purgeAt.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Listing stores owner principal, kind, title, description, category, condition, media references, tags, locale, coarse region cell, status and revision; it has no field that can hold an exact address or coordinates.

Drafts are P3 and live only in the owner's vault (IndexedDB) under the record schema classrup.bazaar.listing_record/v1; the public projection is a different signed statement (classrup.bazaar.listing/v1) produced by F01.S01.M03, and the Listing record itself is never uploaded.
Kind and ownerId are immutable after creation; every other mutation goes through apply_edit or apply_status with expectedRevision.

Photos are stored as media, a list of the shared MediaRef {ref, alt?, decorative?} (F14.S01.M02): ref is a content-addressed blob reference, alt is plain text of at most 140 code points written by the author, decorative marks a photo that needs no description; the same entries are copied unchanged into the signed projection.

Listing ids are minted in the vault with publicRecordId of F10.S02.M03 (UUIDv7 whose embedded time is floored to the UTC hour, random remaining bits), so the public projection reveals no finer creation time; a supplied id must already have that form.
Input is parsed strictly against classrup.bazaar.listing_record/v1; unknown keys are rejected and location keys are rejected with a dedicated code.
Referenced category, media and subtype must resolve locally before the draft is stored.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Media entries are validated as MediaRef: blob checks per photo, alt text plain and at most 140 code points, and decorative never combined with alt text; a missing description is allowed in drafts and checked at publication by F01.S01.M03.
Listing status follows the declared machine; any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE and nothing changes.
Only the sibling modules F01.S01.M03 and F01.S01.M04 may request status changes, and only through apply_status in their own transaction.
Deleted is terminal; the tombstone keeps id, type and deletedAt for 180 days as required by CTR-PRV-001.

Relay hosting notices never change Listing.status: unpublishing is triggered only by the owner, including the owner's confirmed Unpublish of a publication that a changed policy pack holds in policy_attention (reason policy_changed), never by the pack change itself, and a relay's removal changes only that relay's delivery state in the PublicationRecord of F01.S01.M03 (ADR-0016 §3, §8).
Commands are vault commands run by the unlocked local principal; none contacts a relay, and none produces a signed statement (publication is F01.S01.M03).
Every command writes its state change and its outbox event in one IndexedDB transaction (EVT-8).
Query results contain only the owner's own listings; other principals' listings arrive as verified mirrors owned by F11.S01.M02.

The module implements the ThreadContextPort declared by F08.S01.M02 for context type listing: exists(listingId) is true for an own listing that is not deleted; isParty(listingId, did) is true for the owner, since any other signer may open a listing thread with the author as participant; roster(listingId) is [ownerId]; isClosed(listingId) is true for status closed, archived or deleted. Mirrors of other principals' listings are answered by F08.S01.M02 from the verified projection, not here.
Vault policy (CAP-8) allows only the unlocked local principal to run create, delete and read capabilities; there is no server role.
apply_status and apply_edit are internal ports callable only by the named sibling modules inside the vault; the UI and relays cannot invoke them.
No relay policy row exists for this module because it never calls a relay.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using a local command-key table kept for 24 h.
Concurrent writers inside one vault (two tabs, two devices after sync) are resolved by expectedRevision and never merged silently.
A crash mid-command leaves either the full change with its outbox event or nothing.
Drafts are P3 and never enter logs, events with payload content, exports to others or relay storage.
Records are retained RET-STANDARD until the owner deletes them; deletion writes a tombstone and purges content and blob keys within 30 days.
Location precision is capped at L2 in the schema and re-checked before any projection leaves the vault.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.listings), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every Listing field with its F10.S02.M02 class; unannotated fields fail the CI lint.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters are kept in the local diagnostics store and are exportable by the user.
Vault command and query latency budgets are measured on a Moto G-class device profile.
Sweep duration is observable locally.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command results and event payloads against the schema registry.
Location and privacy rules have negative tests that fail the build when weakened.
The create wizard and drafts list pass automated accessibility checks with zero serious or critical issues and keyboard-only region selection.
The user export contains every own Listing in section bazaar.listings of classrup-export/v1.
Import validates schema version, id collisions and ownerId; foreign-owned records are never made editable.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ListingRevision is an immutable snapshot of the public fields of a listing at one revision number, with changedFields, a material flag and the editor principal.
Revisions are written only for listings that have been published at least once; plain draft edits only bump Listing.revision to bound storage.
Revision snapshots are P1 data in the owner's vault and are retained as commerce evidence because offers cite the revision the buyer saw.

A derived, rebuildable per-listing edit state {listingId, lastProjectedRevision} is kept from consumed bazaar.listing.published and bazaar.publication.renewed events; auction lock state is never cached here but asked from the ListingEditLockPort before each material edit. On an auction host relay a derived host baseline {listingId, projectionCid, listingRevision, public field values} is kept for each accepted auction-kind listing projection. Neither is an exported record; both are rebuilt from the local outbox history or the stored projections.
Edit input is a strict patch; fields that never change (kind, ownerId, status) are rejected.
Published listings are re-checked against the active prohibited-item rules before the edit is stored.
Every rule violation maps to one stable error code.

Material edits (condition, categoryId or price from any source) of a listing of kind auction are refused while the ListingEditLockPort registered by F04.S01.M01 (auctions.auction.edit_lock) answers locked for the listing (N11); a port that cannot answer refuses with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, no registered port means no auction can exist (F04 off), and non-material edits stay allowed.
ListingRevision has no lifecycle beyond creation; the listing's status machine is owned by F01.S01.M01.

Whether a listing has unsent changes is derived by comparing the latest revision with the revision in the last signed projection of F01.S01.M03, learned from the listingRevision of consumed bazaar.listing.published and bazaar.publication.renewed events.
An edit never changes Listing.status.
bazaar.listing.edit is a vault-local command; it produces no signed statement. Sending the new projection is the explicit command bazaar.publication.publish in F01.S01.M03.
bazaar.listing_revision.record is an internal vault port used by sibling modules in their own transaction.
bazaar.listing.edited is emitted only for published or unpublished listings and carries field names, never field values, so it is safe for notification channels.

On an auction host relay the module consumes federation.record.accepted for type classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 with payload kind auction, reads the verified projection with federation.record.get, compares its public fields with the host baseline of the same listing and, when the listingRevision is higher, a field changed and the ListingEditLockPort registered on the host by the auction host returns an auctionId for the listing, emits bazaar.listing.edited host-side with source host_projection; the baseline is updated in the same relay transaction.

The ListingEditLockPort {editLock({listingId}) -> {locked, bidCount, lastKnownAt, auctionId?}} is declared here and implemented by F04.S01.M01 (auctions.auction.edit_lock in the seller vault, answered from hosted auctions on a host relay); it is registered at composition, so this module never lists F04 in depends_on.
Vault policy: only the local principal who authored the listing may edit it; no role or relay can edit.
record is an internal port callable only by F01.S02.M01, F01.S02.M02 and F01.S03.M02 inside the vault.
Revision history is readable only by the owner; other parties get material-change information through the signed projection they receive.
Edits are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and always carry expectedRevision.
The revision snapshot, the Listing update and the outbox event commit in one IndexedDB transaction or not at all.
Edits made offline are committed locally; no relay acknowledgement is claimed, and the UI shows unsent changes until the projection is sent.
Revision snapshots contain only fields that are already public when published; drafts store no snapshots.

Revisions follow RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last related activity); when the listing is purged, revisions cited by an Offer, Negotiation or Deal are kept until evidenceUntil (keepEvidence from F01.S01.M04) and pseudonymized on privacy.deletion.completed, and all other revisions are purged with the listing.
The edited event carries field names only so notifications never reveal old or new values.
The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.listing_revisions), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every ListingRevision field with its F10.S02.M02 class.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters live in the local diagnostics store.
Edit and record commands meet local latency budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Policy evaluation time is measured separately.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command output and bazaar.listing.edited payloads against the schema registry.
Material-change detection has property tests over random patches.
The user export contains all ListingRevision rows of own listings.
Import verifies snapshotHash for every row and that revisionNo values are unique per listing; failing rows are kept as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A PublicationRecord captures one publish attempt: listing revision, policy verdict with the evaluated rule packs and their packsDigest, expiry, federation opt-in, signed statement digest and per-relay delivery states.
The signed projection contains only P0 fields, a region cell of at most L2 and the listing revision; it never contains drafts, exact address, contact data or offers.
PublicationRecords are retained as evidence of what was published and when; delivery state is local knowledge and is labelled as such.

The projection statement classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 has a closed key set equal to the allowlist in the note below, distinct from the vault record classrup.bazaar.listing_record/v1; maxBudget appears only when budgetVisible is true and no other key may be added without a schema version.

The projection names the vault tenantId so that every vault derives the same listing threadId (F08.S01.M02 contextTenantId), and carries each photo as the author's MediaRef {ref, alt?, decorative?} unchanged, so receivers read the author's description.

Policy evidence names what was evaluated without copying listing text: the packs list [{publisherId, packVersion, packCid}] and packsDigest of the F18.S01.M02 evaluate result, each matched rule as {publisherId, ruleKey, ruleId}, and the jurisdiction profiles as ProfileRef {publisherId, code} of F18.S01.M01, whose version is resolved at evaluation.
Publication is allowed only for a complete listing whose kind-specific terms exist and whose region is at least L1.
Policy checks run in the vault before signing and cannot be skipped by the caller.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Before anything leaves the vault, publish runs the in-process spam evaluation moderation.spam.evaluate in mode author_presign and the risk assessment moderation.risk.assess {subjectType listing_publication, publication {draftId, spamScore, publicationsLast24h}} (N19), the federation_publish consent check for every destination relay, which F11.S01.M02 requires for any public projection and which with federationOptIn also covers relay-to-relay forwarding (N6), and assertPublicCell on the region (N8); a risk level of medium or high, which already weighs the spam score, holds the publication for owner confirmation.

The clock sanity check trusts no single relay: it compares the device clock with the median of the latest receipts from at least 2 distinct relays in the last 7 days, discards receipts more than 24 h ahead of that median and flags their relay untrusted, and only warns when fewer than 2 relays are available (ADR-0016 §5).
Unpublishing a listing that has active local inventory holds requires explicit owner confirmation; the holds stay valid and are listed.

Publication refuses a photo that has neither non-empty alt text nor decorative true with BAZAAR_LISTING_MEDIA_ALT_MISSING (params.mediaIndexes), before the risk assessment and before anything is published; F14.S01.M02 relies on this rule and its end-to-end suite.

Publish, confirm and renew call privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending (F10.S01.M04) first and refuse with PRIVACY_DELETION_PENDING while a deletion request of the principal is pending, deferred, executing or failed.

While a publication is in policy_attention, renewal (also when the F01.S01.M04 expiry deferral asks for it) and re-publication of the unchanged revision are refused with BAZAAR_PUBLISH_POLICY_ATTENTION; only a newer revision that passes every check may be published, and jurisdiction profiles are named only as ProfileRef {publisherId, code}.
A PublicationRecord follows the declared machine; every other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Becoming active is atomic with Listing.apply_status to published and with queuing the signed statement.
Per-relay delivery state is tracked inside the record and never changes the record status; a relay rejection or a relay-signed removal does not unpublish locally.

Promotion is tracked per publication as requested, claimed, acknowledged, active, revoked, ended or expired; it is acknowledged only by commerce.payment.acknowledged signed by promotion.operatorDid (verificationSource counterparty, or chain from the operator's own verifier), becomes active only on a verified relay-signed promotion statement after that acknowledgement, and the relay can revoke it; commerce.payment.finalized in the seller vault is only the seller's own verifier observation and never moves the promotion.

A publication that a changed rule pack or category now blocks moves to policy_attention: the owner is notified, renewals and re-publication of the unchanged revision stop, one reminder follows after a grace of at least 7 days, and it leaves that state only by a re-publication of an edited revision that clears the verdict, a later re-evaluation that no longer blocks, the owner's confirmed Unpublish or the expiry at its signed expiresAt; the verdict never causes an unpublish or a tombstone by itself (CTR-FED-001 FED-9, ADR-0016 §3 and §8).

publish, confirm, unpublish, renew and attach_promotion are vault commands; publish, unpublish and renew produce signed statements through the StatementPublisherPort, confirm and attach_promotion produce them only as a consequence of publish or the Deal they open.

Statements produced only through the StatementPublisherPort declared by F11.S01.M01 and implemented by F11.S01.M02: classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 by federation.record.publish {type, audience public, payload, sourceRecordId listingId}, which signs and allocates seq and prev in its storing transaction, and classrup.federation.tombstone/v1 by federation.tombstone.issue {targetCid, reason}; this module holds no signing path and no seq counter, and F11.S02.M01 routes both through one F15.S01.M01 OutboxEntry per destination relay.
No relay command is required: relays accept statements through their own index endpoints defined in F06 and F11.

Relay statements (classrup.federation.relay_removal/v1 hosting-removal advisories per CTR-FED-001 FED-9, classrup.moderation.reversal/v1 hosting restorations and classrup.bazaar.promotion/v1) are accepted only through bazaar.publication.receive_relay_notice after F11.S01.M02 verified them, when signed by the pinned key of the relay of that delivery and targeting this publication's statementCid; they are deduplicated by cid, anything else is quarantined, and they change only that relay's delivery or promotion state, never the Listing (N17).

attach_promotion opens a noncustodial Deal with commerce.deal.open {contextRef {type: listing_fee, id: publicationId}, contextCid: statementCid, payee: the relay operator DID} (N5, FLOW-01); the vault never shows paid or promoted on the strength of a payment event.

Per-relay delivery state is derived from the F15.S01.M01 OutboxEntry of the statement for destination <relayId> (canonical relayId of F15.S02.M01): classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 is audience public with acknowledger none (F11.S01.M01 registry), so its entry becomes completed on a verified classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 and the delivery shows transport_acknowledged, never peer_accepted; relay_rejected when the entry fails with failureReason relay_rejected (rejectReasonCid = lastError.reasonCid), and relay_removed only on a verified relay_removal advisory.

The module implements the F09.S01.M01 ContextTermsPort for context type listing_fee: verify(contextRef {listing_fee, publicationId}, contextCid, parties, obligations) recomputes parties [listing author as payer, promotion.operatorDid as payee] and one obligation {payer listing author, payee operatorDid, amount = price of the tier in the relay's signed price list, purpose listing_fee, allowedMethods crypto|external} from the stored PublicationRecord whose statementCid equals contextCid; openerRole(listing_fee) and ownerRole(listing_fee) are listing author.

bazaar.publication.policy_attention is a vault-local P1 event carrying ownerId for F13 notification routing (N4), with change raised, reminder or resolved; governance.prohibited_rule.changed and governance.category.changed only re-evaluate and never call unpublish, end or federation.tombstone.issue.
Vault policy: only the listing's author principal may publish, confirm, unpublish, renew or attach a promotion.

Statements of this module are signed only by F11.S01.M02 with an authorized device key of the principal (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-8) through the StatementPublisherPort; this module never signs, holds a signing key or allocates seq itself.

Relay policy rows: each relay decides on its own index and promotion; a relay accepts index writes for requests signed by a registered device key, and a relay moderator or operator may remove from that relay only.
Publishing is idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; a replay returns the stored PublicationRecord and never signs a second statement.

federation.record.publish (signing and seq allocation in F11.S01.M02), the PublicationRecord, the Listing status change and the F15.S01.M01 outbox entries commit in one IndexedDB transaction; transport is a separate retried step.
Offline publish commits locally and shows prepared; the UI never reports relay receipt or acceptance before a signed receipt exists.
Only P0 fields leave the device in the projection; the UI shows exactly what becomes public and warns that copies already fetched by others cannot be recalled (PRV-6).
Tombstones are honoured by relays that follow CTR-FED-001; retention of the PublicationRecord is RET-EVIDENCE.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity: the author did:key and relay metadata link all of a principal's publications, and the publish sheet says so.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.publications), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every PublicationRecord field and projection key with its F10.S02.M02 class, and calls privacy.consent.check for federation_publish before federating.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); publication counters and sync states are local diagnostics, exportable by the user.
Local publish latency excludes network transport and is budgeted on Moto G-class hardware.
Relay-side behaviour of accepting index writes is measured by the relay under OBS-1 to OBS-4.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate the signed projection, tombstone and event payloads against the schema registry and verify signatures.
Honesty tests assert that the UI and API never report relay receipt or peer acceptance without a signed receipt.
The user export contains all PublicationRecords and the signed statements they reference.
Import verifies statement signatures and owner; active publications are imported inactive and must be re-signed and re-sent explicitly.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
GiveawayTerms define how a giveaway is run; GiveawayRequest records each requester's signed request and its outcome.
Requests and notes are P2: visible only to giver and requester, travelling only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes and never in public projections.
Anti-hoarding counters are derived from the giver's own stored requests and selections and apply per giver; a requester's behaviour toward other givers is not visible.

The vault record GiveawayRequest (schema classrup.bazaar.giveaway_request_record/v1) is distinct from the signed request statement classrup.bazaar.giveaway_request/v1; each vault keeps its own record with localRole giver or requester.
Incoming request statements are verified before queueing: signature, signer, schema, listing state, block lists and caps.
Selection is validated against queue state, available quantity and the anti-hoarding limits.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; blocked requesters get a silent drop, not a revealing error.
Each rule names the vault that runs it: the giver vault checks against its own records, the requester vault against the verified listing projection (F11.S01.M02 mirror view) and its own requests.
GiveawayRequest follows the declared machine; collected, declined, withdrawn and expired are terminal.
Selecting a recipient is atomic with the inventory hold; if the hold fails, the request stays pending.
A selected request that is not collected within 72 hours expires and releases its hold, making the unit selectable again; no cross-vault lock is claimed.

The requester vault changes a request to selected or declined only on a verified statement signed by the listing author for that exact request, and expires a selection at selectedUntil by its own clock.

Queue order is the order in which the giver's device received requests: requests from one mailbox sync batch or within 60 s of each other are tied and ordered by a giver-local random draw, first-come picks need one giver confirmation, and the UI labels the order as influenced by relays.

define_terms, select, decline and confirm_collected are vault-local commands; select and decline produce signed statements (classrup.bazaar.giveaway_selection/v1 and classrup.bazaar.giveaway_decision/v1); a requester's vault produces classrup.bazaar.giveaway_request/v1 and classrup.bazaar.giveaway_withdrawal/v1 through request and withdraw.
Incoming statements are handled by bazaar.giveaway_request.receive, which verifies and stores them with provenance or quarantines them.

Statements between giver and requester travel only as sealed envelopes through the F08.S01.M01 mailbox: the sender's vault delivers with comms.mailbox.put to the mailbox hint of the verified projection (giver) or of the request statement (requester), the receiving vault reads with comms.mailbox.fetch, passes the unsealed statement to receive, and calls comms.mailbox.ack after the receive transaction committed; the mailbox limits of 1 000 envelopes and 20 MiB, with the unknown-sender share, are F08.S01.M01's.
bazaar.giveaway.recipient_selected is the only catalog event and carries ids and quantity, never notes.

In the requester vault, bazaar.giveaway_selection.receive (capability peer) verifies selection and decline statements: the signer is the author did:key of the verified listing projection, the statement binds requestId, requestCid and listingId (and selectedUntil), it is deduplicated by cid, and anything else is quarantined.
Vault policy: only the giver's principal defines terms, selects, declines and confirms; only the requester's principal creates or withdraws a request.
Incoming statements are accepted only if signed by the stated requester or, for selection, by the listing owner key (CAP-8); otherwise quarantined with a reason.

Relay policy for the sealed envelopes is F08.S01.M01's comms.mailbox.put, fetch and ack (put proof by the sender's device key, fetch and ack by the owner); this module declares no relay capability and the relay cannot read request contents.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; inbound statements are idempotent by requestCid.
Selection, inventory hold and request update commit in one transaction; the signed statement is queued in the same transaction and sent afterwards.
Each sync step states only what is known: prepared, transport_acknowledged by relay receipt, peer_accepted by the peer's signed acknowledgement.
Requests, notes and selections are P2 and travel only end-to-end encrypted to the two parties; relays see ciphertext and routing metadata.
Requests are retained RET-EVIDENCE for the giver and the requester; notes are purged 30 days after a terminal state unless a dispute references them.
The queue is visible only to the giver; requesters never see others in the queue.

The module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every GiveawayTerms and GiveawayRequest field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and pseudonymizes the deleted party in retained requests on privacy.deletion.completed.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); queue sizes and statement outcomes are local diagnostics.
Queue processing for 200 requests meets local budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Mailbox behaviour on the relay is measured by F08.S01.M01 under OBS-1 to OBS-4 without reading content; this module keeps only local counters of put outcomes.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate statements, commands and the recipient_selected event against the registry and verify signatures.
Anti-hoarding limits and ordering are tested with injected clock and receipt sequence.
The user export contains terms and requests (as giver and as requester) in sections bazaar.giveaway_terms and bazaar.giveaway_requests together with their statements.
Import verifies statement signatures and the party roles; expired selections import as expired and never revive a reservation.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
SellTerms stores the asking price as Money (integer minor units string), accepted currencies, payment methods, negotiable flag, minimum offer and fulfilment options for one listing.
SellTerms is P3 while the listing is a draft and P0 inside the signed projection once published; payment instructions are never stored.
Free-text fields are short, plain text and screened so no account number, wallet address or contact detail becomes public.
SellTerms carries the public barterAcceptable flag (default false), exposed in the projection and in bazaar.sell_terms.set so barter matching and discovery filters can use it (N15).
Money is validated as an integer minor-unit string with a registered currency; floating point and unknown currencies are rejected.
Payment methods must be consistent with their supporting fields, and free text must not carry payment details.
Price changes on published listings are rate limited.

The money cap is per currency: amounts are at most 10^10 major units, computed once by the F09.S03.M03 helper maxAmount(currency) from the registry decimals, and the same helper is used by WantSpec, Variant, Offer and NegotiationRound.
SellTerms has no lifecycle of its own; it is a versioned record whose revision increases on each accepted change.
Changes are allowed only while the listing is draft, published or unpublished; closed, expired and archived listings keep their last terms read-only.
Whether terms are unsent is derived by comparing the latest revision with the one in the last signed projection.

bazaar.sell_terms.define is a vault-local command that creates or replaces the terms using expectedRevision; it produces no signed statement, since the signed projection in F01.S01.M03 embeds the P0 part of the terms.
Events are emitted only while the listing is published or unpublished and contain public fields only, never minOffer.
bazaar.sell_terms.get is the only way other modules read the terms; minOffer is returned only to the owner and to the offers module acting for the owner.
Vault policy: only the local principal who owns the listing may define terms.
Reads of the full record, including minOffer, are limited to the owner and to internal callers acting for the owner; public terms reach others only through signed projections.
No relay role or relay policy row applies to this module.
The command is idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and carries expectedRevision when replacing existing terms.
Terms, listing revision record and outbox event commit in one transaction or not at all.

Offline edits are committed locally and remain unsent until the next signed projection is prepared, and count as received by a relay only after its verified receipt; no certainty beyond that state is claimed.
minOffer and drafts are P3 and never leave the vault; the public projection contains asking price, currencies, methods, negotiable and barterAcceptable flags and fulfilment options only.
No payment account, wallet address or contact detail may be stored in public fields; the screening is a safeguard, not a guarantee, and the UI says so.
Terms follow RET-STANDARD with the listing; deleted listings leave a tombstone for 180 days.
The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.sell_terms), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every SellTerms field with its F10.S02.M02 class.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Define meets local latency budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Validation failures are counted by code for local debugging.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate the command, event and Money format against the registry.
Honesty tests assert that no checkout or payment-held wording or field exists.
The user export contains SellTerms of own listings in section bazaar.sell_terms.
Import validates Money, currencies and the one-terms-per-listing rule, and rejects terms for listings that are not own sell listings.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

WantSpec holds the search intent of a wanted listing: category, keywords, the minimum acceptable condition (minCondition, ordered new > like_new > good > fair > poor > for_parts), quantity, optional budget as Money, barter flag, distance bucket and needed-by date.
The maximum budget is P3 by default and part of any projection only when budgetVisible is true, so relay matching never sees it otherwise; keywords, category and minCondition are P0 once published.
WantSpec status is derived from the listing lifecycle events plus explicit owner actions.
Want input is validated strictly, including keyword hygiene and Money rules.
The category must be an active leaf of the active policy pack and the listing must be of kind wanted.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
The budget cap is per currency: maxBudget is at most 10^10 major units through the F09.S03.M03 helper maxAmount(currency), the same helper SellTerms, Variant and Offer use.
WantSpec follows the declared machine; fulfilled and withdrawn are terminal.

A want becomes open only when its listing is published and pauses when the listing is unpublished or expired or when neededBy is more than 7 days past; the matching engine treats only open wants as matchable.
Owner actions and listing events race safely: the first committed transition wins and the other receives CONFLICT_STATE.

Closing the listing moves an open or paused want to fulfilled when closeReason is fulfilled and to withdrawn otherwise; listing expiry pauses rather than withdraws, so a want whose listing is published again is matchable again.
define, mark_fulfilled and withdraw are vault-local commands; none produces a signed statement; the want's public data reaches others in the signed projection of F01.S01.M03.
bazaar.want.declared and bazaar.want.withdrawn carry ids and category only, so matching engines read details through the signed projection or the local read port.
bazaar.want.list_open is the local read port for LocalMutiny matching, including private fields because it runs in the owner's vault.

When the listing has been published at least once, bazaar.want.define calls bazaar.listing_revision.record (source wanted_spec, changedFields such as keywords, condition for minCondition, price for a visible maxBudget, budgetVisible) in the same transaction, so the unsent-changes check of F01.S01.M02 sees every want edit.
Vault policy: only the local principal who owns the wanted listing may define, fulfil or withdraw the want.
bazaar.want.list_open is callable by the owner and by the local matching module acting for the owner; it returns private fields only inside the vault.
Relay matching uses the signed public projection and never reads this record.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; event consumers are idempotent by event id in the local inbox (EVT-3).
State change and outbox event commit in one transaction; events that arrive twice or out of order never regress a terminal state.
Offline edits are committed locally; matching engines on relays learn of changes only through a new signed projection.
The maximum budget is private by default because revealing it weakens the buyer's negotiating position; it is never in an event payload.
Wants follow RET-STANDARD with the listing; fulfilled and withdrawn wants are purged with the listing and leave a 180-day tombstone.
Wants reveal interests, so the UI states that published keywords are public and linkable to the pseudonym.
The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.wants), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every WantSpec field with its F10.S02.M02 class.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Define and list_open meet local latency budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Consumer lag for listing events is visible in local diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs and event payloads against the registry.
Lifecycle tests run listing events in duplicated and out-of-order delivery.
The user export contains all WantSpec rows of own wanted listings in section bazaar.wants.
Import imports open wants as paused so the owner must republish; it validates category, currency and ownership.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
InventoryItem stores on-hand quantity per listing or variant; reserved and available are derived from active local holds and never stored independently.

InventoryHold is a local lease in the owner's vault with holder type, holder id, quantity, expiry, maximum lifetime and renewals; verified reservation statements of other principals are stored separately as PeerReservation evidence and never change availability.
Inventory is P2 data in the owner's vault; the public sees only a coarse in-stock indicator inside the signed listing projection.

PeerReservation records a verified classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 of another principal keyed by (issuerDid, listingId, variantId, reservationCid) with holder, quantity, absolute expiresAt, status and provenance; it needs no local InventoryItem.

Each hold takes a per-item allocationSeq in its creating transaction and every reservation item names it, so a commitment conflict (F11.S01.M01 entry) means one signer promised the same allocation of the same listing and variant to different holders in overlapping unexpired, unreleased windows; several reservations of a multi-unit item with distinct allocations never conflict.
Quantities, lease times and line counts are bounded and validated before any change.
A hold is accepted only when enough local availability exists for every line; otherwise nothing is held.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Hold lines accept {listingId, variantId?} or {inventoryItemId}; holderType cycle is accepted only from F02.S03.M02, the single driver of cycle holds, with holder {type, id} taken from the lock subject (N14).

Before hold, renew, convert and issue_reservation the module calls federation.conflict.is_frozen (F11.S02.M03) synchronously for the reservation subject key of every affected item; frozen refuses with BAZAAR_INVENTORY_FROZEN and a store that cannot answer refuses with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, so a freeze never fails open.
InventoryHold follows the declared machine; converted, released and expired are terminal and a new hold must be requested for new needs.
Hold, release, convert and renew each run in one IndexedDB transaction with the availability check, so concurrent callers in this vault are serialized.
A frozen hold stays frozen until the owner decides or it expires; conflicting signed reservations are never resolved by timestamp or last writer.
Frozen holds expire at expiresAt or maxExpiresAt exactly like active ones, so no hold or reservation stays frozen forever.

A hold with linkedDealId is renewed by the lease sweep in steps of at most 7 days up to maxExpiresAt (the Deal expiry, at most 30 days) while the Deal is open, is released with reason deal_cancelled on commerce.deal.cancelled and converted on commerce.deal.completed (N5).

A cycle hold is renewed only by F02.S03.M02 through bazaar.inventory.renew, in steps of at most 14 days up to maxExpiresAt (default 30 days after creation), and a renewal never re-signs or changes the expiresAt of a reservation already issued for it; a cycle reservation may therefore name an absolute expiresAt beyond the hold's current expiresAt, up to maxExpiresAt.

hold, release, renew, convert and set_quantity are vault-local commands; issue_reservation is vault-local and produces the signed statement classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 through federation.record.publish; record_peer_reservation stores an incoming statement that F11.S01.M02 verified.

The InventoryPort for other modules consists of bazaar.inventory.hold, release, renew, convert, set_quantity, bazaar.inventory.check and bazaar.inventory.get_item, called inside the caller's own transaction when it runs in the same vault.
No command contacts a relay; relays only carry reservation statements as end-to-end encrypted envelopes when a counterparty needs them.

Releasing or freezing a hold before its expiresAt queues the signed classrup.bazaar.reservation_release/v1 {releasesCid, holder, reason} to the audience of every reservation issued for it (for holderType cycle F02.S03.M02 sends its own notice); receiving vaults mark their PeerReservation released or frozen.

set_quantity is a synchronous upsert inside the caller's transaction: it creates the per-variant InventoryItem when missing and supersedes the listing-level item when the first variant item is created; bazaar.variant.changed never creates items.

Reservation and release statements are participant statements published only through the StatementPublisherPort (F11.S01.M02 federation.record.publish {type, audience participants, payload: ciphertext of at most 12288 bytes sealed to the recipients, recipients [{did, mailboxId}], stream thr:<opaque id>}), which signs, allocates seq and prev and routes them to the recipients' mailboxes; receipt is acknowledged by the recipient's F11.S01.M02 with classrup.federation.ack/v1, and this module signs no acknowledgement of its own.

The module consumes federation.conflict.detected and federation.conflict.resolved (candidateCids, statementClass, freezeScope) for classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1, freezing and releasing the named holds, and confirms its F11.S01.M01 commitment entry with subject key reservation:<listingId>:<variantId or _> and the allocationSeq-based overlap test; it does not act on mutiny events.

Vault policy: hold, release, renew and convert are internal ports callable only by the named modules (offers, negotiation, giveaway, cycle lock, deal completion) on behalf of the local principal; the UI uses adjust and release with owner override.
A peer reservation statement is accepted only if signed by an authorized key of the listing owner for that listing; otherwise it is quarantined with a reason (CAP-8).
No relay policy row exists because this module never calls a relay; relays carry encrypted reservation envelopes without reading them.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; holds are idempotent per holder, so a retry never takes units twice.
A multi-line hold is all-or-nothing in one IndexedDB transaction; there is no partial hold.
A local reservation protects only this vault; cross-vault consistency is provided by signed statements with expiry and by explicit conflict detection, never by a lock.
Quantities and holders are P2 and never appear in public projections, relay indexes or notification payloads; the public sees only in stock or out of stock.
Reservation statements travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the listed audience (PRV-5).
Holds are retained RET-EVIDENCE when linked to a deal or cycle; other holds follow RET-STANDARD purge with the listing.

The module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every InventoryItem, InventoryHold and PeerReservation field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and pseudonymizes the deleted principal in retained evidence on privacy.deletion.completed.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Hold and convert stay within local latency budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Lease sweep lag and frozen-hold counts are visible in diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate port inputs, outputs, events and the reservation statement against the schema registry.
The race and fork scenarios are covered by deterministic tests with injected clock and ids.
The user export contains InventoryItem and InventoryHold rows, including peer reservation statements, in section bazaar.inventory.
Import imports active holds as expired when their expiresAt has passed and never revives a lease; frozen holds stay frozen.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A Variant stores label, a small attribute map, price as Money in the listing currency, position and status; quantity is not stored here.
Variants are part of the owner's listing data (P0 once published inside the signed projection, P3 while draft).
At most 50 variants exist per listing and at most 5 attribute pairs per variant.

The projection subset contributed through the ProjectionContributorPort is exactly {variantId, label, attributes, price?, inStock} per active variant; quantities and retired variants are never contributed.
Variant input is validated strictly, including money and currency rules from CTR-MNY-001.
Uniqueness and limits are enforced inside the same transaction as the write.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
The variant price cap is per currency through the F09.S03.M03 helper maxAmount(currency) (10^10 major units), the same helper SellTerms, WantSpec and Offer use.
A Variant moves only along the declared transitions; deleted is terminal and keeps a tombstone for 180 days.
Retiring hides the variant from new offers and reservations but leaves existing holds, offers and history intact.
Reactivation re-checks the 50 variant limit and attribute uniqueness.
All commands are vault-local commands run by the local principal; none produces a signed statement; the changed variants reach others only inside the next signed listing projection from F01.S01.M03.
Each command calls bazaar.inventory.set_quantity and, when the price changed on a published listing, bazaar.listing_revision.record inside the same transaction.
bazaar.variant.changed carries ids and a change enum only, so the inventory and offer modules can react without reading private data.

bazaar.inventory.set_quantity is a synchronous upsert: add creates the per-variant InventoryItem in the same transaction, the first variant supersedes the listing-level item there, and no InventoryItem is created asynchronously from bazaar.variant.changed.
Vault policy: only the local principal who owns the listing may add, update, retire or remove variants.
Reads are limited to the owner; other parties see variants only inside signed listing projections.
No relay role participates and no relay policy row is needed.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision when changing an existing variant.
The variant write, quantity change in the inventory module, revision record and outbox event commit in one transaction or not at all.
Offline edits are committed locally; buyers see them only after a new signed projection has been sent and accepted.
Variant data is P3 while the listing is a draft and becomes public only through the signed projection; quantities are never part of it beyond an in-stock flag.
Variants are retained RET-STANDARD with the listing; tombstones are kept 180 days.
Attribute text is plain text and is scanned by the same prohibited-item rules as listing text at publication.
The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.variants), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every Variant field with its F10.S02.M02 class.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Variant commands including the inventory call meet local latency budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Variant list rendering with 50 variants stays interactive.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate commands, events and the Variant schema against the registry.
Limits and atomic rollback are tested with fault injection.
The user export contains all Variant rows of own listings.
Import validates the 50-variant limit, attribute uniqueness and currency match, and rejects violating rows in the dry-run report.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A Negotiation links a buyer, a seller, a listing, an optional variant and the root Offer; each NegotiationRound is immutable and stores the signed statement digest.
Negotiation data is P2 and visible only to the two parties; rounds travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes and are never federated or sent to notification channels in plain form.
Timestamps in rounds are the signer's claims; ordering uses roundNo and the hash chain (prev), not clocks.
Each chain is pinned to the root offer's currency and quantity, recorded on the Negotiation; every round uses them, so the convergence rule compares amounts in one currency (MNY-6).

The vault records Negotiation (classrup.bazaar.negotiation/v1) and NegotiationRound (classrup.bazaar.negotiation_round_record/v1) are distinct from the round statement classrup.bazaar.negotiation_round/v1 they store.

Every outgoing command and every incoming statement is validated for roles, turn, convergence, currency, listing revision and expiry before it changes state, in the vault each rule names: the buyer vault against the verified listing projection (F11.S01.M02 mirror view), the seller vault against its own listing and sell terms.
Statements that fail verification are quarantined with a reason and never change a negotiation.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
A round in another currency or quantity than the root offer is refused with VALIDATION_FAILED.

Before counter, accept, reject, withdraw, discard_frozen and keep_frozen, and before applying an inbound round, close, confirmation or acceptance consent, the vault calls federation.conflict.is_frozen (F11.S02.M03) synchronously for consent:bazaar_negotiation:<negotiationId>; frozen refuses with CONFLICT_STATE (params.state frozen) except for discard_frozen and keep_frozen, and a store that cannot answer refuses with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.

Negotiation follows the declared machine; rejected, withdrawn and expired are terminal, accepted is left only through a late timeout close or a hold-fork freeze in the seller vault, and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Agreement is reached only when the seller's vault has taken the hold, opened the Deal handoff and signed the confirmation; a buyer's acceptance alone leaves the chain in accept_sent.

Two different signed statements for the same round number, or an acceptance and a counter for the same round, freeze the chain; frozen chains are never resolved automatically and leave only by discard, by an explicit keep after a hold fork, or at the hard deadline.

A vault waiting for the other side's decision on its own round or acceptance applies a verified confirmation or acceptance until expiresAt + 24 h; after that grace it sends a signed timeout close, and a seller vault that had confirmed cancels the Deal (commerce.deal.cancel) so the hold is released.

The first seller counter moves the root offer to rejected with reason countered through bazaar.offer.reject in the same transaction (N10); a buyer vault that receives round 1 for a root offer it already withdrew closes the chain as withdrawn with a signed close.

counter, accept, reject, withdraw, discard and keep are vault commands; counter, reject and withdraw produce signed statements (classrup.bazaar.negotiation_round/v1, classrup.bazaar.negotiation_close/v1); acceptance is a consent statement signed through comms.consent.sign; receive handles inbound rounds, closes and confirmations; confirm is produced by the seller vault as classrup.bazaar.negotiation_confirm/v1.

Sync state of every outbound statement is prepared, transport_acknowledged (relay receipt) or peer_accepted (classrup.federation.ack/v1 signed by the peer's F11.S01.M02); the UI shows no more than the reached state.
Events are emitted in each vault from local state changes after verification; the two vaults emit equivalent events independently.

Statements and signer roles are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.bazaar.negotiation_round/v1 signed by the proposer (buyer or seller of the chain), classrup.bazaar.negotiation_close/v1 signed by the closing party, classrup.bazaar.negotiation_confirm/v1 signed by the seller; the earlier name classrup.bazaar.negotiation_accept/v1 is an alias of the consent statement.

Acceptance is signed with comms.consent.sign {subjectType bazaar_negotiation, subjectRef negotiationId, subjectRevision roundNo, subjectRevisionHash (ID-3 cid sha256-<base64url> of ConsentSubjectPort.canonicalBytes, which equals the round statementCid), statementKey consent.bazaar.negotiation.accept.v1, statementLocale (BCP 47 locale of the wording shown), statementTextHash} and verified with comms.consent.verify; the module registers the ConsentSubjectPort for bazaar_negotiation, a conflicted status (decline, revocation after commit or peer-reported invalidity) freezes the chain, and every received consent statement is echoed to the other participant before the vault commits on it (N13).

Round, close and confirmation statements are published only through the StatementPublisherPort (F11.S01.M02 federation.record.publish, audience participants, recipients [{did, mailboxId}], ext.stream = streamId, sealed ciphertext of at most 12288 bytes) and acknowledged by the receiving vault's F11.S01.M02 with classrup.federation.ack/v1; this module signs no acknowledgement and declares no relay capability.

The module registers the NegotiationTermsPort {roundTerms(rootOfferId, roundCid) -> {buyerId, sellerId, amount, quantity, accepted}} with F01.S04.M01, whose ContextTermsPort for context type offer verifies Deals opened on an accepted round; bazaar.negotiation.countered carries rootOfferId so consumers need no lookup.
Vault policy: only the local principal acting as buyer or seller of the chain may counter, accept, reject or withdraw, and only on its own turn for counter and accept.
Inbound statements are accepted only when signed by the stated buyer or seller key and consistent with the chain; otherwise quarantined (CAP-8).

Relay policy for the sealed envelopes is F08.S01.M01's comms.mailbox.put, fetch and ack (put proof by the sender's device key, fetch and ack by the recipient), reached through F11.S02.M01 routing; this module declares no relay capability and relays cannot read or alter rounds.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; inbound statements are idempotent by statementCid.

In the seller vault, the Deal-linked hold (ttl 7 d, maxExpiresAt = Deal expiry), the Deal handoff, the Negotiation update and the signed confirmation commit in one transaction; if the hold or the handoff fails, nothing is confirmed and a signed close is sent instead.
Conflicting signed promises are detected and frozen; no last-writer-wins for consent, money or inventory.
Amounts and notes are P2 and never appear in public projections, relay indexes, federation or notification payloads; relays see ciphertext and routing metadata only.
Negotiations are retained RET-EVIDENCE; on principal deletion (privacy.deletion.completed) the deleting vault replaces the party with the pseudonym and the counterparty keeps its own copy.
Notes are plain text; links are rendered as text and can be reported.

The module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every Negotiation and NegotiationRound field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and pseudonymizes retained chains on privacy.deletion.completed.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Local command latency and statement verification meet budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
Sweep lag and frozen-chain counts are visible in diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate statements, commands and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Race, fork and expiry scenarios are covered by deterministic two-vault tests with injected clocks and ids.
The negotiation card and accept dialog pass automated accessibility checks with zero serious or critical issues and keyboard-only operation.
The user export contains all Negotiations and NegotiationRounds the user is a party to, with the signed statements.
Import re-verifies every signature and the hash chain; open chains import as expired and accepted chains import read-only with their evidence.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An Offer stores listing (with the cid of the verified projection the buyer saw), variant, quantity, buyer, seller, amount as integer minor units, currency, optional note, expiry, status and the cid of the signed offer statement, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Offer records are P2 (visible to buyer and seller only), exist only in those two vaults, and are retained under RET-EVIDENCE because accepted offers form commerce evidence; they are purged when the evidence window ends.
The offer amount is immutable after creation; changing the price requires a new offer or a negotiation round.

The vault record classrup.bazaar.offer_record/v1 is distinct from the statements classrup.bazaar.offer/v1 (signer buyer), classrup.bazaar.offer_decision/v1 (signer listing author) and classrup.bazaar.offer_withdrawal/v1 (signer buyer); the acceptance is a classrup.comms.consent/v1 statement signed by the listing author (N13).
Offer input is validated strictly against the schema; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.

Business rules check listing state, currency acceptance, self-dealing, blocks and open-offer caps before persistence; each rule names the vault that runs it, the buyer vault evaluating against the verified listing projection (F11.S01.M02 mirror view) and the seller vault against its own records.
Every rule violation maps to exactly one stable error code with a localized message key.

On receipt in the seller vault an offer below SellTerms.minOffer is stored as rejected with reason below_minimum and hidden from the seller list; the buyer sees exactly what an unanswered offer shows: the same classrup.federation.ack/v1 signed by the seller's F11.S01.M02, no rejection statement and expiry at expiresAt with reason timeout.

Inbound statements are verified before they change state: Ed25519 over JCS, signer = buyerId for offer and withdrawal statements, signer = author of the verified listing projection for decisions, decisions and withdrawals bound to the offer statement cid, cid deduplication; failures are quarantined with signature_invalid, role_mismatch or binding_mismatch.

Before accept, reject, withdraw and resolve_conflict, and before applying an inbound acceptance, decision or withdrawal, the vault calls federation.conflict.is_frozen (F11.S02.M03) synchronously for consent:bazaar_offer:<offerId> and, in the seller vault, for the reservation subject of the offered item; frozen refuses with CONFLICT_STATE (params.state frozen) and a store that cannot answer refuses with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.
Offers follow the declared lifecycle; any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Acceptance in the seller vault is atomic with the inventory hold, the Deal creation and the consent signature; if any of them fails, the offer stays made.
Accepting one offer for the last available unit expires all other open offers on that variant with reason superseded, and each of those buyers receives a signed decision.

The first counter by F01.S04.M02 moves the root offer from made to rejected with reason countered in the same transaction (N10); once countered the offer can no longer be accepted or withdrawn, and the buyer vault applies the same transition on the verified first round.

Expiry is evaluated in each vault: the seller vault expires at expiresAt on its clock without a statement, and the buyer vault applies a verified acceptance until expiresAt + 24 h; after that grace the buyer vault sends a signed timeout close, and a seller vault that had accepted cancels the Deal (commerce.deal.cancel) and the hold is released.

Within one vault two offers for the same unit are never both accepted; acceptances from forked devices of the seller are both kept, frozen through bazaar.inventory.conflict_detected and resolved only by the owner keeping one and sending a signed close to the other buyer.

Every seller-side close except timeout and below_minimum is sent to the buyer as a signed decision; the buyer vault derives listing changes and unavailability from verified mirror updates (federation.record.accepted, federation.tombstone.applied), never from bazaar.listing.* events, which fire only in the seller vault (EVT-8).
The module exposes the vault commands make, receive, accept, reject, withdraw and resolve_conflict and two queries with the signatures below.
Every command emits exactly the listed events in the same transaction as the state change.

In the seller vault the module consumes listing, inventory and block events to keep open offers consistent; in the buyer vault it consumes verified mirror updates (federation.record.accepted, federation.tombstone.applied) and consent events instead of bazaar.listing.* events.

Statements and signer roles are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.bazaar.offer/v1 and classrup.bazaar.offer_withdrawal/v1 signed by the buyer, classrup.bazaar.offer_decision/v1 signed by the listing author; the vault acts only on statements this module or F08.S02.M02 accepted.

Acceptance is signed with comms.consent.sign {subjectType bazaar_offer, subjectRef offerId, subjectRevision 1, subjectRevisionHash (ID-3 cid sha256-<base64url> of ConsentSubjectPort.canonicalBytes, which equals offerCid), statementKey consent.bazaar.offer.accept.v1, statementLocale (BCP 47 locale of the wording shown), statementTextHash} and verified with comms.consent.verify; the module registers the ConsentSubjectPort for bazaar_offer, a conflicted status (decline, revocation after commit or peer-reported invalidity) freezes the offer, and every received consent statement is echoed to the other participant before the vault commits on it (N13).

Offer, decision and withdrawal statements are published only through the StatementPublisherPort (F11.S01.M02 federation.record.publish, audience participants, recipients [{did, mailboxId}], ext.stream thr:<streamId>, sealed ciphertext of at most 12288 bytes) and acknowledged by the receiving vault's F11.S01.M02 with classrup.federation.ack/v1; the module implements the F09.S01.M01 ContextTermsPort for context type offer, including Deals on an accepted negotiation round read through the NegotiationTermsPort that F01.S04.M02 registers here.

Vault policy (CAP-8): only the unlocked local principal acts: the buyer vault makes and withdraws, the listing author's vault accepts, rejects and resolves conflicts; inbound statements count only when signed by an authorized key of buyerId (offer, withdrawal) or of the listing author of the verified projection (decision, acceptance consent).
Offers exist only in the buyer's and the seller's vaults; any other local query returns NOT_FOUND and relays hold only ciphertext.
No relay role can read offers; a party may voluntarily attach decrypted offer evidence to a report on one relay, and that relay's moderators see only what was attached (CAP-9, PRV-5).
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision; inbound statements are idempotent by cid.

Concurrent acceptances within one vault (two tabs) serialize on the inventory hold so exactly one wins; acceptances on two forked devices of the seller are both kept, detected by F01.S03.M01 and frozen for the owner, never resolved by timestamp.
A failure after the hold but before commit leaves neither hold, Deal nor consent (single IndexedDB transaction).
Offer amounts and notes never appear in public listing views, search, federation or notification payloads.
Offer evidence is retained for RET-EVIDENCE and pseudonymized on principal deletion (privacy.deletion.completed) in the deleting party's vault; the counterparty keeps its own copy.
Offer spam and lowballing harassment are limited by caps, rate limits and seller-side filters, including the private minimum, which gives the buyer no observable signal.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section bazaar.offers), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every Offer field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed to pseudonymize retained offers.
Vault command latency and outcomes are recorded as local diagnostics only (OBS-7); no telemetry leaves the device.
Make, receive and accept meet local budgets on Moto G-class hardware, accept including hold, Deal and consent signature.
Expiry sweep lag is visible in local diagnostics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command input/output and event payloads against the schema registry.
The accept race within one vault and the two-device fork are covered by deterministic concurrency tests.
A user's export contains offers they made and offers on their listings.

Import verifies statement signatures and that the importing principal is buyerId or sellerId, with no relay lookup; records that fail are quarantined and other principals' offers are never imported as editable.
Schema changes to Offer follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ProposalRevision is immutable after creation; its snapshot, contentHash, author and signature never change and a correction is a new revision.

The snapshot carries parties, legs with item references and declared values, compensation legs, accepted imbalances, normalization with quote ids and rates, deadlines and the cited feasibility report hash, and the digest covers subject type, subject id, revision number, prev and author together with the snapshot.
Revisions of one subject form a chain by prev hash and number with at most 20 entries, and the head is the revision with the highest number that is not part of a fork.
Revisions are P2 and travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes addressed to the subject's parties (PRV-5).

contentHash = cid (sha256-base64url) of JCS({subjectType, subjectId, revisionNo, prev, authorId, snapshot}); canonicalBytes returns exactly these JCS bytes, and the F08 subjectRevisionHash is the contentHash cid itself (CTR-ID-001 ID-3 form sha256-<base64url>, N13), so one digest is compared in one encoding everywhere and a hex-encoded hash never matches.
A revision is accepted locally only if its number, chain, author role, turn, size, hash and signature all verify.
Cycle revisions may change money terms, quotes and deadlines but never participants or items.
Every violation maps to exactly one stable code and the offending statement is quarantined with that code rather than discarded.

Ingest runs the number checks in a fixed order after V04 (hash) and V05 (signature): V01 limit, V12 duplicate, V11 fork, V13 gap, V14 chain, then V02, V03 and V06..V10, so a concurrent same-number revision is always detected as a fork and an early arrival is buffered, never rejected.
A revision has no state transitions; creating a new revision is the only way to change terms.
After a fork is detected no further revision on that subject is accepted, and the subject owners freeze the subject for explicit renegotiation as a new subject.
Closing a subject (accepted, rejected, withdrawn, expired, cancelled, declined, frozen by a conflicting promise) makes further revisions fail with CONFLICT_STATE.
create is a vault command that produces the signed statement classrup.mutiny.proposal_revision/v1; ingest is a vault command that verifies a statement from another party; queries are local.
Revision events are emitted in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change and the statement goes to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
Consumers of mutiny.proposal.revised treat it as voiding all earlier consents for the subject.

This module is the single ingest owner of classrup.mutiny.proposal_revision/v1, registered with the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with signer role 'party of the subject; coordinator for cycle'; F02.S01.M01 and F02.S03.M01 react only to mutiny.proposal.revised, and revisions from DIDs the principal blocked are dropped silently (N7).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal create revisions, and only when the principal is a party and it is their turn or they are the coordinator.
An incoming revision is accepted only if signed by a key registered to a party DID of the subject; otherwise it is quarantined with a reason.
Reading revisions is limited to the vault owner; no relay can read a revision's plaintext.
create and ingest are idempotent; ingest dedupes by contentHash and create by Idempotency-Key.
Revision creation is one IndexedDB transaction covering the record, the event and the outbox entry.
Forks are never merged automatically, and recovery is explicit renegotiation as a new subject.
Revisions are P2, end-to-end encrypted in transit and never published, federated or sent to push in plaintext.

Evidence retention is RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last related activity) and revisions are pseudonymized, not deleted, if a party deletes their identity locally, because the counterparties' signed copies stay valid.
Spam by revision flooding is bounded by the 20-revision cap and local rate limits.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.revisions), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every ProposalRevision field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes local metadata while signed snapshots remain verifiable evidence.
Local diagnostics record create and ingest outcomes with codes but without DIDs, values or snapshots (OBS-1 style, no telemetry per OBS-7).
Revision creation including hashing and signing completes within 50 ms at p95 for 8 legs on a mid-range phone.
Relays that carry revision envelopes expose only counts and sizes of ciphertext.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests verify the statement envelope against CTR-FED-001 and hash equality with an independent JCS implementation.
Fork, turn-taking and 20-revision cap are covered by deterministic tests with an injected clock.
Export contains all revisions of subjects the user is a party of, including peer revisions with provenance, because they are signed evidence.
Import verifies hash and signature of every revision, skips identical ones, rejects conflicting IDs and keeps forked flags.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A TradeLeg stores giver, receiver, 1..5 item lines (1 line in cycles), the listing cid and listing revision hash seen when defined, declared value from the owner's ItemValuation and the subject reference.
Legs are immutable after definition; their only mutable fields are status and the referenced marker.
Legs are P2 and are exchanged only inside signed ProposalRevision snapshots, where receivers materialize their own read-only copies with provenance.
Legs are validated against the schema strictly, with business rules for ownership, availability, duplicates and limits evaluated before persistence.
The basis of every availability fact is recorded so the UI never presents a signed claim as local verification.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
A leg is defined, then referenced when a sealed revision includes it, and voided only if never referenced.
Defined legs that no revision references within 24 hours are voided automatically so abandoned drafts do not accumulate.
Legs materialized from a peer revision start as referenced because the revision that carries them is already sealed.
define and void are vault commands that produce no statement, because legs reach other parties only inside a signed revision.
materialize from a peer revision is performed by the intake of F02.S01.M04 through the same module port and emits leg.defined with actor.kind federated.
Queries are local and return only legs of subjects stored in the vault.
Only the unlocked local principal defines or voids legs, and only for subjects stored in its vault.
The principal may define a leg whose giver is another party only to describe a request, never as a reservation or commitment of that party.
Legs of other parties are readable only as part of subjects the principal is a party of.
define is idempotent per Idempotency-Key and by (subjectId, position, items) so a retry cannot create a second leg.
Definition and the optional inventory read happen in one IndexedDB transaction.
A leg defined against a listing that later changes keeps its recorded listing revision hash and is flagged, never rewritten.
Legs expose only what is already in public listings plus the declared values the owners chose to publish; nothing about addresses or exact location.
Legs of closed subjects are retained as evidence for 2 years and pseudonymized if a party erases their identity locally.
Abuse such as listing other people's items is limited because peer items require a signed listing authored by the giver.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.legs), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every TradeLeg field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased party in retained legs.
Define and void outcomes are counted in local diagnostics without identifiers (OBS-7).
define completes within 40 ms p95 including IndexedDB reads for 5 items.
Garbage collection of 200 legs completes within 100 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests verify leg shape inside revision snapshots and event payloads against the registry.
Fixtures include 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party leg sets.
Export contains referenced legs of the user's subjects with provenance, since they are part of signed evidence.
Import verifies each leg against the revision that references it and rejects legs not referenced by any imported revision.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ProposalParty links one DID to one subject with a ring position, role, status, mailbox hints and the time it joined or left on the local clock.
The roster is canonical only through the signed revision snapshot; local rows are a view that must match the head revision's party list.
Mailbox hints are public routing data (relay ids) and nothing else about a party is stored here.
Roster creation validates size, uniqueness, reachability, blocks and limits before anything is stored.
Block failures return BLOCKED_PARTY without parameters that identify the pair.
Roster rows must equal the party list of the head revision snapshot whenever a revision is sealed or ingested.
A party is active until it leaves or is removed; both are terminal and never reversed.
Removal never substitutes another party and never reorders positions, so the ring stays exactly as consented.
Local status changes are recorded with a reason code that is shared with other parties only as a coarse code (declined, withdrew, unavailable, timeout).
