join and leave are vault commands that change only local rows and produce no statement; the signed decline, withdrawal or revision that carries the same fact is produced by the owning module.
Events are emitted in the same IndexedDB transaction as the roster change.
Queries return only rosters of subjects stored in the vault.

Only the unlocked local principal changes the roster in its vault, and only the principal's own party can be marked left by an explicit leave; other parties are marked only from verified signed notices or local rules.
A signed notice that a party left is accepted only if signed by that party's registered device key.
Rosters are readable only by the vault owner.
join and leave are idempotent; replaying the same body returns the stored result.
join creates all rows in one IndexedDB transaction so a partial roster never exists.
A mismatch between roster and head revision is surfaced and blocks consent until reconciled by ingesting the signed revision.
No roster field, event or error reveals that a block exists or who holds it; the principal's own block list never leaves the vault.
The roster holds pseudonym DIDs and relay ids only and is retained as evidence for 2 years with its subject.
Subject spam against a person is limited by the principal-side limit of 5 open subjects and by recipients' local filtering.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.parties), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every ProposalParty field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed replaces the erased DID with the deletion pseudonym in retained rosters.
Roster command outcomes are counted in local diagnostics without DIDs (OBS-7).
join for 8 parties completes within 30 ms p95.
Roster mismatch occurrences are visible in diagnostics for support.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests verify that block failures leak no identifying parameter.
Fixtures include 2-, 3-, 4- and 8-party rosters.
Export contains rosters of the user's subjects including status and coarse leave reasons.
Import checks each roster against its head revision and marks mismatches as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A TradeProposal is the local aggregate of one vault and stores the two parties, head revision pointer and hash, status, deadline claim and verified consent and reservation references, with the revision chain held by F02.S01.M04.
The record is P2, retained as RET-EVIDENCE, and never stored or federated in plaintext on a relay; only signed envelopes encrypted to the two parties are exchanged.

Consent and reservation facts are stored as references to the statements accepted by their owners (F08.S02.M02, F02.S03.M02) with their direction and local receive time; decisions use the local clock, and a relay receipt time can only shorten the deadline, never extend it.
Inputs are validated strictly and business rules on parties, legs, deadline, limits and duplicates run before anything is stored or signed.

A consent is valid only if it signs the exact current head digest and revision number under subjectType mutiny_proposal and statement key consent.mutiny.proposal.accept.v1 with a registered, non-revoked device key of the party, and comms.consent.verify reports it valid.

Incoming statements count only when signed by one of the two parties with the signer role the F11.S01.M01 registry requires; statements from DIDs the recipient blocked are dropped silently (N7) and all others are quarantined with a reason code.
Acceptance is a local verdict derived from verified statements, not a message that either party can force on the other, and it is re-evaluated whenever a consent, reservation or revision arrives.
Any new revision voids all consents and returns the proposal to draft until the author's consent on the new hash is signed, which makes it open again.
Terminal states never reopen; a forked or expired proposal is renegotiated as a new proposal that cites the old one.

Expiry is decided by the vault's own clock; a relay receipt time later than the deadline on a statement needed for acceptance shortens the window and the proposal is expired with reason clock_disagreement, while a relay time can never extend the deadline.

create, accept, counter, reject and withdraw are vault commands; each names the signed statements it produces, and ingest is a vault command that verifies only peers' classrup.mutiny.proposal_response/v1 withdrawals and produces none.
Every command writes its record, events and outbox entries in one IndexedDB transaction (EVT-8) and statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
The module consumes revision, consent, reservation, roster, block and inventory events only to re-evaluate the local verdict and never acts for another party.

Statement schemas and signer roles registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): classrup.mutiny.proposal_response/v1 signed by the head author (withdraw only, ingested here); consents and declines use classrup.comms.consent/v1 signed by a proposal party (ingest owner F08.S02.M02); reservations use classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 signed by the item owner (ingest owner F02.S03.M02); revisions use classrup.mutiny.proposal_revision/v1 signed by its author (ingest owner F02.S01.M04). The module acts only on records the receiving vault's owner module accepted.

The module registers the F08.S02.M02 SubjectCanonicalizerPort for subjectType mutiny_proposal (inverted registration; F08.S02.M02 never depends on F02): canonicalBytes(proposalId, rev) returns F02.S01.M04 canonicalBytes(trade_proposal, proposalId, rev); currentRevision(proposalId) returns {revisionNo: headRevisionNo, revisionHash: headRevisionHash}; partyRole(proposalId, did) returns party for proposerId and counterpartyId and none otherwise; isCommitted(proposalId) is true once the proposal is accepted. It reads comms.consent.signed and comms.consent.received with the N13 field names subjectType, subjectRef, subjectRevision, subjectRevisionHash (ID-3 cid), statementKey, statementLocale, kind and aliasOf, and a received record with aliasOf is a duplicate of the named kept consent and is never counted twice.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal create, accept, counter, reject or withdraw, and only when the principal is one of the two parties and the role rule for the head revision holds.
Incoming statements are accepted only when signed by a registered device key of the proposer or counterparty with the role the statement claims; everything else is quarantined.
Relays have no capability over proposals; they carry ciphertext and cannot read, accept or alter anything.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands carry expectedRevision for the local aggregate.
Each command is one IndexedDB transaction covering the aggregate, reservation, consent record, events and outbox entries, so a crash leaves either the old or the new state.
Forked or conflicting signed promises are detected, frozen and renegotiated explicitly; consent, money and inventory are never resolved by last-writer-wins.
Cross-vault outcomes are never presented as certain; the UI shows the highest sync state reached.
Proposal content is P2 and travels only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the other party; relays see recipient mailbox id, size and time only (PRV-5).
Evidence is retained for RET-EVIDENCE and pseudonymized, not deleted, if a party erases their local identity, because the counterparty's signed copies remain valid.
Harassment by unwanted proposals is limited by recipient-side muting, per-sender quarantine and proposer-side limits, since no central moderation exists (ADR-0016).

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.proposals), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every TradeProposal field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased party in retained proposals.
Local diagnostics record command outcomes and sync-state transitions without DIDs, item names or values; nothing is transmitted (OBS-7).
create and accept complete locally within 300 ms at p95 on a mid-range phone including hashing, reservation and signing.
Relays that carry statements expose only ciphertext sizes and delivery counts under CTR-OBS-001.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.

Contract tests verify the withdrawal statement schema, the F08 consent fields this module relies on (subjectType, statement key, statement locale, subjectRevisionHash as the contentHash cid, aliasOf), the reservation holder and the sync-state progression against fake relays.
The two-vault flow is tested end to end with two in-memory vaults, a fake relay and an injected clock, including forks and clock disagreement.
Export contains the user's proposals with all referenced signed statements, because they are evidence of what was signed.
Import verifies every statement and hash, skips identical records, rejects conflicting IDs and imports non-terminal proposals as frozen so no stale consent is acted upon.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A FeasibilityReport stores the subject reference with its revision hash, evaluation time on the local clock, overall result, and one entry per executed check with status, basis, affected participant or leg and parameters.
Reports are deterministic functions of their input hash and the local clock, are local derived data, and become stale after 10 minutes.
The check set is fixed at C01..C13 and every code is stable; adding a check is additive and follows the schema compatibility rules.
Each feasibility check is a rule with a stable code and maps to one module error code returned to callers.

The tolerance rule implements MNY-5 exactly, toleranceBps of the larger side or the absolute minimum (the profile's reference amount, 5.00 EUR by default, converted to the settlement currency with the subject's pinned barter_normalization quote or, when none covers EUR, the toleranceRef rate sealed in the head snapshot, MNY-4 HALF_EVEN), whichever is greater, with the effective length profile read from this module's registry.
Checks never read another party's private records; they use own vault data, signed projections and statement contents only.
Reports have no state transitions; a new evaluation creates a new report and the previous report for the same subject revision remains for audit until retention.
Staleness is computed from the local clock at read time and a stale report is never accepted for consent or commit decisions.
The pure function has no side effects other than the optional storage of its report.
check is a vault-local command that stores a report and emits one event; no statement is produced and nothing is sent to any peer.
The same pure function is exported as a library so F02.S01.M01, F02.S02.M03 and F02.S03.M01 can run it inside their own transactions.
get and list queries return only reports stored in this vault.
Only the local principal can run and read feasibility checks in its vault.
Checks use only data the principal is already allowed to see, so a report never discloses a peer's private data.
Relays never run this module for private subjects; relay matching uses only the public edge admission rules of F02.S02.M03.
Check is idempotent for the same subject, revision hash and inputHash within the same 10 minute window and returns the stored report.
A failing port, such as an unavailable quote service, yields a warn with basis unverifiable rather than a pass.
Checks never block the UI thread; evaluation of 8 participants completes in one pass.
Reports contain pseudonym DIDs, item references and values already visible to the principal, and are never sent to relays or peers.
Failure explanations never reveal block lists, exclusion lists or other cycles that reserve an item.
Reports are purged after 30 days, except that the report hash cited in a signed proposal revision remains part of that revision's evidence.

The module registers DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 and an ExportSectionPort that declares the derived section mutiny.feasibility as excluded (N6), and annotates every FeasibilityReport field with its F10.S02.M02 class.
Check duration and outcome counts are recorded in local diagnostics without participant identifiers and not sent anywhere (OBS-7).
A full 8-participant evaluation completes within 20 ms at p95 on a mid-range phone with warm caches.
Failure codes are countable locally so the UI can show the most common reasons to the user.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Each check C01..C13 has a positive and a negative unit test with fixed clock and fixtures for 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party subjects.
The MNY-5 tolerance arithmetic is tested at the exact boundary with bigint values.
FeasibilityReports are derived data and are not exported; the hash of the report cited by a signed revision travels inside that revision.
After import every imported subject is re-checked before any consent or proposal action is allowed.
Check codes are never renamed or reused; new codes are additive in a minor release of the schema.

The length-4 profile is a typed, versioned constant with the FLOW-05 per-leg tolerance and the stricter distance stated above and is registered at startup with the F02.S02.M05 registry, which the engine reads.
Overrides are accepted only inside bounds (tolerance 0..1000 bps, absolute minimum reference 0..100.00 EUR, pair bucket ordinal 0..4) and effective values are copied into each explanation.
The explanation model is derived and stores nothing of its own.
Admission rules specific to 4-party cycles are evaluated by the engine through this module's provider and reported with stable reason codes.
Overrides are validated against bounds before taking effect.
Amount arithmetic uses bigint and the settlement currency exponent.
There are no lifecycle states; a new profile version applies to later runs and earlier suggestions keep their recorded version.
Engine and explanation read the profile through the same F02.S02.M05 registry so they cannot disagree.
A missing provider falls back to the engine default profile with a diagnostic and never to the 3-party profile.
The module exposes two read-only queries and no commands because it holds no state and produces no statements.
The catalog lists mutiny.cycle.suggested for this module, but the single producer is the engine F02.S02.M03; this module emits nothing itself.
Queries run in the vault for the local principal.
Only the local principal reads explanations in its vault.
Explanations show only data the principal already has, labelled by basis.
No write capability exists in this module.
Queries are pure reads, safe to repeat.
A missing registration at startup is reported as degraded and handled by engine defaults.
Cached explanations are rebuilt from suggestions after a crash.
Explanations expose no block or exclusion information and no other trades of the principal.
Cached explanations are P2, device-only and deleted with their suggestion.

Participant load (other open cycles) is never evaluated by the proposer or the engine; each participant's own vault enforces the limit of 2 other open cycles at consent time from local counts (F02.S03.M01), so no counter is published or inferred.
Explanation latency is recorded locally; nothing leaves the device.
Explanation computation for 4 participants completes within 10 ms.
The active profile version is visible in engine run statistics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The 4-party worked example is a golden test with exact bigint outputs.
The module is tested for emitting no events and sending no statements.
The module owns no records, so export contains nothing of its own; profile version p4.2 is carried inside each exported CycleSuggestion.
Imported suggestions keep their recorded profile version and are re-verified with the importing vault's profile.
Profile changes are versioned and rollback restores previous constants without data migration.

A CycleSuggestion stores an ordered ring of legs (giver, receiver, item, satisfied want), its cycleKey, score tuple, mode, expiry and status; it is advice and contains no consent, reservation or signature of any participant.
The cycleKey is sha256 over the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the ring rotated so the smallest giver DID is first, so the same cycle yields the same key in every vault and on every relay.

A CompatibilityGraph is a derived, short-lived cache of nodes and edges plus run statistics (expansions, duration, truncation) and an inputHash used to prove determinism; it is never exported and is purged after 24 h.
Edge, node and result caps are fixed numbers, at most 2000 nodes, 20000 edges, 8 legs per cycle and 500 suggestions per run.
Run parameters are validated before any search; Lmax outside 2..8 in the vault, Lmax above the tenant limit maxCycleLength on a relay, or budgets above the ADR-0005 caps are refused.
Edge admission rules are pure functions of signed projections, profiles, valuations and local blocks, applied identically in vault and relay modes.
A relay-delivered suggestion is accepted for display only after its signature and every leg are re-verified locally; otherwise it is stored unverified and cannot be proposed.

Relay-side matching (compute_public) reads TenantPort.limits(tenantId).maxCycleLength (integer 3..6, default 5, F15.S04.M03) before any search, uses it as the default and the maximum lmax of the run and refuses a larger lmax; when TenantPort cannot answer the run is refused with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and never falls back to 8.

Want admission reads WantSpec.minCondition (ordered new > like_new > good > fair > poor > for_parts, which replaced conditionsAccepted) from bazaar.want.list_open for the principal's own wants and from the want subset of retained classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 projections for peer wants; maxBudget is applied only when budgetVisible is true, the only case in which a projection carries it (N15), so a private budget that list_open returns inside the owner's vault is never used and vault and relay runs admit the same edges.
A suggestion is advice with a short lifecycle; it moves to proposed only when F02.S03.M01 reports that a participant proposed it.
Expiry, supersession and dismissal are terminal, and a dismissed cycleKey is suppressed for 30 days so it is not suggested again.
A later run that finds the same cycleKey still valid refreshes expiresAt instead of creating a second record, so suggestions are stable between runs.
The vault commands generate, import and dismiss change only local records and send no statement; only the relay command compute_public runs on a relay and is optional.
Every command is idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and emits its events in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change (EVT-8).
Runs are serialized per vault with a Web Locks mutex so at most one run executes at a time, and the relay serializes runs per tenant.
The engine consumes want, listing, profile, valuation, block and cycle events only to mark the graph dirty or to change suggestion status; it never acts on another party's behalf.

classrup.mutiny.cycle_suggestion/v1 envelopes are registered with the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with signer role 'relay that computed it' (evidence of a relay assertion only); this module is their single ingest owner, and a relay run calls the relay platform hook notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push after each mailbox put (N17), with no build dependency because the hook is provided by the relay runtime.
Vault commands run only for the unlocked local principal; no other actor can generate, import or dismiss suggestions in that vault.

A relay run requires relay policy permission; the relay computes only from public projections it indexes, but it knows every ring composition it computed (a derived P2 composition) and learns from mailbox metadata which participants fetched it, so it keeps computed rings RET-EPHEMERAL, never logs them and receives no proposal or accept feedback.

A suggestion is visible to the principal of the vault that holds it, including the other participants' pseudonyms and public item data that are already public projections; the other participants learn of it only when someone proposes it, except that a relay run delivers the same suggestion to every participant's mailbox, which the suggestion UI and the F02.S02.M04 disclosure state.
Generate and import are idempotent; a replay with the same Idempotency-Key within 24 h returns the stored result without a second run.
The same inputHash with the same parameters and the same expansion budget must yield byte-identical suggestions; only the time budget can shorten the deterministic prefix.
A crash during a run leaves the previous suggestion set intact because new records are written in one IndexedDB transaction at the end of the run.
Matching consumes only public projections and the local principal's private data; it never reads another party's P2 or P3 records.
Suggestions are P2, stay in the vault, and are purged 30 days after creation unless they led to a proposal, in which case the proposal evidence is retained under RET-EVIDENCE by F02.S03.M01.

A relay that computes suggestions knows each ring composition it computed, a derived P2 composition, and learns from mailbox metadata which participants fetched it; it keeps computed rings RET-EPHEMERAL, never logs them, delivers them only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes, and receives no proposal or accept feedback, and this limit is shown in the F02.S02.M04 opt-in disclosure.

Gaming by flash wants, fake inventory or self-dealing rings is limited by want age, per-participant caps, local rechecking, the trust panel, exclusion of identities with no history by default and the key-linked ring flag.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.suggestions), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates CycleSuggestion and CompatibilityGraph fields with their F10.S02.M02 class, and purges graph caches through RetentionPurgePort 24 h after startedAt.
Run duration, expansions, truncation and result counts are recorded locally per run and, on relays only, as metrics per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
A relay run over a graph of at most 5000 edges with Lmax 5 completes within 250 ms at p95 on the reference relay.
Determinism is observable by exposing inputHash in run statistics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Property tests prove every suggested cycle is elementary, uses each participant once, uses each item at most once, respects Lmax and budgets, and is deterministic for the same input.
Contract tests check command output and event payloads against the schema registry and verify relay signatures.
Fixtures include explicit 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party cycles and a greedy conflict case.
Export includes active and recent CycleSuggestion records of the user, flagged derived, and excludes CompatibilityGraph caches.
Imported suggestions are always re-verified before they can be proposed and expire at their original expiresAt.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A MatchingProfile stores opt-in state with the accepted disclosure version, maximum cycle length, distance bucket, compensation flag, pause time and exclusion list, with one record per principal.
The vault record is P3 because it contains exclusions; only the derived projection with four coarse fields is P0 and signed with the principal's Ed25519 key.
Projections from other members are stored as read-only mirrors with provenance and a per-author seq chain; tombstones win over any projection with an equal or lower seq.
Profile input is validated strictly against the schema and unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.
Opt-in preconditions (disclosure, region, relay selection) are checked before any projection is signed.
Incoming peer projections are verified before they influence matching; failures quarantine the record with a reason code.
The local profile follows opted_out, opted_in and paused states and every change that alters the public projection increments seq by exactly 1.
Opting out always publishes a signed tombstone, even when relays are unreachable, by queueing it in the sync outbox until transport acknowledged.
A pause expires by local clock evaluation without a statement because pause is a local filter, not a public fact.
update is a vault command that may produce a signed projection statement; ingest is a vault command that verifies peer projections; queries are local.
Statement delivery to user-selected relays goes through the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged, peer_accepted, and the UI never shows more than the reached state.
The module emits mutiny.matching_profile.updated for local changes and for accepted peer projections (actor.kind federated).

classrup.mutiny.matching_profile/v1 (projection and tombstone) is registered with the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with signer role 'the DID the projection describes'; this module is its single ingest owner and drops projections of DIDs the principal blocked from matching silently (N7).
Only the unlocked local principal can change its profile; vault policy rejects every other actor.
A peer projection is accepted only when signed by the DID it names; otherwise it is quarantined.
Relay policy decides which projections a relay indexes; this module never grants a relay any right over the principal's profile.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and update uses expectedRevision for optimistic concurrency inside the vault.
Projection publication is at-least-once through the sync outbox and receivers dedupe by cid.
A crash between local commit and statement signing leaves the record committed with syncState local_committed and the next open re-prepares the statement.
Exclusions, pause reasons and block interactions never leave the vault in any event, log, projection or request.
The published projection contains exactly four coarse fields plus region at L1 and the author DID, nothing finer than L2 location.
Opt-in is explicit, versioned and withdrawable, and the UI states that already fetched copies cannot be recalled (PRV-6).

Projections are published only after privacy.consent.check(federation_publish) per relay and assertPublicCell on regionL1; the module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.matching_profile), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates fields per F10.S02.M02, and its opt-in disclosure states the relay matching limit: a relay that computes suggestions knows each ring composition it computed and learns from mailbox metadata which participants fetched it.
Local diagnostics record update and ingest outcomes without DIDs or exclusions and send nothing off the device (OBS-7).
Relay deployments export projection ingest counts under CTR-OBS-001.
Eligibility checks for 8 participants complete within 5 ms on a mid-range phone.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests verify the projection envelope against CTR-FED-001 and the schema registry, and that exclusions never appear in it.
Abuse tests cover forged, replayed and future-dated projections.
Export contains the local MatchingProfile including exclusions and the last published seq, but not peer mirrors, which are re-fetchable.
Import restores the local profile and requires the user to re-confirm opt-in before the next projection is published.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

The length-3 profile is a typed, versioned constant with the numeric defaults stated in the responsibilities and is registered at startup with the F02.S02.M05 LengthProfile registry, which the engine reads.
Overrides are accepted only within the stated bounds and the effective values and profile version are copied into every suggestion's explanation so later changes never rewrite history.
The explanation model is derived from the CycleSuggestion legs and local ports and stores nothing of its own.
Profile overrides are validated against bounds before they take effect.
The explanation query validates that the subject is a 3-party suggestion owned by the caller's vault.
All amounts in the explanation are computed with bigint arithmetic in the cycle settlement currency.
There are no lifecycle states; a profile version change applies to suggestions generated after it, and earlier suggestions keep their recorded version.
Engine and explanation always read the profile through the F02.S02.M05 registry so they cannot disagree.
Profile lookups for length 3 never fall back silently to another length's profile; a missing provider falls back to the engine default and logs a diagnostic.
The module exposes two read-only queries and no commands because it carries no state and produces no statements.
The catalog lists mutiny.cycle.suggested for this module, but the single producer is the engine F02.S02.M03; this module emits nothing itself.
Queries run in the vault for the local principal and on a relay only for the relay's public profile description.
Only the local principal reads explanations in its vault, and a relay exposes only the public profile numbers.
Explanations show only data the principal already has, with basis labels for peer claims.
There is no write capability in this module, so no statement can originate here.
Queries are pure reads and safe to repeat; there is nothing to replay.
If the engine registration is missing at startup the module reports degraded and the engine default profile is used.
Cached explanations are rebuilt from suggestions after a crash.
Explanations reveal no block lists, exclusion lists or other trades of the principal.
Cached explanations are P2, device-only and purged with their suggestion.
Profile numbers are public and carry no personal data.
Explanation latency is recorded locally and no data leaves the device.
Explanation computation completes within 10 ms for 3 participants.
Profile version in use is visible in engine run statistics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The 3-party worked example is a golden test with exact bigint outputs.
The module is tested for emitting no events and no statements.
The module owns no records, so export contains nothing of its own; the profile version is stored inside each exported CycleSuggestion explanation metadata.
Imported suggestions keep the profile version they were computed with and are re-verified with the importing vault's profile.
Profile version changes follow semantic versions and a rollback restores the previous constants without data migration.

A Cycle is each vault's own view of one exchange ring of 2..8 participants, identified by a coordinator-generated UUIDv7 that equals the TradeProposal id when the cycle originates from an accepted two-party proposal.

A CycleConsent references one participant's ConsentStatement accepted by F08.S02.M02 (subjectType mutiny_cycle and statement key consent.mutiny.cycle.commit.v1, or mutiny_proposal and consent.mutiny.proposal.accept.v1 for consents imported from an accepted proposal), the revision number and digest it signed, the local receive time and a validity verdict; consents on any other number or hash, and revoked consents, are void evidence.
Cycle composition is P2 and is exchanged only as end-to-end encrypted signed envelopes to the participants; the commit verdict is a local derivation and is never itself a signed fact.
The deadline, execution window and every timestamp from other parties are claims; only the local clock decides expiry.
Proposing a cycle requires a verified suggestion, a fresh feasibility report, no infeasible check, reachable participants and the coordinator's own reservation.

A consent is valid only if F08.S02.M02 accepted it with subjectType mutiny_cycle and statement key consent.mutiny.cycle.commit.v1 from a non-revoked registered device key of the signer, it names this cycle, the head revision number and the head digest cid as subjectRevisionHash, comms.consent.verify reports it valid, and it arrived before the deadline on the local clock.
Commit requires every condition simultaneously and is re-checked inside the same transaction that records the last piece of evidence.
Equivocation, overload and unknown-sender limits are evaluated only from data held in this vault and never disclose another vault's data or another participant's counts.

The commit verdict is a pure function of verified evidence and the local clock; it is re-evaluated whenever evidence or the clock changes and never depends on a message from a coordinator saying committed.

Any decline, revocation of a counted consent by its author, expiry, fork, equivocation, conflicting promise or participant loss before commit ends or freezes the cycle for this vault or voids that consent, and no replacement participant is ever substituted.
Terminal states do not reopen; renegotiation after a freeze or cancellation is a brand-new cycle with new consents.
The consent deadline is evaluated on each vault's own clock, and if the clock disagrees with a relay receipt time about the deadline, the cycle is expired.
The opening state always has an exit: imported evidence that fails verification freezes the cycle and a passed consent deadline cancels it.

propose, consent and decline are vault commands that each name the signed statements they produce; this module ingests no envelope type and reacts only to the events of each statement type's single ingest owner (F08.S02.M02 consents, declines and revocations; F02.S03.M02 reservations; F02.S01.M04 revisions; F02.S03.M03 withdrawals).
Commit is never a command; it is the local verdict emitted as mutiny.cycle.committed in the transaction that records the final piece of evidence.
Statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI shows no more certainty than the state reached.
Events produced here drive local consumers only; nothing leaves the device except the signed statements.

Statement schemas and signer roles registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): consents and declines use classrup.comms.consent/v1 (subjectType mutiny_cycle, key consent.mutiny.cycle.commit.v1) signed by a cycle participant, ingest owner F08.S02.M02; reservations use classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 signed by the item owner, ingest owner F02.S03.M02; revisions use classrup.mutiny.proposal_revision/v1 signed by the coordinator, ingest owner F02.S01.M04; classrup.mutiny.cycle/v1 and classrup.mutiny.cycle_consent/v1 are local records and are never sent. Statements from DIDs the principal blocked are dropped silently by their owners (N7).
Every event payload carries the participant DIDs (participantIds or parties) that notification routing needs to resolve recipients (N4).

mutiny.cycle.committed carries legs [{legId, giverId, receiverId}] in ring order, giverId and receiverId being DIDs as in mutiny.cycle.completed, together with parties [{did, role}] and revisionHash, which consumers use as contextCid, so F07.S03.M01 issues review tickets only to leg-connected counterparties.

The module registers the F08.S02.M02 SubjectCanonicalizerPort for subjectType mutiny_cycle (inverted registration; F08.S02.M02 never depends on F02): canonicalBytes(cycleId, rev) returns F02.S01.M04 canonicalBytes of the cycle's revision chain (subjectType cycle, or trade_proposal for origin trade_proposal); currentRevision(cycleId) returns {revisionNo: headRevisionNo, revisionHash: headRevisionHash}; partyRole(cycleId, did) returns participant for a DID in participantIds and none otherwise; isCommitted(cycleId) is true once this vault's verdict reached committed (committedLocallyAt set). It reads comms.consent.signed and comms.consent.received with the N13 field names subjectType, subjectRef, subjectRevision, subjectRevisionHash (ID-3 cid), statementKey, statementLocale, kind and aliasOf, and a received record with aliasOf is attached to the kept consent it names and never counted twice.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal propose, consent or decline, and only as a participant of the cycle; a consent signed by anyone else is never created locally.

Statements count only after their single ingest owner accepted them as signed by a registered, non-revoked device key of a participant DID with the signer role registered in F11.S01.M01; statements from DIDs the principal blocked are dropped silently (N7).
Relays and moderators have no capability over cycles; relay roles govern only what that relay hosts.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands carry expectedRevision for the local aggregate.

Each command and each evaluation is one IndexedDB transaction covering the cycle, consents, reservation release, events and outbox entries, and the commit verdict is evaluated inside that same transaction.
Forked or conflicting signed promises are detected, frozen and renegotiated explicitly; consent, money and inventory commitments are never resolved by last-writer-wins.
Delivery is at-least-once and out of order; duplicates are skipped by their owners by cid and the verdict converges once the same evidence is present.

Cycle composition, values and consents are P2, travel only in end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the participants and are never published, federated or sent to push in plaintext; relays see recipient mailbox id, size and time only (PRV-5).
Evidence is retained for RET-EVIDENCE and pseudonymized, not deleted, if a participant erases their identity locally.

Coercion and spam through unwanted cycle proposals are limited by recipient-side muting, per-sender quarantine, the per-vault cap on open cycles from identities with no history, and the proposer's cap of 5 open cycles and proposals.
The UI states that pseudonymity is not anonymity and that counterparties can see the public items, pseudonyms and the distance bucket.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.cycles), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every Cycle and CycleConsent field with its F10.S02.M02 class, reports every committed or executing cycle of the principal as a DeletionPort.plan() blocker {kind: cycle, ref: cycleId, counterparties: the other participantIds}, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased participant in retained cycles.

Sybil rings are made visible rather than claimed impossible: each participant has a trust panel, key-linked rings need explicit confirmation, and the review screen recommends a simultaneous handover for legs adjacent to new identities.
Local diagnostics record transitions, verdict inputs and error codes without DIDs, values or statements; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
propose for 8 participants completes locally within 500 ms at p95; consent within 300 ms; evaluation of one owner event within 80 ms.
Verdict evaluation for 8 participants completes within 20 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Multi-vault tests use in-memory vaults with a fake relay that drops, delays, duplicates and reorders, and an injected clock per vault.
Property tests show commit is impossible without every consent and reservation on the head hash, and that revisions void consents.
Fixtures cover explicit 2-, 3-, 4- and 8-party cycles.
Export contains the user's cycles with all consents and the statements they depend on, because they are signed evidence of what was agreed.
Import verifies every consent signature and hash, skips identical records, rejects conflicting IDs, and imports non-terminal cycles as frozen so no stale consent or deadline is acted upon.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A DropoutRecord is append-only evidence that a participant stopped participating, with the coarse reason shared with others, the finer private reason kept locally, the phase and the evidence basis.

Records created from a participant's own signed withdrawal carry the Ed25519 statement; records created from timeouts or local signals are labelled local_clock or local_signal and are not signed facts about the other person.
The phase is computed in the same transaction as the record from the handover evidence that this vault holds, and it is stored so later arrivals cannot change history.
Only a participant can withdraw themselves, and withdrawal is allowed while the cycle is proposed, committed or executing.
Peer notices are accepted only when signed by the participant they concern; timeouts and signals are accepted only from the local clock and local rules.
Phase and outcome are computed from verified handover evidence in the same transaction and never from a claim in the notice.

Before any handover evidence exists a dropout cancels the cycle and the vault releases its own reservations in the same transaction through the F02.S03.M02 LockPort.releaseForSubject, and exactly one cancelled event is emitted per cycle.
After any handover evidence exists a dropout never cancels the cycle; it is recorded and the cycle moves to partially_executed with a recovery case, so already handed-over items are not abandoned.
No dropout, timeout or loss signal adds, removes or substitutes participants, and the next step for the others is only a fresh suggestion and fresh consent.
Late evidence arriving after cancellation never reopens the cycle; it is stored and may open a standalone recovery case.

withdraw is a vault command that produces the signed statement classrup.mutiny.cycle_withdrawal/v1; ingest verifies peers' notices and produces none; evaluate is a vault-local sweep that produces a signed withdrawal only when the principal itself must leave.
Events are written in the same IndexedDB transaction as the records, and statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
The module exposes coarse reasons only to other participants and keeps private reasons local.

Statement schemas and signer roles registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): classrup.mutiny.cycle_withdrawal/v1 signed by the withdrawing participant, ingest owner this module; declines and revocations use classrup.comms.consent/v1 (ingest owner F08.S02.M02) and arrive as comms.consent.received and comms.consent.revoked; statements from DIDs the principal blocked are dropped silently (N7).
Every event payload carries the participant DIDs that notification routing needs to resolve the remaining participants (N4).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal withdraw itself; no one can withdraw another person, and a peer's withdrawal counts only if signed by that peer's registered key.
Local timeouts and signals are produced by the vault itself on behalf of the principal's vault policy and are labelled as local evidence.
Relays and moderators cannot create, cancel or alter dropouts.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; a repeated withdraw returns the stored record.

A withdrawal, the phase computation, the cycle cancellation and the release of the principal's reservations happen in one IndexedDB transaction, with F02.S03.M02 LockPort.releaseForSubject called inside it, so no state exists where the cycle is cancelled but items are still held; the mutiny.cycle.cancelled event is additionally consumed by F02.S03.M02 idempotently and orphan reconciliation runs on vault open.
Conflicting evidence, such as a handover attestation arriving after cancellation, never reopens a cycle and is escalated to recovery rather than merged.
Other participants receive only the coarse reason (withdrew, unavailable, timeout); the finer private reason, including that a block exists, never leaves the vault.
Dropout records are retained as evidence for RET-EVIDENCE and pseudonymized if the person erases their identity locally.
Griefing by repeated withdrawals is limited by local reputation signals, recipients' quarantine of repeat withdrawers and the cap on open cycles, since no central reputation write exists.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.dropouts), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every DropoutRecord field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased participant in retained records.
Dropout outcomes are counted in local diagnostics by public reason and phase without identifiers (OBS-7).
Withdraw including phase computation, cancellation and release completes within 200 ms at p95 for 8 participants.
Deadline sweep over 50 cycles completes within 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Multi-vault tests with per-vault clocks cover 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party cycles and the three phases.
A negative test proves no code path can change participantIds or substitute a participant.
Export contains the user's dropout records and the signed statements they depend on, with privateReason included only in the user's own export.
Import verifies statements, keeps phase and outcome as recorded, and never reopens or alters the status of a cycle because of an imported dropout.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A CycleLock holds one giver's reserved item set for one subject, the revision hash it was made against, the absolute expiry, the direction own or peer and, for own reservations, the local inventory hold ids.

The record references the signed classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 statement (by reservationCid) so peers' copies are verifiable evidence, and the own copy additionally links local holds that exist only in this vault; classrup.mutiny.cycle_lock/v1 names only this local record and is never sent (N14).

The statement's absolute expiresAt is never extended; the local inventory hold behind it is renewed internally under the same absolute expiry, and extending the promise means issuing a new reservation that supersedes the old one (supersedesCid) before it expires.
Reserve validates ownership, availability, quantities and expiry range before any hold is taken, and takes all holds in one transaction or none.
Incoming reservation statements are verified for signature, signer role, digest binding and expiry before they count toward any commit verdict.
Conflict detection compares only data this vault legitimately holds and never claims knowledge of other vaults.

A reservation is active until the earliest of release, conversion after handover evidence, supersession, expiry by the local clock or conflict detection, and after partial execution undelivered legs are held for the recovery case.

Conversion happens per lock when the giver's own handed_over attestation is recorded or every item of the lock has a verified signed receipt from the receiver, whichever comes first; partial receipt alone keeps the lock active.
Expiry is evaluated lazily and on a 60 s timer while the vault is open, without any background guarantee, and always before any command touching the lock.

reserve produces classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 through bazaar.inventory.issue_reservation and release produces the notice classrup.mutiny.reservation_release/v1 (alias of classrup.bazaar.reservation_release/v1); ingest verifies a peer's reservation or release notice and produces none; classrup.mutiny.cycle_lock/v1 is the local record only.
The reserve command takes all holds and writes the statement and event in one IndexedDB transaction, and it is idempotent.
Events locked and unlocked are emitted for own reservations and for verified peer reservations, with direction in the payload.

Statements registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 with holder.type cycle, signer role 'owner of the listed items and giver in the head revision' (ingest owner here, storage through F01.S03.M01 record_peer_reservation), and classrup.mutiny.reservation_release/v1 with aliasOf classrup.bazaar.reservation_release/v1 (payload schema, audience and signer role 'signer of the released reservation' of that entry); statements from DIDs the principal blocked are dropped silently (N7).

This module is the single caller of the F01.S03.M01 InventoryPort for holderType cycle (hold, renew, release, convert); F01.S03.M01 does not act on mutiny events and sends no classrup.bazaar.reservation_release/v1 for holderType cycle, and the unlocked event names holdIds for own locks.

Release notices carry exactly the classrup.bazaar.reservation_release/v1 payload {releasesCid, holder {type: cycle, id: subjectId}, reason} under the alias type; the local releaseReason maps to reason frozen for fork_frozen, for item_lost to the reason of the F01 hold release when it is owner_override, listing_gone or deal_cancelled (released when the F01 reason is expired), and to released for every other reason; no notice is sent for converted locks or for locks that reach their signed expiresAt, because conversion is evidenced by attestations and expiry by the signed expiresAt.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal reserve or release, and only items the principal owns.
A peer reservation statement is accepted only when signed by a registered device key of a giver in the subject's head revision and only for items that giver lists; otherwise it is quarantined.
Relays have no capability over reservations and see only ciphertext.
Reserve and release are idempotent, and all holds plus the statement are written in one IndexedDB transaction so there are no orphan holds and no statements without holds.
Concurrent reserve attempts inside one vault are serialized by an IndexedDB transaction and a Web Locks mutex; the first transaction to commit wins and the others fail with a conflict.
After a crash, expiry and orphan-hold reconciliation run first on vault open.
Cross-vault double promises are detected on evidence and frozen, never silently resolved.
Reservation statements are P2, encrypted to the subject's parties, and reveal only item references already public in listings, the subject id and the expiry.
Error messages never reveal which other subject holds an item.
Item hoarding through reservations is limited by the cap of 5 active sets, absolute expiry and per-subject recipients' quarantine of repeat offenders.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.locks), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every CycleLock field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed releases own holds and pseudonymizes retained records.
Reservation outcomes and expiry sweeps are counted in local diagnostics without identifiers (OBS-7).
Reserve of 5 items completes within 100 ms at p95 on a mid-range phone.
Expiry sweep over 200 locks completes within 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Concurrency inside a vault is tested deterministically with two simulated transactions, and all-or-nothing is tested by failing the last item.
Cross-vault tests use in-memory vaults and a fake relay with drops, delays and duplicates.
Export contains the user's own and verified peer reservation statements of non-purged subjects because they are signed evidence.
Imported active reservations never revive holds; they are imported as expired unless the subject is re-confirmed and reserved again.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A HandoverAttestation is an immutable signed statement by a giver or receiver about one leg, with the kind, the items covered, a claimed time, an optional note up to 280 code points and up to 3 stripped evidence attachments.

A RecoveryCase is the local aggregate that tracks which legs were handed over or received, which options were proposed, accepted or completed, any linked dispute, and the per-leg disposition of remaining reservations.
Both records are P2, retained as RET-EVIDENCE, exchanged only as end-to-end encrypted signed envelopes to the cycle's participants, and verified by each vault before use.
Local receive time is the only time used for decisions, and claimed times are shown as claims.

completionCid = cid (sha256-base64url) of the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of {cycleId, revisionHash, receipts: ascending list of the cids of the valid received attestations, one per leg, settlements: ascending list of the compensation settlement evidence cids}; every participant can recompute it from the signed attestations delivered to them, so it is verifiable proof of what was attested, not of delivery.
Attestations are accepted only from the right party for the leg, in a cycle state that allows them, with a verified signature and a plausible claimed time.
Recovery options are accepted only inside an open case and only from participants of the cycle; acceptance requires a signed accept from every participant in the option's requiredSignerIds.
Completion is derived from verified evidence and never from a message that says completed.

A cycle is completed in a vault only when every leg has a valid receiver attestation and every compensation leg is settled, as verified in that vault, and the verdict is re-evaluated whenever evidence arrives.
Issue reports, dropouts after handover and execution deadlines with partial evidence move the cycle to partially_executed and open exactly one RecoveryCase; nothing is cancelled or rerouted.
A RecoveryCase resolves only through signed agreement on options, a dispute outcome from F09.S02.M02, or by closing as unresolved after 30 days without activity.
No relay, moderator or counterparty can mark a leg received or a case resolved for someone else; only that party's signature counts.

Every leg's disposition is backed by the signed acceptance of that leg's own giver and receiver or by a dispute outcome they acknowledged, so other participants of an N-party cycle can never settle a leg they are not part of.

attest and the recovery commands propose_option, respond and escalate are vault commands that name the signed statements they produce; ingest commands verify other participants' statements and produce none.
Events are written in the same IndexedDB transaction as the records, and statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
Completion and partial execution are local verdicts emitted as events, not commands and not signed facts.

Statement schemas and signer roles registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): classrup.mutiny.handover_attestation/v1 signed by the leg's giver (handed_over, returned), receiver (received, issue_reported) or original giver (return_confirmed); classrup.mutiny.recovery_action/v1 signed by a participant, accept counted only from requiredSignerIds; this module is the single ingest owner of both and drops statements from DIDs the principal blocked silently (N7).

Completion and recovery events carry contextId, completionCid, parties [{did, role}] and legs [{legId, giverId, receiverId}] (N3), and every event carries the participant DIDs that notification routing needs (N4).

The module registers the F09.S02.M02 DisputeContextPort resolver for context type cycle (inverted registration; F09.S02.M02 never depends on F02): resolve({type: cycle, id: cycleId}) returns parties = the cycle's participantIds as [{did, role: participant}] and contextCid = the head revisionHash the cycle was committed on, read from F02.S03.M01, and returns unknown when the cycle is not stored in this vault or was never committed here and has no RecoveryCase; escalate always names contextRef {type: cycle, id: cycleId}, and dispute events are matched by that contextRef.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal sign attestations and recovery actions, and only for legs and cases where the principal has the required role in the signed revision.
Incoming statements are accepted only when signed by a registered, non-revoked device key of the participant whose role the statement claims; otherwise they are quarantined.
Relays, moderators and mediators cannot attest, resolve or alter cases; a mediator acts only through F09.S02.M02 after a participant escalates.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001, attestations dedupe by cid and by (leg, kind), and mutating recovery commands carry expectedRevision.
Each command is one IndexedDB transaction covering records, completion verdict, events and outbox entries.
Execution is a saga with compensating transitions (IDM-6); no step assumes another party's physical action happened without that party's own attestation.
Conflicting evidence, such as giver says handed over and receiver says not received, is never merged; both are kept and the case is escalated or resolved by signed agreement.
Attestations, notes and evidence photos are P2, end-to-end encrypted in transit to the participants, and never published; photos are re-encoded with metadata stripped before attaching.
Evidence is retained for RET-EVIDENCE and pseudonymized, not deleted, if a participant erases their identity locally.
False attestations and issue reports are limited by signature accountability, the 48 h and giver-attestation rules for issues, and by disputes that compare signed statements.
The UI states that signatures evidence what each person asserts and that ClassRup does not verify delivery.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.execution), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every HandoverAttestation and RecoveryCase field with its F10.S02.M02 class, reports every open or escalated RecoveryCase as a DeletionPort.plan() blocker {kind: cycle, ref: cycleId, counterparties: the other participantIds}, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased participant in retained evidence.
Local diagnostics record attestation and recovery outcomes without DIDs, notes or photos and send nothing (OBS-7).
attest including signing and completion check completes within 150 ms at p95 on a mid-range phone.
Completion evaluation for 8 legs completes within 10 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Execution flows are tested across in-memory vaults with a fake relay and per-vault clocks for 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party cycles.
Property tests show completion is impossible without every receiver attestation and settled compensation, and that cancelled cycles never reopen.
Export contains the user's attestations and recovery cases with signatures, since they are the evidence of what each party asserted.
Import verifies every signature and cid, skips identical records and rejects conflicting IDs, and imports open recovery cases as read-only history with an option to start a new case.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A NormalizationRecord pins, for one subject and revision, the settlement currency, each item's declared and converted Money, and every FX quote used with id, rational rate, asOf, expiresAt and source label.
Conversions use CTR-MNY-001 MNY-4 with HALF_EVEN rounding applied once per conversion, bigint arithmetic and no floating point anywhere.
The record is P2, embedded in the signed revision snapshot, and its hash covers the quotes so changing a rate changes the digest participants sign.
Normalization refuses unregistered currencies, missing quotes, expired or soon-to-expire quotes, and more than 5 currencies or 8 quotes.
Recomputation by receivers uses exactly the same integer arithmetic so any difference is a mismatch and not a tolerance issue.
The effective consent deadline can never be later than the earliest quote expiry.
A record is current until a newer record supersedes it, its earliest quote expires, or its subject commits or closes.
Expiry before commit emits an event that tells the coordinator a quote_refresh revision is needed; expiry after commit has no effect because the consented numbers are fixed.
Records are immutable, and refreshing creates a new record and a new revision with fresh consent from everyone.
compute and verify are vault commands that produce no signed statement, because the record travels inside the signed revision snapshot of F02.S01.M04.
Quotes are requested through F09.S03.M02 and pinned by id; the module never invents rates.
Events are written in the same IndexedDB transaction as the records.
Every quote request names purpose barter_normalization and a lifetime of at most 24 h, and the module closes records of subjects that ended, forked or froze.

verify calls F09.S03.M02 commerce.fx_quote.verify_embedded once per quote of a received revision and stores sourceSigned, issuerSigned, verificationLabel, label, expired and the ECB re-derivation deviation in quoteChecks; manual quotes are issuerSigned true but sourceSigned false, direct-provider quotes read 'source asserted by <issuer pseudonym>, not verifiable', and the UI shows only these results.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal compute or verify normalization in its vault.
Records of other parties are accepted only as part of a signed revision whose author is a party of the subject.
Quote sources are external adapters with their own policy; this module never grants a source any right over records.
compute is idempotent by (subjectId, inputs hash) and returns the same record while its quotes remain valid.
Rate source failures degrade to MUTINY_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE and never to a guessed rate.
A crash during compute leaves no partial record because the record and event are written in one IndexedDB transaction.
Records are P2 and travel only inside signed end-to-end encrypted revision envelopes to the subject's parties.
Quote requests to rate sources carry only the currency pair and requested lifetime, never DIDs, items or amounts.
Rate manipulation by a proposer is limited by labelling sources, recomputation by every participant and each participant's own consent on displayed numbers.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.normalizations), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every NormalizationRecord field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes local metadata while the pinned numbers stay verifiable.
Local diagnostics record compute and verify outcomes without amounts or DIDs and send nothing off the device (OBS-7).
compute for 16 items with 4 quotes completes within 60 ms at p95 excluding network quote retrieval.
Verify of a peer record completes within 20 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Conversion arithmetic is tested against a reference implementation for 10 000 random cases including negative exponents and zero-decimal currencies.
Expiry, refresh and mismatch behavior is tested with injected clocks.
Export contains normalization records of the user's subjects because they document the numbers that were signed.
Import verifies hashes and arithmetic, keeps quote data exactly, and marks records whose quotes have lapsed as expired without altering them.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A CompensationLeg records payer, payee, kind (money or extra_item), positive amount in the settlement currency, status, due date and the F09 deal and payment claim references; it never records a balance or a paid flag.
Legs become part of the immutable revision snapshot, so their amounts are consented to on the exact revision hash; after commit their amounts and parties never change.
Money legs use integer minor units in the cycle settlement currency, with no further conversion and no rounding.
Status values mirror CTR-COM-001 and the UI labels them accordingly; a leg is settled only by payee acknowledgement (cash, external) or final chain confirmation (crypto).
Compensation legs are validated for parties, currency, amount bounds and consistency with the subject's normalization before they can be sealed in a revision.
Claims are accepted only from the payer for a due leg and acknowledgements only from the payee for a claimed leg, through F09.
Crypto claims are never presented as paid without chain finality evidence, and a missing verifier leaves them claimed.
A leg is proposed in a revision, becomes due when the cycle is committed, is claimed by the payer, and is settled only by payee acknowledgement or chain finality as reported by F09.
A cycle cancelled before any handover withdraws all non-terminal legs, while a partially executed cycle keeps due legs for the recovery case to waive, adjust by agreement or dispute.
Expiry follows COM-3, 14 days without progress, and is shown to both parties; an expired leg never counts as settled.

Disputed legs are resolved only by the outcome of F09.S02.M02, by a waiver agreed in recovery, or end as expired when the dispute is withdrawn without acknowledgement for too long, lapses or the recovery closes unresolved; a disputed leg always has an exit.
Money legs of a recovery case become due only when the payer and the payee both accepted the compensation option.

propose, withdraw and suggest_plan are vault commands or pure queries that produce no statement, because legs are consented inside the signed revision; claim produces the payment claim statement defined by F09.S01.M01.
Acknowledgement by the payee is a F09.S01.M01 command and arrives here as a consumed event; this module never marks a payment acknowledged on its own.
Events are written in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change and statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.

Deals follow the N5 contract: commerce.deal.open {contextRef {type: cycle_compensation, id}, contextCid, parties, obligations} with deterministic dealId, commerce.deal.cancel on cancellation, and payment events matched by dealId with obligationId or claimId; this module produces no statement of its own and acts only on F09 records the receiving vault accepted (N2).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal propose or withdraw legs it is allowed to author, and only the payer can claim; the payee acknowledges through F09.S01.M01.
Claims and acknowledgements from other parties arrive as signed statements verified by F09.S01.M01 and are accepted only from the named payer or payee.
Relays and moderators have no capability over legs or payments.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands carry expectedRevision.
The claim and the leg update are one IndexedDB transaction with the outbox entry, so a crash leaves either no claim or a complete one.
Payment evidence is never auto-confirmed, and a missing verifier or unreachable F09 service leaves legs due or claimed.
Legs, claims and references are P2, end-to-end encrypted in transit to the participants and never published; claimRef is free text and never indexed.
The platform never holds funds or keys and the UI states 'Payments happen between you and the other person. ClassRup holds no money.'
False claims and false acknowledgements are limited by signature accountability, payee-only acknowledgement and disputes.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.compensation), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every CompensationLeg field with its F10.S02.M02 class, reports every leg with status due, claimed or disputed in which the principal is payer or payee as a DeletionPort.plan() blocker {kind: deal, ref: the leg's dealId, counterparties: [the other party of the leg]}, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the erased party in retained legs.
Local diagnostics record leg and claim outcomes without amounts or DIDs and send nothing off the device (OBS-7).
The planner for 8 participants completes within 5 ms.
Claim command including F09 call completes within 200 ms at p95 locally.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The planner is tested with golden fixtures for 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-party cycles and as a property test that residuals are within tolerance and sums are conserved.
Payment status handling is tested with fake F09 events including crypto without a verifier.
Export contains the user's compensation legs with claim references because they are part of the signed terms and payment evidence.
Import keeps amounts and statuses exactly as exported, never marks anything settled by itself, and asks F09 to re-sync claim status for due and claimed legs.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
An ItemValuation links one inventory item to a declared Money amount, basis, optional reference price, plausibility verdict, status and the per-author sequence of its signed projection.

The declared value is a public claim of the owner once the owner opts the item into barter, and the UI discloses this before signing; the published projection fields are P0 and retained RET-STANDARD until the owner deletes them, while the local ItemValuation record is P2 because it also holds flags, flagger DIDs and lock state.
Flags are stored as local records on the flagger's side and as received statements on the owner's side, with only the reason code, the flagger's subject and an optional comment up to 280 code points.

The projection classrup.mutiny.item_valuation_projection/v1 carries exactly {ownerId, inventoryItemId, listingCid, declared, basis, note, plausibility, ackNote?, seq, prev}; ackNote is present only when the owner acknowledged an automatic plausibility flag and is published because it is the owner's own explanation of a public verdict, written under the disclosure 'visible to anyone who sees your listing'; flags, flagCount, lockedBySubjectId, referencePrice and ratioPermille are never published.
Declarations are validated strictly on amount, currency, basis, ownership and lock state before anything is signed.
Plausibility thresholds are fixed numbers evaluated with integer arithmetic so every vault gets the same verdict.
Flags are accepted only from participants of a non-terminal subject that contains the item and in which the owner already signed consent or the reservation, and acknowledgements need a justification.
A valuation is declared, may be flagged automatically or by participants, may be acknowledged by the owner, and is superseded when the owner redeclares.
Every change that alters the signed projection increments seq by exactly 1 and is only possible while no reservation holds the item.

An automatically flagged valuation blocks matching and consent for the item everywhere until acknowledged or superseded, a peer flag blocks only the flagger's subject, and an acknowledgement never hides the flag history.
Flag-triggered state changes are capped at one per item per 30 days so repeated flags cannot keep re-blocking an item.

declare and acknowledge are vault commands that produce the signed projection statement classrup.mutiny.item_valuation_projection/v1 (whitelisted fields only); flag produces the signed statement classrup.mutiny.valuation_flag/v1 addressed to the owner, and the owner's answer to a peer flag is classrup.mutiny.valuation_flag/v1 kind ack to the flagging subject's participants; ingest commands verify other parties' statements.
Events are written in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change and statements go to the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
The module consumes listing, sell-terms and reservation events to keep references and locks consistent.

Statement schemas and signer roles registered with the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2): classrup.mutiny.item_valuation_projection/v1 signed by the item owner; classrup.mutiny.valuation_flag/v1 kind flag signed by a participant of the named subject and kind ack signed by the owner; this module is the single ingest owner of both and drops statements from DIDs the principal blocked silently (N7). classrup.mutiny.item_valuation/v1 names the local record only and is never sent.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal declare or acknowledge values of items it owns and flag values only as a participant of an active subject.
Incoming projections and flags are accepted only when signed by the owner (projections) or by a participant of the named subject (flags).
Relays may index public valuation projections under their hosting policy but have no capability to change or remove them except by refusing to host.
declare, flag and acknowledge are idempotent, and projections dedupe by cid and ordering by seq.
Each command is one IndexedDB transaction covering the record, event and outbox entry.
A valuation changed while a reservation exists is refused; there is no merge of conflicting values from two devices, and the higher seq after user confirmation wins for the public projection.
Declared values are public once the owner opts the item into barter and the UI says so before signing; flags are private between the flagger and the owner.
Valuations never contain addresses or exact location, and flags carry no personal data beyond the flagger's DID.

Value manipulation to game tolerance and flag abuse to block rivals are limited by plausibility thresholds, the rule that only participants of a subject in which the owner already signed may flag, the subject scope of peer flags, a 30-day per-flagger limit, a cap of one flag-triggered state change per item per 30 days and the owner's acknowledgement path.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section mutiny.valuations), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every ItemValuation field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish) before publishing the projection to each relay.
Local diagnostics record outcomes without amounts or DIDs and send nothing off the device (OBS-7).
declare completes within 80 ms at p95 including signing; list_for_items for 200 items within 50 ms.
Relay deployments that index projections expose counts by plausibility class under CTR-OBS-001.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Plausibility thresholds are tested at their exact boundaries with integer arithmetic.
Cross-vault tests cover projection chains, flags and locks with an in-memory relay.
Export contains the user's own ItemValuation records with signatures and sequence chain, and not other owners' projections, which are re-fetchable.
Import verifies signatures and chains, continues seq from the highest stored value and never imports a lock marker.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
An AvailabilityCalendar stores the provider, IANA zone, weekly windows, exceptions, buffers, notice, horizon and tz database version; slots are derived, never stored as local strings.
A SlotHold stores UTC start and end, the quote it serves, the holder, an expiry, a reconfirmation flag and a status, and is a P2 record kept only in the provider vault with RET-SHORT after it ends.

Calendar rules are P3 in the vault under schema classrup.services.calendar/v1; only the signed summary classrup.services.availability_summary/v1, built from rules and exceptions with an explicit field allowlist and no client names or hold data, leaves the device on provider action, as P0 to relays and P2 end-to-end encrypted to a client.
Calendar input is validated strictly; zone names are checked against the bundled tz database, not against the device locale.
Slot holds are validated for overlap including buffers, horizon, notice and exceptions before they are stored.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

A slot hold follows held to committed, released or expired, may be extended once while held, and committed can only be released by a booking cancellation; a re-hold after expiry is a new hold that references the old one.
Hold expiry is evaluated against the provider vault clock at command time and by a local sweep, so a stale hold can never block a slot after its expiry.
Commit is atomic with the booking confirmation written by F03.S02.M01 inside one IndexedDB transaction and is refused while the hold needs reconfirmation.

Rule changes, new exceptions and tz database moves flag every affected held hold needsReconfirmation; such a hold commits only after the provider reconfirms it with services.slot.reconfirm, and committed holds keep their UTC interval.
Calendar and slot commands are vault-local; only publish_summary produces a signed statement (classrup.services.availability_summary/v1).
Every command writes its local events in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change.
The module consumes quote outcome, booking cancellation, block, device key and deletion events to release held or committed slots and keep stored data consistent.
Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal who owns the calendar may run any command or query in this module.

The signed summary is accepted by receivers only when its signature verifies against the provider DID carried in the summary (providerId) and, when it names an offering, that offering's verified projection names the same provider; otherwise it is quarantined with a reason.
No relay role is involved; a relay may refuse to host the summary by its own policy, which changes only the sync state.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and hold creation is atomic with its overlap check.
Concurrent holds are serialized by a Web Locks lock per calendar; no distributed lock exists or is claimed.
A crash between a hold and its event leaves neither (single IndexedDB transaction).
Calendar rules and holds never leave the vault except the signed summary, whose allowlisted fields are generated from rules and exceptions only and contain no client identities, holds or bookings.
Summaries have a 14 day expiry so stale availability disappears from receivers' vaults.
Slot hoarding by clients is limited by per-client and per-calendar hold caps and short expiries.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section services.calendars), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates fields with their F10.S02.M02 class, calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) before signing any relay summary, and pseudonymizes holder DIDs on privacy.deletion.completed.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); local counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault.
Slot generation for 31 days meets p95 ≤ 50 ms on a mid-range phone.
Hold and commit commands meet p95 ≤ 100 ms with 5 000 stored holds.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
DST behaviour is covered by property tests over every zone in the bundled database for the years 2026 to 2028.
Statement and event payloads are checked against the schema registry.
The vault export contains calendars, exceptions and holds; expired holds are exported only as history.
Import validates the zone against the bundled tz database and flags holds whose local time moved.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A ServiceOffering stores provider, linked service listing, skill codes, rate type, rate Money, service area cell, provider time zone, remote flag, credentials, status and projection sequence with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Offerings are P3 records in the vault with fields classified through F10.S02.M02, and only the signed projection built through the F11.S01.M01 allowlist is P0; they are retained under RET-STANDARD, and credential evidence attachments are P2 and sent only inside an end-to-end encrypted quote thread.
