Rate type and currency are immutable after first publication; changing either requires a new offering so historical quotes stay interpretable.
Offering input is validated strictly; unknown fields are rejected and every violation maps to one stable error code.
Taxonomy, currency, region precision (F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell) and credential limits are checked before persistence and again at publish and on every published revision.
Free text is plain text only and is length-limited by code points.
Offerings follow draft, published, withdrawn; withdrawn is terminal and a new offering is created to return to market.

Publish re-runs all validation, requires a published service listing, a calendar from F03.S01.M02 and federation_publish consent for each selected relay, has the projection signed and stored through StatementPublisherPort.publish and writes the local event in the same IndexedDB transaction; a revision of a published offering republishes the projection with seq+1 and prev in the same way.
Withdrawal is automatic when the linked listing is unpublished or expired; relay-side refusal or removal never changes the local status and is recorded only in that relay's sync state.
The module exposes create, revise, publish and withdraw as vault commands (publish, and revise of a published offering, additionally produce a signed projection statement) and two local queries.

Each command writes its local events to the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change per EVT-8; only publish, a revision of a published offering and the key-revocation re-sign create a signed statement (EVT-9), always through StatementPublisherPort.publish, and the withdrawal tombstone is issued by F11.S01.M02 from services.offering.withdrawn.

The module consumes listing, device key and deletion events so that offerings never stay published locally without a published listing or with a revoked signature; relay moderation never arrives as an event because it changes nothing locally.

Every classrup.services.offering/v1 projection is signed and stored only through the F11.S01.M01 StatementPublisherPort.publish implemented by F11.S01.M02, the stored projectionCid and the projectionCid of services.offering.published equal the cid that call returns, and the module never calls a signing primitive, holds a key, keeps an envelope chain counter or calls issueTombstone.
Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal who authored an offering may create, revise, publish or withdraw it; there is no server role.
The signed projection is readable by anyone who fetches it from a relay; drafts and the full vault record never leave the vault. Relay policy decides whether a relay indexes or serves it.
Foreign projections received from other authors are stored read-only with provenance only when the signature verifies against the listed author key; otherwise they are quarantined with a reason.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using a local command id, and revise, publish and withdraw require expectedRevision.
Publish, a revision of a published offering and withdraw are atomic with their local outbox event and sync outbox entry; a crash between them leaves neither.
Listing and device key events are consumed idempotently using the inbox table.
Offerings never contain exact addresses; the service area is exactly L2, and publishing warns that copies already fetched by other vaults cannot be recalled (PRV-6).
Credential evidence attachments are P2, travel only inside end-to-end encrypted envelopes to a client with an open QuoteRequest, and relays see ciphertext only.
Fake credentials and keyword stuffing are limited by self-attestation labels, local caps, receiver-side filtering and each relay's hosting policy; there is no central suspension or takedown.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section services.offerings), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies fields with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) for every relay before calling StatementPublisherPort.publish, and calls F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell on serviceAreaCell (N8).
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the error log stay in the vault and can be exported by the user.
Create, revise and publish meet a local write budget of p95 ≤ 100 ms on a mid-range phone with 1 000 offerings in the vault.
Local reads meet p95 ≤ 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command inputs, outputs and event payloads against the schema registry.
Privacy tests prove that no credential evidence or area other than an L2 cell appears in the signed projection and that unverified inbound projections are quarantined.
The vault export (IOX-1, primary backup) contains all the provider's offerings including drafts, withdrawn ones and sync states.
Import validates IDs, schema version, taxonomy codes and currency before accepting a record.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A ServiceDisputeLink stores booking, optional milestone, scope, opener, counterparty, statement, evidence pack, case reference, pre-dispute state, state, resolution and close reason, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
Links are P2 and kept under RET-EVIDENCE; the evidence pack stores cids and hashes, never copies of deliverable bytes.

A link is unique per booking and scope key among links that are not withdrawn or link_failed, and at most one link per booking is open (pending_link or linked); duplicates are merged rather than stored twice.
Eligibility, scope and statement are validated before any case is requested.

Inbound dispute notices are validated for signature and party role and then re-checked against the receiving vault's own records and clock (window with 24 h tolerance, limits, duplicates, milestone and state rules) before a link is created; failures are quarantined and emit nothing.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.
Links move pending_link, linked, resolved; withdrawn and link_failed are terminal exits, link_failed happens only before a case is linked and never blocks a new open.

Resolution is reported only by F09 resolution and withdrawal events and mapped to service effects by the table in the note below; this module never decides an outcome and no effect changes an obligation.

Opening emits services.dispute.opened exactly once per link, when the link becomes linked to a verified case, so downstream freezes are idempotent; every terminal transition emits services.dispute.closed exactly once.

When commerce.dispute.resolved carries the advisory F09 disposition {kind continue|settled|cancelled|waived, favouredDid?, agreedAmount?}, the service effect follows the disposition kind per the mapping note; only when it is absent, or ignored because favouredDid is not a party of the booking, does the outcome-type mapping apply, and neither path changes an obligation.

The module exposes vault commands open, withdraw and receive; open produces the signed notice statement and calls the F09.S02.M02 case port (the single case-creation path) in the same vault transaction.

services.dispute.opened and services.dispute.closed are local events; they leave the device only as the signed dispute notice and dispute withdrawal statements, and an opened event derived from a received notice carries origin federated and never creates a case.
The module consumes F09 case events to link, resolve and close; it never writes to the DisputeCase except through the open and withdraw ports.
Vault policy - only the local principal who is client or provider of the booking can open or withdraw a dispute for it.

Inbound notices and withdrawals are accepted only when the signer is the other party of the booking (the opener of the referenced notice for withdrawals); otherwise they are quarantined, and a notice from a locally blocked party of an existing booking is quarantined for review rather than dropped (exception to N7).
Relay roles are not involved; a relay can refuse to carry the notice, which changes only the sync state.
Open is idempotent by local command id and by scopeKey; a repeated open returns the existing link.
A failure of the F09 case port leaves a pending_link that retries with backoff and the link id as idempotency reference, and never creates two cases.
The notice and the link commit in one vault transaction; a crash leaves neither.
Statements and evidence references are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the counterparty and the case handler chosen in F09, and never appear in logs or notifications.
Retaliatory or repeated disputes are limited by eligibility, per-booking caps and per-day quotas.
A dispute does not publish anything about the counterparty; any reputation effect is decided by F07 from signed resolutions, not here.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section services.disputes), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies fields with F10.S02.M02 and pseudonymizes the counterparty in retained links on privacy.deletion.completed.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and diagnostics stay in the vault.
Open and preview_evidence meet p95 ≤ 200 ms with 25 evidence items on a mid-range phone.
Evidence assembly never blocks the UI thread longer than 50 ms per slice.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate the notice and withdrawal statements, events and the F09 case port calls against the schema registry.
Two-vault tests with a hostile relay cover duplicate, dropped and simultaneous notices.
The vault export contains links, notices and evidence packs so a dispute can be reconstructed without the relay.
Import verifies notice signatures and cids; unverifiable notices are kept as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Milestone stores booking, sequence, parallel flag, title, amount, due date, status, the ordered list of submissions with their cids, the approval cid, the dealId of its Deal and the derived payment proof level, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
Milestones are P2, stored in both participants' vaults, kept under RET-EVIDENCE, and the amounts of one booking sum exactly to the booking total in one currency.
Submission and approval records are immutable once signed; a new submission supersedes the previous one and never edits it.
Milestone ids, seq, titles, amounts and parallel flags come from the milestone plan in the quote the client signed (quoteCid); the provider cannot assign ids or change amounts after acceptance.
Statements are validated in the order schema, signature, signer role, booking and milestone references, cid binding, business rules.
Submissions, approvals and change requests are checked against the milestone state and round limits before any change.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key; quarantined statements store the code.
Milestones follow pending, submitted, approved, settled with a change loop; cancelled and settled are terminal.
Approval requires the exact current submission cid; payment never changes approval and approval never implies payment.
Settlement requires payee acknowledgement or chain finality; a claim alone never completes a milestone or the booking.
Approval opens the milestone's Deal through commerce.deal.open in the same vault transaction; if the Deal cannot be opened, approval is not signed and the milestone stays submitted.

Disputes freeze submitted and approved milestones as disputed with their pre-dispute status stored and only set an overlay on other states; the matching commerce.dispute.resolved or commerce.dispute.withdrawn restores the pre-dispute status per the F03.S02.M03 mapping, and an obligation is released only by a mutually signed Deal cancellation.
A reorg or failure reported by F09.S01.M03 lowers the proof level shown and never leaves a milestone showing a stronger state than the claim reached (COM-4, FLOW-11).
The module exposes vault commands for submit, approve, request_changes and completion signing; each produces a named signed statement and a sync outbox entry in the same vault transaction.
Inbound statements are applied by an ingestion command that drops statements from blocked DIDs silently, verifies, deduplicates by cid and derives local events with actor.kind federated.
Milestones are created locally on services.booking.confirmed from the client-signed quote plan, and payment status is derived from F09 events resolved through the milestone's dealId.
Event payloads carry clientId and providerId for notification routing (N4), and services.booking.completed carries contextId, contextType, completionCid and parties as N3 requires.
Vault policy - only the local principal who is the booking provider may submit; only the principal who is the booking client may approve or request changes.

Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches the role for that statement in this booking; statements from blocked DIDs are dropped silently (N7) and other mismatches quarantined with a reason code.
Payment events are applied only when their dealId equals the dealId of a milestone of a booking in this vault; relays have no role.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements are idempotent by cid; replays and duplicate relay deliveries never advance a milestone twice.

Contradictory signed statements for one milestone (two submissions with the same predecessor, or approvals of different cids) freeze the milestone and require explicit renegotiation, never last-writer-wins.
Each state change, its event and its sync outbox entry commit in one IndexedDB transaction.
Milestone content, deliverables and notes are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the two participants, and never appear in logs or notifications.
Deliverable hashes bind evidence to files without exposing them; relays see ciphertext and size only.
Approval pressure, dummy deliverables and fake payment claims are limited by hash checks, explicit proof labels and the dispute path.
Deliverables are F08.S01.M03 images of at most 5 MiB or external hash references whose bytes never pass through ClassRup.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section services.milestones), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies fields with F10.S02.M02, drops milestone statements from blocked DIDs at ingestion (N7) and pseudonymizes the counterparty on privacy.deletion.completed.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and diagnostics stay in the vault.
Milestone commands meet p95 ≤ 150 ms excluding attachment hashing, and hashing of a 5 MiB attachment or a streamed external file runs in a worker without blocking the UI longer than 50 ms per slice.
Payment event handling meets p95 ≤ 50 ms per event.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate statements, events and the commerce.deal.open call against the schema registry and the F09 contract.
Two-vault integration tests with a hostile in-memory relay cover duplicate, dropped and reordered statements.
The vault export contains milestones, submissions and the signed statements with their cids so approval evidence survives vault loss.
Import verifies each signature and cid before restoring and keeps unverifiable records as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
QuoteRequest, ServiceQuote and Booking are P2 records stored in the vault of each participant, with revision per CTR-ID-001 and the cid of each signed statement they derive from.

Money is integer minor units per CTR-MNY-001; an hourly total is computed once as rate times estimatedMinutes divided by 60 with HALF_EVEN rounding (F09.S03.M03), and the milestone amounts must sum exactly to the total.

A quote is immutable after issue; changing anything requires a superseding quote with a new cid, and acceptance binds to the exact quote cid and its milestone plan, whose milestone ids are derived as uuid(sha256(bookingId + ':' + seq)).

Every inbound statement is validated in a fixed order - block check (statements from blocked DIDs are dropped silently), schema, signature, signer role derived from the signer key, referenced cids, expiry, business rules - and the first failure decides the error.
Business rules check offering state, blocks, limits, money, plan equality and slot availability before any state changes.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key; quarantined statements store the code.
Requests, quotes and bookings follow the declared lifecycles; a statement that implies another transition is refused and quarantined with CONFLICT_STATE.
A booking is confirmed only by the provider's signed confirmation; acceptance alone yields awaiting_confirmation.

Confirmation commits (or re-holds and commits) the slot and stores the signed confirmation in one vault transaction; failure of either step leaves the booking awaiting_confirmation, and no Deal is opened here.

Both vaults run the 24 h confirmation timeout and the vault whose timer fires signs and sends a confirmation_timeout cancellation; a confirmation that crosses such a cancellation moves the booking to conflicted (frozen for explicit renegotiation, ADR-0016 section 5) instead of being quarantined.

Disputes overlay the booking - services.dispute.opened freezes a confirmed or in_progress booking as disputed with its pre-dispute status stored, and only sets openDisputeLinkId on bookings in other states; the matching commerce.dispute.resolved or commerce.dispute.withdrawn restores the pre-dispute status per the F03.S02.M03 resolution mapping, and obligations change only through mutually signed statements.

In-progress and disputed bookings are cancelled only by mutual consent through F08.S02.M02 (consent.services.booking.cancel.v1 over the booking revision hash), and a conflicted consent freezes the booking.
The module exposes vault commands for each party action; commands that another party must rely on also produce a named signed statement and enter the sync outbox in the same vault transaction.

A single ingestion command applies inbound statements; it drops statements from blocked DIDs silently, verifies, deduplicates by cid, derives local events with actor.kind federated and quarantines failures.
Events are local (EVT-8); they leave the device only as the statements named below.

Event payloads carry the client and provider DIDs that F13.S01.M03 needs to route notifications (N4), and services.booking.cancelled carries quoteId and slotHoldId so F03.S01.M02 can release the hold without reading the Booking.

services.booking.confirmed carries contextId (bookingId), contextType booking, contextCid (the confirmationCid of the provider-signed booking_confirmation, which binds quoteCid and acceptanceCid) and parties [{did, role client or provider}], identical in both vaults, so F07.S03.M01 can open the pending review window from the bilateral opening statement.
Vault policy - requests and acceptances can be created only by the local principal acting as client; quotes, confirmations and withdrawals only by the local principal who is the offering provider.

Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer key belongs to the party whose role the statement type and reason require for this request or booking (the role is never read from the payload); statements from blocked DIDs are dropped silently and other failures are quarantined with a reason code.
No relay role is involved; relays only carry ciphertext and cannot create, alter or confirm any record.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements are idempotent by cid, so duplicate delivery through two relays is harmless.

Conflicting signed promises (two confirmations, a confirmation crossing a timeout cancellation, two different acceptances of one quote, or a conflicted consent) freeze the affected booking as conflicted and require explicit renegotiation; there is no last-writer-wins for money or commitments.
Each state change and its sync outbox entry are one IndexedDB transaction; a crash leaves neither.
Requests, quotes and bookings are P2 and travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the two participants; relays see ciphertext and routing metadata only.
Descriptions and attachments never enter public projections, logs or notifications; notifications carry a reference and a template key only.

Spam requests, Sybil floods from fresh DIDs and phishing text are limited by receiving-vault caps across all senders, first-contact queuing, local quotas, receiver-side filtering and relay hosting policy; no global enforcement is claimed.

Late-fee claims are computed from delivery evidence both parties can check (the earliest relay-signed receipt time from a relay the canceller selected, else the receiving vault receipt time), the claimed signing time counts only within the 5 minute skew tolerance, and the signed cancellation carries one fee number the counterparty accepts or disputes through F03.S02.M03 (scope cancellation_fee).

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section services.bookings), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies fields with F10.S02.M02, drops statements from blocked DIDs at ingestion (N7) and pseudonymizes the counterparty on privacy.deletion.completed.

An on-site address is never stored in these records - it is shared only as an L4 location share (F06.S02.M02) through the encrypted F08 thread with a TTL of at most 24 h, stored P3 in the provider vault, purged at TTL and excluded from evidence packs; L3 is the default disclosure before booking and the request sheet warns when a description looks like a street address.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); local counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Vault commands meet p95 ≤ 150 ms on a mid-range phone with 2 000 bookings stored, excluding network delivery.
Statement verification meets p95 ≤ 30 ms per envelope.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate all statement schemas, signatures and event payloads against the schema registry.
Cross-vault flows are covered by two-vault integration tests with an in-memory relay that can drop, duplicate, delay and reorder envelopes.
The vault export contains requests, quotes, bookings and all signed statements with their cids so evidence survives vault loss.
Import verifies every statement signature and cid before restoring; unverifiable items are kept as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Bid stores auction, terms cid, bidder, alias, kind, visible amount, optional proxy maximum, signed validity window, host sequence and time, ledger hashes, receipt and status, with revision per CTR-ID-001.

The proxy maximum, bidderId and clientNonce are P3 in the bidder vault and P2 to the host, the only listed participant - they travel only inside the bid envelope end-to-end encrypted to hostKeyId (PRV-5) and the host holds them under its published retention - while public projections show only alias, amount, kind and host time.
The visible amount and sequence are immutable once the host has assigned them; a change is a new bid or a retraction entry.
The ledger hash input includes bidCid, so each held receipt binds the bidder-signed bid it acknowledges.

The host first looks up (bidder, auction, clientNonce) in the idempotency store - the same body returns the stored receipt and a different body returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED - and then validates in a fixed order - schema, signature, host acceptance, validity window, auction state and host time, minimum or max-only rule, eligibility and revoked keys, rate limits, the bids_per_day account limit - and the first failure decides the error.
The bidder vault performs the same checks it can (schema, host acceptance, block check, minimum from the last known state) before sending, but only the host decision counts.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; eligibility failures never reveal the linkage that caused them.
Proxy resolution follows the numbered rules PX1 to PX5 (proxy-v1) below, which are the reference model for the property tests and for ledger replay.

Bids follow submitted, then winning, outbid, rejected or not_placed, with retraction only from winning; won comes only from auctions.auction.won naming the bidder and can still become void; lost, retracted, rejected, not_placed and void are final, and host_silent covers a host that never reports.
Leader changes are decided only inside the per-auction lease by the deterministic proxy algorithm, so replaying the ledger always reproduces the same prices.
A retraction of the leader promotes the highest remaining maximum to leader at a recomputed price, using the same algorithm.
At close the outcome decides - an unsold auction makes its leader lost, never won - and a bid without a receipt resolves to not_placed or lost rather than staying submitted.

The bidder vault command auctions.bid.submit signs the bid and sends it to the host; the host relay command auctions.bid.place validates, orders and receipts it; retraction mirrors this pair with auctions.bid.retract and auctions.bid.apply_retraction.

Bid events are host-local events and are derived in participant vaults only from host-signed statements - bid_receipt, retraction_receipt and bid_outbid - ingested with auctions.bid.receive (actor.kind federated); max amounts are never in any event.
Bidding has no offline queue; time and order are decided by the host.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 with their signer roles - classrup.auctions.bid/v1 and classrup.auctions.bid_retraction/v1 by the bidder key (bidderId), classrup.auctions.bid_receipt/v1, classrup.auctions.retraction_receipt/v1 and classrup.auctions.bid_outbid/v1 by the host key named in the terms - and vaults act only on records they accepted (N2).

The host delivers bid_outbid to the outbid bidder's mailbox so its vault can derive auctions.bid.outbid, and calls the relay hook notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push to that bidder when it set pushOptIn (N17).

The host delivers a seller copy of the bid_receipt of each accepted bid with a visible amount to the seller's mailbox - the first at once, later ones coalesced to the newest at most once per 60 s - and the seller vault derives auctions.bid.placed from each verified copy with listingId, sellerId, seq and bidCount and without bidderId or bidId, so the seller vault's listing edit lock (F04.S01.M01 for F01.S01.M02) knows that bids exist (N11, N17).

Bid intake - auctions.bid.place and auctions.bid.apply_retraction - returns with the host-signed receipt a classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 from F15.S02.M01 ReceiptPort.issue with destination '<relayId>/auction/<auctionId>', digest over the exact request bytes and no cid; the bidder vault verifies it against the host relay's published key set and records it as transport acknowledged only, because only the host-signed bid_receipt shows the bid placed.
Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal can sign bids and retractions for its own key; no one can bid on behalf of another key.

Relay policy - the host accepts a bid only when the bid signature verifies against the bidder key inside it, the host acceptance names this host, and hosting policy and quotas allow it; no relay access token substitutes for the bidder signature.

Public ledger reads expose aliases only; the seller learns the winner's key only through the host-signed result disclosure, and a non-winning bidder's key only if the host lists it as a second-chance candidate after a seller-signed non-payment report, which the bidder trust panel discloses.

Bids are idempotent by (bidder, auction, clientNonce) for 24 h on the host, looked up before validation; a replay with the same body returns the original receipt and a different body returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
All bids of one auction are serialized by the per-auction lease (IDM-8) with a fencing token; ledger append, price projection and soft-close decision commit in one SQLite transaction.
A crash before commit leaves no ledger entry and no receipt; a crash after commit and before reply is repaired by receipt fetch.

A signed bid is valid only until its notAfter (at most 60 s after the bidder's createdAt claim), so neither the host nor delayed transport can place it later, and a bid with no receipt resolves to not_placed.

After a host restore this module's AuctionHostPort implementation freezes, before the restored relay accepts a bid, every hosted auction whose bids may lie in the announced lost window, so the host never assigns a sequence number that a receipt it signed before the restore already holds; bidders keep their receipts and relay receipts as evidence.

Proxy maxima, bidder keys and nonces never appear in public projections, logs, errors or other users' exports, and maxima never in events; the host holds them, received only inside envelopes encrypted to hostKeyId, and the UI says so.
Aliases are stable only within one auction and derived under a per-auction host secret, so they cannot be linked across auctions; this is pseudonymity, not anonymity, because the host sees keys.
Bid spam, probing of proxy maxima and rapid retract abuse are limited by increments, rate limits, a single retraction and host quotas.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section auctions.bids), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates Bid fields with their F10.S02.M02 class (maxAmount, bidderId and clientNonce P3 in the vault and P2 with the host as the only listed participant), consumes privacy.deletion.completed, and sets pushOptIn only after privacy.consent.check(notify_push) for the host is granted.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); the host relay exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6, without maxima or keys.
Bid placement meets p95 ≤ 150 ms on the host at 50 bids per second across 500 auctions, and p99 ≤ 400 ms for one hot auction at 20 bids per second.
Ledger verification of 5 000 entries in the vault completes in ≤ 500 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The proxy algorithm is covered by property tests on random bid sequences with a reference model, and the ledger by replay tests.
Concurrency is covered by deterministic tests with an injected clock and lease, including expiry and fencing.
The bidder's vault export contains their bids, receipts and own maxima; it does not contain other bidders' data.
Import verifies receipt signatures and chain hashes against the stored host key; failures are kept as read-only history with a warning.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An AuctionResult stores outcome, winner alias and commitment, final price, reserve check, ledger head, the cids of the public result and the disclosure, the vault's role, deal links per buyer, settlement state and second-chance data, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
The result is created once per auction by the host and mirrored read-only in participant vaults; participant-specific fields (role, deal ids, local state, host void application) are local.

Result visibility is tiered by two host-signed statements - the public classrup.auctions.result/v1 (outcome, final price, winner alias, winnerCommitment, ledger head) that every bidder verifies, and the P2 classrup.auctions.result_disclosure/v1 (winnerId and salt) end-to-end encrypted to the seller and the winner, who verify both.
finalPrice is the price of the ledger head entry at close; the close never computes a price of its own.
Close preconditions are checked under the lease - auction is open, host time is at or after currentEndsAt, lease token is current.
Inbound results, disclosures, reports, offers and responses are validated for signature, signer role and referenced ids before any local state changes.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Block checks (F07.S02.M02 isBlockedEither) run in the vaults - on result receipt in the seller and winner vaults and before a second-chance offer or response - because only a vault knows its principal's blocks; the host never filters by blocks.

A result is determined once and then follows its role - the host row and non-party mirrors are recorded, the seller and winner follow the sale path to completed - or ends unsold, failed or voided; terminal states never change.
completed requires commerce.deal.completed with acknowledged or final payment per CTR-COM-001; a claim alone does not complete.
Non-payment and second chance are explicit and signed; day 10 only prompts the seller, there is no automatic transition or penalty, and the host only records a signal.

A host void is a finding each vault applies on its own - voided when the local Deals have no acknowledged or final claim, otherwise recorded as void after payment with no state change - and it never cancels a Deal, which needs every party's signed cancel in F09.

The host relay command auctions.result.determine runs from the close tick and produces the host-signed public result and disclosure; participant vaults ingest them with auctions.result.receive and the other parties' signed statements with auctions.result.receive_statement.
Seller and candidate actions are vault commands that produce named signed statements and go through the sync outbox and the host.

Auction closed, won and unsold events are host-local and are derived in each participant vault, the seller vault included, on receipt of the verified host-signed result (actor.kind federated, N17); auctions.auction.unsold carries listingId from the verified terms so the listing modules can follow it (N11).

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 with their signer roles - result, result_disclosure and second_chance_candidates by the host key in the terms, non_payment_report and second_chance_offer by the seller key (sellerId), second_chance_response by the nominated candidate key - and vaults act only on statements they accepted (N2).

Host-produced events call the relay hook notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push - closed and unsold to the seller, won to the seller and winner, second_chance_offered to the candidate - for recipients who set pushOptIn (N17).

This module registers an AuctionHostPort.freezeActivityIn(lostWindow) implementation with the relay process (inverted registration, no depends_on edge; F15.S03.M03 calls it and the F04.S01.M02 implementation after a restore before the port opens) that freezes, through F04.S01.M01 auctions.auction.freeze with cause close_possibly_lost, every hosted open auction whose currentEndsAt is at or before lostWindow.to and that has no result row; on auctions.auction.frozen a vault holding the verified result returns it, with the disclosure in the seller and winner vaults, once to auctions.result.readopt, which re-adopts the host's own signed statements and re-emits the host-local closed and won or unsold events.

Relay policy - only the host's close scheduler holding the close lease may determine a result, and no host operator or moderator can call determine; record_non_payment and nominate act only on a non-payment report signed by the auction's sellerId key.

Vault policy - only the local principal who is the seller reports non-payment and offers second chance; only the nominated candidate key responds; incoming results and disclosures are accepted only when signed by the host key in the auction terms, and other statements only from their registered signer role.
Public result projection exposes no winner key; seller and winner receive it inside the end-to-end encrypted disclosure.
Close is idempotent by the unique result per auction; repeated or concurrent close attempts produce exactly one result.
The result, the mark_closed call and the outbox event are one host SQLite transaction under the lease and fence token.
Result delivery is at least once via mailboxes and idempotent by result cid in the vaults.

Applying a void is a local decision in each vault on its own Deal state; no lock spans vaults, and a payment acknowledged after the void was applied completes the Deal as F09 records it while the result stays voided.

A host restore never yields a second result - an auction whose close may have been lost is frozen before the close tick runs, re-adoption stores exactly the returned host-signed result and is idempotent by result cid, and a frozen auction that nobody re-adopts is cancelled with reason host_restore by F04.S01.M01, never closed anew.
The winner key is shared only with the seller and the winner; bidders see aliases, the winner commitment and the host-signed ledger head.
Non-payment reports and second-chance offers are P2, end-to-end encrypted, and carry no reputational automation; the host records only a count for its own fraud queue.
False non-payment reports are limited by the day-3 floor and day-30 ceiling, the no-acknowledged-payment guard, signed evidence of the Deal state, and the dispute path.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section auctions.results), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates fields with their F10.S02.M02 class (winnerId, winnerSalt and candidate keys P2 to seller, winner and host), consumes privacy.deletion.completed to pseudonymize winnerId, sellerId and candidateId in retained evidence, and silently drops statements from DIDs blocked either way (N7).

A non-winning bidder's key reaches the seller only as one of at most 3 second-chance candidates after a seller-signed non-payment report, which the F04.S01.M02 trust panel discloses before the first bid.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); the host exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6.
Close lag p95 ≤ 2 s and p99 ≤ 5 s after currentEndsAt on the host with 1 000 auctions ending in the same minute.
Result verification in the vault completes in ≤ 300 ms with 5 000 ledger entries.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Close concurrency is covered by deterministic tests with injectable clock and lease, including extension races, double workers and lease expiry.
Contract tests validate result, disclosure, report, candidate, offer and response statements and the Deal context against schema registries.
The participant's vault export contains results, signed statements and Deal references so the outcome can be reconstructed without the host.
Import verifies the host signature, the disclosure commitment and the ledger head; unverifiable results are kept as read-only history with a warning.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An Auction stores listing and pinned listing cid, seller, host relay identity and key, currency, start price, reserve commitment, increment table, schedule with acceptBy, soft-close rules version, extension counters, price projection and status, with revision per CTR-ID-001.

The reserve value and its salt are P3 in the seller vault and P2 to the host, the only listed participant - they travel only inside an envelope end-to-end encrypted to hostKeyId (PRV-5) and the host holds them under its published retention - while public terms and events carry only the salted hash commitment and a reserveMet flag.
Money is integer minor units per CTR-MNY-001; increments are computed from a tiered table in major-unit templates converted with ceiling to the currency exponent.

The signed terms pin listingCid (the cid of the published listing projection), acceptBy and softCloseRulesVersion softclose-v1, so the host cannot accept late, the listing text that bids rest on is identifiable, and the soft-close constants cannot change during the auction.
Terms are validated strictly in the seller vault before signing and again by the host relay before countersigning.
The host never accepts terms that fail the same rules, whatever the seller vault claims.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key; the reserve value is never echoed in an error.

Schedule and accept_hosting check the listing (published, kind auction, subtypeRef equal to this auction, listingCid current) because create allows a draft without a listing; the published check is never made at create.

Auctions follow draft, proposed, scheduled, open, closed, with cancelled as an exit before close and cancel_pending, host_silent and needs_host_check as vault states for an unanswered cancel, a silent host and an unconfirmed import; closed and cancelled are terminal.
Scheduled requires the host's verified countersignature; no host acceptance means no auction.

Opening, end adjustment, host cancellation and closing are host-clock decisions; the seller vault shows them only after receiving the host-signed statements (auction_opened, extension, host_cancel, result).

A vault never cancels a proposed auction silently - at acceptBy it sends a signed auction_cancel and waits in cancel_pending - and an auction whose host stops answering moves to host_silent, which releases the listing lock but still yields to a later valid host statement.

A host restore freezes every auction whose bids or close may have been lost - on the host through auctions.auction.freeze before the restored relay accepts a request, in vaults from the verified restore announcement - and a frozen auction takes no bid, extension or close until it is renegotiated - re-adoption of the host's own signed result closes it, and the seller's cancel or the host's cancel 72 h after the freeze, both with reason host_restore, cancel it; no new result is ever determined for it.

Vault commands create, schedule and cancel the seller's auction; schedule and cancel produce signed statements to the host; the host relay offers accept_hosting, open, apply_cancel, adjust_end and mark_closed as relay commands and answers with host-signed statements that the vault ingests with auctions.auction.receive.

Auction events exist on the host as relay-local events and are derived again in each participant vault when the host-signed statement arrives (actor.kind federated); they never leave a device otherwise.
The module consumes listing events to cancel auctions whose listing becomes unavailable.

Every statement this module sends or accepts is registered with the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with its signer role - classrup.auctions.auction/v1 and classrup.auctions.auction_cancel/v1 by the seller key (sellerId), classrup.auctions.host_acceptance/v1, classrup.auctions.auction_opened/v1 and classrup.auctions.host_cancel/v1 by the host key named in the terms - and vaults act only on records they accepted (N2).

The vault query auctions.auction.edit_lock answers F01.S01.M02 before a material listing edit from the bidCount the seller vault folds in from auctions.bid.placed (derived from the host-signed seller copies of bid receipts, F04.S01.M02) and from the cached host projection, so material edits are refused while the auction has bids or may have them (N11).

Host-produced auction events call the relay hook notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push - opening to the seller, a host cancellation to the seller and bidders - for recipients who set pushOptIn (N17); the hook is provided by the relay runtime.

Auction events derived in the seller vault carry listingId and come only from verified host-signed statements - auctions.auction.scheduled from host_acceptance, auctions.auction.opened from auction_opened and auctions.auction.cancelled from host_cancel, the only local exceptions being a discarded draft and Release anyway - so F01.S01.M02 and the other listing modules follow the auction of a listing without a direct call (N11, N17).

auctions.auction.freeze is the host-internal command that the AuctionHostPort implementations of F04.S01.M02 and F04.S01.M03 call while F15.S03.M03 restores the relay; it emits the host-local auctions.auction.frozen and calls notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push to opted-in participants, and auctions.auction.receive derives auctions.auction.frozen in each vault from the host relay's verified classrup.platform.relay_restore/v1 for every local auction of that host whose open interval overlaps the lost window, whatever its local status.
Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal who is the seller creates, schedules or cancels the auction; the seller also reads the reserve.

Relay policy - the host accepts terms only when signed by the seller key named in the terms, at or before acceptBy and within its hosting policy; open, adjust_end, mark_closed and freeze are host-internal and callable only by the host's own scheduler, its restore hook and sibling modules holding a current fence token.

Host moderators may cancel an auction on that host with a stated reason; this affects only that host. Bidders and viewers read the public projection with no capability beyond a signed or anonymous request.

Vaults accept host_acceptance, auction_opened and host_cancel only when signed by the host key named in the seller's own terms and bound to termsCid, and a restore announcement only when signed by a non-revoked key of the host relay (V13); anything else is quarantined.
Vault commands are idempotent through local command ids; host commands are idempotent by terms cid and auction id.
Host open, adjust_end and mark_closed run inside the per-auction lease (IDM-8) and are safe to repeat; a stale lease token is refused.
A seller vault crash after signing terms but before recording them is repaired by re-sending the same terms cid, which the host deduplicates.

A lost acceptance is never resolved by a silent local cancel - the vault sends auction_cancel at acceptBy and keeps the listing locked until the host answers, the seller explicitly releases it, or the host_silent deadline passes.

A host restore never contradicts what the host signed before it - auctions whose bids or close may lie in the announced lost window are frozen before the restored relay accepts a request, a frozen auction is never reopened or closed with a new result, and freeze, re-adoption and the restore cancel are idempotent per auction.

The reserve is committed by salted hash publicly and known only to the seller and the host; bidders learn whether it has been met, and when a proxy maximum lifts the visible price exactly to the reserve (F04.S01.M02 reserve rule PX4) the price reveals the reserve value, which the setup screen states; the seller can verify the host's commitment at close.
Public projections carry listing reference, start price, increments, times, host identity and reserveMet, but not bidder identities, aliases tied to keys, or max bids.
The host sees the reserve and bids in plaintext and can misbehave; this trust is stated before the seller schedules and before each bidder's first bid.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section auctions.auctions), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates every Auction field with its F10.S02.M02 class (reservePrice and reserveSalt P3 in the vault and P2 with the host as the only listed participant), consumes privacy.deletion.completed to pseudonymize retained evidence, and calls privacy.consent.check for federation_publish before the public projection is sent and for notify_push before setting pushOptIn.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); the host relay exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6.
Open runs within 5 s of startsAt at the 95th percentile on the host.
Vault commands meet p95 ≤ 150 ms; host accept_hosting meets p95 ≤ 300 ms at 20 req/s.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate terms, host acceptance, events and the public projection against the schema registry, including that the reserve never appears.
Two-party integration tests run a seller vault and an in-memory host relay with an injectable clock.
The seller's vault export contains their auctions, signed terms, host statements and the reserve with its salt; the reserve appears in no other user's export.

Import verifies signatures and cids; auctions that were scheduled or open on import enter needs_host_check and are re-verified with the host before being shown as scheduled or open, and the sweep never cancels them.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ShillCheck stores auction, subject key, verdict, reason codes, evidence references, score, host time and status, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
ShillChecks are P3 host records because they reveal key linkage; they never appear in public projections, events to bidders, exports of other users or logs.
Only denied and flagged evaluations are stored; allowed evaluations leave only counters.

Revoked keys and revoked attestations stay in the linkage cache as linked for the seller for at least 30 days, and permanently for auctions scheduled before the revocation; linked_host_registration evidence is never dropped on revocation.
The eligibility check evaluates deterministic linkage first and heuristic scoring only afterwards and asynchronously.

Scoring inputs are bounded - the last 20 bids of the subject and the last 30 days of host data, taken from consumed host-local auctions.bid.* and auction result events - and the features, points, caps and thresholds are the fixed constants of scoring table shill-v1 in this specification.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; the bidder-facing code never discloses the reason.

Linkage evidence is limited to signed or host-recorded co-occurrence - key sets of identity documents (identity.portable_doc.key_set and find_by_key), same_owner attestations signed by both DIDs (identity.attestation.list_linkage), one signed device-link or registration request, one relay access-token session (identity.session.linked_keys) - and never IP addresses, network ranges, time proximity or device fingerprints; no rotation chain is read while account key rotation is Future in F07.
An evaluation ends at once as denied, or as flagged, or is not stored; flagged moves through review to confirmed or dismissed, or expires when no review takes it up or a review never closes.
Flags never alter bids, prices or results; only F04.S02.M03 decisions do.

Review outcomes arrive per check in auctions.review.closed (confirmedCheckIds) from the fraud review module; only the listed checks are confirmed, the other checks of that review are dismissed, and no outcome is assumed.
The host relay exposes auctions.shill.check as an internal synchronous command called inside the bid transaction and auctions.shill.score as an asynchronous job command.
Moderators read the review queue through a relay query; the public policy query describes the controls and their limits in words.
The module consumes host-local bid and result events, identity events and review events on the host; nothing here runs in participant vaults.
auctions.shill.check also answers whether the bidder key is revoked as known to the host, so the bid path rejects revoked keys with the same generic error (F04.S01.M02 V07).

Linkage is read only through the in-process F07 reads on the host - identity.portable_doc.key_set, identity.portable_doc.find_by_key and identity.portable_doc.key_status (F07.S02.M01), identity.attestation.list_linkage for kind same_owner signed by both DIDs (F07.S03.M02) and identity.session.linked_keys (F07.S01.M02) - cached at most 24 h; no rotation chain is read until account key rotation leaves Future in F07 (N11 as narrowed by F07).
Relay policy - check and score are callable only by the host's own bid path and job runner; allow_pair and review queries require the host operator or moderator role on that host.
No vault command exists in this module; bidders and sellers cannot read ShillChecks, including their own.
Roles are per host (CAP-9) and affect only auctions hosted there.
Check and score are idempotent per (auction, subject, trigger sequence); repeated calls return the stored verdict.
The synchronous check never writes an allow record, so a crash cannot leave partial state; deny and flag writes are single transactions.

Linkage data unavailability degrades by one rule - the seller-key equality and revoked-key checks always run on host-local data, other linkage uses cached F07 data while it is at most 24 h old, beyond that linkage reasons fail open with a linkage_stale flag for review, a counter and an operator alert, and the check returns DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE only when the equality check itself cannot run.
Linkage evidence and scores are P3 on the host and visible only to host moderators and operators; they are never sent to sellers, bidders or federated peers.
The generic denial prevents using the bid endpoint to probe who is linked to whom.
Scoring uses only the host-local auction events of shill-v1 and linkage uses only the evidence named in 02.R04 - no device fingerprinting, IP addresses, location or telemetry.

ShillChecks are host operator data - the module registers ExportSectionPort for the operator audit scope only (section auctions.shill_checks, excluded from user exports), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates fields with their F10.S02.M02 class, pseudonymizes subject keys on deletion, and purges denied and confirmed checks after RET-EVIDENCE and dismissed or expired checks after RET-SHORT.
The host exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6 without key material in labels or messages.
The synchronous check meets p95 ≤ 40 ms and p99 ≤ 100 ms with 10 000 linkage cache entries.
Scoring completes within 5 s of the trigger bid at p95 under 50 bids per second.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Linkage and scoring are covered by fixture-based unit tests and a labelled synthetic dataset with measured precision and recall.
Contract tests validate the event payload and that no check data leaks into bidder-facing payloads.
ShillChecks are host operator data; they are exported only in the host operator's audit export and never in a user's vault export.
Import of a host audit export validates ids and schema version and restores checks as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An AuctionReview stores auction, optional result, triggers with per-check outcomes, priority, assignee, evidence snapshot references, findings, decision, the EnforcementAction id, and void and rescission statement references, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
Reviews are P3 host records visible only to host moderators and operators; participants receive only the void statement with a reason category and never the evidence or other parties' keys.

The evidence is frozen at assignment - the listing and bids through F12.S01.M02 snapshots of target types listing and bid, and the ledger head, extension history and result by their host-signed cids - so later bids or edits cannot change what the decision rested on.
Review commands check the actor's host role, conflict of interest including keys F04.S02.M01 links to a party, and the review state before any effect.

Void decisions check the facts the host holds - a won result that is not voided and closed at most 60 days ago - the two-moderator rule and the reason enum before signing; payment state is never checked on the host because it lives only in the parties' vaults.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.
Reviews move opened, in_review, optionally void_proposed, and end voided or dismissed; both are terminal.
Voiding requires propose and confirm by two different moderators within 72 hours of the proposal, otherwise the proposal lapses back to in_review.
Every terminal transition emits auctions.review.closed, and a void additionally emits auctions.result.voided, in the same host transaction.
A successful appeal never changes the terminal review status; it adds an advisory host-signed rescission, and vaults show that statement without reopening the sale.
Reviews are host relay commands authorized by host moderator roles; vaults only ingest the signed void and rescission statements.

Decisions are atomic on the host with their events, statements, the host's own result row and the calls into F04.S01.M01 or F12.S02.M01; vault-side effects follow only from the host-signed statements.

Reviews are opened by consumed events - shill suspicion, relay-local moderation.report.received about the auction, its listing or its bids (never the reporter's vault-local moderation.report.filed, EVT-8), non-payment counts and listing edits after bids - or manually; no participant can open or read a review.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 - classrup.auctions.void/v1 and classrup.auctions.void_rescission/v1 by the host key named in the terms (N2) - and the host calls notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push to the seller and the auction's participants with pushOptIn when a void or rescission is issued (N17).

Each void records a host-policy EnforcementAction through the in-process F12.S02.M01 moderation.action.record_host_policy (source auction_review, hostRef reviewId, kind remove_from_index, targetRef the auction, subject the seller, proposerKey and deciderKey the two moderators) whose actionId and caseId are stored on the review; moderation.appeal.decided is matched on that actionId only with origin relay - overturned yields the rescission, reduced records reducedTo while the void stays, and upheld changes nothing.
Relay policy - only host moderators (and operators) of the hosting relay can read, assign, dismiss, cancel, propose or confirm; roles are per host (CAP-9) and every allow or deny is audited (CAP-7).
Conflict of interest is enforced - a seller, a bidder, or a key F04.S02.M01 links to either cannot be assigned, propose or confirm.
Vault policy - vaults only ingest void and rescission statements signed by the host key named in the auction terms; no vault role can change a review.
Review commands are idempotent per review and expectedRevision; a repeated confirm returns the stored void statement.
Confirm, the void statement, the EnforcementAction, the events and the move of the host's own result row to voided commit in one host transaction; a failure leaves the review in void_proposed.
Delivery of the void statement to participants is at least once through mailboxes and idempotent by cid in vaults.
No lock spans vaults - the host never serializes a void against payments it cannot see; each vault applies the void against its own Deal state in one local transaction (F04.S01.M03).
Evidence, findings and keys of suspected parties remain P3 on the host; participants receive only the reason category and the signed void statement.
The void statement is the host's finding under its policy; it names no individual, and the UI says it is not a court ruling.
Abuse of the review process by moderators is limited by the two-moderator rule, conflict checks, audit entries and the participants' ability to choose another host.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (operator section auctions.reviews; user section auctions.voids with received void and rescission statements), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), annotates fields with their F10.S02.M02 class, and pseudonymizes moderator and subject keys on deletion.
The host exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6 without evidence content or keys; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
Review open and decision commands meet p95 ≤ 300 ms excluding the evidence snapshot, which completes within 5 s for ledgers of 5 000 entries.
The queue query meets p95 ≤ 150 ms for 50 items.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The two-moderator rule, conflict checks and voidability are covered by deterministic unit and integration tests.
Contract tests validate review events, the void statement and its signature checks in vaults.
Reviews and evidence are host operator data exported only in the operator audit export; user vault exports contain only the void and rescission statements they received.
Import of an operator audit export validates ids, schema version and statement signatures and restores reviews as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
An Extension stores auction, sequence number 1 to 30, the triggering bid sequence, previous and new end, host time and the host signature, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
Extensions are public P0 because bidders must be able to audit the end time; they contain no bidder identity or key.

The rule constants (window 120 000 ms, extension 120 000 ms, maximum 30) are rules version softclose-v1, which the seller signs as softCloseRulesVersion in the auction terms and the host echoes in host_acceptance (F04.S01.M01), so they cannot change during a running auction.
The qualification test uses only host-side data - host time, currentEndsAt, extensionCount and the kind of the triggering entry - never client-claimed times.
Extension application is a compare-and-set against extensionCount so concurrent paths cannot exceed the cap.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; non-qualifying bids are not errors for the bidder.
Vaults verify each extension's rulesVersion against the softCloseRulesVersion of the auction terms they hold, and its signature, sequence and previous end, and quarantine any extension that fails.
Extensions are immutable facts; there is no lifecycle beyond creation, so no state machine applies.
The only effect of an extension is a new currentEndsAt on the auction, applied in the same transaction.
Closing re-reads currentEndsAt under the lease, so an extension committed before the lease is always honoured.
The host relay exposes auctions.extension.apply as an internal command called from the bid transaction; it is not callable by vaults.

Anyone can read the extension history through a public query; vaults derive auctions.auction.extended locally when the host-signed extension arrives, embedded in the bid receipt (F04.S01.M02 extension field) or fetched from the history, and ingested with auctions.extension.receive.
The module consumes the auction closed event to stop applying extensions and nothing else on the host.

classrup.auctions.extension/v1 is registered with F11.S01.M01 with signer role host key named in the terms (N2), and the host calls notify.notification.dispatch for a content-free push to the seller and to bidders with pushOptIn on each extension, collapsed per auction (N17).
Relay policy - apply is system-only inside the bid transaction on the host that owns the auction; no principal and no relay access token can call it.
Reading extensions and previews needs no capability beyond a public read; they contain no personal data.

Vaults never create extensions; a vault that receives an extension verifies the host signature against the host key in the auction terms and the rules version against the terms, and quarantines mismatches.
Apply is idempotent per auction and triggering bid sequence, so a repeated call returns the existing extension and never adds a second.
Extension row, adjust_end and the bid ledger entry commit in the same SQLite transaction; a crash leaves none of them.
Concurrent apply attempts are impossible inside the lease and are additionally prevented by the unique (auction, seq) index and the compare-and-set on extensionCount.
Extensions are public and contain no identities, so there is no privacy cost beyond the bid timing already public in the ledger.
Manipulation by repeated late bids to keep an auction open is bounded by the cap of 30 extensions and the increment rules.

The rule constants are public and versioned, the version is signed in the terms and echoed in the host acceptance, and vaults reject extensions under any other version, so hosts cannot change them mid-auction.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section auctions.extensions), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6) and annotates every Extension field P0 in F10.S02.M02; extensions hold no DIDs, so deletion removes cached histories and pseudonymizes nothing.
The host exports metrics and logs per OBS-1 to OBS-6; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
Apply adds at most 5 ms to the p95 of the bid transaction.
The extension history is cacheable and meets p95 ≤ 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Boundary and cap behaviour is covered by deterministic unit tests and by a property test against a reference model.
Contract tests validate the extension statement and event, and the host-signature check in vaults.
Vault exports carry the extension history for auctions the user took part in, with host signatures.
Import verifies each signature against the host key, the rules version against the terms and the contiguity of seq; broken histories are kept as read-only history with a warning.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A RentalOffering stores owner, listing, rates, quantity, durations, buffers, lead time, horizon, blackouts, late-fee terms, cancellation policy, declared value, checklist template, time zone and status, with revision per CTR-ID-001; its public projection is a signed P0 statement limited to the F11.S01.M01 field allowlist.

A RentalReservation stores offering, renter, owner, interval, occupied interval including buffers, units, price, rate unit, the terms copied from the signed request, the checklist template, the absolute request expiry, status and the cids of its signed statements and consents, and is P2 in both vaults.
Rent, late-fee rate and cap, cancellation fee and declared value are integer minor units per CTR-MNY-001; the rent is computed once, with ceiling on rate units and no rounding of minor units.
Inbound statements are validated in a fixed order - schema, signature, signer role, offering state, terms binding, interval, capacity - and the first failure decides the error.
Interval checks use UTC half-open intervals [occupiedFrom, occupiedUntil) and count units against quantity, including frozen units.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key; quarantined statements store the code.

Request expiry, confirmations and cancellations are judged against the signed absolute expiresAt and each statement's signed createdAt with a 72 hour receipt bound, never against one vault's receipt time alone.

Reservations follow requested, confirmed, handoff_pending once the pickup window passes, in_use, optionally overdue, returned and closed, with lapsed, declined and frozen as holding states and cancelled as the exit before use; transitions driven by other modules arrive only as events or local calls.
A reservation is confirmed only by the owner's signed confirmation over the request terms the renter signed; the overlap check and the confirmation commit in one vault transaction.

Conflicting signed confirmations from forked owner devices, and a confirmation plus a decline signed by the owner over the same requestCid in either arrival order, freeze the affected reservations, keep counting them toward capacity, notify each affected renter with a signed reservation_frozen notice and require explicit renegotiation, never last-writer-wins.

Requests expire on the signed absolute expiresAt in both vaults - the owner vault at expiresAt with a signed expired notice, the renter vault at min(expiresAt plus a 24 hour delivery allowance, startsAt − leadTime) - and a valid confirmation that reaches the renter after that is held frozen for the renter's explicit acceptance.

A confirmed reservation is never cancelled automatically while either party may hold a signed handoff report; after startsAt plus 24 hours it is handoff_pending, and only an explicit signed cancellation or the F05.S02.M01 no_handoff cancellation (no signed report by either party at startsAt plus 96 hours) cancels it.
An item that is never returned ends the reservation when rentals.rental.closed arrives without a return, and the occupied interval ends at the closure time.
Offering and reservation commands are vault commands; request, confirm, decline, cancel, renegotiate and publish produce named signed statements and sync outbox entries in the same vault transaction.
One ingestion command applies inbound statements, deduplicates by cid and derives local events with actor.kind federated; failures are quarantined with a reason.
Events are local (EVT-8) and leave the device only as the statements named below; the module consumes lifecycle events from handoff, return, listing, consent, block, Deal and deletion modules.

Rent and cancellation fees are noncustodial Deals opened through commerce.deal.open with contextRef types rental_reservation and rental_cancellation_fee, and a cancelled reservation that holds a Deal produces a commerce.deal.cancel statement for both parties to sign; the module never creates or alters a PaymentClaim.

Every statement schema this module sends is registered in the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with its signer role, consents use comms.consent.sign and comms.consent.verify with this module's SubjectCanonicalizerPort, and the receiving vault acts only on statements it accepted.

Pausing or archiving a published offering, or the unpublish of its listing, emits rentals.offering.withdrawn locally with offeringId, ownerId, listingId, the last projectionCid and the reason, signs no new statement and answers open requests with a signed decline; an offering that was never published emits nothing.

comms.consent.revoked is matched through its revokedIds[] against the reservation's requestConsentCid and confirmConsentCid, its revocationId is recorded and afterCommit is cross-checked with comms.consent.verify, whose result decides; a reservation never freezes on the event alone.
Vault policy - only the local principal who owns an offering manages it, publishes it and confirms, declines or cancels its reservations; only the principal who signed a request is the renter for it.
Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches the role required for that statement in this reservation; otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role is involved; a relay can only carry ciphertext or host the signed public projection and busy summary under its own hosting policy.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements through cid, so duplicate delivery through two relays is harmless.
The overlap check and the confirmation write are one IndexedDB transaction under a Web Locks lock per offering.

Conflicting signed promises from forked owner devices and owner equivocation over one requestCid are detected on merge or receipt, freeze the reservations with a signed notice to each affected renter, keep counting toward capacity and require renegotiation; there is no last-writer-wins.
Reservations are P2 and travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the two parties; the public busy summary holds intervals and unit counts only, with no identities, and expires in 24 hours.

Exact pickup address is L4 and P3, never part of the offering, the projection or any rentals statement; it is shared only by explicit user action in the encrypted F08 thread through an F06.S02.M02 location share gated by privacy.consent.check(location_precise) with a TTL of at most 24 hours.
Request spam and calendar scraping are limited by local quotas, short busy-summary expiry and each relay's hosting policy.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section rentals.reservations), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies every offering, projection and reservation field through F10.S02.M02, pseudonymizes the deleted party on privacy.deletion.completed while signed statements stay verifiable, and calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) before any offering or busy-summary publication.

Blocks (N7) apply only to new requests, which are dropped silently with no BLOCKED_PARTY reply and no statement; statements for reservations confirmed before the block (cancellation, renegotiation, frozen notices) are still verified and stored with notifications suppressed, and the reason blocked never leaves the vault.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Overlap check and confirm meet p95 ≤ 100 ms with 5 000 reservations and quantity 20 on a mid-range phone.
Busy summary generation for 365 days meets p95 ≤ 150 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The interval logic is covered by property tests against a brute-force minute-by-minute reference model for quantities 1 to 20.
Cross-vault flows are covered by two-vault tests with a hostile in-memory relay and by a forked-owner-device test.
The vault export contains offerings, reservations and all signed statements and consents with their cids so evidence survives vault loss.
Import verifies every signature and cid before restoring; unverifiable items stay read-only history; overlap is re-validated for confirmed reservations and violations are frozen.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

DepositTerms stores reservation, parties, amount, declared value, method, due time, agreement consent, funding and release Deals, release and forfeit details, dispute link, outcome and state, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
DepositTerms are P2 in both vaults, retained under RET-EVIDENCE, and money values are integer minor units in one currency per CTR-MNY-001.
Terms are immutable after proposal; a change is a new proposal that supersedes the old one, and agreement binds to the exact terms cid.
Statements are validated in the order schema, signature, signer role, referenced cids, state, business rules, and the first failure decides the error.
Amount rules compare integer minor units in one currency; no conversion is performed in this module.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key; quarantined statements store the code.

Deposits follow proposed, agreed, funded and then release or forfeit paths, with escalation_due, escalated_pending, disputed and frozen as holding states; released, forfeited, withdrawn and expired are terminal.

Funded and released are reached only from acknowledged or final F09 payment proof, and forfeited only from the renter's signed acceptance of the full funded amount (a forfeit response or a both-accepted dispute outcome), never from a claim alone or a mediator-only outcome.

Silence never settles money - a forfeit claim unanswered by its signed respondBy moves to escalation_due with a prefilled draft case that the owner opens explicitly, and an owner who does not decide after return is visible as decision overdue and can be disputed by the renter.

Dispute outcomes are mapped explicitly - refund_claimed or return_agreed accepted by both parties fix releaseAmount (the advisoryRefund, always read as the amount the owner returns to the renter whichever party opened the case, capped at the funded amount, or the full funded amount when absent); no_fault_close, enforcement_referral and lapsed return the deposit to funded with decisionOverdue set; commerce.dispute.withdrawn returns it to the state it was disputed from.

Every path into release_pending fixes releaseAmount (full on cancellation or full release, funded minus the accepted forfeit, or the mapped dispute amount), and the owner can attest that release from release_pending while no release Deal exists, with no return or window condition.

Exactly one vault opens a dispute case per deposit - the renter on contest, decision overdue or a missing release, the owner after an unanswered forfeit claim - and the other vault waits in escalated_pending and links the case from commerce.dispute.opened.

A frozen deposit leaves frozen only by a co-signed renegotiation back to the state it was frozen from, an explicit dispute, or expiry (72 hours before funding, 14 days after funding into escalation_due).
All commands are vault commands; each one that the other party must rely on also produces a named signed statement and a sync outbox entry in the same vault transaction.
One ingestion command applies inbound statements, deduplicates by cid and derives local events with actor.kind federated; failures are quarantined.

Payment status is derived only from F09 events whose contextRef is {rental_deposit, depositId} or {rental_deposit_release, depositId} of this module; the module never creates or alters a PaymentClaim itself.
Every money obligation is a separate commerce.deal.open call with its own contextRef and contextCid (funding at agreement, release at the release attestation); no other payment context API is used.

Statements the counterparty must act on (withdrawal, decline, dispute notice, renegotiation) are named schemas with signer roles registered in F11.S01.M01 and handled by receive, and an agreement received after a withdrawal fails with CONFLICT_STATE in both vaults.

comms.consent.revoked is matched through its revokedIds[] against the agreementCid, its revocationId is recorded and afterCommit is cross-checked with comms.consent.verify, whose result decides; an agreed deposit never freezes on the event alone and a funded or later deposit keeps its state because the payment already happened under the agreement.

Vault policy - only the local principal who owns the reservation proposes, withdraws, attests release or claims forfeit; only the renter agrees, declines and responds; only the designated opener opens a dispute case.
Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches the role for that statement in this deposit; otherwise they are quarantined with a reason code.
Payment events are applied only when their contextRef belongs to deposit terms in this vault; no relay role exists.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements through cid; payment events through the inbox, so replays never double-settle.

Contradictory signed statements (two forfeit claims, responses to different claim cids, two terms with the same reservation, forked devices, a conflicted or revoked consent) freeze the deposit with explicit exits - co-signed renegotiation, dispute or expiry - never last-writer-wins.
Each state change, Deal call, event and sync outbox entry commit in one IndexedDB transaction, so a crash at any point leaves either all or none of them.
Deposit terms, evidence and amounts are P2 and travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the two parties; they never appear in logs, notifications or public projections.

Evidence references are attachment and MediaBlob ids; photos remain encrypted attachments shared with the counterparty and, only when a party explicitly attaches them while opening a case, the mediator.

Deposit theft, bogus forfeits and fake release claims are limited by explicit proof levels, mandatory evidence, a damage-claim reference for damage forfeits and the dispute path; no one is auto-penalized.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section rentals.deposits), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies every DepositTerms field through F10.S02.M02, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the deleted party in retained evidence while signed statements stay verifiable.
