Blocks (N7) never strand a deposit - statements settling obligations of a reservation confirmed before the block (release, response, acknowledgement, claim, notice) are still verified and stored, only notifications are suppressed, and isBlockedEither is checked on new initiations for other reservations.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Vault commands meet p95 ≤ 120 ms and payment event handling p95 ≤ 50 ms on a mid-range phone with 2 000 deposits stored.
Statement verification meets p95 ≤ 30 ms per envelope.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Money and proof rules are covered by property tests with a reference model for amounts, partial forfeits and release remainders.
Two-vault tests with a hostile in-memory relay cover duplicate, dropped, reordered and contradictory statements.
The vault export contains deposit terms, Deal context references, consents and all signed statements with their cids so evidence survives vault loss.
Import verifies every signature and cid before restoring; unverifiable items stay read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A DamageClaim stores reservation, parties, kind, itemized amounts, evidence, the comparison basis with provenance, the signed deadlines, responses, dispute reference and resolution, settlement, outcome and state, with revision per CTR-ID-001.
Claims are P2 in both vaults, retained under RET-EVIDENCE, with integer minor units in the reservation currency per CTR-MNY-001.
Claim content is immutable once signed; a counter or withdrawal is a new signed statement referencing the claim cid.
Statements are validated in the order schema, signature, signer role, referenced cids, state, window, business rules, and the first failure decides the error.
The comparison basis is recomputed by the receiving vault from the two reports it holds, including provenance, and must match the claim.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; quarantined statements store the code.
Windows and deadlines are absolute values carried in signed statements and judged on signed createdAt with a 72 hour receipt bound, so both vaults reach the same decision.

Claims move claimed, optionally countered, then accepted, escalated to resolved or resolved_unsettled, or withdrawn, with escalation_due, escalated_pending and frozen as holding states; accepted, resolved, resolved_unsettled and withdrawn are terminal.

Silence never settles money - unanswered claims and unanswered counters move to escalation_due with a prefilled draft of the F09 case, held in this vault, that only the designated party opens by explicit action; no case is ever opened automatically.
Each terminal transition emits rentals.damage.resolved once with the outcome; escalation produces the case request through the designated party's explicit action before the state changes.

F09 resolutions are mapped explicitly - refund_claimed or return_agreed accepted by both parties set agreedAmount from advisoryRefund (always read as the amount the renter pays the owner whichever party opened the case, 0 when absent, capped at totalClaimed) and record the outcome both parties accepted; no_fault_close, enforcement_referral and lapsed end in resolved_unsettled with no agreedAmount; commerce.dispute.withdrawn returns the claim to the state it was escalated from.

Exactly one vault opens a case per claim - the owner after the renter's silence or when rejecting a counter, the renter on contest or after the owner's silence on a counter - and the other vault waits in escalated_pending and links the case from commerce.dispute.opened.

A frozen claim leaves frozen only by a co-signed renegotiation back to the state it was frozen from, a withdrawal by the owner, or after 14 days into escalation_due with the party that did not fork as designated opener.

Vault commands claim, respond, accept_counter, withdraw, escalate and renegotiate produce named signed statements where the other party must rely on them, and a sync outbox entry, in the same vault transaction.
One ingestion command applies inbound statements, deduplicates by cid, recomputes the comparison, derives local events with actor.kind federated and quarantines failures.
Payment status of an agreed amount is derived from F09 events whose contextRef is {rental_damage, claimId} of this module; the module never creates a PaymentClaim itself.

The excess over the deposit is a separate commerce.deal.open with contextRef {rental_damage, claimId} and contextCid the acceptance, counter acceptance or dispute outcome cid, the dispute contextRef is {rental_damage, claimId}, and every statement schema is registered with its signer role in F11.S01.M01.

A referenced evidence photo is detected as missing only when comms.attachment.download returns NOT_FOUND during ingestion or a re-fetch; it keeps claim, respond and accept_counter refused with RENTALS_EVIDENCE_MISSING and is re-requested from the author through the thread, and comms.attachment.deleted, which F08.S01.M03 emits only in the uploader vault, is not consumed.
Vault policy - only the local principal who is the owner of the reservation claims, accepts a counter, withdraws; only the renter responds; only the designated opener escalates.
Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches the role for that statement in this claim and the recomputed basis matches; otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role is involved; relays carry ciphertext only.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements through cid, so repeated delivery never adds a second response or acceptance.

Contradictory signed statements (two responses to one claim, a counter acceptance for an unknown response cid, forked devices) freeze the claim with explicit exits - co-signed renegotiation, withdrawal or escalation after 14 days - never last-writer-wins.

Escalation requests the F09 case only on the designated party's explicit action, before the state change, and retries that request on failure, so a claim is never escalated without a case request in flight and a crash never leaves a half-applied escalation.

Claims, comparisons, photos and amounts are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes and attachments to the two parties, reach a mediator only when the opener explicitly attaches them to the F09 case, and never appear in logs, notifications or public projections.

Inflated or fabricated claims are limited by the recomputed comparison with recorded provenance, evidence requirements, a declared value cap bound to what the renter agreed, signed response deadlines with escalation, the return waiver check and the dispute path.
No automatic penalty or reputation change is applied; any effect on reputation comes from signed dispute resolutions processed by F07.

Evidence photos are at most 5 MiB each, stripped by the sender through F10.S02.M03, and each vault fetches, decrypts, verifies and stores every referenced photo under RET-EVIDENCE before claiming, responding or accepting, unaffected by later message deletion.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section rentals.damage), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies every DamageClaim field through F10.S02.M02, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the deleted party in retained evidence while signatures stay verifiable.

Blocks (N7) never suppress damage statements for a reservation confirmed before the block - a blocked renter's response is still verified and stored, so an owner cannot block the renter and let the deadline run.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Comparison of two 30-item reports and claim signing meet p95 ≤ 150 ms on a mid-range phone, excluding image handling.
Sweep over 2 000 claims completes in ≤ 100 ms in slices of at most 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The comparison and the amount rules are covered by property tests with a reference model over random checklists.
Two-vault tests with a hostile relay cover duplicate, dropped and reordered statements and silent counterparties.
The vault export contains claims, responses, acceptances, withdrawals, escalation notices, comparison bases and evidence references with MediaBlob ids.
Import verifies every signature and cid and recomputes the basis; mismatches are kept as read-only history with a warning.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A RentalHandoff stores reservation, parties, checklist items, readings, photo references, notes, revision, signatures and state, with revision per CTR-ID-001.

Handoffs are P2 and kept under RET-EVIDENCE; photos are encrypted F08.S01.M03 attachments referenced by MediaBlob id (blob:sha256-…) and attachment id, never embedded, and each vault keeps its own verified copy of every referenced photo as evidence.
A report revision is immutable once signed; any change is a new revision with a new cid, and attestations bind to one cid.
Statements are validated in the order schema, signature, signer role, referenced reservation and report cids, staleness, window, evidence, business rules, and the first failure decides the error.
Report content limits are enforced before signing in the vault and again on receipt, including the decrypted photo bytes.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; quarantined statements store the code.

Inbound statements are judged against their signed createdAt - inside the pickup window and received within 72 hours of createdAt - while local commands use the local clock, so a statement signed on time is never rejected for late delivery within the bound.
Handoffs move drafting, awaiting_counterparty, attested, with frozen as a holding state; expired and cancelled are terminal exits.
The author's report signature counts as the author's attestation; the counterparty's attestation of the same cid completes the handoff.
Attested starts the rental period for this module's purposes; the due time still comes from the reservation endsAt and is never shifted by a late pickup.

A handoff expires only at startsAt plus 96 hours (pickup window plus the 72 hour receipt bound), so no valid late statement can arrive after expiry; only when no signed report by either party is held then does it ask F05.S01.M01 to cancel with no_handoff, and while a signed report is held the reservation is never cancelled automatically.

Concurrent reports by the owner and the renter resolve owner-canonical (the renter's report becomes a changes request), while contradictory statements from forked devices of one party freeze the handoff until a new owner-signed revision or a cancellation.

Vault commands draft, submit, request_changes and attest build local state; submit, request_changes and attest each produce a named signed statement and a sync outbox entry in the same vault transaction.
One ingestion command applies inbound statements, deduplicates by cid, fetches and verifies referenced photos, derives local events with actor.kind federated and quarantines failures.
Events are local (EVT-8); rentals.handoff.attested is derived in each vault only when both signatures on the same cid are held.
Every statement schema this module sends is registered in the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with its signer role, and the receiving vault acts only on statements it accepted.

A referenced photo is detected as missing only when comms.attachment.download returns NOT_FOUND during ingestion or a re-fetch; it is listed in missingPhotos[], keeps attest and request_changes refused with RENTALS_EVIDENCE_MISSING and is re-requested from the author through the thread, and comms.attachment.deleted, which F08.S01.M03 emits only in the uploader vault, is not consumed.
Vault policy - only the local principal who is owner or renter of the reservation can draft, submit, request changes or attest; the counterparty of the author attests.
Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches a party of the reservation and the role rule for that statement; otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role is involved; relays carry ciphertext only.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements through cid, so repeated delivery never adds a second attestation.

Contradictory signed statements from forked devices of one party (two reports for the same revision by one signer, or attestations on different cids) freeze the handoff until a new owner-signed revision or a cancellation, while concurrent reports by owner and renter resolve owner-canonical; never last-writer-wins.
Each state change, event and sync outbox entry commit in one IndexedDB transaction, so a crash at any point leaves all or none of them.
Reports and photos are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes and attachments to the two parties, and never appear in logs, notifications or public projections.

Photos are stripped of EXIF, XMP and GPS metadata by the sender through F10.S02.M03 before encryption (PRV-4), and the receiving vault checks the decrypted bytes and quarantines any photo that still carries metadata; relays see ciphertext only and perform no content check (ADR-0016 §3, PRV-5); faces and plates are not detected or processed.
Fake or doctored photos and one-sided reports are limited by hashes, explicit exact-cid attestation and the dispute path; no condition truth is claimed.

Every referenced photo is fetched, decrypted, SHA-256 verified and stored locally under RET-EVIDENCE in each vault before it can be attested, and a later message or attachment deletion by its author does not affect evidence copies already stored.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section rentals.handoffs), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies every RentalHandoff field through F10.S02.M02, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the deleted party in retained evidence while signatures and photo hashes stay verifiable.
Blocks (N7) never suppress handoff statements for a reservation confirmed before the block - they are verified and stored as evidence with only notifications suppressed.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Signing and verification of a report with 20 photo references meet p95 ≤ 120 ms on a mid-range phone, excluding image re-encoding.
Re-encoding and hashing a 5 MiB photo runs in a worker and completes in ≤ 800 ms without blocking the UI longer than 50 ms per slice.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Signature and cid binding is covered by unit and property tests including revision clearing.
Two-vault tests with a hostile in-memory relay cover duplicate, dropped, reordered and contradictory statements.
The vault export contains handoffs, report revisions, attestations and photo references with MediaBlob ids; photo bytes are exported by user choice as encrypted attachments.
Import verifies every signature and cid before restoring; unverifiable items stay read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A RentalReturn stores reservation, parties, due time, grace, return report content with photo references, the transport receipt of the report, effective return time, late minutes and fee, attestation mode and cids, closure checks, completion signatures and state, with revision per CTR-ID-001.

Returns are P2 in both vaults, retained under RET-EVIDENCE; the late fee is integer minor units per CTR-MNY-001 computed from the terms the renter signed in the rental request and copied into the reservation.
Report revisions and attestations are immutable once signed and bind to the exact report cid.
Statements are validated in the order schema, signature, signer role, reservation and report cids, state, business rules, and the first failure decides the error.

Late-fee computation uses elapsed UTC time, the terms the renter signed in the request and the effective return time bounded by verifiable evidence, never terms edited later or one vault's receipt time.
Every violation maps to one stable error code; quarantined statements store the code.

Inbound statements are judged by their signed createdAt and accepted within 72 hours of it; the silence deadline, the damage window and the effective return time derive only from signed times and relay-signed receipts, so both vaults compute the same values.

Returns move due, optionally overdue, awaiting_owner, attested, completion_pending and closed, with renter_reported_unconfirmed, contested and frozen as holding states; closed is terminal and is also reached for items never returned.
Overdue and late fee follow only from the confirmed end time, grace and elapsed time up to the evidence-bounded effective return time; the owner can lower the fee but nothing raises it.

Owner silence is measured from the later of the report's signed createdAt and the relay-signed transport receipt for the owner's mailbox; after 72 hours it is recorded as renter_reported_unconfirmed, which stops late-fee accrual but never emits rentals.return.attested, and closure still needs the damage window, open claims and deposit checks.
A report that never left the renter's device (sync state prepared) starts no silence clock and is labelled 'not yet delivered'.

An item never returned reaches closed with reason not_returned when a not_returned damage claim ends with outcome accepted, counter_accepted, refund_claimed or dispute_unresolved (withdrawn and return_agreed leave the return open), or when the owner signs a not_returned_declaration 30 days after the due time.

Closure offers a completion over the deterministic completionCid for both parties' signatures and emits rentals.rental.closed with completionCid when both signatures are held; after 7 days without the counterparty's signature a return attested by both closes with its bilaterally signed reportCid as completionCid (completionKind return_attestation), and any other return closes one-sided without completionCid.

The rental closes with reason deposit_unsettled when the deposit is neither absent nor terminal but its owner decision is overdue, so reviews can open while the deposit record stays open in F05.S01.M02.

Vault commands report, attest, record_received, contest, adjust_late_fee, waive_damage, declare_not_returned, sign_completion and renegotiate each produce a named signed statement and a sync outbox entry in the same vault transaction.
One ingestion command applies inbound statements, deduplicates by cid, fetches and verifies referenced photos, derives local events with actor.kind federated and quarantines failures.
Overdue, attested and closed events are local (EVT-8); each vault derives them from its own data and clock and from the signed statements and relay receipts it holds.

The late fee is a noncustodial Deal {rental_late_fee, returnId} opened by the owner vault through commerce.deal.open at attestation, statement schemas are registered with signer roles in F11.S01.M01, and the receiving vault acts only on statements it accepted.

A referenced photo is detected as missing only when comms.attachment.download returns NOT_FOUND during ingestion or a re-fetch; it is listed in missingPhotos[], keeps attest, contest and record_received refused with RENTALS_EVIDENCE_MISSING and is re-requested from the author through the thread, and comms.attachment.deleted, which F08.S01.M03 emits only in the uploader vault, is not consumed.

Vault policy - only the local principal who is the renter reports a return; only the owner attests, contests, records receipt, adjusts the late fee, waives damage claims or declares non-return; either party signs the completion and renegotiates a frozen return.
Inbound statements are accepted only when the signer's key matches the role rule for that statement in this reservation; otherwise they are quarantined with a reason code.
No relay role is involved; relays carry ciphertext and sign transport receipts only.
Commands are idempotent through local command ids and statements through cid, so repeated delivery never adds a second attestation or fee adjustment.
Overdue and closed events are derived once per vault from stored state and signed times, so sweeps that run twice emit once and both vaults derive the same deadlines.
Each state change, Deal call, event and sync outbox entry commit in one IndexedDB transaction, so a crash at any point leaves all or none of them.
Return reports, photos and fees are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes and attachments to the two parties, and never appear in logs, notifications or public projections.
Late fees are claims between the parties and are never collected by the platform; enforcement is by agreement, reputation and disputes only.

False overdue claims and fee inflation are limited by deterministic computation from signed terms, owner-only lowering, and an effective return time bounded by the earliest verifiable evidence rather than either party's own clock.

Return photos are at most 5 MiB each, stripped by the sender through F10.S02.M03, checked for metadata by the receiver after decryption, and kept as verified local copies under RET-EVIDENCE in each vault unaffected by later message deletion.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section rentals.returns), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6), classifies every RentalReturn field through F10.S02.M02, and on privacy.deletion.completed pseudonymizes the deleted party in retained evidence while signatures stay verifiable.

Blocks (N7) never suppress return statements for a reservation confirmed before the block - a blocked party's report, contest or completion is still verified and stored and the clocks run, so an owner cannot block the renter to suppress the return report and then claim not_returned.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and the diagnostics log stay in the vault and are exportable by the user.
Late-fee computation and report signing meet p95 ≤ 120 ms on a mid-range phone, excluding image re-encoding.
The overdue sweep over 5 000 returns completes in ≤ 100 ms in slices of at most 50 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Late-fee arithmetic and the 72 hour rule are covered by property tests with a reference model including DST zones.
Two-vault tests with a hostile in-memory relay cover duplicate, dropped and reordered statements and silent owners.
The vault export contains returns, return reports, attestations, receipts, fee adjustments, waivers, declarations, completion signatures and photo references with MediaBlob ids.
Import verifies every signature and cid before restoring and recomputes the late fee from the stored terms, flagging mismatches.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
The Filter value object has a closed set of keys with typed ranges, and any unknown key is a validation failure.
Compilation output is a pair of SQL text and an ordered parameter array, with SQL text drawn only from a fixed set of fragments.
The canonical form of a filter is deterministic so equal filters produce equal cache keys and saved search comparisons.

Distance filters compile by cell precision - precision-5 cells match geo_cell exactly, precision-4 cells match the stored and indexed geo_cell4 column, and documents with a 4-character (L1) cell match only radii of 25 km or more.

The keys inStock (boolean, compiled to d.in_stock = ?) and wantAcceptsCondition (one condition value, compiled to d.want_min_condition IN (...) over the minimum conditions that accept an item of that condition) filter the columns F06.S01.M01 copies from the projection's inStock and want.minCondition, next to barterAcceptable (d.barter = ?).
Validation is strict and total - every key, range and combination is checked before compilation.
Combination rules prevent meaningless filters, such as prices without a currency and distances without a center.
Each violation maps to one stable error code with the offending path in fields.
The library is stateless; validate and compile are pure functions with no lifecycle.
Identical input always yields identical output and identical parameter order.
Compilation never reads the clock; the caller passes now explicitly for postedWithin.
The module exposes functions only; it has no commands, queries or events.
Callers (F06.S01.M02, relay query handler) are responsible for capability checks and idempotency.

Error codes defined here are returned inside Result values and mapped by callers to HTTP problems; geo codes (DISCOVERY_RADIUS_TOO_SMALL, DISCOVERY_RADIUS_NOT_ALLOWED, DISCOVERY_PRECISION_FORBIDDEN) are defined once in F06.S02.M01 and only referenced here (N1).
The library performs no authorization; it is pure and may be called by any caller that is itself authorized.
Filters can only constrain public SearchDocument columns, so no filter can reach P1-P4 data.
No capability is defined by this module.
Functions are pure and deterministic, so retries and replays are inherently safe.
Invalid input never produces partial output; the result is either a full compiled fragment or an error.
Port failures (category or currency lookup) surface as DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE without partial state.
Filters touch only public columns and carry no personal data; they are stored only inside saved searches (P3) by the caller.
Compilation output is never logged with parameter values.
Hostile filter input cannot inject SQL or trigger unbounded work.
Validation and compilation are fast enough to be negligible in the query budget.
Failures are counted by error code without recording values.
The compiled SQL is covered by an explain-plan test showing index use.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including property tests on canonicalization.
A golden test fixes the SQL fragment text and parameter order for each filter key.
Injection and limit tests run against a real SQLite database.
The library owns no data, so it has no export section; filters travel inside saved searches exported by F06.S01.M02.
Imported filters are revalidated with the current library and rejected if they use unknown keys.
Filter schema changes are additive within v1 and breaking changes use a new major version with a migration function.

A SearchDocument stores only P0 fields from a signature-verified public projection, a location cell of 0, 4 or 5 geohash characters (L0, L1 or L2) checked with F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell, and provenance (author DID, projection cid, origin, provenance relays, first-seen time).
The FTS5 table indexes title and body only; every other attribute is a typed column used by filters and ranking.

Removed documents lose title and body immediately and are purged 30 days after removal; the row until then only guarantees idempotent replay and tombstone handling, and after the purge a stub (source key, highest sourceRevision, removedReason, projectionCid) is kept 180 days so a resubmitted projection is still refused for sticky reasons.

One document exists per listing, keyed by tenantId, sourceKind listing, sourceId (listingId) and authorDid; service offering, rental offering and auction statements enrich that document by listingId instead of creating a second document.
Per-user view recency used for vault eviction is kept in a separate P3 vault-local table that is never exported, federated or placed in the P0 SearchDocument.

barterAcceptable, inStock and, for wanted listings, wantMinCondition are typed columns copied from the verified listing projection (top-level barterAcceptable and inStock, want.minCondition) so that F06.S01.M03 can filter them; a remote document with inStock false stays active, while own documents still follow the inventory events.

Enrichment keeps offeringRef.version, the highest registry version applied per offeringId (payload seq of classrup.services.offering/v1 per FED-3, payload revision of classrup.rentals.offering/v1); an offering event or projection with an equal or lower version is ignored, and a key re-sign with unchanged content only replaces projectionCid and version.
Every upsert is validated against the SearchDocument schema, the author signature and the signer role before it touches the FTS table; failures leave the previous document unchanged.

Location precision, tombstone state, sticky removal state and revision monotonicity are checked on every event so a bad or hostile source cannot widen what is publicly findable or undo a removal it is not entitled to undo.

Text is normalized (NFC, control and bidi characters removed, length limits applied) so index content is stable across browsers and Node; an over-long body is truncated for indexing, never a reason to refuse a valid listing.

On a relay, admission also applies the F15.S04.M03 tenant limits read through TenantPort.limits(tenantId) at write time - maxIndexedListingsPerPublisher active documents per author and allowedCurrencies - so a tenant change applies to the next write and never removes a document already indexed.

On a relay, admission of a listing projection also evaluates the relay operator's prohibited-item rule pack in-process at write time (F18.S01.M02 governance.prohibited_rule.evaluate against the pack applied through governance.prohibited_rule.relay_upload); a block verdict refuses the projection and leaves the previous document unchanged, a pack applied later never removes an indexed document by itself, and a vault index never evaluates.
A document is active only while its signed projection is valid, unexpired and not tombstoned; any removal trigger moves it to removed within the indexing latency budget.

A removed document becomes active again only when its removal reason allows it - unpublished, expired, archived, sold_out, held, auction_closed, auction_cancelled, withdrawn and evicted on a newer verified republish or restore (held and sold_out also on inventory release or restock), hosting_policy only on moderation.action.reverted or the action's expiry (or in a vault through a relay that did not remove it), and tombstoned or deleted never within the 180-day tombstone window for the same record key; it never reuses stale text.
Purging is irreversible and happens 30 days after removal by the sweep; the refusal stub then lives 180 days.

Withdrawals are applied by the kind, issuerKind and advisory flag of federation.tombstone.applied - an author tombstone (kind tombstone, issuerKind author) removes the document from every index, while a relay_removal advisory (kind relay_removal, issuerKind origin_relay, advisory true) removes it only from the issuing relay's own index and, in a vault, only drops that relay's provenance.

Commands are rebuild (a vault-local command on a device, a relay command for the relay operator) and, on a relay only, set_promotion and clear_promotion for the relay operator; none produces a signed statement.

Normal indexing is driven by consumed events - own-vault events for the principal's listings and federation.record.accepted for projections that F11.S01.M02 verified in a vault (fetched or imported) or ingested on a relay through federation.record.ingest; the vault index makes no network call and writes no outbox entry.
Each applied change emits exactly one discovery.index.updated event in the same local transaction as the document change.

Relay-sold promotion is set only by the relay operator's set_promotion bound to a final or operator-acknowledged payment claim, and is cleared by clear_promotion, by commerce.payment.reorged or commerce.payment.expired for that claim, or by the expiry sweep.
On a relay, the public cell feed list_by_cell returns signed projection envelopes by L1 cell only, so vault pulls never carry query text, filters or saved-search identifiers.

On a relay, index writes arrive only through F11.S01.M02 federation.record.ingest, whose response carries one F15.S02.M01 ReceiptPort.issue receipt (classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1) per stored envelope; the index serves that receipt as relayReceipt in list_by_cell items and signs no receipt, index acceptance or peer acknowledgement of its own, because the statement registry gives classrup.bazaar.listing/v1 acknowledger none and F15.S01.M01 completes such entries on the verified receipt.
Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal may run rebuild or read statistics on the vault index; indexing itself runs as the system actor of the local event dispatcher.

Relay policy - rebuild, statistics, set_promotion and clear_promotion on a relay require the relay operator role of that relay; no relay role affects any vault, and promotion exists only on the relay that sold it.

Search reads of documents are authorized in F06.S01.M02 and F06.S02.M03 and expose only public fields; the relay cell feed is public read under that relay's policy and the F12.S03.M03 read.search rate class.
Event handling is idempotent through the inbox and the sourceRevision guard; replays never duplicate or resurrect documents.
A failed handler retries with backoff and moves to dead letter after 8 attempts, leaving the previous document in place.
A crash during rebuild leaves the live index untouched because the swap is one transaction.

Only P0 fields and an L2-or-coarser cell are indexed; exact addresses, drafts, offers, contact data and L3/L4 locations never reach this module, and the vault index never leaves the device - it makes no network call and writes no outbox entry.

Removal is fast and complete so unpublished or tombstoned content is not searchable or recoverable from FTS shadow tables on the same index; copies already fetched by other vaults cannot be recalled, and the publish flow warns about this before signing.
A hostile author cannot flood a relay corpus, backdate content or undo a hosting-policy removal by republishing; caps, first-seen anchoring and sticky removals bound the effect.

The module registers a DeletionPort (plan - remove documents with origin own of the deleting principal with reason deleted, plus the author anchor and view rows; scope taken from the F10.S01.M04 plan) and a RetentionPurgePort (30-day purge, 180-day stubs) with F10, and classifies every field with F10.S02.M02 (all P0 except the P3 view table); SearchDocument has no export section because it is derived (IOX-5).
Index freshness, backlog and rejection counts are measured; relays export them per CTR-OBS-001 and vaults keep them in the local diagnostics log only (OBS-7).
Indexing keeps up with 200 events per second on a relay and 50 events per second in a vault, and freshness stays within 5 seconds at p95.
A full rebuild of 100 000 documents on a relay completes within 10 minutes and of 5 000 documents in a vault within 30 seconds, without blocking reads.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with deterministic clock and ID generator.
Event handlers are verified against recorded event fixtures of the producing modules (F01, F03, F04, F05, F11, F12, F09) and a fake signed-projection reader.
Privacy and signature tests prove that no field outside P0, no unsigned projection and no cell longer than 5 characters can be indexed.
The index is derived data; it is neither exported as its own section nor imported and is regenerated from retained signed projections.
Restoring a vault from export or a relay from backup is followed by a rebuild so the index matches restored sources.
Schema changes to the FTS tokenizer or columns are applied by building a new shadow index and swapping, never in place.

Rebuild copies firstSeenAt and authorFirstSeenAt from the live table keyed by source key and authorDid, and restore takes them from the kernel provenance receivedAt (FED-6), so neither makes an author look new again.

A SavedSearch stores a normalized query, typed filters, an optional area (L1 or L2 cell and radius), alert mode, an alert watermark and match bookkeeping, and is a P3 vault-local record that is never part of any statement.

A vault keeps at most 25 saved searches; each stores at most 200 matched document ids for dedupe, trimmed oldest first, as an optimisation only, because alert uniqueness comes from the watermark rule.
Query results are not persisted beyond a 15 minute snapshot used only for cursor consistency.
Query text and cursors are validated before any database access, with strict limits that bound work per query.
Saved search input is validated like a query plus ownership, count and area rules.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Any relay request with a center (near or filters.distanceKm) is checked and budgeted by F06.S02.M03 exactly as discovery.proximity.search, so it cannot bypass the center-precision, radius and distinct-center limits.
A saved search is active, paused or deleted; only active searches are evaluated.
Deleting is final and removes matched-id bookkeeping immediately.
Pausing and resuming preserve dedupe history, and resuming moves the watermark to the resume time so no backlog alerts fire.
Saved search create, update and delete are vault-local commands that produce no signed statement and never contact a relay.
discovery.search.query is a query served by the vault against the local index and, separately, a relay query endpoint; neither writes state except the relay's ephemeral rate counters.

Matching consumes discovery.index.updated, uses its payload only to pre-select candidate searches, confirms each candidate against the local index with the canonical compiled filter and the sanitized FTS MATCH restricted to that document, and emits discovery.saved_search.matched as a local P3 event in the same transaction as the bookkeeping update.

For source both, local and relay results are separate ranked sections with separate cursors (nextCursor { local?, relay? }); relay items are rendered only from verified signed projections and de-duplicated by (authorDid, sourceId) with the verified higher sourceRevision winning.

The vault pull fetches relay projections for saved-search areas through F06.S01.M01 list_by_cell by L1 cells only, at a fixed interval, and hands the envelopes to F11.S01.M02 for verification before anything is indexed.
Vault policy - saved search commands and queries are available only to the unlocked local principal for their own records; a locked vault returns UNAUTHENTICATED (CAP-10).

Relay policy - the relay query endpoint is public read; whether anonymous callers are allowed and at what rate is the relay operator's policy, expressed as F12.S03.M03 RatePolicy rows (class read.search) plus the shared proximity budget of F06.S02.M03 for requests with a center, and token-bearing callers get a higher quota.
Block and hide filtering happens on the device after results are received; the relay is never told whom the user blocked or what the user hid.
Saved search commands are idempotent and use expectedRevision; queries are side-effect free.
A relay failure never blocks local results and never loses a saved search.
Match evaluation is restartable and alerts at most once per (savedSearchId, documentId), because only documents first seen after the watermark alert and replays are keyed by that pair.

Queries and saved searches reveal interests and are P3; the vault never sends saved searches anywhere, relay queries carry only the text and filters the user chose to run on that relay, and pulls carry only L1 cells.
A relay sees query text and the coarse center cell; the UI states this and offers local-only search.
Query volume and query complexity are bounded to protect relays and devices.

SavedSearch is registered with F10 - ExportSectionPort (section discovery.saved_searches), DeletionPort (plan deletes saved searches and match rows at execution, not at request) and RetentionPurgePort - and every field is classified P3 with F10.S02.M02.
Query latency and outcomes are measured on relays per CTR-OBS-001 and in the vault diagnostics log only.
Local query p95 is at most 120 ms over 5 000 documents on a Moto G-class device and relay query p95 is at most 200 ms over 100 000 documents.
Saved search evaluation processes 500 queued documents against 25 searches within 2 seconds.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including a fuzz test of the query sanitizer.
Contract tests check command inputs, query outputs and the matched event against the schema registry.
Privacy tests prove saved searches never appear in statements, relay requests or logs.
The vault export contains saved searches as section discovery.saved_searches in classrup-export/v1.
Import validates schema version and filters, resets match history so no stale alerts fire, and caps the total at 25.
Schema changes to SavedSearch follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
Location levels map to geohash precision exactly as CTR-PRV-001 defines - L1 is 4 characters, L2 is 5, L3 is 6 - and L4 is exact coordinates that this library never returns.
A Cell is a lowercase geohash string; invalid characters or lengths are rejected, not repaired.
Distance buckets are the closed set lt5, 5_10, 10_25, 25_50 and gt50, derived from cell-center distance by the haversine formula on a sphere of radius 6 371.0088 km.
Coordinates, precisions, radii and cell strings are validated before any computation, and violations return typed errors.
Public-precision enforcement is a separate guard that every module producing public payloads must call.
Radius rules enforce the 5 km minimum and the 512 cell cap.
The library is stateless and deterministic; there is no lifecycle.
Every function is pure and independent of locale, time and platform floating-point mode beyond IEEE 754 doubles.
Results are returned in a stable sorted order so callers can hash them.
The module exposes functions only; it has no commands, queries or events.
Callers own capability checks; this module cannot read or write user data.
Error codes are returned inside Result values and mapped by callers to HTTP problems.
The library performs no authorization and holds no data; any caller may use it.
Authorization for storing or disclosing locations lives in F06.S02.M02 and the modules that publish payloads.
No capability is defined by this module.
All functions are pure, so repeated calls and retries give identical results.
Invalid input returns an error and never a clamped or approximate value.
No function returns more than 512 cells, and the work of cellsForRadius is bounded linearly by the size of its result.
Snapping discards sub-cell information irreversibly; the library never returns the input coordinates and never adds noise that could be averaged out.
The public guard is the single enforcement point for the L2 maximum in every public, search and federated payload.
The library never logs coordinates.
The library emits no telemetry in the PWA (OBS-7) and callers measure its cost within their budgets.
Encode and decode are constant time per character, and radius enumeration is bounded by the 512 cell cap.
Benchmarks guard against regression.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including published geohash test vectors.
Property tests prove snapping idempotence, containment and neighbor symmetry.
A privacy test proves that no public-facing function can output a cell longer than 5 characters.
The library owns no data, so there is nothing to export, import or back up.
Cell strings stored by other modules remain valid across versions because the geohash algorithm is fixed by standard.
Changes to bucket thresholds or radius sets are breaking and require a new major version of this library and a decision record.
LocationSetting stores only cells at precision 4 or 5 and a public level; it has no address field and no raw coordinates.
LocationShare is P3 on the sharer's device and a time-boxed encrypted copy on the recipient's device; its expiry is at most 24 hours after creation and uses the holder's local clock.

The exact coordinates or the L3 cell of a share are stored only encrypted under a per-share key, and that key is deleted in the same transaction that ends the share (crypto-shredding), so the remaining ciphertext cannot be decrypted; no overwrite or erasure timing of storage or memory is claimed.
Home input is validated to cells at precision 5 or coarser and a public level no finer than L2 before storage, and the published cell passes assertPublicCell.

Share input enforces one counterparty, a TTL of 24 hours or less, a non-blocked recipient, location_precise consent, and on receipt an accepted record, a valid signer, bounded claimed times and no replay.
Incoming statements are accepted only when signed by the claimed sharer and addressed to the local principal; otherwise they are quarantined with a reason.
A share is active until the first of revocation, expiry, block, context cancellation or completion, or a deletion request, and every end is permanent.
Ending a share deletes its per-share key and ciphertext in the same transaction and writes an 8-day ended marker.
A new share for the same recipient and context requires the previous one to be ended first.

set_home and clear_home are vault-local commands with no statement; grant and revoke are vault commands that produce signed statements delivered through the sync outbox; receive and receive_revoke are the intake of incoming statements.
Every command emits its local event in the same transaction as the state change; statements are produced by the explicit grant and revoke commands only.
The module consumes block, context (meetup, deal, thread), deletion and accepted-record events to end shares, take in statements and erase data.

Incoming grants and revokes are taken in only from records that F11.S01.M02 accepted with signer role sharer, and the recipient vault returns a signed peer acknowledgement, which alone moves the sharer's outbox entry to peer_accepted.

Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal may set the home region or grant and revoke shares; incoming shares and revokes are accepted only from records F11.S01.M02 accepted, signed by the sharer and addressed to the principal.
There is no relay role and no relay command in this module; relays carry the encrypted envelope as opaque ciphertext and cannot read, create or alter shares.
A blocked party can never create an incoming share on this vault.
Precise sharing and one-shot GPS require a granted privacy.consent.check for purpose location_precise (N6); without it the command is refused with PRECONDITION_FAILED.

A granted location_precise consent only enables precise sharing and never creates, renews, extends or widens a share; every L3 or L4 share still needs its own explicit discovery.location_share.grant by the principal for exactly one counterparty with a TTL of at most 24 h, and this module takes part in the F10.S01.M01 T20 cross-module contract test that proves it.
Vault commands are idempotent through the local command log and use expectedRevision where an aggregate exists.

Delivery of share and revoke statements goes through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never claims more than the reached state.
Expiry and revocation are enforced locally even when the counterparty is unreachable; nothing waits on the network to end a share.

Raw GPS points are never persisted, logged, or put in any event, export of another user or relay-readable payload; references to them are dropped right after snapping or after the share statement is built, and no timing of erasure from memory is claimed.

A share reaches the counterparty only as an end-to-end encrypted envelope (PRV-5); a relay sees ciphertext, size and recipient mailbox id only, and deletes it at the envelope's expiresAt (at most 24 h).
The UI states that the recipient's device can keep a copy and that the share protects against accidental long-lived exposure, not against a malicious recipient.

LocationSetting and LocationShare are registered with F10 - ExportSectionPort (LocationSetting only), DeletionPort (LocationSetting and markers deleted when the plan executes), RetentionPurgePort (ended records after 24 h, markers after 8 days) - and every field is classified with F10.S02.M02; a deletion request only ends active shares.
The PWA sends no telemetry; local diagnostics hold counters of shares granted, expired and failed delivery without positions.
Setting a home cell completes within 100 ms locally and a share grant within 300 ms excluding transport.
Expiry is enforced within 30 seconds of effectiveExpiresAt while the app is open and before any read after unlock.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with an injected clock and a fake geolocation provider.
Contract tests check statements and events against the schema registry.
Privacy tests prove that no raw coordinates, L3 or L4 data appears in logs, events other than the share events, exports of others, or relay requests in readable form.
The user's export contains LocationSetting (home cell and public level) but never active or past LocationShare records, because shares are ephemeral and time-boxed.
Import validates the cell precision and resets changeCount24h; any import carrying a cell finer than 5 characters is rejected.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

The module owns no persisted entity; its inputs are a center cell, a radius and filters, its limits are F12.S03.M03 RatePolicy rows of the shared proximity budget plus F15.S04.M03 relay settings, and its counters are RET-EPHEMERAL RateLimitPort buckets.
The policy row holds numeric limits per caller class and is versioned so operators can audit changes.
A result item exposes a distance bucket, the document's public cell and the public identity fields shared with F06.S01.M02 items, never a number or a finer location.
Center, radius and depth are validated before any search work is done.
Budget limits are checked through RateLimitPort before the index is touched and failures return RATE_LIMITED with retryAfterMs and a reason.
Validation errors never reveal counters or other users' behaviour.
Every relay request with a center - discovery.proximity.search, and discovery.search.query with near or filters.distanceKm - passes the same center, radius and budget checks.
The module has no entity lifecycle; each query is evaluated independently against current counters.

Counter windows slide by fixed buckets (1 min, 1 h, 24 h), reset by expiry, not by operator edits, and survive the daily key-salt rotation because RateLimitPort checks the current and the previous salt for 24 h.
A blocked or rate-limited caller recovers automatically when the window ends.
The only operation is the query discovery.proximity.search, served by the vault locally and by a relay endpoint; it never writes domain state and never produces statements.

Results contain only public P0 fields of SearchDocuments plus a distance bucket, and are reranked with F06.S03.M02 so promoted items carry promoted true and the 'Promoted' explanation key and never exceed floor(20 percent) of a page.
The module emits no events; relay-local abuse counters are metrics, and anomaly reports go to the relay's own moderation signal port.
In the vault, relay items are shown only after their signed projection verifies against authorDid, and blocked or locally hidden authors are filtered at display time.
Vault policy - local proximity search is available to the unlocked principal only and has no rate limit.

Relay policy - the relay endpoint allows anonymous callers at reduced precision and quota, and token or signed-request callers (keyed by their per-relay access token) at the higher quota; a relay may disable anonymous access.
Relay moderators and operators get no extra proximity powers; they can only change policy values.
The query is side-effect free except for ephemeral counters, so retries with the same request are safe and are not double counted.

A rate-limit store failure never skips limits - the query-volume classes fall back to the F12.S03.M03 in-memory half-rate limit, and the center-change class fails closed with RATE_LIMITED for 30 seconds.
Cursors are bound to the center cell, radius and filter hash so they cannot be reused to widen an area.

The center cell is the only location a relay learns from a query; it is L2 or coarser, defaults to the user's public level (never the private home cell at a finer level), and is kept no longer than 24 hours in pseudonymised counters keyed by access token or IP prefix, never by a long-lived device key.
Result distance is bucketed and computed cell to cell, ordering never uses a finer distance than the bucket, and results contain no coordinates.
Trilateration resistance rests on snapping and bucketing; rate limits are a secondary speed bump, and the spec states that a patient attacker with many keys and networks is slowed, not stopped.

Limits run through RateLimitPort (F12.S03.M03, PRV-2, N18) with one set of numbers shared by every relay request with a center; counter keys are HMAC pseudonyms that protect against log readers and backups, not against the relay operator who holds the salt.
Relays export proximity query metrics per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps only local diagnostics.
Proximity queries meet the search budget - relay p95 at most 200 ms over 100 000 documents and local p95 at most 120 ms over 5 000 documents.
Limit triggers are observable by reason.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including a property test that results depend only on cells.
Abuse tests simulate a trilateration attempt and verify the information bound and the limits.
Contract tests check the query signature against the registry.
The module owns no user data; nothing is exported, and the vault keeps no proximity history.
RatePolicy rows of the proximity classes and the relay settings are part of relay configuration and are restored with relay backups; RateLimitPort buckets are never backed up.
Policy value changes are versioned and a rollback restores the previous version.

Input is a list of scored candidates with documentId, projectionCid, sourceId, authorDid, score, recency anchor, promoted flag, authorFirstSeenAt and a score component breakdown, plus page parameters (pageSize, windowStart, carry, promotionEnabled); output is a re-ordered page list with explanation keys and the next window position and carry.
The library has no persisted state; the only parameters are constants per CTR-UX-001 and this spec.
Explanation entries are message keys with parameters so every locale can render them.
Inputs are validated for finite scores, unique document ids and consistent page parameters before any re-ranking.
Violations return typed errors instead of producing a partial or reordered page.
Parameters outside documented bounds are rejected, never clamped.
The library is a pure function over its input; there is no lifecycle.
The same input always yields the same output order and explanations.
Paging over the same snapshot never repeats or drops a result.
The module exposes functions only and defines no commands, queries or events.
Callers apply capability checks and pagination, call rerank exactly once per page of a snapshot window, and store the returned carry in their cursor.
Typed errors returned by rerank are mapped by callers to HTTP problems.
auditPage(page, constants) is a pure check that a vault runs on each relay page and that returns which fairness rule the page breaks, without reordering it.
The library performs no authorization and reads only public document fields.
It has no access to user identity, block lists, history or reputation.
No capability is defined by this module.
rerank is deterministic and side-effect free, so retries are safe.
Windowed paging is stable for the lifetime of a query snapshot (15 minutes).
A failure returns an error and never a partially re-ranked page.
Inputs are public fields only; outputs reveal no private information and no user-specific signals.
Exposure rules do not use protected characteristics, pseudonym text or reputation.
The fairness rules are published in the product's help page and in this spec, and limits against Sybil gaming are stated.
Re-ranking cost is measured inside query latency on relays and in vault diagnostics.
rerank over 200 candidates takes at most 5 ms p95 on a Moto G-class device.
Constraint outcomes are counted for monitoring fairness effects.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including property tests for the constraints.
Golden fixtures pin exact output orders for small candidate sets.
A fairness regression test checks constraints on a 10 000-candidate synthetic corpus.
The library owns no data; nothing is exported, imported or backed up.
Changing a constant (page cap, promoted share, slot count) is a breaking behavioral change and needs a new decision record and a version bump of the library.
Rollback is redeploying the previous release; no data migration exists.
A RankingConfig is an immutable numbered version with bounded numeric parameters, a signature by the publishing relay key, and exactly one active version per relay.

The vault ships a default RankingConfig version 1 inside the app bundle and never edits it; relay configs fetched for display are stored only in a separate cache table and never used for local ranking.
The promotion multiplier cap is a hard maximum of 1.25 that no configuration can exceed.
Every parameter has a documented numeric range and violations are rejected as a whole; nothing is clamped.
Scoring inputs are validated so that NaN or negative values cannot enter a score.
Only relay operators of the relay hosting the config can publish; vault users cannot alter the bundled default.
A new version becomes active atomically and the previous active version becomes retired in the same transaction.
A retired version is never reactivated; a rollback creates a new active version with a new number.
There is never a moment with zero or two active versions.

publish and rollback are relay commands that produce the signed statement classrup.discovery.ranking_config/v1 signed with the relay key; there is no vault command because the vault uses the bundled default.
get_active is a public query available in the vault (bundled default) and on a relay (its active version), and pages through the full 12-month version history.
The event discovery.ranking_config.published is emitted in the same transaction as the activation and is local to the relay.
Relay policy - only the operator role of the relay hosting the config may publish or roll back; the action is recorded in that relay's audit log with actor and version only.
The active config is public read so users can inspect how a relay ranks; the vault's bundled default is read by the principal.
No role can influence another relay or any vault; a vault ignores relay configs for its own local ranking.
Publication is idempotent by Idempotency-Key and guarded by expectedActiveVersion so concurrent publishers cannot both win.
Activation is one SQLite transaction, so a crash leaves exactly one active version.
Scoring is pure, so re-ranking after any failure gives the same order.
Ranking uses only public document fields, query text and the coarse distance bucket; it uses no user identity, history or click data.
Promotion is shown honestly with a 'Promoted' label and a capped multiplier, and is relay-local policy, never claimed as global.
Config publication is auditable and rate limited to prevent silent manipulation.

Relay ranking is presented as that relay's claim; vaults re-apply the F06.S03.M02 page checks to every relay page and label a relay that breaks them, and no history can be flushed from view because get_active pages through the full 12 months.
Scoring cost is measured as part of query latency on relays and in vault diagnostics.
Scoring 1 000 candidates takes at most 20 ms p95 on a Moto G-class device.
Config changes are visible in metrics and logs.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test, including golden score vectors.
Determinism is proven by repeated runs and by cross-platform comparison between browser and Node.
Promotion cap and label rules have dedicated tests.
The vault export contains no RankingConfig because the bundled default is part of the app; relay configs are relay operational data.
A relay's configuration history is part of the relay backup and restored intact with the same version numbers.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An Account stores the did:key, the account root public key, the pseudonym with its normalized skeleton and Unicode data version, the root device flag and timestamps; it holds no email, no password and no private key, only an opaque keystore handle for the root key on the root device.

A DeviceKey stores a public key, label, link evidence with the key's own possession signature, revocation evidence and status; private keys are referenced by keyRef into the kernel keystore where they are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a key derived by scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) per ADR-0013.
A HandleRegistration is relay-side data derived from a signed claim statement and enforces uniqueness of the skeleton only within that relay.

Key custody - the account root key is held only on the root device and inside the recovery kit and signs only classrup.identity.portable_doc/v1, classrup.identity.device_link/v1, classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 and classrup.identity.recovery_notice/v1; every other statement is signed by a device key that the author's current portable document lists as active, with the did:key principal in author and the device key in ext.signerKey (CTR-FED-001 FED-7); verifiers evaluate the signer key at their receipt time (F07.S02.M01 KeyStatusPort), refuse it when the author's latest verified document marks it revoked whatever createdAt claims, and quarantine statements first seen at or after revokesEffectiveAt when they learn of a revocation later.

The fingerprint of a DID or key is the first 16 base58btc characters of base58btc(SHA-256(raw 32-byte public key)), shown in groups of 4, with an 8-word form from the first 88 bits of the same hash; the multicodec prefix of did:key never enters it.
Pseudonyms are normalized and checked before storage using the pinned Unicode data release, with one error code per failure class.
Device key operations verify signatures over JCS bytes of the statement with domain-separated prefixes, so a signature made for one statement type never verifies as another.
Relay registry rules apply only on a relay; the vault never claims global uniqueness.

Device link statements prove possession of the new key, and handle claims and releases are bound to one relay, a fresh claim time and the current registration revision, so none of them can be replayed or reused for another DID.

Revocation signer roles are explicit - the revoked key itself or the root key take effect at once, another active device key only starts a 7 day pending period, and a revoked, pending or contested key cannot revoke.
Accounts are active until the vault is erased; a pseudonym change keeps the account active and bumps its revision.

Device keys move to revoked once and never return; a revocation signed by another device key waits 7 days as revocation_pending for the root key to confirm or for a counter-revocation, and mutual revocations freeze both keys as contested until the root key or the recovery kit decides.
A relay handle moves active to released to purged, and during the released window only the same DID can reclaim it.

Account creation, pseudonym change and device key add and revoke are vault commands; add produces classrup.identity.device_link/v1 signed by the root key and the new key, revoke produces classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 (statement type owned by F16.S02.M02), and a pseudonym change may produce classrup.identity.handle_claim/v1 signed by a device key for registered relays.
handle claim and release are relay commands that verify the signed statement and update only that relay's registry.
Every command emits its events in the same local transaction as the state change.

identity.device_key.added and identity.device_key.revoked describe only the local principal's own keys and carry its DID; when identity.device_key.receive derives them from a verified statement signed on another device of the principal, the event has actor.kind federated and provenance { signerKey, statementCid } (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-7) so F13.S01.M03 can alert this device; counterparty key changes are published by F07.S02.M01 as identity.portable_doc.published with origin received, which counterparty consumers must use.

The module exposes the port registerRecoveredKey to F07.S01.M03 and the pure function fingerprintOf, and consumes the injected ports RecoveryKitStatusPort, KeyStatusPort, ConsentCheckPort and the F10 registries, whose implementing modules depend on this one.

Every classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 this module signs is queued, after privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId), together with the reissued portable document to the relays that document lists (identity.portable_doc.publish with revocations), so a host relay can serve the revocation and the keys it removed through the F07.S02.M01 key-linkage reads (N11).

Vault policy - only the unlocked local principal mutates its Account and DeviceKey records; a new device is authorized only by a link statement signed by the root key and by the new key's own possession signature.

Relay policy - a relay registry accepts a claim or release only when it names that relay and is signed by a device key active in the claimed DID's portable document; relay operators can refuse a handle by hosting policy but cannot create or change a DID.
Pseudonym availability checks on a relay are public and rate limited by relay policy; local checks need only the unlocked vault.

Routine statements are signed by device keys; only the root key may issue identity documents, link devices, confirm another key's revocation and sign recovery notices, and a linked device that lacks it gets IDENTITY_ROOT_KEY_REQUIRED.
Vault commands are idempotent through the local command log; relay commands are idempotent by Idempotency-Key and statement cid.
Statements are queued through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never shows more than the reached state.
Concurrent edits from two tabs or two devices never overwrite each other silently; conflicts surface as CONFLICT_REVISION, a contested key, or a contested identity document.
The vault holds no email, phone, real name or password for the account; the pseudonym is a public label and the DID a stable pseudonymous identifier, which is not anonymity.
Private keys never leave the device unencrypted; the relay never sees them and the recovery kit is separate (F07.S01.M03).
Pseudonym checks never reveal which existing handle a candidate collides with beyond the reason code and the taken flag, except a local warning naming a contact the user already knows.

The module meets the N6 and N6a privacy duties - it implements ExportSectionPort (sections identity.account and identity.device_keys), DeletionPort with the steps sign (signed handle releases), revoke_keys (one classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 per registered device key with reason account_deleted and finalCids of at most 120 final statement cids) and destroy_keys (the last step of the whole deletion) and RetentionPurgePort, classifies every field with F10.S02.M02, checks federation_publish consent through ConsentCheckPort before a handle claim, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as a notification that never deletes or destroys keys.
Relays export registry metrics per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps counters in local diagnostics only.
Account creation completes within 2 seconds on a Moto G-class device including scrypt (N=2^17), and registry claims within 300 ms p95.
Skeleton computation takes at most 5 ms for a 32 code point pseudonym.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with injected clock, ID generator and fixed key pairs.
Pseudonym tests run the UTS 39 conformance vectors for skeleton and a corpus of confusable and mixed-script samples.
Statement tests verify signatures with RFC 8032 vectors and domain-separation negative cases.

Accessibility and UI copy tests check the identity and device screens with axe-core and verify that the honest-limit texts (offline guessing, no global uniqueness, revocation reaching others only on delivery, stolen root device) are present.

The vault export contains the Account and DeviceKey public data and statements; private keys, the root key included, are exported only inside the user's passphrase-encrypted key bundle chosen at export time.
Import validates DID derivation, statement signatures and key uniqueness, and never imports another principal's private data.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A RecoveryKit record of role kit stores the KDF parameters, salt, nonce, encrypted account root key blob, public verifier, the identity document hint and lifecycle fields, and never the 24 words or the derived keys; a record of role observed holds a recovery notice for the own DID that an existing device received.
KDF parameters are fixed to scrypt N=131072, r=8, p=1 with a 16-byte salt and the cipher is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 24-byte nonce; weaker parameters are rejected.

Only one kit is active per account in a vault and creating a new one supersedes the old one locally, but every kit wraps the same root key, so a superseded kit is not revoked and the UI and acceptance criteria say so.
Kit creation validates parameters and confirms the user saved the words; recovery validates words with a checksum before spending scrypt time.

Within one vault only one recovery may be pending and revocation of other devices before the window ends is refused; vaults cannot see each other, so these rules bind only the recovering vault, and receivers enforce their own 72 hour wait from first sight of the notice (F07.S02.M01).
Every failure maps to one stable error code without revealing which word was wrong.

Received recovery notices and disputes are verified against the DID root key and against the device keys of the latest identity document this vault holds, and are rate limited per DID and per signing key.
A kit is active until recovery starts, is superseded, or is used; used and superseded are final.

A pending recovery completes into used, returns to active by the recovering user's cancel or by expiry after 7 days (keeping the new key and cancelling the planned revocations), or becomes contested on a verified dispute, which never revokes the new key or resets the kit.

The recovering vault requests revocation of other devices only after 72 hours, or after 7 days when contested; honest clients and verifying vaults wait 72 hours from their own first sight of the notice, and the product does not claim more.
On existing devices an observed recovery notice moves from received to disputed, accepted or expired, and disputing needs no kit state.

All commands are vault commands; begin produces classrup.identity.recovery_notice/v1 signed by the root key decrypted from the kit, dispute produces classrup.identity.recovery_dispute/v1 signed by an existing device key active in the latest document, and receive_notice and receive_dispute are the intakes of those statements; statements travel through the sync outbox.
No command contacts a relay with a secret; statements go to relays and mailboxes only as signed public or end-to-end encrypted items.

Recovery registers the new device key through the F07.S01.M01 port registerRecoveredKey, issues identity documents through F07.S02.M01 and revokes device keys through F07.S01.M01, which emit the device key events.
Begin obtains and verifies the latest identity document before planning any revocation, or runs in the explicit device_list_unknown mode that can add a key but never revokes others.

create_kit signs classrup.identity.recovery_kit_notice/v1 { did, kitId, supersededKitId?, createdAtClaim } with this device key and sends it end-to-end encrypted only to the principal's own devices; receive_kit_notice on another device verifies it, records a kit_observed entry and emits identity.recovery.kit_created with actor.kind federated and provenance { signerKey, statementCid }, so F13.S01.M03 alerts that device; the notice carries no kit material, words or blob.

begin accepts the kit as the file from a file chooser or as the QR code of the printed sheet, both carrying the same kit core checked against blobChecksum, and the words as a pasted whole phrase or per-word entry, and no input path blocks paste or password-manager autofill (CTR-UX-001 UX-5).
Vault policy - creating and verifying a kit require an unlocked vault; begin runs in a new or empty vault where possession of the words and file is the authorization.

Disputes are authorized by a signature from a device key active in the account's latest document known to the receiving vault; a dispute proves only that such a key signed it and freezes the recovery as contested instead of cancelling it, so a stolen device cannot block a recovery for ever.
Relays have no capability here; they only carry signed notices, disputes and end-to-end encrypted mailbox items.
Kit creation and each recovery step are single local transactions, so a crash leaves either the old state or the new state.
Statements go through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never claims more than the reached state.
A failed recovery never deletes the old kit and never revokes any key on its own.
The 24 words and all derived keys exist only in memory during derivation and in the user's own hands; the vault stores no copy and no relay ever receives them.
The kit file is encrypted and may be stored anywhere the user chooses; the app never uploads it by default and states that the file alone is useless without the words.
The product states plainly that anyone with both the words and the file can control the account, that a newer kit does not revoke an older one, and that words and file should be stored separately.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (section identity.recovery_kit), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort, classifies its fields with F10.S02.M02, pseudonymizes observed notices and disputes kept as RET-EVIDENCE instead of deleting them, checks federation_publish consent before sending statements to a relay, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.
The PWA sends no telemetry; local diagnostics hold counters of kit creation, verification and recovery attempts without secrets.
Key derivation with scrypt N=2^17 completes within 1.5 seconds on a Moto G-class device and 600 ms on a laptop.
Kit creation completes within 3 seconds including printing layout.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with injected clock, fixed salts and fixed key pairs.
Cryptographic tests use known-answer vectors for scrypt, XChaCha20-Poly1305 and Ed25519 and fail on any parameter change.
Privacy tests prove that words and derived keys never reach storage, logs, events, exports or the network.
Abuse tests cover a modified client, concurrent recoveries in isolated vaults, repeated disputes by a stolen device and disputes arriving after completion.
Accessibility and UI copy tests check the kit and recovery screens, including the honest texts about kit possession, superseded kits and the notice window.
The vault export contains kit metadata and the encrypted blob so a user can re-download the file, but never the words.
Import validates KDF parameters, blob checksum and the verifier, and sets the kit to active only if verification of the checksum passes.
Parameter changes (a stronger scrypt) are new kit versions; v1 kits remain valid and readable for 180 days after a new major.
A LoginChallenge stores only the hash of the nonce, the DID it was issued for, the relay it was bound to, and a 120 second expiry; it is relay-side ephemeral data.
A Session stores kind, DID, device key, token hash for relay sessions, idle and absolute expiry, rotation grace and metadata; vault unlock sessions are in memory and never persisted.
Tokens and the vault key are P4 values that never appear in logs, events or exports; only SHA-256 hashes of tokens are stored on the relay.
A challenge is valid only if unexpired, unused, issued for the claimed DID and relay, and signed over the exact domain-separated message.

The signing key must be listed active in the DID's current signed identity document, verified per F07.S02.M01, re-fetched from the document's listed relays when the cached copy is older than 1 hour, or supplied inline on first login.

Every challenge or signature failure on the start path returns the same UNAUTHENTICATED outward response, with the specific reason only in relay diagnostics; EXPIRED is used only for a token past its absolute expiry.

Challenges are issued for every well-formed did:key, with caps per (DID, IP prefix) and oldest-first eviction, so an attacker can neither probe which DIDs a relay knows through the login endpoints nor lock a victim out by filling challenge slots.
Vault unlock enforces the idle timeout range and the local backoff schedule, and a passphrase change requires the current passphrase and a new one that passes the strength rule.
Challenges move from issued to consumed, expired or evicted exactly once and never return.
Sessions are active until locked, revoked or expired; the end is permanent, and a new login creates a new session.
Rotation moves the old session to rotating with graceUntil now plus 30 seconds, inserts the new session in the same transaction, and revokes the old one with reason rotated only when the grace ends.

unlock, lock and change_passphrase (which re-wraps the vault keystore under a new passphrase-derived key) operate in the vault with no statement; challenge, start, rotate and revoke for relay tokens are relay commands, and the start request carries a signature by the device key.
Every command emits its events in the same transaction as the state change, and rotate emits identity.session.revoked for the old session only when the grace ends.

The module consumes device key, recovery, identity document and erase events to end sessions - in the vault it revokes the affected relay tokens on every known relay through the outbox, and on a relay it ends tokens whose device key is no longer active in the stored document.

Vault lock and principal switch (unlocking another principal's vault on this device locks the current one first) drop the in-memory raw relay access tokens and the vault key in the same step, end the vault_unlock session with endReason locked or principal_switch, and send CLEAR_USER_CACHES { reason: lock|principal_switch, partition } to the F15.S01.M02 service worker; outbox entries stay queued unsent, and the next unlock re-runs the relay challenge-response before any relay call.
