On a relay, identity.session.linked_keys is an in-process read for the host's anti-shill checks (F04.S02.M01 linked_host_registration, N11) that returns, for one relay access-token session and its rotation successors, the starting device key and the requestSignerKeys accepted with that token, never IP addresses, network ranges or timing, and is never served over HTTP.
Vault policy - only a person who knows the passphrase or holds the platform-protected key can unlock or change the passphrase; once unlocked the principal acts as the local actor.
Relay policy - challenge and start are open to anonymous callers (they authenticate by signature); all other session commands need a valid relay token of the same DID.
Relay roles from security.role.* apply only to that relay's resources and end sessions so they take effect on the next request (CAP-6).
Token issuance and challenge consumption occur in one relay transaction so a crash never leaves a consumed challenge without a session or a session without consumption.
Revocation is idempotent and takes effect on the next request.
Vault unlock is local and works offline; relay sessions fail closed, and the client re-authenticates with the device key transparently.
Tokens are 256-bit random values returned once, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, sent only in the Authorization header and never logged or placed in URLs.
Relays learn the DID, device public key, /24 or /48 prefix and user agent label only; they never learn the passphrase, vault key or any private key.
The vault passphrase protects against casual access and not against an attacker with a copy of the encrypted vault who can guess offline; the UI says so.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (section identity.sessions with the lock timeout preference only, never sessions), DeletionPort (end every session and delete token hashes on each known relay before keys are destroyed) and RetentionPurgePort (ended sessions after 30 days, challenges after 24 h), classifies its fields with F10.S02.M02, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.
Relays export session metrics per CTR-OBS-001 without DIDs or tokens as labels; the vault keeps only local counters.
Challenge issue and start meet the write budget of p95 at most 300 ms at 50 req/s; vault unlock completes within 1.5 seconds on a Moto G-class device.
Per-request token verification adds at most 2 ms p95.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with injected clock and fixed key pairs.
Signature tests include RFC 8032 vectors and negative cases for wrong domain, relay and nonce.
Privacy tests prove tokens and keys never appear in logs, events, URLs or exports.
Accessibility and UI copy tests check the unlock, passphrase and sessions screens, including the offline-guessing warning.
Sessions are never exported or imported; after an import the user unlocks and re-authenticates to relays.
A relay backup restores token hashes and expiry only; tokens remain valid until their original expiry, and an operator can revoke all with one command.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A PortableIdentityDoc stores the signed document bytes' fields, its cid, sequence, previous cid, status and provenance, for the owner's own versions and for received versions of others.

The signed payload lists the DID, seq, prev, pseudonym, device keys with statuses and possession signatures, hashes of older revoked keys, relays and issuedAt/expiresAt, is signed only by the DID root key, and is at most 8 KiB.

Statuses express verification outcomes - verifying, current, gap_pending, recovery_pending, stale (own, needs reissue), expired, superseded, history and contested - and never imply real-world identity.

The document keeps its root-key seq and prev chain but uses the F11.S01.M03 cid and signed-bytes definition and its shared golden vectors, and each stored version records its earliest evidence time, the first-seen time of every key and the keyrevocation statements verified with it.
Every document is verified for DID derivation, signature, size, possession proofs, chain and field limits before it is stored as anything other than quarantine.
Clock claims are checked with explicit tolerance and never trusted for ordering; seq orders versions.
Relay publication adds quotas and URL checks.

First contact, chain gaps and recovery-driven revocations have explicit rules - trust on first use, a 24 hour gap buffer with fetches from the listed relays, and a 72 hour wait from this vault's first sight of the recovery notice.

Revocations are a grow-only union - a key once seen revoked stays revoked, a resolving document must list every revocation of every competing branch, and the deviceKeys cap is met by moving older revocations to key hashes rather than dropping them.

Key status is evaluated at the receiver's time - a key the latest verified document marks revoked is refused whatever createdAt claims; when a revocation is learned later, statements first seen at or after its effective time are quarantined (replacing plain first-seen acceptance); the effective time is the claimed revokesEffectiveAt clamped to no earlier than earliestEvidenceAt minus 30 days and no later than earliestEvidenceAt, clamped values are labelled, and a revocation is applied whatever its age.
Own documents list only the relays that F11.S03.M01 reports as selected with listInIdentityDoc true, at most 5.

A document moves from current to superseded when a valid newer version is accepted, to stale when the owner's state changes or 150 days pass, to expired when expiresAt passes, and to contested when a fork is detected.
A contested identity is resolved only by a signed document with a higher seq that chains from one competing version, lists every key revoked in any competing branch, and that the user accepts.
Superseded documents are kept for verification of old statements, and lower-seq documents received later are stored as history.

Issue is a vault command that produces the root-signed statement classrup.identity.portable_doc/v1; receive is the vault intake of someone else's document; resolve is the user's explicit choice for a contested DID; publish and the public read are relay endpoints.

The event identity.portable_doc.published is emitted when a document is issued locally, when a received document changes a DID's current document or status, and when a relay stores a verified document, in the same transaction as the state change.
Documents are public P0 statements and are only sent to relays the owner selected, after privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId), or directly to peers.

Key-linkage reads (N11) return the key set with each key's first-seen time and the seq chain of a DID, the keys removed from its documents and the classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 statements verified with them, the DIDs that list a given key, and a key's status at a point in time; on a relay they run in-process only, for the anti-shill checks of an auction whose seller chose that relay as host (PT-15) and for F10.S01.M02 legal-hold approval, and there is no account key rotation chain in MVP.

Counterparty modules learn of other people's key changes only from identity.portable_doc.published with origin received, which carries the added and revoked keys with the clamped effective revocation time; identity.device_key events describe only the local principal's keys.

Ports provided - KeyStatusPort.isActive and keyStatus(did, publicKey, at) at receiver time; KeyLinkagePort.linked(didA, didB) -> boolean, true when a device key is listed, revoked or removed under both DIDs or SameOwnerLinkPort reports a same_owner attestation between them, failing closed when the linkage store is unreadable; IdentityRefreshPort.refresh(did, relays) for F16.S02.M02, which fetches the DID's latest document from at most 5 given relays and runs it through receive. Injected ports - ListedRelaysPort (F11.S03.M01) and SameOwnerLinkPort (F07.S03.M02), wired by the composition roots because both implementers depend on this module.

Vault policy - only the unlocked principal on its root device issues documents for its own DID; any signed document is accepted into the store only after cryptographic verification, so authority comes from the root key signature, not from the sender.

Relay policy - publication is open to anyone presenting a valid signed document within quota (no account needed), and reads are public; a relay operator may refuse a DID by hosting policy but cannot alter a document.
A blocked DID's documents are dropped silently through the injected BlockFilterPort, implemented by F07.S02.M02, and the sender cannot tell.
Issue and receive are idempotent by cid, so duplicate delivery never creates a duplicate version.
Documents are published to relays through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never shows more than the reached state.
Fork detection never discards either version; it records both.
The document is a deliberate public P0 statement containing only public keys, key hashes, the pseudonym and relay URLs, and it never contains P3 data, private keys or recovery material.
The product states before first publication that a published document and copies other vaults fetched cannot be recalled, only superseded or tombstoned.
Relays honor signed tombstones within 24 hours (FED-4, PRV-6) and may not rewrite documents.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (section identity.portable_docs), DeletionPort (tombstone the own document on the selected relays, delete received documents, pseudonymize documents kept as evidence) and RetentionPurgePort, classifies provenance fields with F10.S02.M02, checks federation_publish consent per relay before publication, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.
Relays export publication and read metrics per CTR-OBS-001; vaults keep local diagnostics only.
Signature verification and storage of a document take at most 10 ms p95 on a Moto G-class device and 5 ms on the relay.
Relay reads meet the read budget of p95 at most 150 ms.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with fixed key pairs, JCS test vectors and an injected clock.
did:key encoding is verified against the W3C did:key Ed25519 test behaviour (prefix z6Mk, round trip).
Fork, rollback, gap, recovery-wait and quota behaviour are tested with deterministic fixtures.
Accessibility and UI copy tests cover the identity document and contact screens, including contested, gap, recovery pending and expired warnings and the no-recall notice.
The vault export contains the owner's document history and the documents of contacts, each with provenance, so the identity can move between relays and devices.
Import re-verifies every signature, possession proof, chain and size, keeps valid documents with their original provenance and firstSeenAt and rejects invalid ones with a report.
Schema changes follow expand/contract with v1 readable for 180 days, and a new major carries a signed migration statement.

A Profile stores the display data and per-field visibility; the record is classed P3 as a whole with field-level classes registered with F10.S02.M02 (public fields P0 once published, contacts fields P2, private fields P3), own profiles are editable and received profiles are read-only mirrors with provenance and the original signature.
A BlockEntry is a P3 vault-only record of blockerDid and blockedDid with an optional private note and is excluded from every statement, relay payload, log and event with class below P3.
Avatar and bio have hard size limits so signed statements stay under 32 KiB.
Profile input is validated strictly with exact limits, and avatars are re-encoded, stripped of metadata and size-checked on the device.
Visibility and region rules guarantee that no private field and no location finer than L2 enter a statement, and the region passes F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell (N8).
Block input validates DIDs and the cap, and intake of received profiles verifies signatures before storage.

A profile record in the vault is active, hidden by the local user, or deleted by a tombstone authored by its own DID, the owner's erase or contact removal; a relay's hosting action changes only that relay's copy.
A block is active until removed; removal is permanent for that entry and a re-block creates a new entry.
Hidden profiles return to active only by an explicit local unhide; relay hosting actions and their reversal never change vault records.

update, publish, unpublish, block add and block remove are vault commands; publish produces the signed statement classrup.identity.profile/v1 and unpublish produces classrup.federation.tombstone/v1, both signed by a device key active in the owner's document and both signed and stored only through the F11.S01.M01 StatementPublisherPort (publish and issueTombstone, implemented by F11.S01.M02, which allocates seq and prev); receive is the vault intake of someone else's profile statement.
Block commands emit local P3 events that other modules consume to cancel work; block data is never placed in a statement.
Reads of profiles apply the viewer's perspective - strangers see public fields, conversation participants see contacts fields, the owner sees all.

A tombstone withdraws a received profile only when its author equals the profile's DID and its signer key is active in that DID's document; a tombstone signed by an origin relay only removes that relay from the profile's provenance.
Relay hosting actions (moderation.action.applied and moderation.action.reverted) are consumed only by the relay runtime for the relay's own copy and never change vault records.

F08.S01.M01 calls MailboxHintPort.set(relayId, mailboxId, previousMailboxId?) after comms.mailbox.register and comms.mailbox.rotate; the own profile keeps at most 5 mailbox IDs, and when the profile is published a new version with seq plus 1 carrying the new or replacement ID is published to the relays that hold the current version, with federation_publish consent re-checked (N15).

Vault policy - only the unlocked principal edits, publishes or unpublishes its profile and edits its block list; received profiles are accepted only with a valid signature by a device key that the profile DID's latest verified document does not mark revoked at receipt, and are quarantined when a revocation learned later took effect before this vault first saw them.
Visibility is enforced at composition and at read; a stranger can never read contacts or private fields because those never leave the vault in a public statement.
Relay policy - a relay may host profile statements and stop serving its copy under its policy; it has no access to blocks and cannot change a vault's records.

Vault commands are idempotent through the local command log and use expectedRevision; a profile publish or unpublish is queued through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted.
Blocking is effective locally the moment it commits, independent of any network.
Receiving the same profile statement twice is a no-op keyed by cid.
The block list is P3 and never leaves the vault, never appears in statements, logs, relay requests or events below P3, and the blocked person receives no notification.

Public profile fields are exactly what the user marked public; a published profile and copies other vaults fetched cannot be recalled, only superseded or tombstoned, and the UI says so before first publication.
Region never exceeds L2 and is off by default.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (sections identity.profiles and identity.blocks), DeletionPort (tombstone the own published profile, delete profiles and blocks) and RetentionPurgePort, registers field classes with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) before every public relay publication, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.
The PWA sends no telemetry; local diagnostics keep counters without DIDs or content.
Block checks used by other modules cost at most 1 ms p95 for a single lookup and 5 ms for a list of 500 DIDs on a Moto G-class device.
Profile view renders within the PWA budget (LCP at most 2.5 s on the 4G profile).
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with fixed key pairs and an injected clock.
Privacy tests prove that private fields and blocks never appear in statements, logs or events below P3.
Block enforcement is tested end to end across a consumer module fake.
Accessibility and UI copy tests check the profile, blocked people and other-profile screens, including the no-recall notice before first publication.
The vault export contains the own profile, received profile cache entries the user kept (contacts), and the block list.
Import revalidates avatar and statement limits and signatures of received profiles, and restores blocks as active entries up to the 1 000 cap.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A TrustAttestation stores kind, subject, issuer, claim label, validity, the signed statement fields, endorsement and provenance; it stores no email, phone, document or biometric data.

Every attestation carries the issuer's Ed25519 envelope signature (F11.S01.M03) by a device key in ext.signerKey that the issuer's latest verified portable document does not mark revoked at this vault's receipt (a relay key from the relay key set for relay_email_check), is quarantined when a revocation learned later took effect before this vault first saw it, and is verifiable offline.

Visibility is a local setting of the subject and never alters the signed statement; public display of a claim about another person requires the subject's endorsement countersignature, and a same_owner link requires signatures by both DIDs.
Every attestation is verified for signature, signer key status, kind rules and field limits before it is displayed.
Free-text labels are restricted to plain text with a reserved-word filter so a label cannot pose as an official verification.
Expiry is anchored on the verifier's own clock and capped per kind.

The relay key set used to check relay_email_check is built from the signed descriptors of the viewer's chosen relays and peers (F15.S02.M01 descriptor, F11.S03.M01 peer records, F16.S02.M02 key records) and every affected attestation is re-checked when the set changes.
same_owner attestations require valid signatures by both DIDs, and endorsements must be signed by the subject.
An attestation is active until the issuer revokes it or it expires; both ends are final for that statement.
Revocation takes effect for a viewer only when the viewer receives the signed revocation, and the viewer's UI shows the last-checked time.
Re-issuing creates a new statement and a new attestation record.

A tombstone revokes an attestation only when its author equals the issuer; a tombstone signed by an origin relay only drops that relay's provenance entry, and the subject's endorsement changes display, not the statement.

issue, revoke, endorse and set_visibility are vault commands; issue, revoke and endorse produce the signed statements classrup.identity.attestation/v1, classrup.identity.attestation_revocation/v1 and classrup.identity.attestation_endorsement/v1 signed by a device key and signed and stored only through the F11.S01.M01 StatementPublisherPort (implemented by F11.S01.M02); receive is the vault intake of someone else's statement.

issue_relay is a relay command signed with the relay key that names the relay origin, is delivered only to the subject end-to-end encrypted, and stores no personal data beyond the subject DID and date.
Every command emits its events in the same transaction as the state change.

identity.attestation.list_linkage returns the same_owner links of a DID, signed by both the issuer's and the subject's device keys, with their status for key-linkage checks (N11); on a host relay it runs in-process only over cosigned same_owner attestations published to that relay, for anti-shill checks of auctions whose seller chose it (F04.S02.M01 V03, PT-15), and SameOwnerLinkPort.linked(didA, didB) serves the same data to F07.S02.M01 KeyLinkagePort.

Vault policy - only the unlocked principal issues or revokes attestations under its own DID and endorses, co-signs or sets visibility of claims about itself; received attestations are accepted only on a valid signature by an active key of the stated issuer.

Relay policy - only the operator role of a relay can issue relay_email_check attestations, signed with that relay's key and naming the relay origin; the attestation means only that this relay's operator says it checked an email, and viewers choose which relays they trust.

Viewing follows the subject's visibility and endorsement; non-self claims are issued subject-only and are shown publicly only when the subject republished them with an endorsement countersignature, and private attestations are never included in published or shared profile statements.
Issue, receive, endorse and revoke are idempotent by statement cid, and duplicate delivery never creates a duplicate attestation.
Statements go through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never shows more than the reached state.
A revocation that cannot be delivered still takes effect locally, and the UI says other people may not have seen it yet.
No KYC or contact data is stored; the relay_email_check attestation records only that the operator said it checked an email on a date, never the address.
Attestations are evidence that a signer asserted a claim; the UI never states that a claim is true or verified, and a signer can be a stranger or a throwaway DID.
Subjects decide whether claims about them are shown publicly by endorsing them, but cannot erase another person's signed statement from other vaults.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (section identity.attestations), DeletionPort (pseudonymize attestations kept as RET-EVIDENCE, delete the rest) and RetentionPurgePort, classifies fields with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) before queuing a public attestation or endorsement, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.
Public statements carry only a blinded contextRef, so deal and meetup ids never leak through attestations.
Relays export operator-issued attestation counts per CTR-OBS-001; vaults keep local counters only.
Verification of one attestation takes at most 8 ms p95 on a Moto G-class device.
Listing 50 attestations for a subject completes within 50 ms p95 locally.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with fixed key pairs and an injected clock.
Signature tests include tampering, wrong issuer and wrong kind negative cases.
Privacy tests prove that no email, phone or document data is stored anywhere in the module.
Accessibility and UI copy tests check the trust list, issue sheet and claims-about-me screens, including that no UI string says 'verified'.
The vault export contains attestations issued by the principal and about the principal and those the user kept, with signatures and endorsements.
Import re-verifies every signature, endorsement and kind rule, recomputes effective expiry from the import time capped by the original claim, and skips invalid statements with a report.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Review stores the signed statement fields, an outcome label, the proof (the subject's review ticket for the pair, plus for subject-only reviews the full opening and outcome evidence), provenance and a verification status, and is immutable after posting except for local hide and withdrawal.

A ReviewWindow is created when a context the principal takes part in opens, holds the per-pair tickets exchanged then, opens for 30 days when an outcome event with the N3 fields arrives, and limits the number of pairs to 66.
A ReputationSummary is derived, versioned by algorithm, and fully recomputable from stored reviews and recorded no-show claims, so it can be thrown away and rebuilt.
Public reviews carry only a per-pair blinded reference and the per-pair ticket, never contextId, completionCid or a dispute case cid, so two public reviews from one cycle share no identifier.
Reviews are validated for schema, signature, eligibility and proof before they count; failures are quarantined with a reason, not silently dropped.
Eligibility derives only from bilateral opening evidence - the subject's signed review ticket for the pair - and the pair list, never from the review text or the subject's later cooperation.
Limits on volume and size bound the work a hostile sender can cause.

Signer keys of reviews, tickets and tombstones must not be revoked in the signer's latest verified portable document at receipt (F07.S02.M01 key_status at receiver time), a revocation learned later quarantines those first seen at or after its clamped revokesEffectiveAt, and outcome events must carry the N3 fields and verifiable completion statements or the window is quarantined.
A received review starts pending verification and ends posted or quarantined; a quarantined review may be re-verified when missing evidence arrives.

A posted review can be hidden or restored only by the local user, and withdrawn only by a tombstone whose author is the review's author; relay hosting actions and relay-signed tombstones never change a vault's review records.
A ReviewWindow is pending from the opening of a context, opens for 30 days when an outcome event with the N3 fields arrives, is quarantined when a required field is missing, and then closes.

post, withdraw and hide are vault commands; post produces the signed statement classrup.identity.review/v1, the opening and outcome handlers produce classrup.identity.review_ticket/v1 (for Deals the commerce.deal.opened and commerce.deal.completed handlers, never read from the Deal opening statement), and withdraw produces classrup.federation.tombstone/v1, all signed by a device key and signed and stored only through the F11.S01.M01 StatementPublisherPort (publish for reviews and tickets, issueTombstone for withdrawals, implemented by F11.S01.M02); receive and review_ticket.receive are the vault intakes of someone else's statements.

Opening, completion, dispute, cycle recovery and cancellation events open or update review windows using their N3 fields (contextId, completionCid, parties with roles, legs for cycles, reviewUnlock for cycle recoveries), and a completion opens a window only after the completion statements behind completionCid verify in this vault (V13); they never create reviews by themselves, and a missing field or statement quarantines the window rather than guessing.
Every command emits its events in the same local transaction as the state change.

No-show claims from comms.meetup.no_show are recorded and displayed as claims with zero weight in rep-1, a claim contradicted by the accused's check-in (comms.meetup.no_show_contradicted, or contradicted true on arrival) is displayed together with that check-in statement, and neither creates reviews.

Vault policy - only the unlocked principal posts, withdraws or hides; reviews and tickets are accepted from others only on verified signatures by active device keys and on the subject's ticket, and authority comes from the signed bilateral evidence, not from the sender or relay.
Reviews are readable to anyone who holds the statement; public reviews are P1 community data shared through relays the author chose, and subject-only reviews are end-to-end encrypted to the subject.
Relays may stop serving a review copy under their hosting policy, which a vault may record only as provenance; they cannot create, edit, hide, withdraw or delete the author's statement in any vault.

Posting, receiving, ticket intake and recomputing are idempotent because cids and the unique (author, pairRef) key make duplicates harmless, and a summary can always be rebuilt from stored reviews and no-show claims.

Review statements and tickets reach others through the sync outbox with states local_committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted, and the UI never claims more than the reached state.
Quarantine keeps unverified material out of every score until it verifies.

Reviews are statements by individuals about transactions and are P1; subject-only reviews travel end-to-end encrypted, and comments never contain exact addresses or contact data by rule and by warning.
Reputation is shown with its provenance - the number of reviews and sources seen by this device - because no party holds the complete set.
The product states that dampening reduces but does not remove the effect of fake identities and colluding parties.

The module meets the N6 privacy duties - it registers ExportSectionPort (sections identity.reviews and identity.review_windows), DeletionPort (pseudonymize reviews and windows kept as RET-EVIDENCE, delete the rest, tombstone own public reviews if the user chooses) and RetentionPurgePort, classifies fields with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish, relayId) before queuing any public review to a relay, and treats privacy.deletion.completed only as final cleanup.

Summary inputs are chosen by weight and author diversity, not by recency - every review with weight at least 0.5 is kept, the rest are taken by descending weight with at most 3 per author, up to 500 per subject - so a subject cannot bury genuine reviews with self-made ones.
The PWA sends no telemetry; local diagnostics keep counters without DIDs or content.
Recompute for a subject with 500 reviews completes within 20 ms on a Moto G-class device, and reputation card render fits the PWA budget (LCP at most 2.5 s on the 4G profile).
Verification of a review (author signature plus ticket signature) takes at most 15 ms p95.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test with fixed key pairs and an injected clock.
Golden vectors pin the dampening formula, the input selection and the Bayesian average.
Privacy and abuse tests simulate sybil rings and fabricated completions.
Abuse tests cover a withheld completion signature, burial by 500 sybil reviews, relay-signed tombstones and review unlinkability within one cycle.
Accessibility and UI copy tests check the review sheet and reputation card, including the dampening honesty text, outcome labels and the source note.
The vault export contains the principal's own reviews, received reviews it chose to keep, review windows with their tickets, and not the derived summary, which is rebuilt.
Import re-verifies signatures and tickets and quarantines failures; open windows are restored with their original closesAt.
Algorithm changes bump algorithmVersion, recompute from stored reviews, and keep the previous version's results available for 30 days.

An Attachment stores sender, thread label hash, the MediaBlob reference of the ciphertext, ciphertext size, chunk size and count, ciphertext hash, declared media type and slot state; it never stores the object key, the nonce prefix or any plaintext metadata, and the ciphertext bytes are an encrypted MediaBlob held by F15.S02.M03.

Relay-side attachment rows and blobs are RET-SHORT (deleted 30 days after upload, or earlier on delete) and the vault copy follows the referencing message's RET-STANDARD; deleting the blob removes it from the relay's live store, which is not crypto-shredding in the CTR-PRV-001 sense because every recipient of the message holds the per-object key.

Limits are 5 MiB (5 242 880 bytes) of ciphertext, which allows at most 5 241 600 bytes of processed plaintext in at most 80 chunks, 4096 px maximum on the long edge, and media types image/jpeg, image/png and image/webp only.

Encryption is a STREAM construction over XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a fresh 32-byte key: chunk i (65 536 bytes, last chunk shorter) is sealed with the 24-byte nonce = 20-byte random prefix || uint32 big-endian i and additional data JCS({attachmentId, chunkCount, index: i, last: i = chunkCount - 1}), so reordering, truncation or dropping of chunks fails authentication.

The encrypted message body (F08.S01.M01) carries {attachmentId, relayId, blobRef, key, noncePrefix, cipherSha256, cipherSize, plainSize, chunkCount, declaredType, downloadToken, altText? (plain text ≤ 140 characters, the shared MediaRef limit), decorative?: boolean}; recipients check cipherSha256 and cipherSize of the downloaded ciphertext against these values before decrypting any chunk.
Slot requests and uploads are validated against declared limits before any bytes are accepted.
Finalization verifies stored length and hash against the declared values before the blob becomes downloadable.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Recipients validate the downloaded ciphertext against cipherSha256, cipherSize and chunkCount from the encrypted message body before decrypting any chunk, and reject reordered, truncated or dropped chunks.

Thread archives and blocks never stop evidence for a context confirmed before the block - attaching, uploading, finalizing, relay deletes and downloads of such attachments proceed whatever the thread state, and only notifications are suppressed (N7a).
An Attachment starts pending, becomes uploaded only after hash verification and ends deleted or expired; both ends are terminal.
Pending slots not finalized within 1 hour expire and their partial chunks are erased by a sweep every 5 minutes.

Deletion of the referencing message by its author in any delivery state, abandonment of the message's outbox entry before any relay received it, a signed delete during account deletion, or relay retention expiry 30 days after upload deletes the blob and moves the Attachment to deleted; there is no retention extension.

comms.attachment.uploaded and comms.attachment.deleted are emitted in the uploader's vault when it records a verified finalize response, a delete response or the passing of the relay-signed retainUntil, taking threadId from the local record; relay commands emit no events (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-8, N17).
The module exposes the vault commands attach and remove, the relay commands create_slot, put_chunk, finalize and delete, and a ciphertext download query.

The uploader vault emits comms.attachment.uploaded in the same IndexedDB transaction that records a verified finalize response and comms.attachment.deleted in the transaction that records a delete response or the passing of retainUntil.

The module consumes message, delivery and deletion events locally to issue signed relay delete requests; every command is classed below as vault command or relay command, and the ciphertext is stored as a F15.S02.M03 MediaBlob.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.attachments), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize) and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6); DeletionPort.execute sends signed relay deletes for every blob the user uploaded and erases local keys before F10.S01.M04 destroys the device keys.

The module implements the F09.S02.M02 AttachmentTransportPort send(blobRef, recipients[], perObjectKey) -> { attachmentId, cipherBlobRef, syncState }: it reads the local evidence MediaBlob already stripped by F10.S02.M03, re-runs verifyImageClean, STREAM-encrypts it under the caller's per-object key with a fresh nonce prefix, uploads it with create_slot, put_chunk and finalize (threadLabelHash = HMAC of the caller's context reference under the per-device salt) and delivers the descriptor {attachmentId, relayId, cipherBlobRef, plainBlobRef = blobRef, key, noncePrefix, cipherSha256, cipherSize, plainSize, chunkCount, declaredType, downloadToken} to each recipient as statement classrup.comms.attachment_share/v1 (signer a device key of the uploader, registered with F11.S01.M01, N2, ingest owner this module) sealed through the F08.S01.M01 MailboxPort; a recipient vault verifies it, downloads, checks the ciphertext and stores the plaintext as a local MediaBlob whose content address equals plainBlobRef.

Relay policy lets only device keys registered at the relay (relay access token) create slots, upload and finalize, within the quotas below; vault policy lets only the local principal attach images to its own messages.
Only the uploader device key can delete an attachment; a relay moderator can remove a blob only under that relay's hosting policy with a recorded reason.
Download requires the secret 256-bit token that only the message participants hold; wrong tokens and unknown IDs return NOT_FOUND.
Slot creation and finalize are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; chunk upload is idempotent on (attachmentId, index) and a repeated chunk with different bytes is refused.
Interrupted uploads resume at the first missing chunk index within the 1 hour slot life without re-encrypting.

Finalize is one relay transaction; MediaBlob storage and the attachment row remain consistent through write-then-rename and a reconciliation sweep, and the vault records the response and emits its event in one IndexedDB transaction.

The relay stores only ciphertext and the sizes needed for storage; media type is declared and unverified, filenames and threadIds are never stored; the relay sees the uploader's relay identity and upload time, which is disclosed.

Client-side stripping uses F10.S02.M03 stripImage and verifyImageClean, removing EXIF, GPS, XMP, IPTC and embedded thumbnails by decoding and re-encoding pixels; this is tested on device but the relay cannot verify it inside ciphertext, which is stated in documentation.

Deleting a blob removes it from the relay's live store only; attachment blobs are excluded from this module's relay backup set, but a relay keeping its own backups (up to 12 months under CTR-IOX-001 IOX-3) and recipients who saved the key and blob can still recover the attachment, which the UI and documentation state; true shredding is the sender erasing its key, with recipients erasing theirs on a verified delete request as best effort.

Privacy duties (N6): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered, and deletion sends signed relay deletes before the keys are destroyed.
Relay upload outcomes, bytes and sweep lag are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).
A 5 MiB upload completes within 20 s on a 2 Mbit/s link and server handling of each 64 KiB chunk stays under budget.
Sweeps keep storage within quota and their lag is observable.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command input and output and event payloads against the schema registry.
The metadata stripping pipeline is covered by fixture images carrying every known metadata container.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains attachment metadata and the ciphertext they hold locally, and the key remains only inside the exported encrypted messages.
Import validates sizes, hashes and thread existence; rows whose blob is missing or fails the hash are kept as expired history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; a new chunk size is introduced as a new field value while v1 chunk size 65 536 stays readable.

A Message is a vault record holding plaintext, the signed envelope (nonce, ciphertext, key commitment, signature), the per-recipient wrapped keys, the per-device author chain position (senderDeviceId, seq, prev), the cid of the exact signed envelope and the per-recipient delivery rows, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001; plaintext never leaves the vault except inside the encrypted envelope.

Cryptographic construction is fixed for v1 as a random 32-byte message key K encrypting padded plaintext with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (additional data thread ID, message ID, sender device ID), a key commitment HMAC-SHA256(K, 'classrup.comms.msg.commit.v1' || messageId) inside the signed statement, and K wrapped per recipient device by x25519 ECDH with a fresh ephemeral key against the agreement key that F16.S02.M01 agreementPublicKeyOf derives from that device's Ed25519 key listed active in the recipient's root-signed portable identity document (F07.S02.M01), never against an agreement key from a relay hint, then HKDF-SHA256 and XChaCha20-Poly1305, using @noble/curves and @noble/ciphers 2.4.0.

Messages are P2; the relay stores only a MailboxEnvelope (the sealed wrapper plus relay bookkeeping, no sender identifier) under RET-SHORT for at most 30 days, while vault Messages follow RET-STANDARD under the user's control.
Timestamps from other parties are claims; the vault stores the sender's createdAt as a claim, its own receivedAt, and the relay-signed receipt time as evidence of that relay's clock only.

Delivery is tracked per recipient: each Message holds one delivery row {recipientDid, mailboxId, relayId, outboxEntryId, syncState, relayReceipt, receiptCid} per recipient mailbox; the message-level state is the minimum across rows shown with 'k of n acknowledged', and a row reaches peer_accepted only with a receipt whose messageCid equals the cid of the exact signed envelope.

A relay mailbox is a resource of this module: comms.mailbox.register creates it for an owner DID with the owner's registered device key IDs, an optional push target and an optional list of salted hashes of contacts' request keys (learned from the senderRequestKey inside wrappers from accepted contacts), comms.mailbox.rotate replaces keys, contact hashes or the mailbox ID, and comms.mailbox.close ends it; the relay keeps these rows in its comms_mailbox table and accepts a put only with an RFC 9421 request signature by a request key, never learning the sender DID.

Sealed sender: every participant envelope put into a mailbox - this module's message, receipt and delete statements and every statement F11.S02.M01 hands to the MailboxPort, including F10.S01.M04 deletion notices - travels as the wrapper {v: 1, mailboxId, ciphertext, size, sentAt}, where ciphertext is XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a fresh wrapper key over {envelope, senderRequestKey} padded to 256-byte buckets, prefixed by that wrapper key wrapped for each recipient device by x25519 to the agreement key derived as in 01.R02 (these derived device keys are the only mailbox keys; a mailbox has no key of its own); the put is signed with the sender's request key for that relay - an Ed25519 key pair the vault generates per principal and relay, encoded as did:key in keyid, never listed in an identity document and used for nothing but puts to that relay - so the relay learns no author, type, seq, message ID or sender DID; a wrapper is sealed once per delivery row and its exact bytes are reused by every retry and resend of that row, so the relay deduplicates it on (mailboxId, digest).

The vault keeps one row per own mailbox {relayId, mailboxId, status: active|forwarding|closed, registeredAt, rotateAt, previousMailboxId?, forwardUntil?} plus its request key per relay; mailbox IDs differ at every relay and are rotated every 30 days per relay (comms.mailbox.rotate with newMailboxId and 14 forward days) to limit cross-relay and cross-period linkability (PT-15), and the in-process vault query comms.mailbox.list_own returns the current active pairs {relayId, mailboxId} that F01.S01.M03 puts into listing projections as mailboxHints 1..3 (N15).
Envelope input is validated strictly against the schema in the vault before signing and again by the receiving vault; sizes, lengths and encodings are checked before any decryption.
Relay mailbox commands validate size, quota and request signatures without reading ciphertext.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Inbound acceptance runs the key commitment check, the per-device chain check and the counterparty key status check (F16.S02.M02 security.keyrecord.get_status with its freshness) before a message becomes active.

Limits enforced in the sender's own vault are UX guards that a modified client can skip; the limits that bound abuse are enforced where an attacker cannot skip them, at the relay (RFC 9421 put signatures, tenant limits, per-mailbox and per-key quotas through RateLimitPort and the F12.S03.M04 limits check, N18) and in the receiving vault (caps on pending message requests).

Blocks and thread archives filter only classrup.comms.message/v1 chat envelopes: sealed wrappers carrying any other statement are fetched, acknowledged and handed to F11.S01.M02 ingestion whatever the block or thread state, so lifecycle statements and evidence for a context confirmed before a block (N7a, for example a rental) keep flowing and only notifications are suppressed.

A relay accepts a put only after, in this order, F11.S01.M03 verifyRequest of the RFC 9421 signature (@method, @target-uri, content-digest of the put body, created, keyid, nonce), the wrapper shape check, the tenant limits from TenantPort.limits(tenantId), RateLimitPort.consume per mailbox and request key and per mailbox for unknown keys, and - when that request key has never put to that mailbox on this relay - RateLimitPort.consume class write.mailbox.new_recipient and the F12.S03.M04 check with limitKey new_mailbox_recipients_per_day; the relay never knows the sender DID, so the request key stands for the sender in every relay limit.

Each outbound delivery row advances only forward through prepared, transport acknowledged and peer accepted, becomes failed or expired exactly when its F15.S01.M01 outbox entry does (failed after 6 attempts or a non-retryable refusal, expired 7 days after creation while unsent), and the message-level state is the minimum across rows; the UI shows exactly the reached state with 'k of n acknowledged'.
An inbound Message is created pending_verification and becomes active or quarantined; it can only be deleted afterwards and deleted is terminal and irreversible.
Receipts never change message state other than peer accepted of their own delivery row; they are separate append-only rows.

Every transition into deleted emits comms.message.deleted, with reason author for an author delete in any outbound state (local committed, prepared, failed, transport acknowledged or peer accepted), so referenced attachment blobs are cleaned up whatever the delivery state.

The vault exposes send, resend, delete and acknowledge commands that produce signed statements and the local read queries list_thread and list_own; the relay exposes the mailbox commands register, rotate, close, put, fetch and ack, and this module is the single owner of recipient mailboxes that F11.S02.M01 delivery and other modules use through the MailboxPort.
Each state-changing vault command emits its event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-8) and each relay command is atomic in the relay SQLite store.

The module consumes thread, counterparty key (identity.portable_doc.published with origin received), own device key (identity.device_key.*, the local principal only), block and deletion events to keep recipient sets and inbound filtering correct.

Statement schemas and signer roles are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.message/v1 (a device key of a thread participant), classrup.comms.message_delete/v1 (a device key of the message author), classrup.comms.message_receipt/v1 (a device key of the recipient, bound to messageCid) and classrup.comms.mailbox_close/v1 { mailboxId, relayId, requestId, signedAt, nonce } (a device key registered for the mailbox; the pre-signed close of the deletion sign step); relay mailbox requests are RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures of F11.S01.M03 with the request-signature tag classrup/relay-request/v1, not F16.S02.M03 envelopes.

Every accepted mailbox put calls the relay hook notify.notification.dispatch (F13.S02.M01) for a content-free wake of the mailbox owner when the owner registered a push target (N17); the hook carries only the owner DID, channel push, category activity, template notify.tpl.activity.wake and hookSource mailbox, the relay gate checks only the registered F13 channel consent because privacy.consent.check runs in the vault only, and the hook is bound at relay composition through the MailboxArrivalHook port because F13 modules already depend on this module.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.messages), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6a); in the F10.S01.M04 sign step, before revoke_keys and destroy_keys, DeletionPort signs delete requests for the user's sent messages and a classrup.comms.mailbox_close/v1 for every own mailbox and queues them, the purge step tombstones local messages, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only on which nothing is signed and no relay is called.

The module implements the F11.S02.M01 MailboxPort {put, fetch, ack}, bound at vault composition because F11.S02.M01 cannot depend on this module: MailboxPort.put({ relayId, mailboxId, recipientDid, envelope }) seals the envelope into the wrapper per 01.R07, signs the put with the request key for that relay and returns { envelopeId, receipt } after verifying the receipt; MailboxPort.fetch(mailboxId) returns the unsealed envelopes of the user's own mailbox and MailboxPort.ack acknowledges them only after F11.S01.M02 receive committed each one; F11.S01.M02 routes classrup.comms.message/v1, message_receipt/v1 and message_delete/v1 to this module as their ingest owner and every other statement, including classrup.privacy.deletion_notice/v1, to its own owner.

Every accepted put, a duplicate included, returns in its response field receipt a classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 from F15.S02.M01 ReceiptPort.issue with destination '<relayId>/mailbox/<mailboxId>', digest = sha256-<base64url> of the ciphertext bytes and no cid; the vault verifies it against the relay's published key set, retired keys included, before a delivery row reaches transport acknowledged.

Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal send, resend, delete or acknowledge in threads where it is a participant; inbound statements are accepted only when signed by a key authorized for the sender role in the thread.

Relay policy lets a sender put a sealed wrapper only with an RFC 9421 request signature by a request key within the per-mailbox, per-key, new-recipient and tenant limits, without learning the sender DID; only a device key registered for the mailbox, or its pre-signed close statement, can fetch, acknowledge, rotate or close it; moderators of a relay cannot read ciphertext and may only remove envelopes under that relay's hosting policy.
Non-participants and relay operators learn nothing beyond routing metadata; unknown mailbox IDs return NOT_FOUND to prevent enumeration.
Vault commands commit locally first and relay delivery is a retried outbox step; mailbox put is idempotent on (mailboxId, digest of the ciphertext) so replays return the original receipt.
Inbound processing is idempotent on messageId and fetch followed by acknowledge is at-least-once; a lost acknowledgement only causes a duplicate fetch.

Offline vaults queue sends and replay them in creation order; the author chain is per device, so devices of one principal sending offline never collide, no shared counter or distributed lock is used, and only one device signing two different envelopes for one seq is a fork that is frozen.

A resend reuses the identical signed envelope bytes and messageCid; only wrappedKeys, which lie outside the signature, may be rebuilt, so a resend after a lost relay receipt is deduplicated by every mailbox and every recipient vault.

Deletion residue stays deliverable after the device keys are destroyed - every queued statement is already signed in the sign step, the per-relay request keys that authorize puts stay in the F10 residue store until residue delivery ends 30 days after signing, and each mailbox close is the pre-signed classrup.comms.mailbox_close/v1 that the relay accepts for 30 days.
The relay stores ciphertext and routing metadata only; plaintext, message keys and private keys never leave vaults, and relay logs never contain blobs or plaintext.

Honest limits are shown to users and documented, namely no forward secrecy in the MVP, the relay sees recipient mailbox IDs, times, padded sizes and the per-relay request key of each put (which links puts by one sender on that relay, not to a DID), and a stolen unlocked device exposes its history.

Abuse handling works without relay decryption through local blocking, receiver-side caps on message requests, relay-enforced request signatures with per-mailbox, per-key and new-recipient quotas, and user-initiated reports that carry plaintext and the message key from the reporter's vault so the reviewer can check the key commitment; limits enforced only in the sender's vault are UX guards.

Privacy duties (N6, N6a): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered with F10, and the DeletionPort sign step signs remote delete requests and the closes of the user's mailboxes before any key is destroyed.

Sealed sender and linkability limits (PRV-5, PT-15): stored wrappers carry no sender identifier, the relay keeps request-key first-put rows for 30 days only for the new-recipient limit, request keys differ per relay, and own mailbox IDs differ per relay and rotate every 30 days; the residual linkability of one did:key per principal is disclosed.
Relay mailbox commands are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without logging beyond correlationId and sizes; the PWA records only local diagnostics (OBS-7).
Mailbox put meets the write budget p95 ≤ 300 ms at 100 puts per second and fetch of 100 envelopes meets p95 ≤ 150 ms.
Vault encrypt-and-sign meets a device budget and the relay expiry sweep lag is bounded.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests verify that vault and relay command inputs, outputs, statements and event payloads validate against schema registry entries.
Cryptographic round trips use fixed known-answer vectors plus property tests.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains their messages with plaintext inside the export file protected by the user's chosen export encryption, and the matching signed envelopes.
Import validates envelope structure and signatures; messages whose signature fails are kept quarantined and messages not addressed to the importer's devices are kept as undecryptable history.

Schema changes follow expand and contract; the alg field allows adding algorithms without breaking v1 readers, and relays only ever hold 30 days of ciphertext so relay loss loses no user-owned records.
A Thread is a vault record storing its context type and ID, a participant roster of DIDs with roles and mute state, status and tenant plus revision per CTR-ID-001; there is no relay copy.
Threads are P2 and visible only to participants; retention is RET-STANDARD and archived threads are purged locally 30 days after archive together with their messages unless the user keeps them.
Participant timestamps in a received thread-open statement are claims; the vault stores its own receivedAt separately.
The context binding is immutable after creation; a different context needs a new thread.

The threadId is derived, never random: UUIDv8 from the first 122 bits of SHA-256('classrup.comms.thread.v1' || 0x00 || JCS([contextTenantId, contextType, contextId, sortedPair, generation])), where contextTenantId is the tenantId named in the context's signed statement, sortedPair is present only for one-to-one contexts (listing, proposal, direct) and generation starts at 1 and increases only when a new thread replaces a locally archived one with the same key.

Thread creation and inbound thread-open statements are validated against the context record through the context owner's ThreadContextPort, the per-context entitlement table and the local principal's own block list before persistence.
Roster changes are validated against the participant cap and the owning context's own membership.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Limits enforced only in the creator's vault are UX guards; receiving vaults enforce their own caps on pending message requests (5 per unknown DID, 100 in total), so a modified client cannot flood an inbox.
A Thread is active, or in request until the local user accepts it, until archived; archived is terminal and a new conversation after an archive is a new thread of the next generation.

Archival happens by context closure, the local principal's own block, idle timeout of 90 days, manual action by the local user in one-to-one threads, a declined request, a newer generation (superseded), the verified departure of the other party of a two-party thread, or the local user's account deletion.
Archiving emits comms.thread.archived once and triggers the message purge schedule in F08.S01.M01.

Superseding happens only when a newer generation replaces a thread that one vault had archived; messages in flight for the older threadId are re-homed into the newer thread for 7 days instead of being dropped, and concurrent creates never supersede because they derive the same threadId.
All commands are vault-local; create additionally produces the signed statement classrup.comms.thread_open/v1, and archive, mute, accept_request and decline_request never leave the device.
Roster changes made from context events are internal and are not a public command; they emit no extra events.
The module consumes context, block and identity events and applies verified classrup.privacy.deletion_notice/v1 statements to keep threads consistent.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.thread_open/v1 { threadId, contextTenantId, contextType, contextId?, generation, participants[] } signed by a device key of createdBy; the module verifies classrup.privacy.deletion_notice/v1 owned by F10.S01.M04 (signer role principal: the envelope author is the departing DID per CTR-FED-001 FED-7 and ext.signerKey one of its device keys; the departure payload is exactly { requestId, signedAt, kind: departure, effectiveAt, recourse: none } and never repeats the DID), reads the departing DID only from the envelope author and applies a departure notice to every local thread in which that DID has an entry with leftAt unset, setting leftAt to the local receipt time and departedByNotice to the notice cid; a notice of kind commitment changes no thread.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.threads), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize) and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6); DeletionPort.plan lists the counterparties of the local user's threads as noticeRecipients [{ did, mailboxId, relayId }] so F10.S01.M04 seals its single departure notice to each, DeletionPort.execute archives the user's threads with reason account_deleted and purges rosters while the keys still exist, and the module does not consume privacy.deletion.completed.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal create, mute or archive its own threads, and only with parties it has not itself blocked.

Inbound thread-open statements are accepted only when signed by a key entitled for the context role per the entitlement table; unknown but entitled senders become message requests and others are quarantined with a reason.
Group threads (cycle, booking, rental) are archived only by context events; participants may only mute or leave through the context module. No relay or global role can read or alter a thread.

Create is idempotent on the derived threadId, so a retry or a concurrent create on another vault returns the same thread with existing true; the signed thread-open statement is queued through F11.S02.M01 on the F15.S01.M01 outbox and goes through prepared, transport acknowledged and peer accepted.
Roster updates from events are idempotent through the consumer inbox (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-3) and order-insensitive.
Archiving and message purge scheduling happen in one IndexedDB transaction so a thread is never archived without a purge schedule.
Thread membership exists only in vaults; the relay sees only per-message sender DID and recipient mailbox (F08.S01.M01), and this is disclosed.
Archived threads and their messages are purged locally 30 days after archive and on vault wipe.

Block enforcement uses only the local principal's own block list and never reveals to the blocked party that a block exists; the blocked party's vault state and responses are identical to the unblocked case.

Privacy duties (N6): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered, and a remote participant's departure is applied only from a verified deletion notice.
The PWA records only local diagnostics (OBS-7); no telemetry leaves the device.
Create and archive meet a vault budget of p95 ≤ 50 ms and inbox list meets p95 ≤ 100 ms for 50 threads on a mid-range phone.
Roster consumer lag is visible in local diagnostics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command input and output and event payloads against the schema registry.
Roster consistency is covered by deterministic event replay tests.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains the threads they participate in with roster, thread-open statements and own mute settings.
Import validates thread IDs against their derivation, schema version and thread-open signatures; threads with invalid signatures become quarantined read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A ConsentStatement stores exactly the signed fields v, type, tenantId, signerDid, signerKeyId, subjectType, subjectRef, subjectRevision, subjectRevisionHash (CTR-ID-001 ID-3 cid form sha256-<base64url>), statementKey, statementLocale, statementTextHash, kind, revokes? and signedAtClaim, plus the signature envelope, provenance with first-seen time and the derived status, with revision per CTR-ID-001.

The signed bytes are those of the F16.S02.M03 envelope classrup.security.envelope/v1 - the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the header {v, ctx, kid, alg, signedAt, payloadHash} with ctx classrup/consent/v1, kid the signer key ID and payloadHash = sha256-<base64url>(SHA-256(JCS(signed field set))) - signed hash-only with the signed field set stored beside the envelope as its payload, so a consent signature can never validate as another statement type, and the regenerated known-answer vectors publish these exact header bytes and payload hashes.
ConsentStatements are P2 evidence kept under RET-EVIDENCE, are immutable after storage apart from the derived status, and carry provenance for statements received from other vaults.

id is the CTR-ID-001 ID-3 cid of the JCS bytes of the signed fields and envelope; among non-revoked records with the same dedupe tuple (signerDid, subjectRef, subjectRevisionHash, statementKey, kind) every vault keeps the lexicographically lowest cid as the record and stores the others as aliases.

The v1 statement key registry ships these keys, each with consent wording per locale (plus decline wording where the owner signs declines), its subjectType, subjectRef kind, the signer role SubjectCanonicalizerPort.partyRole must return and the owner whose registered port canonicalizes the subject - consent.bazaar.offer.accept.v1 (bazaar_offer, offerId, listing author; F01.S04.M01, JCS of the offer statement); consent.bazaar.negotiation.accept.v1 (bazaar_negotiation, negotiationId, the accepting buyer or seller; F01.S04.M02, JCS of the round statement); consent.mutiny.proposal.accept.v1 (mutiny_proposal, proposal subjectId, party) and consent.mutiny.cycle.commit.v1 (mutiny_cycle, cycle subjectId, participant), both with decline wording and canonicalized by F02.S01.M04 canonicalBytes, so subjectRevisionHash equals that revision's contentHash cid; consent.services.booking.accept.v1 (services_booking, quoteId, client), consent.services.booking.cancel.v1 with decline wording and consent.services.booking.resume.v1 (services_booking, bookingId, client or provider; F03.S02.M01); consent.rentals.reservation.request.v1 (rentals_reservation, reservationId, renter) and consent.rentals.reservation.confirm.v1 (rentals_reservation, reservationId, owner; F05.S01.M01); consent.rentals.deposit.agree.v1 (rentals_deposit, depositId, renter; F05.S01.M02), whose registered wording states that the owner, not ClassRup, holds the deposit; consent.comms.meetup.agree.v1 (comms_meetup, meetupId, party; F08.S03.M03).
Signing validates the subject through its SubjectCanonicalizerPort (current revision, the signer's role, commit state), the wording and the hash before any signature is made.
Inbound statements are validated for structure, signature, key status, role and hash before storage as valid.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

The commit guard V07 applies only to the local comms.consent.revoke command; inbound revocations are always stored, and verify returns conflicted when the owning module has already committed, so the parties freeze for renegotiation instead of diverging silently.

Validity after a device-key revocation follows one rule: first-seen time is provenance.verifiedAt recorded at the first successful verification, kept through export and import in the signed manifest and never taken from signedAtClaim; a statement first seen after the key's revocationEffectiveFrom is rejected.

Each owning module registers a SubjectCanonicalizerPort for its subjectType; signing and verification for a subjectType without a registered port are refused, and the shared conformance suite checks every registered port.

Each ConsentStatement follows one machine - quarantined until verified, then valid; a valid consent becomes revoked by a verified revocation of the same signer; revoked and erased are terminal; decline and revocation records take status valid when verified and are never revoked themselves; a re-consent after revocation is a new record.
Quarantined statements become valid when the missing subject, key or wording arrives and verification succeeds, or are erased after 7 days.

Conflicts between consent and decline, or between a consent and a revocation that arrived after the owning module committed, for one subject hash are reported by verify as conflicted and are never resolved by comparing claimed times.
The vault commands sign and revoke produce signed statements and are called by owning modules or the UI; accept is a vault command invoked by the transport layer for inbound statements.
Each command emits its event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the stored record (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-8).

Verify and list are pure vault queries with no side effects; verify resolves by the dedupe tuple and its result for consent plus revocation is defined in one table - valid (verified consent, no stored decline or revocation), stale (subjectRevisionHash differs from the current revision), revoked (revocation stored while the subject is not committed), conflicted (consent and decline, a revocation stored after the owning module committed, or a peer-reported invalidity), missing (no record).

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.consent/v1 with kind consent, decline or revocation, signer role = the role the statement key requires per SubjectCanonicalizerPort.partyRole, signed through F16.S02.M03 with context classrup/consent/v1; owning modules echo every received consent statement to all participants before they commit.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.consents, including firstSeenAt in the signed manifest), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize - kept consents get signerDid replaced by the deletion pseudonym when keepEvidence is true and are purged otherwise) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE) with F10 (N6).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal sign or revoke, and only as a party of the subject; the private key never leaves the device or the platform key store.

Inbound statements are accepted only when signed by a key that F16.S02.M02 reports active for the signer at first-seen time and the signer holds the role required by the statement key in the subject; others are quarantined with a reason.
Verify and list are local reads with no network access; relays hold no consent data except as opaque encrypted envelopes and cannot create or alter a consent.
Signing is idempotent on the content address, so signing the same payload again returns the stored statement unchanged.
Inbound acceptance is idempotent on cid and order-insensitive with subject, key and wording arrival.
There is no distributed lock; conflicting statements are stored side by side, flagged conflicted, and handled by explicit renegotiation in the owning module.

Duplicate resolution is deterministic - every vault keeps the lowest cid of a dedupe tuple and stores the others as aliases, and a revocation that targets the tuple revokes every matching cid - so references and revocations resolve the same way in every vault.
Consents are P2 evidence; they contain DIDs, hashes and wording keys, never the subject content, so sending them reveals only that a key holder agreed to a hash.
Retention is RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last related activity) and deletion of a vault does not delete copies held by counterparties, which the UI states before signing.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity because the signer DID is linkable across statements, and the sign sheet says so.

Privacy duties (N6): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered, and on principal deletion kept consents are pseudonymized (signerDid replaced by the deletion pseudonym) instead of erased, unless the user chose not to keep evidence.
The PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7) with counters for signed, accepted, quarantined and rejected statements, and no statement content is logged.
Signing including canonicalization meets a vault budget of p95 ≤ 100 ms and verification p95 ≤ 20 ms on a mid-range phone.
Verification of 1 000 stored statements completes within 5 s.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.

Contract tests verify signed statements, command inputs and outputs and events against the schema registry, using fixed known-answer vectors for JCS and Ed25519 under the classrup/consent/v1 envelope.
Owning modules reuse a shared conformance suite that exercises sign and verify against their own SubjectCanonicalizerPort.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains all consent statements they signed or received with provenance and first-seen time.

Import re-verifies every statement against keys and subjects present in the target vault using the firstSeenAt carried in the signed export manifest, never the import time, and quarantines those that cannot be verified.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; the signed payload field set is frozen in v1 and any change creates classrup.comms.consent/v2 with v1 readable for 180 days.
A ThreadOfferCard stores the thread, kind, referenced record ID, pinned revision cid, poster DID, an optional poster note, and a derived display state, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

The card is a P2 view held only in vaults; it carries a reference and an optional poster note of at most 280 characters that never holds money or item fields, amounts, items and terms are rendered in each receiving vault from the verified pinned revision through the owning module's renderer, and the owning module stays the single source of truth.
The pinned revision hash is the CTR-ID-001 ID-3 cid (sha256-<base64url> of the JCS bytes) of the referenced statement revision and is immutable after posting.
Posting validates the thread, the poster's party role and the referenced revision before the card statement is signed.
Inbound cards are validated for signature, key status, role and hash match before display state posted is assigned.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

A card posted locally starts posted and an inbound card starts waiting; cards move to superseded, closed, frozen or unverified; superseded, closed and unverified are terminal for display, and a posted card becomes unverified when its referenced record disappears or a later re-verification fails.
Closing follows only verified terminal events of the owning module and never the card poster's own claim.
A waiting card that gets no matching record within 7 days becomes unverified and is not retried automatically.

Supersession never follows an unverified card - only a newer card that reached posted, or an owning-module revision event, supersedes - and withdrawn proposals close their cards while forked revisions freeze them until the owning module resolves the fork.
Posting is a vault command that produces a signed statement and delegates delivery to comms.message.send as a typed item; reading is a vault query.
Posting emits comms.offer_card.posted in the same IndexedDB transaction as the local card record, and inbound verification emits the same event with actor kind federated.

The module consumes owning-module events derived from verified statements to update card state, and looks up the root offer of a counter through bazaar.negotiation.get (F01.S04.M02) because the countered event does not carry it.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.offer_card/v1 { threadId, kind, refId, refRevision, refRevisionHash, posterNote? } signed by a device key of a party of the referenced record.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.offer_cards), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize) and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6); cards are purged with their thread and carry no evidence of their own.
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal post cards, and only for records where it is a party and in threads where it participates.
Inbound cards are accepted only when signed by an active key of a party of the referenced record; other signers lead to the unverified state.
Cards have no relay-side resource; relays only carry the encrypted message and hold no card data.
Posting is idempotent on (threadId, refId, refRevision) so a retry returns the existing card.
Inbound cards are deduplicated on statement cid and reprocessed safely when the referenced statement arrives later.
The card record and its signed statement are written in one IndexedDB transaction; delivery follows the per-recipient message sync states of F08.S01.M01.
Cards are P2 and travel only inside end-to-end encrypted messages; relays never see card content or amounts.
Cards never include P3 data such as exact addresses and never include payment instructions.

Spoofed cards are contained by signature, key status and role verification, unverified cards expose no actions, and every amount, item and term is rendered from the verified referenced revision, so a poster cannot show a different amount than the signed record.
Privacy duties (N6): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02 and ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered with F10.
The PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7) with counters for posted, verified and unverified cards.
Posting and state updates meet the vault budget of p95 ≤ 50 ms on a mid-range phone.
Rendering a thread with 50 cards meets p95 ≤ 100 ms.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command input and output, the signed statement and event payload against the schema registry.
Role and hash verification are covered by adversarial fixtures.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains the cards of their threads including card statements and display state.
Import re-verifies card statements and references; cards whose referenced record is missing become unverified read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days; new card kinds are additive enum values.

A Meetup stores the thread, context reference, parties, the current proposal revision (window start and end in UTC, venue snapshot with the spot statement cid), the reschedule count, the agreement statement IDs, and status, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Meetups are P2 and held only in participating vaults; the place is either a SafeSpot snapshot matched to a curator-verified spot statement (public P0 data at L2) or an L3 area label, and exact home addresses (P3) and live locations are never stored or accepted.

The proposal revision hash is the CTR-ID-001 ID-3 cid (sha256-<base64url> of the JCS bytes of the proposal payload), and agreement is a ConsentStatement with statement key consent.comms.meetup.agree.v1 and subjectType comms_meetup on that hash, signed by every party including the proposer.

Signed proposal and cancellation statements are evidence under RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last related activity), kept independently of the thread purge so the agreement consents can still be re-verified against the subject bytes, and pseudonymized on principal deletion.

The module registers the F08.S02.M02 SubjectCanonicalizerPort for subjectType comms_meetup - canonicalBytes(meetupId, rev) returns the JCS bytes of that proposal revision, currentRevision the proposalRevision, partyRole party for every partyDid, and isCommitted true only once the local clock passed windowStart of the agreed revision - so an agreed meetup is not committed and its consents may be revoked until windowStart.
Proposals are validated for time window, place and party rules before signing and again on receipt.
Agreement is accepted only through verified consent statements on the current proposal hash.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

The house-number check applies to the free-text areaLabel only; a safe-spot snapshot is validated by matching it to a curator-verified SafeSpot statement in the local cache (same spot id, version, statement cid and signature).
Block checks use only the local principal's own blocks; statements from DIDs it blocked are dropped silently, and a party blocked by someone else sees no difference in its own vault.
A meetup starts proposed; reschedule creates a new proposal revision, clears prior agreements and stays proposed until every party agreed.

Agreed is computed only from verified consent statements of every party, the proposer included, for the current hash; a reschedule or a verified revocation of an agreement before windowStart moves an agreed meetup back to proposed.

Cancelled, expired and elapsed are terminal; conflicted ends by a new proposal revision higher than every competing one, by a cancellation, or by expiry once the local clock passes the windowStart of every competing proposal.

Propose and reschedule sign the proposer's own consent.comms.meetup.agree.v1 consent in the same transaction, so the agreement evidence is uniform for every party; agreed is not a commit, and consents may be revoked until windowStart (SubjectCanonicalizerPort.isCommitted).
