A conflict is any two distinct valid proposals with the same proposalRevision and different proposalHash, whoever proposed them, and it freezes the meetup for explicit renegotiation.

All commands are vault commands; propose and reschedule produce the signed proposal statement together with the proposer's agreement consent, and agree uses comms.consent.sign, so nothing is a relay command.
Each command emits its event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change, and inbound verified statements derive the same events with actor kind federated.
The module consumes thread, block, context and consent events to keep meetups consistent.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.meetup/v1 { meetupId, threadId, proposalRevision, window, place with spotCid, partyDids } and classrup.comms.meetup_cancel/v1 { meetupId, reason }, each signed by a device key of a party; agreements are classrup.comms.consent/v1 statements of F08.S02.M02.
Event payloads carry the party DIDs needed for notification routing (N4) - comms.meetup.proposed, comms.meetup.agreed and comms.meetup.cancelled all include partyDids.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.meetups with the signed proposal statements), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize - proposal and cancellation statements kept as evidence get the deleted party's DID replaced by the deletion pseudonym) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE, independent of the thread purge) with F10 (N6).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal propose, agree, reschedule or cancel, and only as a party of the meetup.
Inbound proposals and cancellations are accepted only when signed by an active key of a party of the meetup (F16.S02.M02); others are quarantined.
Relays hold no meetup data beyond encrypted envelopes; no relay or global role can change a meetup.

All commands commit locally first; statements travel through F11.S02.M01 on the F15.S01.M01 outbox with states prepared, transport acknowledged and peer accepted, and the UI shows only the reached state.
Statement handling is idempotent on statement cid and agreements are idempotent on (partyDid, proposalHash).
Conflicting proposals are frozen for explicit renegotiation; no distributed lock and no last-writer-wins is used.
Meetups carry only a time window and a public place or an L3 area label; exact home addresses and live locations are never accepted, and the area-label validator rejects address patterns.
Meetup data travels only inside end-to-end encrypted messages to the listed parties; relays see routing metadata only.
The module reduces risk but cannot guarantee safety; the UI repeats the checklist from F08.S03.M01 before the first proposal or agreement.

Signed proposal and cancellation statements are RET-EVIDENCE and survive the thread purge (CTR-PRV-001, FLOW-08), so agreement consents stay re-verifiable; privacy duties (N6) - field classification per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort, RetentionPurgePort and pseudonymization on deletion - apply.
The PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7) with counters for proposals, agreements, reschedules, conflicts and cancellations.
Vault commands meet p95 ≤ 50 ms on a mid-range phone and a thread with 20 meetups renders in p95 ≤ 100 ms.
The expiry sweep processes 1 000 meetups in ≤ 1 s.

A user's vault export contains their meetups, proposal statements and the agreement references.
Import re-verifies proposal and consent signatures; failures are quarantined and meetups with passed windows import as elapsed.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A MeetupCheckin stores, per meetup and party, the status, the claimed check-in time, the local receive time, the signed check-in statement ID and, whenever a verified no-show report about that party exists, the reporter, the report statement and the contradicted flag, whatever the status, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001; no coordinates and no device identifiers are stored.
Check-in times from other parties are claims; the vault stores its own receivedAt and, if a relay receipt exists, the relay-signed time as evidence of that relay's clock only.

A MeetupShare is a P3 record on the owner's device only (relay ID, share ID, expiry, revoked flag and the hash of the share key, never the key); the relay holds a separate opaque share blob row (shareId, ciphertext of at most 2 KiB, expiresAt, creator key ID) under RET-EPHEMERAL that carries no P3 field.

Signed check-in and no-show statements are evidence under RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last related activity), kept independently of the thread purge so they and the meetup agreement consents stay re-verifiable, and pseudonymized on principal deletion (N6).
The share snapshot contains only the owner's own check-in state, the place label and the window; it never contains the counterparty's check-in state, names, DIDs, phone numbers or coordinates.
Check-in, no-show and share inputs are validated against meetup state and time windows on the local clock before any statement is signed.
Inbound check-in and report statements are validated for signature, key status, party role and proposal hash.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Limits enforced only in the reporter's vault are UX guards; receiving vaults keep at most 3 no-show reports per meetup and reporter, and statements from DIDs the local principal blocked are dropped silently (N7).

Each MeetupCheckin starts pending and ends in exactly one of checked_in, no_show or void, which are terminal; a no-show report about a party that already checked in, or a check-in arriving after a report, sets the report fields and the contradicted flag without a state change.

A MeetupShare is active until it expires or is revoked; both end states are terminal, delete the relay blob through comms.meetup_share.delete and emit comms.meetup_share.revoked with reason owner, cancelled, rescheduled or expired.
Check-in states advance only from verified statements and never from timers alone, except void for elapsed windows.

When contradicted becomes true after comms.meetup.no_show was emitted without it, comms.meetup.no_show_contradicted is emitted in the same transaction so consumers that weighed the claim (F12.S03.M02) can reverse it; a report that is contradicted on arrival emits comms.meetup.no_show with contradicted true.

Check-in and no-show report are vault commands that produce signed statements; share creation and revocation are vault commands that call the relay commands comms.meetup_share.put and comms.meetup_share.delete for the share blob, and view is a public relay query returning ciphertext only.
Each state-changing vault command emits its event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the change.
The module consumes meetup agreement, reschedule and cancellation events to create and void check-in records.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.checkin/v1 { meetupId, proposalHash, partyDid, checkedInAtClaim } signed by a device key of that party, and classrup.comms.no_show_report/v1 { meetupId, proposalHash, targetDid, reportedAtClaim } signed by a device key of a checked-in party; share blob requests are RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures of F11.S01.M03 with the request-signature tag classrup/relay-request/v1, not F16.S02.M03 envelopes.

The trusted-contact viewer is served from the app's static, integrity-pinned PWA origin with relay ID, share ID and key in the URL fragment; the relay answers comms.meetup_share.view with ciphertext only, under a CORS allowance for the app origin, and never serves viewer code.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.checkins), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize - kept check-in and report evidence gets the deleted party's DID replaced by the deletion pseudonym, share blobs are deleted while the keys exist) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE independent of the thread purge, shares RET-EPHEMERAL) with F10 (N6).
Vault policy lets only the unlocked local principal check in as itself, report no-show about another party, and create or revoke its own shares.

Relay policy lets only the device key that created a share put, update or delete its blob, while view is open to anyone holding the unguessable share ID but returns ciphertext only and serves no viewer code.
Inbound check-in and no-show statements are accepted only when signed by an active key of a party of the meetup.

Check-in and report commands commit locally first and statements travel through F11.S02.M01 on the F15.S01.M01 outbox with states prepared, transport acknowledged and peer accepted; the UI shows exactly the reached state.
Statement handling is idempotent on cid; share put is idempotent on (shareId, snapshotRevision) and share delete and revoke are idempotent on shareId.
There is no distributed lock; a no-show claim and a check-in from the accused are both kept and flagged contradicted, whichever arrives first.
Check-in never reads or records location; the signature only evidences that a key holder asserted arrival at a time they claim, not that they were at the place.

Trusted-contact links are user-initiated, expire in at most 24 hours and show only the owner's own check-in state, the place label and the window; they are encrypted with a key in the URL fragment, the viewer code comes from the app's integrity-pinned origin and not from the relay, so the hosting relay serves only ciphertext; anyone holding the full link can read it, which the UI states.
No-show reports are claims, labelled as the reporter's claim, capped by receivers, and carry no automatic penalties in this module; contradictions are announced to consumers.

Signed check-ins and no-show reports are RET-EVIDENCE (CTR-PRV-001, FLOW-08) kept beyond the thread purge; privacy duties (N6) - field classification per F10.S02.M02, ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort, RetentionPurgePort and pseudonymization on deletion - apply.
Relay share commands are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).
Check-in and report commands meet p95 ≤ 50 ms in the vault; share view meets p95 ≤ 100 ms on the relay.
The relay expiry sweep keeps lag under 5 minutes.

Contract tests verify commands, signed statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
A privacy test asserts that no location data and no share key reach any server.
Screens meet CTR-UX-001 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 44 px targets, explicit async states, polite announcements) and the a11y items listed for this module.
A user's vault export contains their check-in records and statements, and share records without keys.
Import re-verifies statements; records whose meetup is missing become void history and shares always import as expired.
Schema changes follow expand and contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A SafeSpot is a public P0 statement signed by a curator key with venue name, kind, an optional access note without house numbers, opening hours and the L2 region cell (geohash 5) it belongs to; it carries no street address, no cell finer than L2 and never user data, and its cell passes F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell (N8).

Spots belong to exactly one L2 cell and carry a curator DID, the relay that hosts them, a version and a validity range; a vault shows on every spot where its trust comes from - a curator the user pinned, the app starter list, or a curator delegated by relay R through its signed curator list - and the app bundles no trusted curator keys.
Spot statements are retained under RET-STANDARD in relay indexes and vault caches and are replaced when a newer valid version arrives; retired spots keep a tombstone for 180 days.

The relay's curator list is the relay-signed statement classrup.comms.curator_list/v1 owned by this module and changed only by that relay's operators (F16.S01.M01 operator role); vaults pin curator keys per relay on first use and warn when the list changes.
The bundled starter set is unsigned default data labelled app starter list; users and relays can hide or override any entry, and it never grants curator status to anyone.
Curator input is validated strictly before signing and again by every verifying vault and relay.
Suggestion inputs are validated so that no user location can enter the module.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Every cell in a statement, a suggestion input and an event payload passes F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell, so a 6-character cell fails drafting, publishing, verification and the build (N8).

A SafeSpot is drafted and signed in the curator's vault, becomes active when the hosting relay accepts it, and is retired by its curator, by the relay operator or when validUntil passes; retired is terminal and a returning venue is published as a new spot.
Publishing validates and signs in the curator vault; relays and vaults only verify and store.
Retired spots are removed from suggestions immediately in vaults that received the retirement statement and keep a tombstone for 180 days.

Expiry by validUntil is applied in every vault on its own clock, so an expired spot is filtered from suggestions at once even before the relay's retirement arrives, and the relay retires it with reason expired.

Curators draft and sign spots in their vault and publish or retire them through relay commands that accept signed statements; anyone lists spots of an L2 cell and reads the relay's curator list through public relay queries; members report unsuitable spots through a relay command.
Members get suggestions through a vault command that reads only the local cache and emits comms.safe_spot.suggested locally.
The module consumes relay role events so that only current relay operators can change the relay-signed curator list.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.comms.safe_spot/v1 and classrup.comms.safe_spot_retirement/v1 (signer: a curator key listed in the hosting relay's curator list, or the relay key for operator retirements and expiry) and classrup.comms.curator_list/v1 (signer: the relay key, issued only on an operator's request).

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section comms.safe_spots, including checklist progress and local trust settings), DeletionPort (plan, execute, pseudonymize - a curator's published spots keep the curator DID as public evidence until retired) and RetentionPurgePort with F10 (N6).

Relay policy lets only curator keys listed in that relay's signed curator list publish or retire their spots, lets the relay operator retire any spot it hosts with a recorded reason, and lets only operators (F16.S01.M01) change the curator list.
Anyone, including anonymous clients, may read the public spot list and the curator list; no authentication and no location are required.
Vault policy lets the local principal request suggestions, read the checklist and change its own trust settings, and lets a curator draft and sign spots; suggestions never leave the device.
Publish is idempotent on (curatorDid, venueKey, version) and retirement is idempotent on spotId.
Cache refresh failures leave the previous cache in place and are retried with backoff.
Suggestions are computed locally from the cache and are available offline.
No user location is stored, transmitted or logged; the user picks a region cell label and the app reads from its own cache.
Spot data is public P0 and contains only venue information at L2 precision (name, kind, hours, access note and a geohash-5 cell), never a street address; curators must not publish private homes.
The module does not claim safety; the UI states that listing a place is not a guarantee.

Privacy duties (N6): fields are classified per F10.S02.M02, local trust settings and checklist progress are P3 vault data, and ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are registered with F10.
Relay publish, retire, report and list are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).
Public list queries meet p95 ≤ 150 ms for 100 items and the vault suggest meets p95 ≤ 50 ms with 5 000 cached spots.
Cache age, curator-list changes and refresh failures are visible in local diagnostics.

A user's vault export contains the cached spot statements they use, their checklist progress and their local trust settings, and a curator's export contains their drafts and signed spots.
Import re-verifies signatures and curator-list membership; spots from curators not in the hosting relay's list are dropped and counted.

CashTerms stores dealId, obligationId, receiptRequired, handoverHint, proposer, status, the termsCid of the terms it would replace and signed statement cids per CTR-ID-001, in both parties' vaults.
CashTerms are P2 and retained as RET-EVIDENCE because they bound what each party agreed when the claim was made.
acknowledgementRequired is a constant true; the schema has no field that could mark cash as verified.

Exactly one CashTerms row is in force per obligation - the latest accepted one, the defaults until the payer accepts a proposal - and every cash claim signs that row's termsCid through the MethodRulePort.
Terms input is validated strictly; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.
The cash method rule validates allowed methods, jurisdiction limits and term acceptance before a claim is created.
Guidance never blocks a claim; only the listed rules do.

Incoming terms statements are checked by the StatementHandlerPort handler for signer role (payee for terms, payer for accept and decline), the referenced proposal and revision, and blocks, before any state change.

The jurisdiction cash limit is read at every check from governance.jurisdiction_profile.resolve of F18.S01.M01 with the vault's selected ProfileRefs {publisherId, code} (the query default, never a profile id) as effective.cashLimits - Money[] holding the minimum per currency across the selected profiles; the obligation amount is compared only with the entry in its own currency through F09.S03.M03, no FX conversion is made, no limit applies when no entry has that currency, and a rejection records the profileRef and version that sources names for cashLimits.
Default terms enter directly as accepted when the Deal opens; proposals start as proposed and end as accepted, declined, superseded or expired.
A new proposal supersedes an earlier unaccepted proposal; accepted terms stay in force until the payer accepts a newer proposal, and claims keep the termsCid they were made under.
Expiry after 7 days leaves the prior accepted terms in force, and creates default accepted terms in the same transaction only when none exist.

Terms commands are vault commands that produce the signed statements classrup.commerce.cash_terms/v1, classrup.commerce.cash_terms_accept/v1 and classrup.commerce.cash_terms_decline/v1; no relay command exists.
The module emits no domain events (catalog emits is empty); state is observable through queries and the Deal card.
The module consumes Deal, claim and deletion events to create default terms, show safety guidance, prompt cash receipts and pseudonymize retained terms.

Incoming terms statements are ingested through the StatementHandlerPort of F09.S01.M01 - signer role payee for cash_terms and payer for cash_terms_accept and cash_terms_decline - deduplicated by cid, idempotent, and quarantined with a reason (signer_not_payee, signer_not_payer, deal_unknown, proposal_unknown, stale_revision) or dropped silently when the signer is blocked.
The cash MethodRulePort returns the termsCid of the in-force terms, which F09.S01.M01 signs into the cash claim.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal changes its vault; set requires the payee role and accept and decline require the payer role as recorded in the Deal.
Incoming terms statements are accepted only when signed by the obligation payee (terms) or payer (accept, decline); otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role has any capability over cash terms.
All three commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision.
Concurrent proposals from several tabs serialize and the later one supersedes the earlier one.
Statement delivery uses the sync outbox states and the UI never shows terms as agreed before peer_accepted.
Cash terms are P2 and never leave the vault except inside end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the other party.
The handover hint is public-place guidance only; the UI warns against sharing a home address (P3) and rejects hints that match the user's stored private address.
Pressure tactics are limited by the proposal rate limit and by the dispute path.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.cash_terms), DeletionPort (pseudonymization of retained terms) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE) with F10 (N6), annotates every CashTerms field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Ingest drops statements from blocked dids silently (N7) and uses the bounded quarantine of F09.S01.M01 (500 entries or 5 MiB, oldest-first eviction); once it is full, statements from dids that are party to no known Deal are dropped.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters stay in local diagnostics.
Local commit meets the budgets below.
Guidance and limit rejections are counted locally.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs and statement envelopes against the schema registry.
Honest-label behavior is checked in UI tests.
The vault export contains the principal's cash terms with their signed statements in the section commerce.cash_terms.
Import verifies signatures and parties against the imported Deals and quarantines terms whose signer is not a party.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A CryptoPaymentRequest stores deal and obligation refs, payee-supplied address, chain, asset, Money amount in asset minor units, validity and status, and is signed by the payee as classrup.commerce.crypto_request/v1.

A ChainObservation stores the claimed txid, the verifier used, block data, confirmations, finality flag and a match result, and is kept in the vault only; observations are local evidence and not statements about the other party.
Both entities are P2 and retained as RET-EVIDENCE; no field ever holds a private key, seed or signing material.

Each request records the chain tip height (Bitcoin) or block number (EVM) that the payee's verifier reported at creation, signed into the request, and only outputs included above it, or first seen in the mempool after the request was received, count toward the request.

A request covers its obligation amount through one or more claims; coveredAmount sums the matched receivedAmount of final claims, and the request is settled only when coveredAmount reaches the amount.
Request input is validated strictly, including address format and checksum for the chain and the asset registry binding.
Any free-text or reference field is scanned for private key, seed phrase and extended private key patterns and rejected before storage or logging.
Observation results are validated by amount, destination, asset and chain before any state advances.

A raw 64-hex private key has the same format as a txid, so before a crypto claim is signed or sent its txid is looked up through the configured verifier and the claim stays local and unsent until it is found; with no verifier the payer must confirm 'this is a public transaction ID, never a key', and the residual risk that the lookup itself discloses a mistyped key to the chosen verifier is stated in the UI.
An address already used by another open or claimed request in the vault is refused, and a transaction included at or below the request's chainTipAtCreation counts as before_request and never matches.
Requests and observations follow the declared machines; any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
An observation advances only on data from a configured ChainVerifierPort adapter; with none configured no observation is created and the claim stays claimed (COM-5).

A reorg moves a confirmed or pending observation to reorged; a reorged observation returns to pending if the transaction reappears and becomes failed after the grace period (24 h Bitcoin, 6 h EVM) or immediately for a reverted EVM transaction.
Observation stops when the claim reaches a terminal state, the claim expires after 14 days, or the user removes the verifier.

commerce.payment.confirming is emitted only for a transaction whose destination, asset and amount match the request and whose inclusion is above chainTipAtCreation; a transaction that does not match (underpaid, wrong_address, wrong_asset, before_request) or reverts moves the observation to mismatched or failed and emits commerce.payment.failed with that reason, labelled 'transaction does not match request'.

Every increase of confirmations on a confirmed observation emits commerce.payment.confirming with confirmations and requiredConfirmations and refreshes lastProgressAt; EVM observations show 'awaiting finalized checkpoint' instead of N of M.

Observations are per vault - payer and payee each run their own verifier - and in the payee's vault commerce.payment.finalized makes F09.S01.M01 sign classrup.commerce.payment_ack/v1 with verification.source chain; the payer's vault shows its own final as 'final per your verifier; payee has not confirmed' until that statement arrives.

final is set only when the finality policy is met and is terminal; for 100 further blocks the observation keeps a light watch, and a replaced inclusion block raises a deep-reorg alert without regressing the observation or the claim.

An underpaid transaction leaves the request claimable for the remainder - the payer may claim the received amount and pay the rest in another transaction - and the request is settled only when final claims cover the amount.

Request commands are vault commands that produce the signed statements classrup.commerce.crypto_request/v1 and classrup.commerce.crypto_request_cancel/v1; configure and refresh are vault-local with no statement and no relay command.
Observation transitions emit the catalog events into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the observation update; the extra event commerce.payment.failed is also emitted.
The module consumes the claim and Deal events to start and stop observation and never writes a PaymentClaim status directly.

The module registers a StatementHandlerPort handler with F09.S01.M01 for classrup.commerce.crypto_request/v1 and classrup.commerce.crypto_request_cancel/v1 (signer - obligation payee) that checks the signer role, re-validates address, chain and asset descriptor, deduplicates by cid, buffers statements whose Deal is unknown for 24 h, quarantines with reasons signer_not_payee, address_invalid, asset_mismatch or request_unknown, and drops statements from blocked dids silently.
Every commerce.payment.* event this module produces carries contextRef, obligationId, payerId and payeeId besides claimId and dealId, so consumers route and filter without reading the Deal (N4, N5).

The crypto MethodRulePort returns fail for invalid, secret-looking, reused or out-of-request input, hold(txid_lookup_pending) while a configured verifier has not found the txid, and release or discard through the F09.S01.M01 callbacks; with no verifier it fails with COMMERCE_CLAIM_METHOD_RULE unless txidAttested is true.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal mutates its vault; request creation and cancellation require the payee role in the Deal.
Incoming request statements are accepted only when signed by the obligation payee; otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role has any capability over requests or observations; a relay-hosted verifier endpoint only returns signed observations the vault verifies.
Verifier requests carry no authority at all - no DID, device-key signature or relay access token - so a relay-hosted verifier cannot tie a lookup to the principal through authentication.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and observation updates are idempotent by (claimId, txid).
Endpoint failures never change claim status; the observation keeps its last good state and shows when it was last checked.
Conflicting data from two endpoints or an inconsistent single endpoint freezes progress and warns the user instead of picking a winner.

Receiving addresses, txids and observations are P2 and never appear in public projections, logs at P2 detail or notifications; addresses are shared only inside end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the payer.
The module never requests, derives, stores or logs private keys, seed phrases or signatures that authorize spending; secret-looking input is rejected and discarded.

A user-configured verifier endpoint learns which transactions and addresses the user queries; the UI says so before the first lookup and defaults to the user's own node or a direct endpoint, with a relay endpoint only as an explicit choice.

Verifier lookups are an explicit third-party disclosure gated by privacy.consent.check purpose chain_lookup; requests are unauthenticated and unlinkable (no DID, device-key signature, relay access token or cookie) and use a connection separate from mailbox traffic (PRV-5).
Replay of an older or third-party transaction is blocked by the chain tip signed into each request and by refusing an address still used by another open or claimed request in the vault.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.crypto), DeletionPort (pseudonymization of retained requests and observations) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE with 90-day observation compaction) with F10 (N6), annotates every field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Request statements from blocked dids are dropped silently (N7, F07.S02.M02), and ingest uses the bounded quarantine of F09.S01.M01 (500 entries or 5 MiB, oldest-first eviction), dropping statements from dids that are party to no known Deal once it is full.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); endpoint latency, errors and reorg counts are kept in local diagnostics.
Status updates are applied within one poll interval of the verifier reporting them.
Verifier disagreement and reorg counts are visible to the user.

Polling stays within the per-vault budget - one tip request per endpoint per interval, per-observation calls only when the tip moved - and when the budget runs out observations closest to finality go first, intervals widen and the rest show 'verification paused'; manual refresh is limited to 3 per minute per observation.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Adapter behavior is tested against recorded Esplora and EVM JSON-RPC fixtures with no network access in CI.
Reorg, underpayment, wrong asset and no-verifier scenarios are covered deterministically.
The vault export contains the principal's crypto requests and observations with signed request statements in the section commerce.crypto.
Import verifies signatures and re-validates addresses; open observations restart as watching and are re-verified rather than trusted.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Deal stores contextRef {type, id}, the context statement cid, parties with roles, 1 to 10 obligations (payer, payee, Money amount, purpose), status, open case ids, expiry and revision; its dealId is a UUIDv8 (RFC 9562 section 5.8) made from the first 16 bytes of sha256 over JCS {contextRef, contextCid} with version and variant bits set, an explicit exception to CTR-ID-001 ID-1, so every vault derives the same ID and a new context statement such as an auction second-chance offer yields a new Deal.

A PaymentClaim stores exactly the COM-2 fields plus dealId, obligationId, the method reference signed into the claim (cash termsCid or crypto request cid), verification per COM-4, statement cids and local receivedAt; there is no paid boolean anywhere in the schema.

Deals and claims are P2 (parties only), kept by each party (a vault, or the relay for a listing_fee Deal whose payee is that relay's operator) as RET-EVIDENCE, and travel only as end-to-end encrypted signed envelopes between the parties (PRV-5).

dealCid is the cid of JCS {contextRef, contextCid, parties, obligations}, so independent opens of the same terms converge on one dealCid, and completionCid is the cid of the completion body {dealId, dealCid, outcome: completed} that every party signs as classrup.commerce.deal_completion/v1.

Money in a Deal or claim whose currency is crypto or outside the bundled ISO snapshot carries the F09.S03.M01 asset descriptor {code, chainId, contract, decimals, digest}, so every vault reads the same minor units.
Every command input is validated strictly against the schema; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.
Incoming signed statements are verified for envelope shape, Ed25519 signature over JCS bytes (FED-2), signer role and chain position before any state change.
Every violation maps to exactly one stable error code with a localized message key.

Deal statements are checked against the signed context - ContextTermsPort recomputes parties and obligations from the verified context statement, the signer must hold the opener role the context type requires, and any mismatch is quarantined with COMMERCE_DEAL_CONTEXT_CONFLICT.

Ordering follows the per-author seq and prev chain (FED-3); an unknown prev is buffered for up to 24 h, and only two different statements by the same author with the same prev or seq count as a fork, so reordered delivery and sequential partial claims are never frozen.

Statements whose Money uses a crypto or non-snapshot currency are accepted only when the embedded asset descriptor equals the local CurrencyDef; a mismatch is quarantined with COMMERCE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

Block filtering follows N7 and the N7a rentals exception - for a Deal whose context ContextTermsPort.blockExempt(contextRef, contextCid, blockedDid) reports exempt (a rentals context whose reservation was confirmed before the block), commerce.deal.open and commerce.payment.claim are not refused with BLOCKED_PARTY and its statements are verified and stored with notifications suppressed, never dropped, and the reason blocked is never sent.
Deal and PaymentClaim follow the declared machines; any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Crypto statuses are set only by events from the crypto module (F09.S01.M03) and reflect this vault's own verifier; no command can set confirmed or final directly (COM-5).
Any non-final claim without a payee acknowledgement moves to expired after 14 days without progress, computed from local lastProgressAt.
A Deal completes only when its obligations are covered by payee-acknowledged claims, and a disputed Deal returns to open only when every case on it has been resolved or withdrawn (openCaseIds empty).

A context owner can cancel an open Deal unilaterally through DealPort.cancel while no claim is acknowledged or final, with reason context_voided, withdrawn_before_accept, non_payment, buyer_timeout or conflict_resolved; the signed deal_cancel is applied by the other vaults and shown as one-sided, and every other cancellation needs all parties' signatures.

For crypto the payee's vault signs classrup.commerce.payment_ack/v1 with verification.source chain when its own verifier reports final; the payer's vault labels its own final 'final per your verifier; payee has not confirmed' and completes the Deal only on that signed statement, and no Deal expires while this vault knows a final observation that awaits the payee's statement.

An open Deal whose obligations are partly covered expires at expiresAt with reason expired_partial, a disputed Deal expires only 30 days after expiresAt, and a case opened on a completed, cancelled or expired Deal only sets disputeFlag.

Chain events for a disputed crypto claim continue the crypto machine with the dispute statement kept, a transaction that does not match the request fails the claim with its reason, and chain events for a terminal claim only update verification fields and are acknowledged by the consumer instead of failing.

Labels follow COM-4 exactly - claimed (unverified), acknowledged by payee, confirmed N of M per your verifier (awaiting finalized checkpoint on EVM), final per your verifier with or without the payee's confirmation - and no label shows completion on a payer claim alone.

A Deal whose dealId appears in bazaar.inventory.conflict_detected linkedDealIds is frozen in this vault without a status change - no acknowledgement, chain acknowledgement or completion proceeds (COMMERCE_DEAL_FROZEN) while cancel, dispute and expiry still apply - until the context owner keeps it through DealPort.unfreeze or cancels it unilaterally with reason conflict_resolved; the fork is never resolved automatically.

Commands are vault commands run locally with the unlocked principal as actor; those marked statement also produce a signed envelope for the other parties; the only relay command is commerce.payment.acknowledge run by a relay operator for a listing_fee Deal whose payee is that operator.
Every command emits its events into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change (EVT-8).
The module consumes crypto, dispute (opened, resolved, withdrawn) and deletion events to drive claim and deal status and never accepts a crypto status from user input.

Event payloads carry contextRef and the party DIDs consumers route on (N3, N4, N5) - payment events contextRef, obligationId, payerId, payeeId and parties, commerce.payment.acknowledged also acknowledgedBy (the DID whose key signed payment_ack, the relay operator for listing_fee), commerce.deal.opened and commerce.deal.cancelled contextCid and parties, and commerce.deal.completed { dealId, contextRef, contextId (= dealId), completionCid, parties, completedAt }.

commerce.statement.ingest dispatches every commerce envelope type to the handler registered through StatementHandlerPort (this module's own types, F09.S01.M02 cash terms, F09.S01.M03 crypto requests, F09.S02.M01 receipts and F09.S02.M02 dispute statements), each with the signer role listed in the note, cid deduplication and quarantine reasons.

Context modules use DealPort {open, cancel, unfreeze} in-process and implement ContextTermsPort {verify, openerRole, ownerRole, blockExempt}; a claim the method rule holds (txid not yet found or not attested) stays local, unsigned and unsent until the method module releases it.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked local principal mutates its vault; payer-only and payee-only commands also check the role recorded in the Deal.
Incoming statements are accepted only if signed by the key of the party named in the Deal for that role; otherwise they are quarantined with a reason.

No relay role grants any capability over other parties' Deals or claims; relays carry encrypted envelopes and see only routing metadata, and the one relay-side capability is the operator acknowledging claims on listing_fee Deals where that relay's operator is the payee.
Unilateral cancellation is allowed only to the context owner role that ContextTermsPort names for the context type, and receiving vaults verify that role before applying it.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs, and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Statement delivery uses the sync outbox with states prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted; the UI shows only the state reached (IDM-7).
Conflicting signed statements are detected, frozen and surfaced; there is no last-writer-wins for money or consent.
Deals and claims are P2 and are never in public projections, search, federation or notification payloads; notifications carry a reference and template key only.

Evidence is retained for RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after last activity, jurisdiction override via F18) and pseudonymized on account deletion; signatures are retained as evidence and marked unverifiable-after-pseudonymization.
Claim spam, false claims and acknowledgement pressure are limited by per-vault limits, local blocking and the dispute path; signatures evidence assertions only.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.deals), DeletionPort (the pseudonymization above) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE) with F10 (N6), annotates every Deal and PaymentClaim field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Ingest is flood-bounded - per-did buffering applies only to known parties, the quarantine holds at most 500 entries or 5 MiB with oldest-first eviction, and once it is full statements whose signer is party to no known Deal or context are dropped instead of quarantined.

Statements from a blocked did are dropped silently at ingest (N7, F07.S02.M02), except statements for a Deal with an open dispute case or a Deal that ContextTermsPort.blockExempt reports exempt under the N7a rentals exception, which are stored as evidence with notifications suppressed (F07.S02.M02 filterBlocked) and never answered with the reason blocked.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters and error logs stay in local diagnostics that the user can export.
Local command latency meets the budgets below on a mid-range phone.
Quarantine and fork counts are visible to the user in local diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs, statement envelopes and event payloads against the schema registry.
Fork, quarantine and idempotent open scenarios are covered by deterministic two-vault integration tests.
The vault export contains the principal's Deals and claims with their signed statements and provenance, in the section commerce.deals.
Import verifies signatures, schema versions and ID collisions; foreign statements are verified again and quarantined when the signer is not a party.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A party can export the completion proof of a completed Deal as classrup-deal-completion/v1 - the deal_completion/v1 body {dealId, dealCid, outcome}, its completionCid and every party's signed completion envelope, without amounts, obligations or contextRef - for voluntary submission to a relay through F12.S03.M04 moderation.accountlimit.submit_completion.

A DisputeCase stores contextRef {type, id}, opener, respondents, optional mediator, reason, evidence references, outcome, status, deadlines and revision, mirrored in each party's vault from signed statements.
Cases are P2 (parties and an explicitly accepted mediator), retained as RET-EVIDENCE, and never public or federated.

Outcome and money are decoupled by schema, because the outcome has no executable fields, only advisory ones - an optional advisory refund Money amount and an advisory disposition {kind, favouredDid, agreedAmount}.

Attachment evidence is an F15.S02.M03 MediaBlob ref (blob:sha256-<base64url>, at most 5 MiB) whose bytes were stripped of EXIF, XMP, IPTC and GPS metadata by F10.S02.M03 before encryption; the case stores only refs, hashes, sizes and captions.

A mediator record embeds the relay-signed directory entry {mediatorDid, relayId, policyUrl, validUntil} when one exists and its trust (relay_verified or self_declared), plus the set of parties that signed acceptance.
The case stores the parties [{did, role}] and contextCid returned by DisputeContextPort.resolve when it was opened, so every mirror derives the same respondents.
Case and evidence input is validated strictly, including context resolution through the DisputeContextPort and party membership.
Incoming statements are verified for signature, signer role and chain position before any state change.
Outcome rules enforce who must accept and that outcomes carry no executable money action.

Context types are a registry - only types a module registered through DisputeContextPort are accepted, and an unregistered type or a context the resolver cannot resolve returns COMMERCE_DISPUTE_CONTEXT_INVALID.

A block never removes the right to dispute - commerce.dispute.open is never refused with BLOCKED_PARTY for any context type, including booking cases opened through the F03.S02.M03 port and rental_deposit or rental_damage cases of a reservation confirmed before the block (N7a), and serviceScope is accepted only for booking contexts.
Cases follow the declared lifecycle; any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Terminal states have no exits and no state change executes any money movement.
Conflicting signed outcomes freeze the case for renegotiation instead of choosing a winner.
The case clock is evaluated locally and every deadline is shown as a date.

The mediator becomes active only when acceptedBy equals the full party set of the case (opener and all respondents), and a self-declared mediator may propose outcomes but every outcome it proposes needs acceptance by every party.

Open, add_evidence, respond, select_mediator, accept_mediator, propose_outcome, accept_outcome, reject_outcome and withdraw are vault commands that each produce a signed statement; ingest is an internal vault command; no command is a relay command.
Mediator actions run in the mediator's own vault as the same commands under role-in-statement authorization; a relay only publishes relay-signed mediator directory entries under its hosting policy.

The module consumes payment, services-dispute and deletion events to prefill drafts and pseudonymize retained records, and never opens a case automatically; services.dispute.opened at most prefills evidence in the opener vault and is ignored when origin is federated, because the F03.S02.M03 port call is the single creation path for booking cases (N21).

Event payloads carry the exact contextRef, openerId, respondentIds and parties [{did, role}] (N3, N4) - commerce.dispute.opened, evidence_added, outcome_proposed, resolved and withdrawn - resolved and withdrawn also carry caseCid for reputation (F07.S03.M01), resolved also carries contextCid, acceptedBy and outcomeCid, and opened carries serviceScope for booking cases.

dispute_outcome/v1 and commerce.dispute.resolved carry an advisory, non-executable disposition {kind continue|settled|cancelled|waived, favouredDid?, agreedAmount?}; when it is absent each consumer applies the outcome-type mapping in its own spec, and for deal and payment_claim contexts the default mapping in the note is normative.

Every dispute statement type is registered with its signer role in F11.S01.M01 and reaches commerce.dispute.ingest through the F09.S01.M01 ingest dispatcher (StatementHandlerPort), with cid deduplication, quarantine reasons and the block exception for open cases.

commerce.dispute.open accepts optional serviceScope {scope, scopeKey, milestoneId?} for booking contexts and idempotencyRef (the F03.S02.M03 linkId), signs serviceScope into classrup.commerce.dispute/v1, carries it in commerce.dispute.opened, and returns the existing case for a repeated idempotencyRef.

Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal acts in its vault; party-only commands check membership in the case, and mediator commands check that the mediator did was accepted by every party of the case in signed statements.
Incoming statements are accepted only when signed by a party or the accepted mediator for that statement type; otherwise they are quarantined.

Relay policy only governs the mediator directory a relay publishes; relay moderators have no authority over a case unless every party of the case selected them, and then only the power to sign statements.

A mediator's link to the relay it claims to moderate is proved only by a directory entry signed by that relay's key and verified by each vault; a self-declared mediator cannot decide a mediator-only outcome.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs and expectedRevision on mutations.
Statement delivery uses the sync outbox states and the UI shows only the state reached.
Forked or conflicting signed outcomes are detected, frozen and surfaced; there is no last-writer-wins.

Statements of an open case from a party this vault blocked are stored as evidence with notifications suppressed and are never dropped, the timeline says 'responses from a party you blocked are hidden', and the response window flag is noResponseReceivedHere, which such stored statements clear.
Cases and evidence are P2, travel only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes to parties and, after every party accepts, to the mediator; relays see ciphertext and routing metadata only.
Evidence shared with a mediator is shared per item by explicit party action, and the UI says the mediator's relay operator cannot read it but the mediator can keep a copy.
Dispute abuse such as harassment, evidence flooding and mediator shopping is limited by quotas, duplicate rules and mutual mediator acceptance.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.disputes), DeletionPort (pseudonymization and crypto-shredding of the deleted user's own evidence) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE) with F10 (N6), annotates every field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Attachment evidence follows N9 and FLOW-10 - MediaBlob of at most 5 MiB, EXIF, XMP, IPTC and GPS stripped by F10.S02.M03 before encryption, per-object key - so no exact (L4) location reaches the respondent or the mediator through image metadata.
Ingest uses the bounded quarantine of F09.S01.M01 (500 entries or 5 MiB, oldest-first eviction) and, once it is full, drops statements from dids that are party to no known context.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); case counters, deadlines and errors stay in local diagnostics.
Relays that publish a mediator directory follow CTR-OBS-001 for that endpoint.
Local commit and ingest meet the stated budgets.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs, statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
Mediation and fork scenarios are covered by deterministic multi-vault integration tests.
The vault export contains the principal's cases with all signed statements and evidence references in the section commerce.disputes, and evidence blobs the user holds in the export blob list.
Import re-verifies every statement and quarantines those whose signer is not a party or the accepted mediator.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A Receipt stores claimId, dealId, statement type, canonical statement body, signerId, role, signedAt (the signer's claim), local receivedAt, signature and receipt cid, matching COM-6.
Receipts are P2, retained as RET-EVIDENCE, and immutable once created; corrections are new receipts.

The statement body binds the claim cid, dealId, the Deal's contextCid, amount and currency so a receipt cannot be moved to another claim or Deal (the F16.S02.M03 inventory binding for classrup/receipt/v1).

signerId is the principal DID of the Deal party and signingKeyId names the device key that signed; the receipt embeds the device-link chain (root-signed classrup.identity.device_link/v1 statements) or an identity-document snapshot, so offline verification can link the key to the principal.

Key status is stored with the trusted receipt time it was derived from - local receivedAt, or a relay-signed receipt time labelled as that relay's evidence - and the revocation's effective-from time; signedAt is never used for key status.
Receipt input is validated strictly; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.
Role and claim-state rules check that the signer is a party and that the claim status supports the assertion.
Signature verification is exact, so any byte change in the canonical content invalidates the receipt.

Verification is delegated to F16.S02.M03 verify(envelope, {expectedContext classrup/receipt/v1}, keyStatus, payload) - the signature covers JCS({v, ctx, kid, alg, signedAt, payloadHash}), the module supplies the statement as payload for hash-only envelopes and the key status for kid at the trusted receipt time - party binding is checked through the embedded device-link chain against F07.S01.M01 and F07.S02.M01, and a key revoked before the trusted receipt time is refused at ingest.
Receipts are immutable; there is no editing or deletion by status change.
Delivery progress is tracked by the sync outbox states, not by receipt status.
Verification is recomputed on demand and cached with its check time.

Issue is a vault command that produces the signed statement classrup.commerce.receipt/v1; ingest is a vault command for received statements; verify and export are vault queries; no relay command exists.
Issue and ingest emit commerce.receipt.issued into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the insert.
The module consumes claim and key-revocation events to prompt for receipts and to update key status.

classrup.commerce.receipt/v1 (signer - the claim payer for payer_asserts_paid, the claim payee for payee_asserts_received, through a device key linked to that principal) is registered with the F09.S01.M01 ingest dispatcher through StatementHandlerPort, which hands it to commerce.receipt.ingest with cid deduplication, quarantine reasons and block filtering.

The verify output names both the device key that signed and the principal it is linked to, with partyBinding, keyStatus and the trusted receipt time used, and its label never shows Valid together with 'revoked later' on the strength of signedAt.

The module acts only on F16.S02.M03 result.accepted - issue stores, ingest stores and emits, and verify reports valid only when accepted is true - supplies the statement as payload for hash-only envelopes, and keeps the F16 reason (SECURITY_*) with every quarantined receipt.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal signs with its own device key; the role in the Deal limits which statement type it may sign.
Incoming receipts are accepted only when the signature verifies and the signer is a party of the claim; otherwise they are quarantined.
No relay role has any capability over receipts; relays see only ciphertext.
Issue is idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs and unique (claim, signer, type).
Signing and storing are one local transaction so there is no signed-but-unstored receipt.
Delivery uses the sync outbox; the UI never claims the counterparty has the receipt before peer_accepted.
Receipts are P2 and travel only inside end-to-end encrypted envelopes to the counterparty or in files the user chooses to share.
The UI states that a receipt shows what the signer asserted and that a signed time is the signer's claim, not proof of time.
Misuse such as forced signing or fake receipts is limited by role checks, signature verification and the dispute path.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.receipts), DeletionPort (pseudonymization of signerId) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE) with F10 (N6), annotates every Receipt field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Receipts from blocked dids are dropped silently (N7, F07.S02.M02) unless the claim's Deal has an open dispute case, and ingest uses the bounded quarantine of F09.S01.M01 (500 entries or 5 MiB, oldest-first eviction), dropping receipts from dids that are party to no known Deal once it is full.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); signing and verification timings stay in local diagnostics.
Signing and verification meet the stated budgets on a mid-range phone.
Quarantine counts are visible in local diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Signatures are tested with RFC 8032 vectors and JCS vectors from RFC 8785.
Verification is tested against tampered, replayed and revoked-key receipts.
The vault export contains the principal's receipts with signatures in the section commerce.receipts.
Import re-verifies every signature and quarantines receipts that fail or whose signer is not a party of an imported claim.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ReconciliationReport stores scope, time window, record counts, a list of at most 500 mismatches and a status, and is derived data that can always be recomputed.
Each mismatch has a stable key made of kind and subject IDs so repeated runs recognize it.
Reports are P2 because they reference deals and claims, are kept in the vault only for 30 days, and never leave the device except in the user's own export.
Run requests are validated for scope and rate before scanning starts.
Each mismatch kind has an explicit, testable detection rule evaluated over read-only snapshots.
Dismiss input is validated and attributable to the local principal only.
A run is running until it completes or fails; reports are immutable after that except for dismiss marks.
The ten mismatch kinds and their rules are fixed by this spec and listed in the mismatch catalog below.
Runs are restartable; a failed run leaves no partial effects.
Run and dismiss are vault commands (local, no signed statement, no relay command); queries return the latest and past reports.
A completed run emits one commerce.reconciliation.mismatch_found event per new mismatch key into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the report update.
The module consumes settlement events only to schedule coalesced incremental runs and never to change data.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal runs, dismisses or reads reports in its vault.
The module has read-only access to other modules' records through ports and no write access to them.
No relay role has any capability over reports; they never leave the device.
Runs are idempotent for identical vault state, so the same mismatch keys are produced and events are emitted only for keys not seen before.
An interrupted run is marked failed and restarted from scratch; there is nothing to roll back because the scan is read-only.
Two tabs cannot run concurrently; the second joins the first.
Reports reference P2 records and stay in the vault; they contain IDs and kinds only, never amounts, notes or addresses.
Reports are kept 30 days and are regenerated on demand, so deletion of source data removes the underlying subject at the next run.
Alert fatigue and misleading alarms are limited by severity levels, dedupe by key and dismissal.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.reconciliation), DeletionPort (reports of a deleted principal are deleted, since they are derived) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-SHORT, 30 days) with F10 (N6), annotates every report field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); run duration and mismatch counts stay in local diagnostics.
Scans are chunked so the main thread is blocked no longer than 50 ms at a time.
Run duration meets the budget for large vaults.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Each of the ten mismatch kinds has a fixture that triggers it and a fixture that does not.
The read-only guarantee is verified by a write-spy test on other modules' stores.
The vault export includes only the latest completed report in the section commerce.reconciliation for reference.
Import never trusts an imported report; it is stored as imported and a fresh run is scheduled.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A CurrencyDef stores code, kind (fiat or crypto), name, decimals, optional chain binding, status and revision per CTR-ID-001, scoped per vault.
Currency definitions are P0 reference data retained as RET-STANDARD; they hold no personal data.
Decimals, kind and chain binding are immutable after registration; only status and display name can change.

An AssetDescriptor {code, kind, chainId, contract, decimals} and its digest (sha256 cid of the JCS bytes of those five fields, absent fields as null) identify a currency across vaults; every statement carrying Money in a crypto currency or a code outside the bundled ISO snapshot embeds it, and every CurrencyDef stores its own descriptorDigest.
Registration is validated against the schema and the configured chain list before persistence.
Every lookup of an unknown code returns COMMERCE_CURRENCY_UNKNOWN with the offending code in params.
Status changes check for dependent open records through the CurrencyUsagePort.

An embedded asset descriptor is accepted only when its code, kind, chainId, contract and decimals equal the local CurrencyDef (and its digest matches); any difference returns COMMERCE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH, and the ingesting module quarantines the statement.
Currencies move between active and disabled freely; retirement is permanent.
Disabling never alters existing records; it only blocks new use.
Retirement requires the usage check to show zero open references.
Register and set_status are vault commands (local, actor is the unlocked principal, no signed statement and no relay command); get and list are vault queries.
Registration and status changes emit events into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change.
Other modules resolve currencies through the query or the in-process CurrencyRegistry cache, refreshed within 30 s of a change.

The in-process AssetDescriptorPort {descriptorFor(code), check(descriptor)} and the query commerce.currency.check_descriptor give every ingesting module the same equality check, and register accepts a fromStatement descriptor for peer-seen assets.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked local principal reads, registers or changes currencies in its vault.
A relay may expose its accepted-currency list read-only to anonymous clients as a relay policy row; relay operators change that row under relay policy, outside this module's records.
Every state-changing decision is written to the vault's local audit log with no payload content.
Registration and status changes are idempotent under CTR-IDM-001 (vault command IDs) and use expectedRevision where applicable.
The unique (vault, code) index serializes concurrent registrations from several tabs so exactly one wins.
The in-memory cache falls back to IndexedDB if invalidation messages between tabs are lost.
Currency data is public reference data and contains no personal information.
Local changes are recorded in the vault's local audit log (RET-AUDIT, 1 year).
Crypto contract addresses are validated and shown with a checksum so users can verify the asset they are paying with.
A look-alike or rescaled asset in a peer statement never reaches a Money value, because the descriptor check quarantines it and registration from a statement requires an explicit checksum review.
Lookups are cached and meet a very low latency budget.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); counters stay in local diagnostics and relay metrics follow CTR-OBS-001 where a relay hosts the list.
Cache staleness is observable.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs and event payloads against the registry schemas.
Immutability is covered by property and migration tests.
The registry is included in the vault export as a configuration section so a restored vault keeps custom assets.
Import validates codes, decimals and chain binding and rejects rows that conflict with existing immutable fields.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
Money is { amount: decimal integer string of minor units with optional leading '-', currency: registry code } on the wire and a bigint plus currency code in memory (MNY-1).
The absolute value of any amount is limited to 38 decimal digits (fits an unsigned 128-bit integer) so storage in SQLite text columns and cross-language vectors stay unambiguous.
The library owns no persistent entity; it defines the value types Money, Rational, RoundingMode and AllocationResult only.

maxAmount(currencyDef) returns Money { amount: 10^(10 + decimals), currency: code } - 10^10 major units in minor units - from the caller-supplied F09.S03.M01 CurrencyDef { code, decimals }, because this library has no registry access and F09.S03.M01 depends on it; when decimals exceeds 27 the result is the 38-digit bound 10^38 - 1, and amounts are capped with amount <= maxAmount.
Parsing accepts only the canonical grammar and rejects everything else with COMMERCE_MONEY_INVALID, including whitespace, plus signs, leading zeros, decimal points and exponents.
Conversion and allocation validate their rational and weight inputs before computing.
Mixed-currency arithmetic is a programmer error that throws (MNY-6) rather than returning a Result.
The library is stateless and pure; every function returns the same output for the same input with no clock, random or I/O access.
Rounding happens exactly once, at the end of a conversion or percentage computation, never between intermediate steps (MNY-3).
Operations never mutate their inputs; Money values are immutable.
The public API is the TypeScript package surface listed in the note; there are no relay commands, queries or events.
Error codes returned by Result-style functions are stable and listed in the errors table; mismatched currencies throw.
The package exposes language-neutral test vectors (JSON) so non-TypeScript clients can verify identical results.
The library performs no authorization; callers authorize before using it.
It has no network access, no storage access and no ambient authority, so it cannot leak data by construction.
Importing the package into a client bundle adds no more than 12 KiB gzip.
All functions are deterministic and idempotent; repeated calls with the same input return identical results.
There is no shared mutable state, so concurrent callers cannot interfere.
Failure is signalled with Result errors for input problems and thrown errors only for programmer mistakes.
The library holds no personal data and never logs inputs.
Error messages carry only the error code and the offending argument position, never amounts.
Oversized inputs are bounded (38 digits, 1000 weights) so hostile payloads cannot cause denial of service through bigint growth.
The library emits no metrics itself; callers measure around it.
Single conversion or allocation of 1000 weights completes within the stated budgets on a mid-range phone.
Test and vector counts are reported by CI.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Property tests run at least 10 000 cases per property with a recorded seed.
Golden vectors are shared between implementations and checked in CI.
The library has no data to export or import; the canonical Money JSON form is the interchange format used by other modules' export sections.
The package version and golden vector file are versioned together and published with each release.
A rounding behavior change is a breaking major change and requires a new vector set and an ADR.
An FxQuote stores base, quote, rational rate {num, den}, source, sourceKind, asOf, expiresAt, issuer reference and optional source signature per MNY-4, in the principal's vault.
Quotes are P1 reference data (the issuer's did is the only identity) and retained as RET-EVIDENCE in the vault because proposals pin them; a quote embedded in a signed statement is carried in full.
A quote is immutable after issue except for revocation of manual quotes.

Every FxQuote records purpose (general or barter_normalization) and sourceSigned; issuerRef is mandatory (the fetching principal's did for direct-provider quotes, the issuing principal's did for manual quotes, the relay key id for relay-signed quotes), and only a relay-signed quote whose relay signature verifies has sourceSigned true; a manual quote signed by its issuer has issuerSigned true, which proves who asserted the rate, not its origin, and keeps sourceSigned false (F02.S04.M02 V07).

A quote received inside a peer statement is stored with receivedFrom (the embedding statement's signer), the local receivedAt, its verification label and, when re-derived, the reference rate and deviation.
Quote requests validate currencies, source availability, source signature (for relay quotes) and rate sanity before issuing.
Provider values are parsed as decimal strings into exact rationals; floating point parse is forbidden.
Staleness and deviation checks run on every provider quote.

Quotes embedded in peer statements are verified before display - relay-signed quotes by the relay key, manual quotes by issuerRef, which must equal the embedding statement's signer unless the quote carries its own valid issuer signature - and unsigned provider quotes are labelled 'source asserted by <issuer pseudonym>, not verifiable' with sourceSigned false.
A quote is issued once and ends as expired or revoked; it is never extended or edited.

Expiry is evaluated against the local clock of the vault doing the check; any relay-signed asOf or expiresAt is shown as that relay's claim, receivers check embedded quotes against their own clock with the 10-minute skew note used by F09.S01.M01, and consumers must call the validity check before using a pinned quote.
Revocation applies to manual quotes only; a revoked quote that was already embedded in a statement sent to a peer is superseded by a signed revocation statement and peers invalidate it at next sync.

A barter_normalization quote lives at most 24 h and is shown as 'pinned rate agreed by all parties'; it is never extended, and a deadline beyond its expiry needs a re-quote and fresh consent (N16, F02.S04.M02).

Commands request, issue_manual and revoke are vault commands (local, actor is the unlocked principal); relay_issue is a relay command that returns a relay-signed quote; revoke additionally produces the signed statement classrup.commerce.fx_quote_revocation/v1.
Each issue emits commerce.fx_quote.issued into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the insert.
Consumers pin quotes by ID only and never copy rates without the ID.

classrup.commerce.fx_quote_revocation/v1 (signer - the issuerRef of the manual quote) is ingested through the internal vault command commerce.fx_quote.ingest_revocation, idempotent by cid, with quarantine reasons signer_not_issuer, not_manual and quote_unknown (buffered 24 h), and statements from blocked dids are dropped silently.

commerce.fx_quote.verify_embedded is the one check consumers (F02.S04.M02, offers, Deals) call for quotes inside peer statements; it returns sourceSigned, the verification label, local-clock expiry with a skew note and, when asked, the ECB re-derivation.

Approximate values are rendered only through F14.S02.M02 formatApprox, reached through the injected ApproxFormatPort that the vault composition binds (F14.S02.M02 depends on this module, so there is no static edge back), with the QuoteLabel { source, sourceKind, issuerDisplay, label, signatureVerified, asOf, expiresAt, status, pinned?: { consentCollected } } from commerce.fx_quote.quote_label - issuerDisplay resolved and signatures verified before the call, signatureVerified true only for a verified relay signature, a verified manual issuer signature or a quote this vault fetched through its own direct adapter, status evaluated on the local clock, and pinned passed through only from the caller that pinned the quote.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked local principal requests, issues manual quotes for, checks or revokes quotes in its vault.
Under relay policy a relay serves relay_issue to requests signed by a registered device key and only relay operators configure which sources it offers.
Manual quote issuance is logged in the vault's local audit log with reason; relay issuance is audited by the relay under RET-AUDIT.

Incoming revocations are accepted only when signed by the issuerRef of the manual quote they name; relay keys sign only relay_issue quotes and carry no authority over a vault's quotes or their expiry.
Quote requests are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 in the vault; a replay returns the same quote ID and relay calls carry the same Idempotency-Key.
Provider and relay fetch failures use bounded retries and then fall back to local manual quotes or fail visibly.
The rate cache is a read-through cache; losing it only costs a provider call.

Quote requests carry no location or identity to providers; providers only receive the pair, and the UI states that a direct provider sees the device IP while a relay proxy hides it from the provider but not from the relay.
Manual rate abuse is controlled by the mandatory label, reason and pseudonym attached to the quote, and by counterparties consenting to the exact pinned quote.
Quotes are kept as evidence for 2 years because proposals pin them.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section commerce.fx_quotes), DeletionPort (pseudonymization of issuerRef and receivedFrom) and RetentionPurgePort (RET-EVIDENCE, unreferenced quotes after 30 days) with F10 (N6), annotates every FxQuote field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed.

Forged source attribution is never shown as verified - unsigned provider quotes read 'source asserted by <sender>, not verifiable', manual quotes need issuerRef's signature, revocations from blocked dids are dropped (N7), and the revocation ingest uses a bounded quarantine of 100 entries with oldest-first eviction.
Relay metrics follow CTR-OBS-001; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7) and keeps counters in local diagnostics only.
Quote issue meets the local write budget and the relay budget at 50 req/s from cache.
Manual quote counts are visible in the vault's local diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Adapter behavior is tested against recorded provider fixtures with no network access in CI, and signature verification is tested with fixed relay test keys.
Expiry boundaries are tested with a controllable clock.
The vault export includes quotes pinned by the user's proposals through the pinning module's section as references with the quote data embedded.
Imported quotes keep their original expiresAt; those already past it are stored as expired.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A PrivacyConsent stores purpose, scope (relay, verifier endpoint and record kinds), policy id, version and SHA-256 hash, locale of the text shown, grant and withdrawal times, status and source; federation_publish, notify_email and notify_push are scoped to exactly one relay named by its canonical self-certifying relayId (F15.S02.M01, 'relay:' plus 26 lowercase base32 characters of the genesis key hash, never a hostname), and chain_lookup is scoped to exactly one HTTPS verifier endpoint origin.
The history is append-only; a new grant creates a new row and supersedes the previous one rather than editing it.

Consents are P3 in the vault and retained as RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after withdrawal) as proof of what was agreed; the vault entity schema classrup.privacy.consent/v1 never leaves the vault except in the user's own export.

The relay-facing statements have their own schemas with explicit field allowlists, registered with signer role in the F11.S01.M01 statement registry (N2): classrup.privacy.consent_statement/v1 with payload exactly {consentId, purpose, relayId, recordKinds, policyId, policyVersion, policyHash, grantedAt} and classrup.privacy.consent_withdrawal/v1 with payload exactly {consentId, targetCid, purpose, relayId, withdrawnAt, reason}; the did appears only as the envelope author, with per-author seq and prev (CTR-FED-001).
Grant input is validated strictly, including purpose, scope and policy hash.
A grant is accepted only for the currently bundled policy version of the purpose.
Defaults are enforced in code, so processing is allowed only when a granted, non-lapsed consent exists.

Withdrawal always succeeds locally whatever its source (user, unsubscribe, deletion step or lapse) and is never refused for rate reasons; only the outgoing withdrawal statements are coalesced in the sync outbox.
A relay accepts a consent or withdrawal statement only after verifying signer key and role, audience, field allowlist, chain position and that the grant was not already withdrawn.

Scope identifiers are validated in canonical form only, a relayId per F15.S02.M01 and a chain_lookup endpoint as a bare HTTPS origin, and a consumer whose check is not granted refuses with PRIVACY_CONSENT_REQUIRED.
A consent is granted until it is withdrawn, superseded by a newer grant or lapsed by a material policy change.
Withdrawal takes effect in the same local transaction and is final for that row; consent again means a new grant.
Lapse is evaluated at unlock and daily against the bundled policy versions, and a lapse of a federation consent queues the same signed withdrawal statement as an explicit withdrawal.

Grant and withdraw are vault commands; for federation_publish they also produce classrup.privacy.consent_statement/v1 and classrup.privacy.consent_withdrawal/v1; check and list are vault queries; privacy.consent.relay_register is the relay command that accepts and acknowledges those statements, and privacy.consent.relay_check is an in-process relay query.
Grant and withdraw emit events into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change.

Other modules must call privacy.consent.check (or the guard privacy.consent.require) before processing for a purpose, treat any failure as not granted and refuse with PRIVACY_CONSENT_REQUIRED, the one consent-missing code defined here.

Each statement declares signer role and audience for the N2 registry; both are signed by the principal and addressed to one named relay, sealed to that relay's published key because they are P2 for that relay only (PRV-5), and notify_email and notify_push produce no statement here because the F13.S02.M03 channel consent carries consentId and purpose.
The privacy ports of this module are defined in the note, including the DeletionPort step that withdraws every consent and signs the federation withdrawals before F07.S01.M01 destroys the keys.

privacy.consent.check is bound as ConsentCheckPort in the kernel port registry at vault composition, so modules that this module depends on (F07.S01.M01 checks federation_publish before a handle claim) call it through the port with the same inputs, outputs and fail-closed behavior, and chain_lookup is matched by purpose plus the exact endpoint origin.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked local principal grants, withdraws or reads its own consents.
privacy.consent.check is callable by other modules in the same vault in-process; it never reveals consent state to other principals.

Relays authorize receipt of consent statements under their own relay policy through privacy.consent.relay_register, accept only statements signed by the principal and addressed to themselves, and cannot grant or alter consent.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs and expectedRevision on withdrawal.

Withdrawal commits locally first and never fails for rate or connectivity reasons; relay delivery of the signed withdrawal retries until peer_accepted (the relay-signed acknowledgement of privacy.consent.relay_register) or the relay is removed.
The check function fails closed, so any error means not granted.
Consent records are P3 and never leave the vault except as the signed federation statements to the named relay and the user's own export.
Consent is never pre-ticked, bundled or inferred, and each purpose is a separate decision with its own text.
The UI states the limits of withdrawal, namely that future processing stops, copies already fetched by other vaults and relays cannot be recalled.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); consent counts and check latency stay in local diagnostics.
The check function meets a low latency budget with an in-memory cache invalidated on change.
