Lapse and withdrawal propagation are observable locally.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate command outputs, statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
Default-off behavior is covered by a test that enumerates every purpose on a fresh vault.
The vault export contains the full consent history in the section privacy.consents.
Import re-evaluates each consent against the bundled policy hashes and lapses any whose hash is unknown or outdated.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A DeletionRequest stores the principal did (until completion only), status, request time, grace end (14 days), deferral limit, evidence option, per-module step states, per-relay and per-counterparty delivery states and the completion summary.
The pseudonymization salt exists only inside the request until completion and is then destroyed, so the pseudonym cannot be recomputed from the did afterwards.

A deletion ledger entry is kept for 180 days after completion in the residue store, keyed by HMAC-SHA256(ledgerSalt, did) with a separate, kept ledger salt and holding no requestId, pseudonym or plain did; the completed request record in residue form is P3 and retained as RET-EVIDENCE as proof of the deletion request.

A per-origin residue store outside the erased principal vault holds only the completed DeletionRequest without did or salt, the ledger entries, outbox entries of statements already signed and still awaiting delivery (until peer_accepted, or 30 days after signing), and, when keepEvidence is true, a pseudonymized evidence-only vault retained per RET-EVIDENCE; nothing else of the principal survives on the device.

The relay deletion statement classrup.privacy.deletion_statement/v1 and the counterparty notice classrup.privacy.deletion_notice/v1 have their own schemas with explicit field allowlists and signer role principal, are registered in the F11.S01.M01 statement registry, and are separate from the vault-only entity schema classrup.privacy.deletion_request/v1.

The deletion notice has two kinds - a commitment notice per open commitment for its counterparties, and one departure notice signed once in the sign step and sealed separately to the mailbox key of every thread counterparty that the F08 DeletionPort plans list, so all thread counterparties receive the same cid; the deleted did is the envelope author and is never repeated in the payload.
Requests are validated for fresh unlock, typed confirmation and the single-active-request rule.
Execution validates that grace has ended, that deferral limits are respected and that every registered module has a plan.

Incoming relay deletion statements are verified for signature by a registered, non-revoked key of the did (or one listed as final by its account_deleted revocation) and for replay rather than age: dedupe on (did, requestId, batch hash) and accept signedAt up to 30 days old plus 10 minutes of clock skew.
Publishing and new commitments are refused during an active request through the guard privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending, which every publishing and commitment module calls.
Deletion notices are validated against the allowlist of their kind and sent only to recipients that a DeletionPort plan listed as commitment counterparties or thread counterparties.
Deletion requests follow the declared machine; the point of no return is the transition to executing and the UI says so before the request.
Open commitments defer execution for at most 30 days and never silently extend further.

Execution is a resumable sequence of idempotent DeletionPort steps in a fixed order in which every signed statement is produced before any key is revoked or destroyed, and the final step is F07.S01.M01 destroying the device keys.

Cancellation emits privacy.deletion.cancelled; before execution, consumers of privacy.deletion.requested take only reversible actions (hide, pause) and never purge or tombstone, which belong to execution.

Request and cancel are vault commands; execution is driven by an internal sweep and is not a user command; the relay command privacy.deletion.relay_apply serves relays that receive the signed deletion statement, and privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending and privacy.deletion.ledger_check are in-process guard queries.

Execution produces the signed statements classrup.privacy.deletion_statement/v1 (to relays) and classrup.privacy.deletion_notice/v1 (end-to-end encrypted to the counterparties of open commitments and, as one departure notice, to every thread counterparty) and orchestrates classrup.federation.tombstone/v1 per published record through the F11.S01.M02 DeletionPort step; all are signed before any key is revoked or destroyed.
The module consumes commitment-closing and commitment-cancelling events to end deferral and never accepts a request to shorten the grace period.
DeletionPort is defined in the note with typed methods, step order, error semantics and a CI conformance check, and open commitments are reported as blockers by plan().

privacy.deletion.requested permits only reversible actions, privacy.deletion.cancelled tells consumers to undo them, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only on which consumers must not sign, pseudonymize or call relays.

DeletionPort registrations are discovered through the kernel port registry at vault composition, by inverted registration for modules that cannot list this module in depends_on without closing a cycle (F07.S01.M01, F15.S01.M01 platform.outbox, F15.S04.M03 platform.local_settings); a module registered twice fails composition and every registrant takes part in the fixed step order.

The sign step runs every registered sign implementation before revoke_keys and destroy_keys, including F07.S01.M01 signed handle releases, the tombstone of its own identity document and session revocations on relays, the F08 signed message and attachment deletes and mailbox closes, and this module's departure notice to the thread counterparties that the F08 plans list.

F18.S02.M01 and F18.S01.M01 register their DeletionPorts from the vault composition root by inverted registration, because each sits on the path F10.S01.M02 -> F18.S01.M01 -> F18.S02.M01 - the F18.S02.M01 sign step signs a classrup.federation.tombstone/v1 (format owned by F11.S01.M02) for each of the principal's own policy comments, and the F18.S01.M01 port deletes the ProfileSelection and the age declaration in the purge step.

Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal requests or cancels deletion of its own vault, with a fresh unlock within 5 minutes; deletion rights survive suspension on any relay (CAP-5, CAP-9).

Relays accept privacy.deletion.relay_apply only for statements signed by a registered key of the deleted did, or listed as final by its account_deleted revocation; relay operators cannot start deletion of a user's vault.
Operators can view relay-side deletion counts but not subjects' vault contents, and users learn only whether some relay copies are retained under legal obligation, never a count.
Request and cancel are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs and expectedRevision.
Every execution step is idempotent and its state is persisted, so a crash or closed tab resumes where it stopped.
A failure never leaves a half-deleted principal unannounced; failed state is visible and retried every 6 hours.

Deletion removes content and shreds keys; evidence classes under RET-EVIDENCE are pseudonymized and kept until their retention ends unless the user chooses to purge their own evidence copies; pseudonymized is not anonymized.

The UI and completion summary state that deletion covers this device and browser profile only, that the recovery kit and other devices can re-create the identity unless destroyed, that copies fetched by other vaults and relays, exported files and user backups cannot be recalled, and that relay legal holds may retain relay-held copies sealed.
Abusive or coerced deletion is limited by the fresh unlock, typed confirmation, 14-day grace with banners, and cancellation.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); step states, durations and failures stay in local diagnostics that the user can export, and relays measure relay_apply per CTR-OBS-001.
Execution completes within the budget for typical vaults and never blocks the UI thread over 50 ms.
Failed steps are surfaced with the module name.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Execution is tested with a controllable clock and stub DeletionPorts for every module including failing ones.
The no-resurrection property is tested by restoring an old export after completion.
The vault export includes DeletionRequest metadata in the section privacy.deletion and the user is prompted to export before the grace period ends.

A restore or import into this browser profile consults the deletion ledger before committing and never resurrects a completed deletion without the user's explicit override that creates a new identity; restores on other devices or profiles are outside this guarantee and the UI says so.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days; the ledger format is stable for at least 180 days.
An ExportJob stores status, include-media flag, per-section state and hash, totals, manifest hash, signing key ID, and expiry (readyAt plus 7 days).
The bundle itself is not a database record; it is an encrypted file in origin-private storage identified by the job ID, and the job holds its size and SHA-256.
ExportJob is P3, retained as RET-SHORT (30 days) after expiry as a record that an export happened, and never contains user content.
A multi-part export set shares a setId; each part has its own signed manifest with index, total, media date range and the hash of the part-1 manifest, so the parts are linked and each verifies alone.
Requests are validated for recent unlock, limits and size estimate before collection starts.
Each module section is validated against its registered schema list and its own line format before it is accepted.
The manifest is validated and its signature verified before the job becomes ready.
Export jobs follow the declared machine; any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
A job is ready only after all sections are done, the manifest is signed and verified, and the bundle is stored.
Expiry after 7 days deletes the bundle and shreds its key; failure and cancel delete partial files immediately.
The 30-minute job timeout counts active foreground collection time only; a job not started within 24 h, or not resumed within 24 h of its last activity, fails with errorCode EXPIRED.
Request, cancel and open_download are vault commands (local, no signed statement to others, no relay command); the signature is a local artifact inside the bundle.
ExportSectionPort is the contract each module implements; the orchestrator calls sections in parallel at most 4 at a time.
State changes emit events into the vault outbox in the same IndexedDB transaction as the job update.
ExportSectionPort is defined in the note with typed methods, error semantics and a CI conformance check, and DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort are implemented for ExportJob and bundles.

Export sections are discovered through the kernel port registry at vault composition, by inverted registration for modules that cannot list this module in depends_on, a section name registered by two modules fails composition, and the registrants include identity.account and identity.device_keys (F07.S01.M01), platform.outbox (F15.S01.M01), platform.local_settings (F15.S04.M03) and the federation sections federation.records and federation.tombstones (F11.S01.M02), federation.routes (F11.S02.M01), federation.conflicts (F11.S02.M03), federation.peers (F11.S03.M01), federation.block_rules (F11.S03.M02) and federation.migrations (F11.S03.M03).

The governance sections are registered from the vault composition root by inverted registration, because F18.S01.M01 and F18.S02.M01 sit on the path F10.S01.M02 -> F18.S01.M01 -> F18.S02.M01 and cannot list this module in depends_on - governance.policy_comments, governance.trusted_publishers and governance.pending_statements, with governance.policy_proposals, from F18.S02.M01, and governance.profile_selection (including the age declaration, P3 for the owner only), with governance.jurisdiction_profiles, from F18.S01.M01.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal requests, cancels, reads or downloads its own export, and a fresh unlock within 5 minutes is required to start and to download.
Suspension on any relay never affects export rights because the vault is local (CAP-5, CAP-9).
Relays have no capability here and receive nothing from this module.

Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using vault command IDs; replaying the same command ID returns the stored result, and a new request while a job is active returns PRECONDITION_FAILED with params.activeJobId.
Collection is resumable by section; a section either completes with its hash or is rerun from its start.
A failed or cancelled job leaves no files and no key material behind.
The bundle contains P3 data and is encrypted at rest with a per-job key; the key is deleted at expiry, and the UI warns that the downloaded file is plain JSON Lines that the user must protect.

The export excludes other users' P2 and higher content and all P4 secrets; device private keys are never exported, and recovery material is exported only as the user's own recovery hints (P3) and never as keys.
Export abuse by someone with brief access to an unlocked device is limited by the fresh-unlock requirement, rate limit and an on-screen notification of every export.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); job timings, sizes and failures stay in local diagnostics.
Export throughput meets the budget on a mid-range phone without freezing the UI.
Failures name the failing module for support exports of diagnostics.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Round-trip tests export a seeded vault and import it into a fresh one through the IOX-2 dry-run and commit path.
Tamper, missing-section and over-limit scenarios are covered deterministically.
This module's own output format is classrup-export/v1; the module contributes a section privacy.exports listing past export jobs' metadata only.
Import of a bundle is performed by the vault restore flow, which verifies the manifest signature and section hashes produced here before committing any record.
The format follows expand/contract; a new major version keeps the previous major readable for 180 days.
A RetentionPolicy stores scope (vault or relay), retention class, duration in days, source and bounds, and is unique per scope and class.
A LegalHold stores relay, subject, reason code, a non-personal reference, requester, approver, status and review dates, and exists only on the relay that placed it.
Vault-scope policy rows are P3 (owner only) and relay-scope policy rows are P0 (the relay's published policy); holds are P3 operator records retained as RET-AUDIT for 1 year after release.

Run records hold counts per kind and class plus startedAt; the latest startedAt of a committed vault run is the high-water clock, and the latest relay-signed receipt time the vault has seen is kept beside it for clock-jump detection.

RET-SIGNAL (CTR-PRV-001 PRV-8) is expiry-bounded - a signal record is kept until its own expiresAt and never longer than 365 days after its createdAt, is then folded into a counts-only rollup that holds no identifiers, and the rollup is kept 365 days; its policy row sets only the rollup duration, fixed at 365 days, and the defaults row exists in every vault and relay scope for F12.S03.M02 Signal records.

A jurisdiction-source row names its profile by the ProfileRef {publisherId, code} of F18.S01.M01 that supplied the class value, with the version resolved at the last refresh, never by a bare jurisdiction code; a missing or unknown ref resolves to the bundled generic profile, and a row whose value became Looser keeps priorDurationDays and looserFrom so that records created before looserFrom keep the stricter retention.
Policy and hold input is validated strictly against schema and class bounds.
Hold approval enforces separation of duties, an admin in every requester and approver pair, unlinked DIDs and current relay roles.
Sweeps validate that every record kind has a registered purge port and that anchor times are not in the future.

A vault sweep that finds the clock more than 24 h ahead of its high-water clock, or more than 24 h ahead of the latest relay-signed receipt time, runs as a dry run and purges RET-SHORT, RET-STANDARD or RET-EVIDENCE records only after the user confirms.

A RET-SIGNAL kind is accepted only with an expiresAt anchor, a createdAt field and a registered counts-only rollup kind, and its records are purged at expiresAt or at createdAt plus 365 days, whichever comes first.

A ProfileRef is validated for shape only; a well-formed ref that is missing or unknown resolves to the bundled generic profile, and resolved values are clamped into this module's class bounds before they become rows.

A RetentionPurgePort kind may declare a fixed anchorOffsetDays together with a createdField, as F18.S02.M02 does for TransparencyCounter (RET-AUDIT, anchorField publishedAt, 90 days), only when the offset does not exceed the effective class duration and the kind holds no did, device key or free text, and the class duration counted from createdField stays a hard cap.
Legal holds follow the declared machine and every activation and release needs two different, unlinked operators of whom at least one is a relay admin.
An active hold excludes its subject from every sweep and relay purge until released.
Retention policy rows have no lifecycle; a change creates a new revision effective from the next sweep.
Retention policy and sweep commands exist in two forms, vault commands for the user's vault and relay commands for operators, with identical rules and different authorization.
Hold commands are relay commands authorized by relay policy for operator and admin roles; they produce no statement to users and never touch vaults.
Sweeps emit privacy.retention.purged with counts only, and holds emit placed and released events on the relay.
RetentionPurgePort is defined in the note with typed methods, anchor semantics, error semantics and a CI conformance check.

On a relay, purges of an author's data start only from a verified deletion statement applied through privacy.deletion.relay_apply (F10.S01.M04), which calls privacy.legal_hold.check and purgeSubject, or from federation.tombstone.applied; vault-local events such as privacy.deletion.completed never reach a relay.

privacy.legal_hold.placed and privacy.legal_hold.released carry the hold subject as subjectKind and subjectRef, stay relay-local P3 events for relay-system handlers (for example F12.S01.M02 evidence and F12.S03.M02 signals), and never reach a vault or a federation sink.

RetentionPurgePort kinds are discovered through the kernel port registry at vault and relay composition; modules that list this module in depends_on (F07.S01.M01, the F11 federation modules for records, tombstones, conflicts, peers, block rules, migrations and routes, and F12.S03.M02 for signals and their rollup) and modules that cannot without closing a cycle (F15.S01.M01 platform.outbox_entry and F15.S04.M03 platform.local_settings, by inverted registration) register the same way, and one kind name registered by two modules fails composition.

governance.jurisdiction_profile.activated is consumed in the vault for scope vault and on the relay for scope relay - changes released, retired, selected, deselected and upgraded refresh that scope's jurisdiction rows from governance.jurisdiction_profile.resolve by ProfileRef, upgrade_pending changes no row, and a Looser value applies only to records created at or after the later of the profile's effectiveFrom and the time the version came into use.

F18.S02.M02 registers the relay-scope kind governance.transparency_counter (class RET-AUDIT, anchorField publishedAt, anchorOffsetDays 90, capped by the effective RET-AUDIT duration from its createdField) through its depends_on edge at relay composition only, and F18.S01.M01 and F18.S02.M01 register their kinds at vault composition by inverted registration because each sits on the path F10.S01.M02 -> F18.S01.M01 -> F18.S02.M01.
Under vault policy (CAP-8) only the unlocked principal changes policy or runs sweeps for its own vault; legal hold commands do not exist there.

Under relay policy (CAP-9) only operators and admins of that relay request, approve, reject and release holds, with two different, unlinked people for each pair of steps and at least one admin in each pair (CTR-PRV-001, CAP-4).
Hold records are visible to relay operators and admins only; hold status is never exposed to users beyond a generic retained-under-legal-obligation notice without case details.
Policy changes and hold steps are idempotent with Idempotency-Key on the relay and vault command IDs in the vault, and use expectedRevision.
Sweeps commit in batches with a persisted cursor and resume after interruption without double counting.
Hold checks fail closed, so if the hold table cannot be read, relay purges of that subject are skipped.
Run records contain counts and kinds only, never record contents or identifiers of users.
Holds are the only way to keep relay-held data past policy, require two unlinked operators including an admin, are audited under RET-AUDIT and reviewed every 180 days.
Abuse of holds by a rogue operator is limited by separation of duties, mandatory reference, review reminders and visibility to all relay operators.

A Looser jurisdiction value never changes the retention of records created before it came into use in the scope, whatever effectiveFrom the publisher claims, and a fixed anchor offset never shortens the retention of records that carry a did, device key or free text.
Relay sweeps and holds are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7) and keeps vault sweep records locally.
Sweep throughput meets the budget so a night run completes inside its window.
Overdue sweeps and overdue hold reviews raise alerts on the relay.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Sweeps are tested with a controllable clock and stub purge ports for every record kind.
Separation of duties and fail-closed hold checks are tested with adversarial scenarios.
The vault export includes the principal's retention policy rows in the section privacy.retention; legal holds are never exported to users.
Relay backups include holds and policies (IOX-3); after restore, holds are re-evaluated before any sweep runs.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
The library defines the value types CleanImage {bytes, mime, width, height, sha256}, IpNetwork, PublicTimestamp and UaFamily and owns no persistent entity.
Output images carry only pixel data and the minimal container structure required by the format, with a fixed sRGB treatment and no embedded profiles beyond sRGB.
Coarsened times and daily-salted rate-limit keys are the only time- and IP-derived forms that other modules may store or log; truncated networks exist only in memory.
CleanImage bytes are at most 5 MiB, the MediaBlob limit (N9), reached by stepping quality and then dimensions down; otherwise the call fails with PRIVACY_METADATA_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE.

Public projections carry only hour-floored timestamps and record IDs minted by publicRecordId, and ordering inside an hour uses the per-author seq of the envelope (CTR-FED-001 FED-3), never a time value.
Inputs are validated for supported types, size, dimensions and decodability before processing.
Verification flags any residual metadata marker including GPS IFD, EXIF, XMP packet, IPTC, MakerNote and text chunks.
IP and timestamp helpers validate their input formats and never return unmodified raw values.
All functions are pure and deterministic given the same input and, for rate-limit keys, the same daily salt.
Image processing is a fixed pipeline of decode, orient, downscale, re-encode, size step and verify, and any step failure aborts without output.
Output is never a partially cleaned image; the verification step must pass before bytes are returned.
The public surface is the TypeScript package; there are no vault or relay commands, queries or events.
Errors are Result values with codes in the errors table; image processing runs in a worker and returns within the budget or fails with the documented code.
The package exposes fixtures and a verifier CLI used in CI to scan sample uploads.
The library performs no authorization; callers decide who may upload and which view is public.
It has no network or storage access, so it cannot leak data.

Clients apply stripImage before upload and relays apply verifyImageClean on receipt and reject non-clean images; neither side trusts the other, and relays never re-encode or substitute bytes because blobs are content-addressed (N9).
Functions are deterministic; stripping an already clean image returns an equivalent clean image.
A failure at any pipeline step returns an error and no bytes, so there is no partial unsafe output.
Image work runs in a worker with a 10 s timeout; on timeout the upload is cancelled and can be retried by the user.

Relays store exactly the client-cleaned bytes whose content address is referenced by the signed listing and reject anything else; original uploads never reach relay storage, and the client keeps the original only if the user keeps it in their own gallery.

IP addresses and truncated networks are used only in memory for the current request; the only retained form is the daily-salted rateLimitKey (RET-EPHEMERAL, 24 h), and logs contain no address or network.
Public time coarsening and user-agent reduction are applied at the boundary where data becomes public or is logged.
Outbound requests follow the header policy, namely Referrer-Policy no-referrer, no third-party requests, no analytics cookies, and a CSP whose connect-src lists only the relays the user chose.
The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7); stripping timings and failures stay in local diagnostics and relays follow CTR-OBS-001 for upload outcomes.
Image stripping meets the latency budget on a mid-range phone and verification meets it on a relay worker.
CI reports the corpus pass rate and findings by type.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
A corpus of 40 images with GPS, EXIF, XMP, IPTC, MakerNote, thumbnails and polyglots is processed and scanned by an independent parser (exiftool) in CI.
IP and time helpers are tested with exhaustive edge vectors including IPv6 forms and hour boundaries.
Images exported from a vault are the clean bytes the user published or kept; the export never adds metadata.
Images imported from older exports or other vaults pass through stripImage and verifyImageClean before they are accepted into listings.
Codec or pipeline changes are versioned, and previously stored clean images are never re-processed in place.
The library defines the value types PrivacyClass, LocationLevel, Sink, ClassificationMap and RedactionStrategy and no persistent entities.
A ClassificationMap assigns a class to every field path of a schema, with optional location level, and is stored beside the schema in the registry as part of its version.
The default class for any unannotated or unknown path is P4, which is denied for every sink including export and ui_owner, so an unclassified field never appears in any output.
The class-by-sink matrix in the note, covering 5 classes by 11 sinks plus a location cap per sink, is the normative oracle for canFlow and every redaction helper.

A field annotation may declare a single-recipient disclosure {as P2, recipientRole}; the field keeps its own class (for example P3) for every sink, and only participant_envelope accepts it, as P2, when the envelope is encrypted to exactly one recipient of that role - used by F04.S01.M01 reservePrice and reserveSalt and by F04.S01.M02 maxAmount, bidderId and clientNonce with recipientRole auction_host, the host key named in the auction terms.

The only path for P2 content to a non-participant is the PRV-9 moderation disclosure - a redact/1 copy of a P2 message, offer or cycle proposal, sealed to exactly one relay moderation key, accepted only when the envelope context declares the approved preview in state export_prepared with its preview digest.
Classification maps are validated against the schema's fields so every path is covered and no path refers to a missing field.
Redaction refuses outputs that would carry a class above what the sink allows.
Location handling validates the geohash cell precision and never accepts coordinates for public sinks.
P4 fields are denied to every sink including event, export and ui_owner, and L4 locations are denied to the event sink (EVT-5).

Single-recipient disclosures and the PRV-9 moderation disclosure are validated from the declared envelope context, so a missing or mismatched recipient role, more than one recipient, an unencrypted envelope, or a disclosure that is not the approved redact/1 output in state export_prepared is refused.
All functions are pure and deterministic; they hold no state and never mutate inputs.
Class comparison is a total order P0 less than P1 less than P2 less than P3 less than P4, and flow rules are monotonic.
Adding a new class or sink is a breaking change requiring a new library major version.
The public surface is the TypeScript package; there are no relay or vault commands, queries or events.
Errors are returned as Result values with the codes in the errors table, and logging the redaction summary uses only counts and paths.
The package exposes a test helper assertSinkSafe(value, schema, sink) for module tests.
The library performs no authorization; callers decide the sink and viewer context and the library applies class rules to that context.
It has no ambient authority, meaning no network, storage or clock access.
Sink context must be passed explicitly; omitted context defaults to the most restrictive sink (public log).
Redaction is idempotent, so redacting an already redacted value returns the same value.
A failure to find a classification map fails closed with PRIVACY_CLASSIFICATION_MISSING and treats all fields as P4.
There is no shared mutable state, so concurrent calls cannot interfere.
The library never stores or logs input values; it logs only counts and paths of dropped fields.
Fail-closed defaults prevent new fields from leaking before review.
Hostile inputs such as deep nesting are bounded so redaction cannot be used for denial of service.
The library emits no telemetry; callers may count redactions locally and CI reports lint results.
Redaction of a typical record meets the latency budget on a mid-range phone.
CI reports the number of classified fields and unclassified findings.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
The sink matrix of this spec, which refines CTR-PRV-001, is tested exhaustively for all class and sink pairs.
Property and fuzz tests cover nesting, arrays and unknown paths.
Classification maps ship inside the schema registry and are part of each release; they hold no user data.
The export helper redactForExport is used by the export orchestrator to exclude P4, unclassified paths and other users' P2 and higher content.
A change to a field's class is a schema version change and is reviewed as a privacy change.
The catalog is a versioned YAML file (threats.yaml) plus rendered Markdown, with one entry per threat holding id, title, adversaries, assets, attack, controls, residual risk, tests and status.
Controls reference real requirement IDs of the form PS-NNN-pp.Rnn and test IDs of the form PRIVT-<area>-<nn>.
Entries are P0 documentation and contain no personal data or exploit code.
Every active threat entry must have at least one adversary, one control, one test and a non-empty residual-risk statement.
Control and test references must resolve to existing requirement IDs and test IDs.
The catalog must cover the mandatory topics list, and a topic without an active or retired entry fails the check.

The mandatory topics include cross-relay linkability (one DID on every relay, mailbox hints in public projections, key-linkage reads by host relays), enumeration and scraping of public indexes, and the integrity of signed privacy statements (replay, forgery, signer-role confusion, fork or equivocation).
Threat entries move from active to retired only with a recorded reason, never by deletion.
Each release candidate triggers a review task listing changed modules since the last review.
Accepting residual risk requires a named reviewer and date.
The module exposes no runtime commands, queries or events; its interface is the catalog file and the CI check command.
The CI check prints a table of threats with control and test counts and exits non-zero on any violation.
The check output is machine readable JSON in addition to text for the completeness report.
The catalog is public documentation readable by anyone; there is no runtime authorization.
Changes go through normal code review with at least one privacy reviewer approval recorded in the entry.
The CI check has no secrets and no network access.
The CI check is deterministic and idempotent for the same repository state.
A failing check blocks release; there is no override flag, only fixing the catalog or recording a retirement.
Review tasks are generated again if a release candidate is rebuilt, without duplicating entries.
The catalog contains no personal data, real user examples, credentials or working exploit details.
Attack descriptions are kept at the level needed to verify controls; sensitive details go to the security disclosure process (F16.S03.M03).
The model states limits honestly, namely that pseudonymity is not anonymity, relays see routing metadata, copies already fetched cannot be recalled.
The CI check reports counts of threats, controls and tests, and the age of the last review.
A review older than 90 days fails release candidate builds at once, while other builds warn on days 91 to 104 and fail from day 105.
The check runs within the CI time budget.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test of the check tool or a documented manual review step.
The mandatory topic list is verified by a fixture-based test.
Link integrity between the catalog and module specs is verified on the real repository in CI.
The catalog is exported as part of the documentation release bundle and the repository is its backup.
Importing a catalog from another fork runs the same check before acceptance.
Format changes are versioned with schemaVersion and old versions remain readable for 180 days.
The module owns no stored entity; it defines allowlist tables, the statement-type registry and draft value types keyed by envelope type string.
Allowed payload fields per type are listed in code and in the schema registry and each is annotated P0 by F10.S02.M02; a field without an annotation is not exportable.

Location is carried only as a geohash string of length ≤ 5 plus locationLevel L1 or L2, never coordinates; finer cells are snapped to their containing L2 cell before the F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell check.

The statement-type registry is static versioned data that names, for every registered envelope type, the audience, the signer role a receiving vault must verify before acting on the statement, how that role is resolved, the payload schema, the optional subject key and commitment predicate used by F11.S02.M03, and the maximum age used by F11.S01.M02 V08.

Relay roles resolve only through relay keys pinned in F11.S03.M01 or, for relay_identity roles, through the self-certifying relay key history of F15.S02.M01, and user roles only through the author principal's portable identity document (F07.S02.M01), so a relay key never satisfies a user role and a user key never satisfies a relay role.

Unregistered types, and registered types whose role cannot be resolved, are quarantined by receivers with FEDERATION_SIGNER_ROLE_INVALID; the registry check (V01) is separate from the portable-allowlist check (V08), which applies only to audience public portable types.

The StatementPublisherPort (publish and issueTombstone) is declared here and implemented by F11.S01.M02, so every producer (F01, F03, F07, F11.S03.*) signs through the single F11.S01.M02 path that allocates seq and prev, without a dependency cycle.

Every timestamp member of a public portable payload and the envelope createdAt are floored to the UTC hour with F10.S02.M03 publicTime (busy-block interval ends are raised to the next full hour so a busy interval never shrinks), and an author's records are ordered by the registry version member or the per-chain seq, never by time.

Every registry entry also names its acknowledger (counterparty, destination_relay or none) and the privacy class F10.S02.M02 registers for its payload schema, both read through entryFor(type) by the F15.S01.M01 sync outbox, and the compiled registry is exported as machine-readable data with one row per type.

roleFor(type, context) is the implementation of the F16.S01.M01 RoleResolverPort; the vault composition root injects it into F16.S01.M01 authorizeStatement, so F16.S01.M01 needs no dependency on this module and F11.S01.M02 calls only authorizeStatement.

Audience community addresses a statement to one hosting relay that serves it only to that relay's authenticated members; it is never indexed publicly, never sent relay to relay and never routed by F11.S02.M01, its owner module sends it to the hosting relay as a relay command, and its registry defaults are acknowledger destination_relay and privacy class P1.

Delegated roles resolve only through the injected delegations resolver over the publisher's verified authority lists (registered by F18.S02.M01) and relay operator context roles only through the injected operatorKeys resolver over the relay's latest verified tenant_config (registered by F15.S04.M03), both by inverted registration at composition without a depends_on edge, and a missing resolver, list or tenant_config resolves no role so the statement is quarantined with FEDERATION_SIGNER_ROLE_INVALID.
Outbound mapping is default-deny, so a new local field is never exported until it is added to an allowlist and reviewed.
Inbound payload validation uses the same allowlist and location rules and rejects unknown fields and any location finer than L2 instead of ignoring or trimming them.
Every rejection returns a stable code that the calling module surfaces without echoing field values.

Location precision is enforced on both paths through F06.S02.M01 assertPublicCell; outbound cells are snapped to L2 before the check (PRV-1) and inbound payloads with a cell longer than 5 characters or with coordinate members are rejected.

Outbound portable drafts carry no timestamp finer than the UTC hour, checked with F10.S02.M03 assertCoarseTime over the draft's declared timestamp members and createdAt after publicTime has floored them.
The mapper is stateless and the draft/mirror conversion is a pure function of its inputs.
The only sequencing rule is that a draft must be signed and stored through the F11.S01.M02 publish path (StatementPublisherPort) before it is visible to any peer.
No lifecycle is stored here, so there is no state machine.
The module exposes TypeScript functions only and no network commands or queries.
Functions return Result<T, AppError> and never include rejected field values in error params.
The module emits no events; draft building is a local pure step.

F11's own statement types and their signer roles are listed in the registry table of the domain schema (N2); other modules contribute entries for their own types, and every entry has an audience, signer role, role resolution, payload schema and maximum age.

The compiled registry is exported as machine-readable data (statement-registry.json) with one row per type {type, owner, audience, signerRole, roleResolution, payloadSchema, subjectKey?, version?, commitment?, maxAge, acknowledger, privacyClass, aliasOf?}, from which F17.S01.M03 generates one contract row per entry plus a wrong-role negative case.
roleFor(type, context) implements the F16.S01.M01 RoleResolverPort and is bound by the vault composition root; this module never calls authorizeStatement and stores no decision.
The library performs no authorization; callers (listing publication, profile settings, delivery) decide who may federate which record.

The opt-in flag is read from the source record at draft time and re-checked by F11.S01.M02 publish inside the signing transaction; an opt-in revoked after drafting refuses the publish with FEDERATION_NOT_OPTED_IN, and one revoked after signing cancels still-prepared deliveries through F11.S02.M01.
Mirror views contain only P0 data and may be shown to anonymous readers when the tenant has public browse enabled.
Draft building is deterministic for identical record and clock, so retries cannot create divergent drafts.
A failed draft leaves no state; the caller retries after fixing the record.
This module never allocates seq or prev; F11.S01.M02 publish allocates them in the transaction that stores the envelope, so a lost response never skips or duplicates a sequence number.
Only owner-opted-in P0 data at maximum precision L2 can leave the vault as a public projection; every other field is refused or the export refused.
Exact home address (P3), contact details and anything P1-P4 can never appear in a draft; tests assert this on every release.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity, so the consent preview states that all records of one did:key are linkable and that deletion propagates by tombstone but cannot recall copies.
Mapping outcomes are counted per rejection code without recording field values.
Building one draft takes under 1 ms p95 for a typical 4 KiB listing.
Allowlist and registry coverage is reported as a build artifact on every CI run.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
A privacy test suite enumerates every field of every source record type and proves non-allowlisted fields never appear in a draft.
Round-trip tests prove that a draft payload maps back to an equal mirror view.
The library stores nothing, so user export and import of federated content is handled by F11.S01.M02 and F11.S03.M03.
Allowlists and registry rows are versioned data; adding a field is a schema minor change and removing one is a major change with a 180-day dual-read period.
Rollback to a previous release must never widen an allowlist or relax a registry role, so a downgrade fails closed.

A FederatedRecord stores the full verified envelope, its cid, author, signer key, chain key (author, signer key, stream), seq, prev, type, audience, recipients and the local provenance object receivedFromRelay, receivedAt, via and verifiedAt, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

A Tombstone stores target (cid or record id), kind (author tombstone or relay_removal advisory), issuer kind, reason, statement of reasons for advisories, the signed envelope, appliedAt and a stub retention end of at least max(180 days, the target type's maxAge).

Public records are P0 read-only mirrors and participant records are statements decrypted from sealed mailbox envelopes and held only in the vaults of their participants; the record class is P2 because a vault holds participant statements, while a relay stores public-audience records only.

Mirrored records are read-only; purged content leaves only a stub with cid, record key, author, chain key, seq and purgedAt until the stub retention ends, and the stub still satisfies chain continuity for later records.

Chains are scoped per (author, signer key, stream), with stream pub for public projections and one stream per participant thread (thr:<id>), so two devices of one principal never fork each other and a recipient can always obtain every predecessor of its own thread.

A receiver with no head for a chain anchors at the first verified envelope at any seq and records chainAnchor and anchoredAt; the chain then detects equivocation and orders delivery but never gates acceptance.
Commitment statements are indexed by subject key and digest (FederatedRecord.subjectKey and promiseDigest); this promise index, owned here, is what F11.S02.M03 conflict detection reads.

Supersession of portable records uses the registry version member of the type (listingRevision, offering seq, rental offering revision) and otherwise the per-chain seq, never createdAt; a newer version of an already mirrored record is stored as a new FederatedRecord, the older one gets supersededBy, and federation.record.accepted fires for the newer one with recordKey, version and supersededRecordId.
Checks run cheapest first and blocklists run before anything is persisted, so a blocked peer, author or cid never reaches storage.
Inbound responses to peers never reveal which block rule matched; every blocklist hit returns the generic FEDERATION_NOT_ACCEPTED while the internal reason is logged and evented.
Every rule violation maps to exactly one stable code and the per-envelope outcome is returned in a results array in request order.

Authorship is proven by the signature and the registry role alone; no relay is bound to an author, the sending relay is provenance for display, and where to fetch an author's records comes from the relays listed in the author's portable identity document.

Payload checks depend on the audience; the portable allowlist and federation opt-in apply only to audience public portable types, control types use their registry schema, and participant statements are checked for ciphertext shape and size.

Revocation lag is judged by this vault's receipt time and never by createdAt; a statement received after the revocation arrived is refused with FEDERATION_SIGNER_ROLE_INVALID and kept in the quarantine list with reason signer_key_revoked, and accepted statements this vault first received inside [revocationEffectiveFrom, arrival of the revocation] are re-marked signed during claimed compromise and quarantined, with the effectiveFrom exactly as F07.S02.M01 reports it after the F16.S02.M02 clamp to at most 30 days before the earliest evidence.

Relay intake from a hosted vault key runs relay-local admission before indexing, in this order, failing closed with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE when a dependency cannot answer; privacy.consent.relay_check (F10.S01.M01) for the author's public portable records, tenant allowedCurrencies from F15.S04.M03 TenantPort, F12.S03.M04 moderation.accountlimit.check with limitKey index_writes_per_day, then F12.S02.M02 moderation.spam.evaluate in mode relay_intake over the projection text; tombstone, move and move_cancel statements are exempt so withdrawals always propagate.

Relay-to-relay inbox requests honour the F16.S03.M03 containment sentinel federation_off; a request whose keyid resolves to a peer relay receives FEATURE_DISABLED with params.reason federation_killed while requests from vault device keys hosted on the relay continue, and the sentinel is not a feature flag, so CTR-FLG-001 FLG-2 does not apply.
Envelopes move only along the declared FederatedRecord and Tombstone transitions; any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
A record becomes visible to readers only in status accepted; buffered, held_on_fork, hidden and quarantined records are never served.
Tombstoned, rejected and dropped are terminal, so a rejected envelope can only be reconsidered by a new submission and purged content cannot be restored; hidden is reversible and never purges.

Every non-terminal state has an exit; buffered records are released (with chainGap when predecessors never arrive), held_on_fork records follow the conflict resolution, and quarantined records are discarded, released, resolved or dropped after 30 days unless an open conflict holds them.
A pending tombstone is never applied without checking its issuer against the arriving target; a tombstone whose issuer does not match is rejected and the target accepted.

Accepted statements this vault first received inside [revocationEffectiveFrom, arrival of the revocation] move to quarantined with signerKeyMarker signed_during_claimed_compromise, and for commitment statements F11.S02.M03 opens a key_compromise conflict that freezes the dependent coordination in the same transaction.
The module exposes relay inbox ingest, vault receive, publish, tombstone issue, discard and release commands plus read queries with the signatures below.
Each command emits exactly the listed events in the same transaction as the state change, one event per envelope outcome.
The module consumes block, peer, conflict, migration, identity document, deletion and listing lifecycle events to keep mirrors consistent with policy.

When receive accepts a participants statement whose ext.recipients names the local principal, it signs a classrup.federation.ack/v1 over that exact cid on the same thread stream and stores it, so F11.S02.M01 routes it to the sender's mailbox; incoming acks are received like any statement and reach F11.S02.M01 through federation.record.accepted.

federation.record.publish and federation.tombstone.issue are the only signing path for the vault principal and the relay key; the listing and expiry consumers link an existing tombstoneCid and issue a tombstone only when none exists for that target, and the services.offering.withdrawn consumer is the only issuer of offering tombstones (F03.S01.M01 signs none), so one withdrawal never spends two seq numbers.

federation.record.accepted carries recordKey, version, supersededRecordId and the verification facts {signerDid, keyId, keyStatus, checkedAt} of the F07.S02.M01 key_status check, so F11.S02.M01 passes them to F15.S01.M01 platform.outbox.record_peer_ack and buyer and requester vaults see every newer projection (seq n+1 or a higher version) of a mirrored listing.

The relay inbox returns, per accepted envelope, a classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 from F15.S02.M01 ReceiptPort.issue (destination the relay's canonical relayId, digest over that envelope's exact bytes, cid), and this module registers a TombstoneSourcePort listSince(cursor) -> [{tombstoneCid, targetCid?, targetRecordKey?, receivedAt}] with the relay process for the F15.S03.M02 tombstone ledger (inverted registration, no depends_on edge).

Account deletion tombstones (reason account_deleted) are signed only in this module's DeletionPort sign step when F10.S01.M04 executes the deletion, and retained provenance is pseudonymized in its pseudonymize step; privacy.deletion.requested is not consumed, because nothing reversible is needed during grace, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).

Vault policy applies in the browser vault where only the unlocked local principal may publish statements, issue tombstones or discard quarantined statements, and received statements are accepted only when signed by a key authorized for the role.

Relay policy applies to the inbox where access requires a registered device key or an allowlisted peer relay; relay roles moderator and operator govern only what that relay hosts (CAP-9), so a relay operator issues removal advisories for its own index and never author tombstones.
Public mirror reads are open to anyone the relay or vault serves; provenance diagnostics are local-principal or relay-operator reads.
Ingest and receive are idempotent per envelope by cid, and relay requests also by batchId and Idempotency-Key, so senders may retry whole batches safely.
Each envelope is committed in its own transaction so one bad envelope never rolls back its valid neighbours, and results report each outcome.
A crash between storing a record and writing its local event cannot occur because both are written in one IndexedDB or SQLite transaction (EVT-8).

Seq and prev of own statements are allocated inside the transaction that stores the signed envelope under the unique (author, signerKey, stream, seq) index, so two producers in one vault can never take the same head+1 and two devices of one principal write to different chains.

Sync state shown for an own statement never exceeds the state reached; it is local committed until F15.S01.M01 records a verified relay receipt (transport_acknowledged) and peer accepted only with a verified signed acknowledgement from a recipient.

Only P0 data at L2 or coarser is ever stored on relays or federated relay to relay; participant statements travel only as sealed mailbox envelopes {v, mailboxId, ciphertext, size, sentAt} through F08.S01.M01, so relays see no author, type, seq or claimed time of participant traffic, and exact home addresses never exist in this module.
Provenance must not leak user metadata, so peers receive neither reader identity nor IP addresses, and media is fetched by the relay and served locally rather than hot-linked.

Author tombstones remove content within 24 h of receipt and their stubs are kept at least max(180 days, the target type's maxAge); relay_removal advisories remove content only from the issuing relay's index; this is deletion propagation, not recall (PRV-6), and the UI states before withdrawal that peers who copied content earlier may keep it.

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort for own statements, tombstones and the quarantine list; DeletionPort whose sign step signs account_deleted tombstones for own records at deletion execution, whose pseudonymize step pseudonymizes retained provenance and whose purge step deletes mirrors; RetentionPurgePort for the sweeps), classifies fields with F10.S02.M02 and calls privacy.consent.check(federation_publish) before publishing public statements; privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).

In the vault, statements from a DID blocked in either direction (F07.S02.M02 isBlockedEither) are dropped silently, with no ack, no event and the same outcome a sender sees for an unanswered statement (N7).
On relays, every ingest outcome is counted; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7) and keeps the same counters in local diagnostics that the user may export.
Every ingest outcome is counted by outcome and code, and purge timeliness is measured against the 24 h tombstone deadline.
A batch of 100 envelopes is processed with p95 ≤ 800 ms at 10 batches per second on the reference relay.
Alerts fire when purge lag exceeds 1 h, when buffered records exceed 5000, or when a peer's rejection ratio exceeds 20 percent over 15 minutes.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
An adversarial suite covers forged provenance, replay, flood, fork, pre-emptive tombstones, relay takedown attempts and metadata leakage against a two-relay, two-vault test harness.
Contract tests validate envelopes, results, events and mirror views against the schema registry, the CTR-FED-001 vectors and the shared golden envelopes of F11.S01.M03.

A user's export contains the user's own federation settings, own signed statements with their chain keys and the tombstones they issued; mirrored third-party records are not part of a personal export.

Operator export and relay import re-verify every envelope signature and re-apply tombstones before records become readable; the owner's own vault import and restore re-verify signatures but are exempt from the V08 age limit.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
The library owns no stored entities; its value types are Envelope, Cid, DidKey and RequestSignature, all defined by CTR-FED-001.

The signed bytes are exactly the RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 serialization of the envelope object with the sig member removed (the cid member stays, so the cid is signed), and the cid is "sha256-" + unpadded base64url of SHA-256 over the JCS bytes of the envelope with both sig and cid removed; this is the only normative definition and the golden vectors in tests/fixtures/federation/envelope-golden.json are shared with F11.S01.M02, F11.S01.M01 and F07.S02.M01.
Keys and signatures are fixed-size binary types with enforced lengths of 32 bytes (public key), 64 bytes (signature) and 32 bytes (SHA-256 digest).

The verification key of an envelope is ext.signerKey when present (a device did:key of the author principal) and otherwise the author did:key itself (a principal root key or a relay key); verifyEnvelope returns {cid, author, signerKey} and never decides delegation.
Every input is validated before cryptographic work to keep verification cost bounded and failure codes stable.
Envelope size is capped at 262144 bytes of canonical JSON and nesting depth at 32 to bound CPU use.
Each rule violation maps to one stable error code so callers can count and rate-limit by cause.

Request signatures follow RFC 9421 with the covered components @method, @target-uri (including the destination authority), content-digest (RFC 9530) and the parameters created, keyid and nonce (batchId for inbox batches); verification checks the created window of ±300 s, the digest, the ed25519 signature over the signature base and that (keyid, nonce) was not seen in the last 600 s; resolveKey covers peer relay keys (F11.S03.M01) and device keys (F07.S02.M01 portable document).
Received envelope text is parsed by a strict parser that rejects duplicate member names, so every implementation canonicalizes exactly the same object.

The ext member of a received envelope is preserved byte-exact, is at most 4096 bytes of canonical JSON, and every member named in ext.crit must be understood by the reader (the injected understood-extension set from the F11.S01.M01 registered ext members), otherwise the envelope is refused with VALIDATION_FAILED.

Device-to-relay requests use the profile tag="classrup/relay-request/v1" and must carry the parameters created, expires (at most created + 300 s), keyid, nonce and tag over @method, @target-uri and content-digest; relay-to-relay requests use the FED-10 profile and, when they carry expires, it is also at most created + 300 s.
The library is stateless and every call is a pure function of its arguments and an injected clock.
Verification is a fixed pipeline with no hidden state, so the same input always yields the same Result.
There is no lifecycle to model, so no machine is declared.
The module exposes functions, not network commands, and therefore has no capability-guarded commands or queries.
Function signatures return Result<T, AppError> per CTR-ERR-001 and never throw for bad input.
The module emits no events; callers record the outcome of verification in their own events.
This module is the single owner of the envelope and signature error codes; F11.S01.M02, F11.S02.*, and F11.S03.* reference them by listing F11.S01.M03 in depends_on and never redefine them (N1).

This module is the single owner of the JCS, strict Ed25519, did:key and RFC 9421 request-signature primitives; F16.S02.M03 builds its domain-separated envelopes and the classrup/relay-request/v1 tag inventory on them and has no canonicalizer, Ed25519 or did:key implementation of its own.

The library runs in the vault under the unlocked local principal and on relays under relay policy, and has no roles of its own; authorization of who may submit or accept envelopes is enforced by the modules that call it.
The relay private key is readable only by the relay signing service and never exposed through any API or log.
The module must not read any user private key; device keys are passed in by on-device callers only.
All functions are deterministic and side-effect free, so repeating a call is always safe.
Verification never partially succeeds; a Result is either Ok with the verified cid, author and signer key or Err with one code.
Clock skew handling is explicit through an injected now parameter and a fixed 300 s tolerance for request created times.
Private key material is never logged, serialized into errors or included in metrics labels.
The library emits no telemetry from the PWA (OBS-7); counters are kept locally for diagnostics and exported only by the user.
Verification cost is bounded so that malformed envelopes cannot be used to exhaust relay CPU.
did:key values are pseudonymous identifiers, not anonymous; this module documents that a did:key links all records of one author.
Verification outcomes and latencies are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without logging keys or payloads.
Verification of one typical 4 KiB envelope meets a p95 budget of 2 ms on the reference relay CPU.
A batch of 100 envelopes verifies in under 250 ms on a single worker.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Conformance is proven with public vectors (RFC 8785 appendix, RFC 8032 section 7.1, RFC 9421 appendix B ed25519 and RFC 9530) and the shared golden envelopes, run in CI on Node and Chromium.
Property tests prove sign-then-verify round trip and rejection of any single-bit mutation.
The library stores nothing, so there is no export, import or backup of its own.
Envelopes created by any past release must keep verifying; the signed-bytes and cid definitions are frozen for envelope v=1.
A change to canonicalization or hashing requires a new envelope version number and never alters v=1 behavior.
A ConflictRecord stores the author, subject, conflict kind, class (public_projection or commitment), up to 5 candidate cids with provenance, status, resolution and freeze scope.

Commitment ConflictRecords are P2, visible only to the vault owner, never leave the vault by themselves and appear in logs as IDs only; public_projection ConflictRecords are the only kind a relay holds and are visible to that relay's operator.
Candidate claimed times are stored as claims and relay receipt times as evidence of that relay's clock only.
Commitment conflict predicates and subject keys come from the F11.S01.M01 registry, and the promise index they are evaluated against is the FederatedRecord subject index owned by F11.S01.M02.

A key_compromise ConflictRecord holds exactly one candidate, a commitment statement this vault first received inside [revocationEffectiveFrom, arrival of the revocation] of its signer key, freezes that statement's subject like a commitment conflict and closes only by drop_all or superseded by a statement re-signed with a current key by every required signer.
A conflict is opened only from verified envelopes, so unsigned or invalid statements can never freeze a trade.
Resolution input is validated against the candidate set and the caller's authority.
Each violation maps to one stable error code.

A commitment conflict accepts only drop_all, which releases the freeze locally and cancels the dependent coordination, or superseded by a renegotiated statement whose digest every required signer of the registry entry has signed; keeping one candidate is refused.
A relay operator may resolve only public_projection conflicts on that relay.
Conflicts move only along the declared transitions and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.

Public projections may auto-resolve after 7 days by the origin-wins policy based on the author's portable identity document; commitments may only be released locally by drop_all or superseded by a statement every required signer signed.
Resolution is recorded permanently and never rewrites the signed candidates.

The freeze takes effect in the receive transaction that detects the conflict, and domain modules check is_frozen synchronously before acting, so the freeze never fails open while events are in transit.
The module exposes detect, resolve and read operations plus the synchronous is_frozen check; detect is an internal vault or relay command and resolve is a review action.
Each command emits its events in the same local transaction as the state change.

The module consumes account move, identity document and peer suspension events to recompute the author's listed relays and review windows; retained evidence is pseudonymized only in its DeletionPort pseudonymize step, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only that never triggers pseudonymization (N6a).

Domain modules that act on commitments (F01.S04.M01 offers, F02 proposals, F01.S03.M01 reservations, F08.S02.M02 consent, F09 deals, F11.S03.M03 moves) consume federation.conflict.detected and resolved and call is_frozen before acting; these are N-note obligations recorded for their owners.
In the vault only the unlocked local principal may resolve conflicts; on a relay only that relay's operator may, and only public_projection conflicts.
Detection is an internal capability granted only to F11.S01.M02 and F11.S03.M03 code paths, never to external requests.
Conflict records are visible only to the owner of the vault or the operator of the hosting relay; others receive NOT_FOUND.
Detect is idempotent per (author, chain key, seq) or subject so repeated arrivals append at most new candidates and never open duplicates.
Resolve requires expectedRevision and is idempotent on identical replay.
A crash between opening a conflict and writing the event cannot lose the freeze because both are in one local transaction with the quarantine of the candidates.
Conflict records hold cids, provenance and public payload diffs only; commitment conflicts reference participant statements by cid, never store plaintext and never exist on a relay.
A relay operator sees only public projections and therefore resolves only public_projection conflicts on that relay.
Attackers must not be able to freeze someone else's trade with unsigned or role-less statements.

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort, RetentionPurgePort) and classifies fields with F10.S02.M02; its DeletionPort pseudonymize step (pseudonymize(ctx{requestId, pseudonym}), the only call that receives the pseudonym) replaces the deleted principal's DID in retained RET-EVIDENCE conflict records, its purge step deletes the open commitment records of that principal's own vault, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).
Forks are attributed to the author; after 20 open conflicts the author's further envelopes are quarantined, and forwarding relays are never penalized for an author's equivocation.
Open conflicts, age and resolution decisions are measured on relays and kept as local diagnostics in the vault.
Detect and resolve meet write budget p95 ≤ 300 ms.
An alert fires on a relay when any public_projection conflict is open longer than 8 days or more than 50 are open.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
A two-vault and two-relay harness reproduces fork, prev mismatch and commitment conflicts.
Contract tests validate commands, events and ConflictRecord against the registry schemas.
A vault export contains conflict records with candidate cids and decisions; the candidate envelopes themselves are exported by F11.S01.M02.
Import re-verifies every candidate signature and keeps open conflicts open, restoring their freeze before any domain action is allowed.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and v1 stays readable for 180 days.

The module owns no entity; its inputs are an Envelope, the ChainHead of its chain key (author, signerKey, stream) or none, the known cids and stored neighbours of that chain, buffer counts per author, source and tenant, and the open conflict candidates, and its output is a Decision value type.

The chain rule follows CTR-FED-001 per chain key (seq starts at 1, prev is the cid of the previous seq of the same chain and is absent only at seq 1), but a receiver with no head anchors at whatever seq it first sees.

The buffer limits are constants of this module (24 h window, gap 100, 50 per author with history, 5 per freshly anchored author, 500 per source, 5000 total of which at most 1000 for freshly anchored authors) so every relay and vault behaves identically.

Chains detect equivocation and do not gate acceptance; forks are detected only on (author, signerKey, stream, seq) collisions or prev mismatches with stored neighbours, and every other verified envelope is eventually accepted.
Decisions are deterministic functions of (envelope, chain view, buffer counts, open conflicts, now).
Out-of-range inputs are rejected before any state is considered.
Each rejection maps to one stable code so peers and users see consistent reasons.

Buffer capacity is shared fairly; caps apply per source and per author, freshly anchored authors use a bounded share, and eviction starts with the source that exceeds its cap, so a Sybil flood cannot refuse legitimate out-of-order envelopes.
A predecessor older than its type's maxAge, or one that was tombstoned, is used only as a continuity stub (cid, seq, prev; no content stored), so the F11.S01.M02 age limit never blocks a chain.
The library has no state of its own; the lifecycle of a buffered or held envelope is the FederatedRecord machine of F11.S01.M02.
Decision precedence is fixed as duplicate, then held_on_fork, then fork, then anchor, then next, then backfill, then reanchor, then buffer.
The decision for a given input never depends on arrival order of unrelated authors.
The module exposes pure functions only and no vault, relay or network commands.
Functions return Result<Decision, AppError> and never throw for bad input.
No events are emitted; the caller turns decisions into events.
The library has no roles; it is called by F11.S01.M02 after authorization and signature checks.
It never reads secrets and holds no keys.
Callers must not call decide() on unverified envelopes; the API requires a VerifiedEnvelope type so this is enforced by types.
Calling decide() repeatedly with the same inputs returns the same decision, so retries are safe.
Draining is idempotent since releasing an envelope already accepted yields duplicate.
Failures leave no partial state because the library writes nothing.
The module reads only cids, authors, signer keys, streams, seq and prev, never payloads, so it cannot leak content.

Buffer caps per author, per source and per tenant, the bounded share of freshly anchored authors and offending-source eviction cap the memory an attacker can pin with forged future seq numbers or Sybil authors.
Retention of buffered envelopes is at most 24 h, after which they are released with chainGap rather than kept or silently dropped.
Decision counts are exposed per kind so operators can see duplicate ratios and buffer pressure.
decide() has a p95 budget of 0.2 ms excluding storage lookups.
Buffer occupancy is a gauge and alerts when above 80 percent of 5000.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Property tests prove convergence of any arrival permutation of a valid chain at a fresh receiver and rejection of every splice.
Boundary tests cover each numeric limit at limit and limit plus one.
The library stores no data, so export, import and backup of chain heads and buffers belong to F11.S01.M02.
Importing a vault or relay backup must rebuild each chain head by running verifyChain() over stored envelopes before ingest resumes.
The limits are constants of the envelope v=1 protocol; changing them requires a new release note and does not alter stored data.

A PeerOutbox entry (relay only) stores the envelope cid, the destination peer relay as its canonical F15.S02.M01 relayId, state, attempt counters, next attempt time, last error code, the sent digest and the classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 receipt, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001; vault-side deliveries are F15.S01.M01 OutboxEntry rows whose destination descriptor this module defines.
Entries hold references to envelopes stored by F11.S01.M02 and never copies of payloads, so deleting a record purges its queued delivery content.
Receipt times are stored as evidence of the issuing relay's clock only and are labelled so in the UI.

Vault outbox states and limits (7-day unsent expiry, 30-day acknowledgement wait, attempt counts and the prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted states of IDM-7) are owned by F15.S01.M01; this module's transport adapter only reports receipts, per-envelope outcomes and acknowledgements to it.

PeerOutbox is limited to relay-to-relay forwarding (destinationKind peer_relay) and is not a vault outbox; it uses the F15.S01.M01 state names where the meaning is the same (prepared, transport_acknowledged, failed) plus the relay-only states delivered, paused and cancelled, and its receipts are classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 statements verified like F15.S01.M01 V14.
An entry is created only for a statement stored locally with a valid signature whose audience matches the destination kind (public to selected or peer relays, participants to recipient mailboxes).
Receipts and acknowledgements are verified before they change state, so a relay cannot claim recipient acceptance.
Each rule violation maps to one stable error code.
Public statements are routed and dispatched to a relay only after privacy.consent.check(federation_publish) for that relay, and a failed or unavailable check fails closed.
Participant statements leave the vault only through the MailboxPort as sealed wrappers, and recipient mailbox routes are re-resolved after a recipient moves.
Relay forwarding of a hosted author's public records is gated by F10.S01.M01 privacy.consent.relay_check, while tombstones, move and move_cancel are always forwarded so withdrawals propagate.

Outbound relay-to-relay delivery honours the F16.S03.M03 containment sentinel federation_off by pausing peer entries, which stay queued for at most 7 days; vault-to-relay delivery is unaffected and the sentinel is not a feature flag, so CTR-FLG-001 FLG-2 does not apply.
PeerOutbox entries advance only along prepared, transport_acknowledged and delivered, and never move backward or skip a state they did not reach.
Delivered, failed and cancelled are terminal and every entry is terminal by its expiresAt; failed entries can be re-queued only by creating a new entry through an operator retry.

The UI renders each vault delivery state only through the F15.S01.M01 shared catalog keys sync.state.<value>, which claim no more than the state proves; a relay receipt shows sync.state.completed for a public statement or sync.state.transport_acknowledged for a participants statement, and only a verified recipient acknowledgement shows sync.state.peer_accepted.
Paused entries resume on federation.peer.reinstated or when flag F11 turns on, and are cancelled on federation.peer.removed or at expiry.

A verified relay restore announcement of the destination peer that covers an entry's receipt returns a transport_acknowledged entry to prepared and re-queues a delivered entry as a new prepared entry, both resent under the same cid.

The module exposes enqueue, retry, cancel, acknowledge and dispatch commands, the relay pull query and the relay queue list, plus the vault transport adapter called by F15.S01.M01, with the signatures below.

Commands that send data produce no new signed statement except the signed request itself; acknowledgements are signed by F11.S01.M02 receive in the recipient's vault, and the statements delivered were signed earlier by their authors.
The module consumes record, tombstone, peer, migration, identity document, consent and flag events to keep the queue consistent with policy.
On a relay, only public records and author tombstones accepted from a hosted device key are forwarded to peers, one hop, and records received from a peer are never forwarded.
Recipient mailbox delivery goes through the MailboxPort implemented by F08.S01.M01 comms.mailbox.put, never through POST /fed/v1/inbox.

The vault pulls the user's own mailboxes only through MailboxPort.fetch, hands each envelope to F11.S01.M02 federation.record.receive with source mailbox and calls MailboxPort.ack after the receive committed; each put carries a sender put proof signed by this device's key (V15).

federation.delivery.failed is emitted for relay PeerOutbox entries that fail or expire and for vault F15.S01.M01 federation entries that reach failed or expired, once per entry, so consumers such as F08.S01.M03 can delete attachment blobs of messages that were never delivered.
federation.outbox.acknowledge passes the verification facts {signerDid, keyId, keyStatus, checkedAt} that F11.S01.M02 recorded for the verified ack to F15.S01.M01 platform.outbox.record_peer_ack.
In the vault only the unlocked local principal routes and acknowledges its statements; vault outbox commands (resolve, discard) belong to F15.S01.M01.
On a relay, dispatch and pull are authorized by relay policy for allowlisted peers and registered device keys, and the relay operator may read queue statistics, retry and cancel entries.
Queue contents of one vault are never visible to other vaults or to relay operators beyond cid prefix and destination.
Sending is at least once and receivers deduplicate by cid, so a repeated batch is harmless.
Every batch carries a batchId used as the Idempotency-Key and as the RFC 9421 nonce, so a retried request returns the original results and a captured request is never processed twice.
Local commit comes first; a failed or unreachable destination never rolls back the local record.
Only the audience declared by the owner is delivered; participant statements travel only as sealed wrappers to listed mailboxes and public statements only if the owner opted in at L2 or coarser.

Delivery metadata leaks as little as possible, so batches contain no reader or device identifiers, relay-to-relay pushes add 0 to 5 s random delay, sealed wrappers carry no author, type or seq, and logs hold cid prefixes only.
The UI states before a delivered statement is withdrawn that tombstoning it cannot recall copies already fetched (PRV-6).

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort for relay operator export of PeerOutbox and the vault's recipient routes, DeletionPort that cancels routes of a deleted principal, RetentionPurgePort for terminal entries) and classifies fields with F10.S02.M02.
On relays, queue depth, age, outcome and latency per destination are exported as metrics; the PWA sends no telemetry and shows the same numbers in local diagnostics.
Dispatching a batch of 100 envelopes costs p95 ≤ 500 ms of local work excluding network time.
Alerts fire when the oldest prepared entry is older than 15 min or the failure ratio per peer exceeds 20 percent over 15 minutes.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Chaos tests simulate relay outages, duplicated batches and partial batch failure.
Contract tests validate request, response, receipt and acknowledgement shapes against the registry schemas.
Relay operator export includes PeerOutbox entries; the vault outbox is exported by F15.S01.M01 and this module exports only the vault's recipient routes.
Import restores non-terminal PeerOutbox entries as prepared and relies on receiver dedup for any envelope that was already delivered.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and v1 stays readable for 180 days.
A BlockRule stores type, value, action, reason, source, optional publisher list reference, optional expiry and status with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Local block lists are private to the vault owner or relay operator and are classed P3 because a person's block list is sensitive.
Values are exact matches only (relay id, did:key, cid, content hash), with no patterns or regular expressions.

A content_hash value is either the SHA-256 of JCS(payload) in the sha256- form or the N9 MediaBlob id of a referenced blob in the blob:sha256- form, both computed by F11.S01.M02 before it calls evaluate.
