Rule input is validated strictly against the schema and value formats per type.
Imports are bounded and signature-checked before any entry is shown for review.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.
Statements that propagate deletion or moves (classrup.federation.tombstone/v1, move/v1 and move_cancel/v1) bypass author and cid rules, while peer rules still apply to them.
Rules follow the declared lifecycle and any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Imported rules cannot reach active without an explicit review decision by the owner or operator.
Expired and removed are terminal so history of what was blocked remains auditable.
Local rules start active when created by add or by a personal block, imported rules start pending_review, and each creation path is a declared transition.
The module exposes add, import, review, enable, disable, remove and publish commands plus list and evaluate queries.
Each command states whether it is vault-local, produces a signed statement or is a relay command, and emits its events in the same transaction.
The module consumes the personal block events to keep federated content hidden consistently with the user's block list, and the deletion event to remove a deleted principal's rules.

The meaning of each action on stored records is defined by F11.S01.M02; reject refuses at ingest and purges stored matches, and hide stores but never serves matched records and is undone when the rule is disabled, removed or expires.
In a vault only the unlocked local principal manages rules; on a relay only that relay's operator does, with an audit entry.
Evaluate is an internal capability for the verified receive and delivery pipelines and is not exposed to external requests.
Rules are never readable by other users or other relays unless the owner publishes a list on purpose.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Imports are all-or-nothing so a failed import leaves no partial pending rules.
Evaluation uses an in-memory snapshot refreshed in the same transaction as every rule change, so a restart cannot lose an active rule.
A person's block list is P3 and never leaves the vault except when the person publishes a selected list deliberately.
Rejections caused by block rules return one generic code so senders cannot probe which rules exist.
Imported lists are advisory and bounded; they can never silence a person on a relay without that relay's operator review.

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort for the owner's rules, DeletionPort whose purge step deletes the principal's local and personal_block rules and which retains nothing to pseudonymize, RetentionPurgePort for removed rules after 30 days) and classifies fields with F10.S02.M02; privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).
Rule counts and match counts are exported on relays and kept in local diagnostics in the vault; the PWA sends no telemetry.
Evaluate adds at most 0.5 ms p95 to ingest.
An alert fires when a relay's matched-reject ratio exceeds 50 percent over 15 minutes, signalling a misconfigured rule.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Tests prove that block rules are applied before storage and that imports never self-activate.
Contract tests validate commands, the blocklist statement and events against registry schemas.
A vault export contains the owner's rules for the owner only, never in any shared or federated section.
Import of rules from another vault or from an export keeps local rules as written and returns imported-source rules to pending_review.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and v1 stays readable for 180 days.

A MigrationRecord stores kind, subject, from and to relay, the move statement cid, the claimed announcement time, this receiver's first verified receipt and computed effective time, redirect end, status, copy progress and direction (own or observed) with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
The move statement is a public signed statement and carries only did, relay ids, base URLs and times; it never contains record contents or contact details.
The redirect period is 180 days, equal to the minimum tombstone stub retention, so a moved author cannot be resurrected on the old relay by replay.

A move is valid only when signed by a device key that the subject's latest verified portable document lists as active at the receiver's time of evaluation, and when all timing, key-age and cool-down rules hold.
Observed moves from others are verified exactly like own moves and ignored otherwise.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

The veto window is measured on each receiver's own clock from its first verified receipt (or the old relay's signed receipt time), never from the claimed announcedAt, so a backdated move is still held for a full 24 h and can be vetoed.
A relay move signed by a key other than the pinned relay key is dropped and counted only against the sender that signed the delivering request, never against the relay it names.
A move advances prepared, announced and effective and may be cancelled only before it becomes effective.
The redirect and the switch of the author's fetch hints start only at effective, never at announce, and no acceptance rule depends on them.
Closed and cancelled are terminal; a later move creates a new record.
Conflicting move statements for one subject open a commitment conflict in F11.S02.M03 through detect, hold both moves and activate no redirect until the conflict is resolved.
The module exposes prepare, copy, announce, cancel and receive commands plus status and redirect queries with the signatures below.
Each command states whether it is vault-local, produces a signed statement or is a relay command, and emits its events in the same transaction.
Only a verified move that became effective on this receiver emits federation.account.moved, and observers act on it only after their own verification.

Move statements and signer roles are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2): classrup.federation.move/v1 signed by a device key of the subject (relay moves by the pinned relay key) and classrup.federation.move_cancel/v1 signed by a device key of the subject, a veto by a key other than the move signer; both are signed through F11.S01.M02 publish.
Only the unlocked local principal can prepare, copy, announce or cancel an own move, and only with a device key listed active in its portable document.
Any device key of the principal other than the signer may veto during the window.
The redirect lookup is public, and observed moves are accepted by any vault or relay only after verification.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
The copy step is resumable and re-sends only entries without a receipt, relying on cid dedup at the new relay.
A failure before effective leaves the old relay as the user's selected delivery relay and the vault untouched; no relay is authoritative for the principal's records.
A move statement reveals the old and new relay of a pseudonymous did:key, which is public by design and stated in the wizard.

A stolen device key must not silently move an account, so a 24 h veto window on each receiver's clock, a 24 h minimum key age and a 30-day cool-down limit the damage, and the UI says when only one device key exists and no veto is possible.
The move never transfers private data between relays; the vault re-establishes mailboxes and encrypted material itself.

During a deletion grace period the module takes only reversible actions, so copy and announce of the open own migration are refused with PRIVACY_DELETION_PENDING through privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending and continue unchanged after privacy.deletion.cancelled, while cancelling the migration and signing its move_cancel happen only in the DeletionPort sign step at execution.

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort for the migration history, DeletionPort, RetentionPurgePort for RET-EVIDENCE records) and classifies fields with F10.S02.M02; its DeletionPort sign step cancels the open own migration and signs move_cancel for an announced one, its pseudonymize step (pseudonymize(ctx{requestId, pseudonym}), the only call that receives the pseudonym) replaces the principal's DID in retained own MigrationRecords, and privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).
Moves, vetoes and failures are counted on relays and shown in local diagnostics in the vault; the PWA sends no telemetry.
Redirect lookup meets read budget p95 ≤ 150 ms.
Alerts fire on a relay when more than 5 vetoes occur in 24 h or when a copy step stays incomplete for 24 h.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Security tests cover stolen key, backdated announcement, forged move, replay and veto race.
A documentation check verifies that bridge mappings exist and are labelled Future.
A vault export carries the data needed to restart on another relay, namely public records, tombstones and the move history, and never private keys.
Import on a new relay is performed by sending the exported statements through the normal verified inbox path, so no special trust is created.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and v1 stays readable for 180 days.

A Peer stores identity (relay id and did:key), URL, kind, proposal origin, opt-in flags for both sides, trust level, quotas, health score and status, and for selected relays whether the user lists it in the identity document, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Peer records are relay-local or vault-local operational data classed P1 and are never federated or exported to other users.
The pinned key history keeps the current and the previous key for 7 days so rotation can overlap without accepting arbitrary keys.
Peer input is validated strictly; unknown fields are rejected and URLs are checked on every connection, not only at creation.
Activation needs verified statements from both sides (for a selected relay, the relay's signed identity and hosting-policy statement) and a recorded fingerprint confirmation.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

Unsolicited peer offers are bounded; each is at most 8 KiB, at most 5 per day are accepted per source IP prefix and per relay id, each is verified before it is stored, and unanswered ones expire after 14 days.
A peer activates only when both sides opted in, and suspension or removal takes effect on the next request.
Suspended peers keep their pinned key and history and can be reinstated by an explicit action, never automatically.
Removed and expired are terminal; peering again creates a new Peer record.

The handshake has an inbound path on both sides; a verified peer_offer creates or merges an inbound proposed Peer that needs operator action, and a verified peer_accept matching the offer cid activates the proposer once its fingerprint is confirmed.
The module exposes propose, receive_offer, accept, receive_accept, suspend, reinstate, remove and update commands plus list, get and resolve queries.
Each command states whether it is vault-local, produces a signed statement, or is a relay command, and emits its events in the same local transaction.
The module consumes rejection, conflict and delivery failure events to maintain health scores for relay-attributable faults only, plus the flag and deletion events.

Health penalties apply only to relay-attributable faults (invalid signatures, cids or canonical forms it forwarded, invalid request signatures, forwarding traffic relays never forward, quota breaches, receipts it signed that contradict each other, and equivocation signed by its own relay key); author forks, local-policy rejections and gap or buffer codes never change a peer's health.

Peer statements and signer roles are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2); peer_offer by the proposing relay key, peer_accept by the accepting relay key, key_rotation by the current pinned key and relay_identity by the relay key it names, all signed through the StatementPublisherPort.

Every pinned relay key change is published as a local event: federation.peer.added carries the pinned relayKey and federation.peer.key_rotated {peerId, relayId, kind, oldRelayKey, newRelayKey, effectiveAt, previousKeyUntil} is emitted in the transaction that applies a verified rotation statement, so consumers (F16.S02.M02 peer key pins, F07.S03.M02 relay attestations) never wait for a periodic refresh.
In a vault only the unlocked local principal manages the selected-relay list.
On a relay only that relay's operator manages peers, and every change is written to the relay audit log.
resolve_key is internal to F11.S01.M02 and F11.S02.M01 code paths and not exposed to external requests.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Quota counters are updated in the same transaction as the acceptance they count, so a crash cannot grant free capacity.
If peer data cannot be read, requests fail closed with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE rather than accepting traffic.
Peer records contain no user data; they hold relay identity, quotas and health only.

A user's selected relays are vault data; only relays the user marks 'List in my identity document' (at most 5) are published in the portable identity document (F07.S02.M01, P0, readable by anyone who holds the document), unlisted relays are never shared with other users or relays, and the user is told which metadata a relay can observe (mailbox ID, size, time, IP).
Pseudonymity is not anonymity, so the relay chooser states that a relay sees the IP address of connecting devices and the did:key of each author.

The module registers the N6 ports (ExportSectionPort for the selected-relay list, DeletionPort whose purge step deletes the principal's selected-relay list and which retains nothing to pseudonymize, RetentionPurgePort for RET-AUDIT peers) and classifies fields with F10.S02.M02; privacy.deletion.completed is a notification only (N6a).
Peer status counts, health scores and quota use are exported on relays; the PWA keeps the same information in local diagnostics only.
resolve_key and quota check add at most 2 ms p95 to inbox handling.
Alerts fire on any automatic suspension and on health below 60 for an active peer.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Security tests cover SSRF, key substitution, health-based suspension, unsolicited offers and opt-in on both sides.
Contract tests validate commands, statements, events and the Peer record against registry schemas.
A vault export contains the user's selected relays and their listing choice without secrets; an operator export contains peers with keys and quotas.
Imported peers never become active automatically; they import as proposed or suspended and need fresh opt-in confirmation.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and v1 stays readable for 180 days.

An Appeal stores the contested action reference, appellant key, statement, optional attachments, reviewer key (relay copy only), status with moot reason, outcome with reasons, rule IDs, typed reduced outcome and sync state, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Appeals are P2 between appellant and the relay's moderators and retained under RET-EVIDENCE with the action they contest.
An appeal is immutable after filing except for assignment, status and decision fields written by the relay and verified by the vault.
The reduced outcome is typed as reducedTo { kind, expiresAt?, restrictedCapabilities? } and is never more severe, longer or broader than the contested action.
Appeal input is validated strictly and the appellant must be the subject of the contested action.
The 30-day window is computed from the relay-signed statement of reasons time, never from the appellant's clock.
Decisions require a reviewer whose principal differs from the decider, the subject and every reporter of linked reports, a reasoned text and at least one policy rule ID.
The relay accepts an appeal only when its signed relayId is the receiving relay, and deduplicates appealId for as long as it retains the appeal.
Appeals follow the declared lifecycle and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Assignment requires an eligible reviewer and otherwise leaves the appeal awaiting_reviewer with an honest notice.
A decision is final for that relay; overturned and reduced outcomes emit the decided event that makes F12.S02.M01 revert or replace the action.

An appeal on an action that a moderator reverts or that expires before a decision closes as moot with mootReason action_reverted or action_expired, receives a relay-signed moot notice, is never labelled overturned and emits no decided event.

An appeal in review returns to awaiting_reviewer when an operator unassigns the reviewer, the reviewer loses the moderator role, or the day-10 escalation passes without a decision, and reassignment runs immediately.
Every command declares whether it is vault-local, a signed statement or a relay command, and the signatures below do so.

Receive emits moderation.appeal.filed on the relay after it verifies the signed statement, decide emits moderation.appeal.decided, and the appellant's vault derives its own moderation.appeal.decided from the verified decision statement (EVT-9).

The module consumes action events to open the 30-day window and to close open appeals as moot when the action is reverted by a moderator or expires, and consumes role revocations to reassign reviewers.

Statements are classrup.moderation.appeal/v1 and appealwithdrawal/v1 (signed by the appellant) and appealreceipt/v1, appealstatus/v1, appealdecision/v1 and appealmoot/v1 (signed by the relay key only).

The outcome enum (upheld, overturned, reduced) and the origin enum (relay, vault) of moderation.appeal.decided, and the relay-local moderation.appeal.filed event, are a stable v1 vocabulary bound by the F18.S02.M02 transparency dimensions appeals_filed and appeals_decided and its contract test T22; moot closures never produce moderation.appeal.decided, and adding, renaming or removing a value is a breaking change that needs a new major event schema (CTR-SCH-001 SCH-3) coordinated with F18.S02.M02.

Vault policy: only the local principal can file, withdraw and read its appeals, and incoming receipts, statuses, decisions and moot notices are accepted only when signed by the key of the relay that issued the action.

Relay policy: only the action's subject can appeal, also while its key is suspended or restricted on this relay; only an assigned moderator whose principal differs from the decider, the subject and every reporter can decide; operators read the queue and reassign through moderation.appeal.reassign.

Reviewer identity is hidden from the appellant: decision, status and moot statements are signed by the relay key only, the reviewer key stays in the relay copy and the relay audit log, and the appellant sees 'a moderator who did not make the original decision'.

Conflict-of-interest checks compare principals, not single keys, using the F07.S02.M01 key set, same-owner attestations, the relay moderator registry and the F12.S01.M01 report ledger, in assignment, reassignment and decide.
Keys suspended or restricted on this relay keep moderation.appeal.receive and moderation.appeal.read_status_own, which F12.S02.M01 refuses to list in restrictedCapabilities.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Concurrent assignment attempts serialize on appeal revision within the relay store; there is no cross-vault lock.
Decision and event are written in one relay transaction, and a vault that misses the decision statement can refetch it by appeal ID.
Relay deduplication on appealId lasts as long as the relay retains the appeal, and a retry with the same statement digest always returns the stored signed receipt.
Appeals and decisions are P2, readable only by the appellant and the relay's assigned reviewer and operators, and never federated or sent in plain notifications.
Appeal records follow RET-EVIDENCE with the action, and the appellant may keep the signed decision in their vault regardless of relay deletion.
Appeal abuse (spam appeals, reviewer harassment, deadline gaming) is limited by one appeal per action, size caps, relay-clock windows and reviewer anonymity.
The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying every Appeal field per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.
Relay appeal intake, queue age and decision latency are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without statement text in logs.
Receive and decide meet the write budget (p95 ≤ 300 ms) at 50 req/s.
Overdue appeals are observable and alerting.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check commands, statements and events against the schema registry.
Reviewer independence and window arithmetic are covered by deterministic tests with an injected clock.
The vault export contains the user's appeals and signed decisions, and the export is the primary backup.
Import verifies signatures of decisions and receipts; unsent or pending appeals are not re-sent automatically.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

An EvidenceSnapshot stores target reference, target revision, the author's signed envelope, canonical content, SHA-256 content hash, capture reason, disclosure mode, blob references and integrity state, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Snapshot bodies are P2 between the store owner and the moderators of the relay that received them and retained under RET-EVIDENCE; each body and copied media item lives in an encrypted evidence blob with its own key, destroyed by deleting that key once no active snapshot references the blob.
Snapshots are immutable; only the integrity flag, lifecycle and legal-hold fields change and every change is recorded in the access log.

Evidence blobs are declared in this module's store (EvidenceBlob rows with blob id, SHA-256, size, key id and reference count) and P0 media is referenced by blob:sha256 from F15.S02.M03 MediaBlob (N9) instead of being copied.

A message snapshot records the F08.S01.M01 messageCid as targetCid and the sender-signed envelope without wrapped keys (nonce, ciphertext, key commitment, signature) as its metadata, and keeps the message key K inside its encrypted body only for an approved participant disclosure whose redact/1 preview removed nothing, with commitmentStatus verified once K has been checked.
Capture input is validated strictly and the caller must hold the target with a verifiable author signature, except for a labelled reporter claim on an unsigned message.
Size limits are enforced before any storage so evidence is never truncated, and they are at least the listing limits (10 media items of 5 MiB each).
Verification and read requests are validated against the accessor's purpose and case context.

A P2 target is captured metadata_only unless the reporter runs the disclosure preview, whose rules redact/1 remove L3/L4 location shares, geohash cells longer than 5 characters, email addresses, phone numbers and attachments before approval.

A message key K is accepted only for an unredacted message disclosure and only when HMAC-SHA256(K, 'classrup.comms.msg.commit.v1' || messageId) equals the signed key commitment and the XChaCha20-Poly1305 decryption of the signed ciphertext (additional data thread ID, message ID, sender device ID), unpadded, equals the disclosed plaintext; a redacted disclosure never carries K because K and the ciphertext would reveal what was redacted.
Snapshot lifecycle, integrity and disclosure follow the declared machines and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
A failed hash verification sets integrity to failed, which never returns to verified, raises an alert to the store owner, and does not exempt the snapshot from retention-end purge.

Purge happens only when retention has ended and no legal hold applies; it removes the snapshot's blob references and destroys a blob's key, then the blob, only when no remaining snapshot references it.
Disclosure of a P2 target moves from metadata_only through a local redacted preview to export prepared only by an explicit reporter approval of that exact preview.
Capture and verify are vault or relay local commands that produce no signed statement; snapshots travel inside signed report or case bundles only.
Capture emits moderation.evidence.captured in the same transaction as the snapshot and its access row.

The module re-checks legal holds through privacy.legal_hold.check when hold events arrive and before every purge, consumes privacy.deletion.completed, and is purged only through the RetentionPurgePort it registers with F10.S01.M02, never by a purge-completed event.
Relay intake of a report or appeal bundle stores the evidence it carries as relay snapshots after re-verifying hashes and author signatures, and resolves referenced P0 media by blob:sha256.
Vault policy: only the unlocked local principal captures, verifies, previews, approves disclosures and reads snapshots in its vault, and the author-signature check is part of capture.

Relay policy: relay moderators read relay-held snapshots only for an assigned case or appeal, operators read the access log, and content authors read snapshots of their own content tied to an appeal and a redacted access log.
Every read, verify, export and purge writes an access row and a refused read writes none.
Capture is idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and reuses the stored evidence blob, incrementing its reference count, when identical bytes already exist in the store.
Capture, blob write or reference increment, access row and outbox event commit in one transaction or not at all.
Purge is two-step and crash-safe, recording the reference decrement and any key destruction before blob deletion, and the sweep resumes after a crash or tab close.

Snapshot bodies and media are P2 between the store owner and the moderators of the relay that received them, encrypted per blob, and leave a store only inside a sealed report or case bundle addressed to a relay moderation key, or in the owner's own export.

Retention is RET-EVIDENCE with legal-hold override on relays, and destruction is cryptographic shredding of a blob key once no active snapshot references it; copies already sent to a relay or fetched by others cannot be recalled and the UI says so.
Every access is logged and neither moderators nor vault apps expose a way to edit or delete access rows.

A report on a P2 target gives the relay only metadata by default; plaintext leaves the vault only as a participant disclosure the reporter approved after a redact/1 preview reached export prepared, the single exception to ADR-0016 §3 and PRV-5 this module relies on.
The content author's view of the access log shows only purpose, accessor role and time, with accessor keys redacted and reporter-side rows excluded.
The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying snapshot and access fields per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.
Relay capture, verify and read durations and outcomes are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without content in logs, and the vault keeps only local diagnostics (OBS-7).
Capture meets p95 ≤ 300 ms on a relay and ≤ 150 ms in a vault for bodies up to 256 KiB, with media copied asynchronously within 30 s.
Integrity failures and unusual access volume are alerting metrics on the relay and local notices in the vault.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Hash stability, canonicalization and signature checks are covered by property tests with known vectors.
Access logging and non-disclosure are covered by abuse tests.
Evidence export is limited to the owner's own vault export, case bundles sent to a relay moderation key, and legal-hold exports approved under F10.S01.M02.
Import verifies every content hash and author signature and refuses bodies whose hash does not match.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A Report stores reporter key, relay target, content target (id, content id and revision seen), subject key, reason code, optional details, evidence snapshot reference, disclosure mode, sync state and status, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

The report statement sent to a relay is P2 between the reporter and that relay's moderation role: a signed header the relay reads (reportId, relayId, reporterKey, subjectKey, targetType, targetId, targetCid, reasonCode) drives dedupe, caps and case linking, only the details and evidence body are sealed to the relay's moderation key, local-only fields stay P3 in the vault, and the relay copy is retained under RET-EVIDENCE per relay policy.
A report is immutable after filing except for sync state, status, case reference and outcome; details cannot be edited, only withdrawn and refiled.
An AdvisorySubscription stores a publisher key, mode and last verified sequence, is P3 and local to the vault, and changes only through the subscription commands.

Advisory labels are applied only from verified advisories that are unexpired and unretracted; a verified retraction from the same publisher or the advisory's expiresAt removes the label without touching local records.

A LocalHide row stores exactly one of targetRef { type, id, cid? } or authorDid, an optional reportId when it came from filing, and the creation time; it is P3, device-only, never synced or sent, and exists until the user unhides it or deletes their vault.
Report input is validated strictly against the schema in the vault and again by the receiving relay; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED.
The target must be a record the vault holds with a verifiable author signature, or an unsigned end-to-end message filed as a labelled reporter claim, and must not belong to the reporter.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a localized message key.

The receiving relay accepts a report only when the signed relayId is its own DID and the body is sealed to its current moderation key, so a report forwarded to another relay is refused and never multiplied.
Reports follow the declared lifecycle and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.

Sync state advances only through local committed, prepared, transport_acknowledged (relay transport 2xx or mailbox acknowledgement) and peer_accepted (verified relay receipt bound to reportId and statement digest), and the UI never shows more than the reached state.
A reporter can withdraw a report while it is filed or linked; withdrawal sends a signed withdrawal statement but cannot recall evidence the relay already holds.

The relay sends a signed reportlinked statement when it attaches a received report to a case and a signed reportoutcome statement when that case closes, so the reporter's vault can reach linked and resolved and see the outcome actioned or no_action.

A local hide is active from hide until the user's explicit unhide, which deletes the row so the item or author shows again at the next query; hiding again creates a new row, and withdrawing a report does not unhide its target.
Every command declares whether it is vault-local, produces a signed statement, or is a relay command, and the signatures below do so.
File emits moderation.report.filed as a local event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the Report; the statement leaves the device only through the sync outbox.

The module consumes case events on the relay to link and resolve received reports and to send the reportlinked and reportoutcome statements, and the reporter's vault applies only those verified statements.

moderation.report.receive verifies the statement, stores the relay copy and the signed receipt, and emits the relay-local moderation.report.received with receiptId, subjectKey and snapshotId in the same relay transaction; only this event opens or extends a case in F12.S02.M01, and moderation.report.filed never leaves the reporter's vault (EVT-8).

When a case closes with outcome no_action, the relay emits moderation.report.dismissed { reportId, reporterKey, relayId, reasonCode, caseId, exempt } for every received report linked to it, relay-local and P3, consumed in-process only by F12.S03.M02; minor_safety reports carry exempt true.

F12.S02.M01 calls the in-process moderation.report.link_case in its intake transaction whenever it opens a case for a received report or merges one into an open case, so every linked reporter receives exactly one reportlinked statement.

LocalHidePort is the in-process vault read port behind moderation.localhide.check (isHidden({ targetRef? | authorDid? }) → { hidden, by: local_hide|advisory, hideId? }) and moderation.localhide.filter (filterHidden(items[{ targetRef, authorDid }]) → { visible, hiddenCount, labels }); F06.S01.M02 and F06.S02.M03 call it at query time instead of removing index documents, and moderation.localhide.add and moderation.localhide.remove are the explicit hide and unhide vault commands.

A message report carries the F08.S01.M01 messageCid as targetCid and the sender-signed envelope (nonce, ciphertext, key commitment, signature, without wrapped keys) in its metadata, and the message key K travels only inside the sealed body of an approved participant disclosure whose redact/1 preview removed nothing (PRV-9), so the relay moderator can check the key commitment and Dec(K, C) = P without receiving more plaintext than the reporter approved.

The 12-code reasonCode taxonomy (spam, scam_fraud, prohibited_item, harassment, hate, sexual_content, violence, counterfeit, privacy_leak, impersonation, minor_safety, other) of moderation.report.received is a stable v1 vocabulary bound by the F18.S02.M02 transparency dimension reports_received and its contract test T22; adding, renaming or removing a code is a breaking change that needs a new major event schema (CTR-SCH-001 SCH-3) coordinated with F18.S02.M02.

Vault policy: only the unlocked local principal can file, withdraw and read its reports and manage advisory subscriptions; incoming receipt, link and outcome statements are accepted only when signed by the relay key the report was addressed to.
Relay policy: a relay accepts report statements from any registered or signed-request key not blocked by its hosting policy, and only that relay's moderators can open sealed report bodies.
The reported party never receives report objects from the relay; relay queries return NOT_FOUND for non-moderators.

Reporter keys are readable on the relay only by moderators working an open case and by the in-process ledger used for conflict-of-interest and report-abuse checks; they never appear in events, case records or statements to the subject.
Vault commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 using local idempotency keys, and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Filing is atomic in the vault with the evidence snapshot and local outbox event; a failed capture leaves no report.

Delivery is at-least-once through the sync outbox; the relay deduplicates on reportId for as long as it retains the report and returns the stored signed receipt for a retry with the same statement digest, so retries never create duplicate cases.

Reporter key and details are P2 between the reporter and the addressed relay's moderation role, travel only in the report statement to that relay (details sealed), and never appear in federation payloads, public projections, events or logs.
Reports are retained under RET-EVIDENCE; on the relay the retention is the relay's published policy, never less than the case duration.

Report abuse (mass reporting, retaliation, spoofed outcomes, forwarded reports) is limited by per-key and per-prefix relay caps, dedupe, relay binding, signature checks and local-only effects of advisories.

A report on a P2 target (message, offer, cycle_proposal) carries only metadata (targetCid, sender key, sender signature, reason) by default; plaintext travels only in a participant disclosure the reporter approved after a redacted preview (F12.S01.M02), and the sheet warns that the reported party can infer who reported a private message.

The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying every Report and AdvisorySubscription field per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.

Local hides are P3 device-only preferences that are never synced, sent, logged or shown to anyone, are applied only at query time in the owner's vault, and are included in the owner's export and removed by the owner's deletion.
Relay report intake is measured per CTR-OBS-001 and logs contain no report details or reporter keys; the PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
Vault file completes locally within 150 ms p95 for a 256 KiB snapshot, and the report sheet meets PWA budgets (OBS-5).
Relay intake lag between received and linked is observable and alerting.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command input, output, statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
Reporter non-disclosure and statement verification are verified by dedicated abuse tests.
The vault export contains the user's reports and advisory subscriptions, and the export is the primary backup (IOX-6).
Import validates IDs, schema version and signatures of stored receipts; open reports are not re-sent automatically.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A PolicyRule version stores rule ID, version, family, severity, allowed actions, change type, locale texts, effective and retirement times and the relay signature content id, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Published rule versions are P0, immutable and retained under RET-EVIDENCE because moderation decisions cite them.
Rule IDs follow POL-<FAMILY>-<NNN>, are never reused and version numbers increase by one.
Each version has a derived in-force state (scheduled, in_force, superseded) computed from effectiveAt, later versions and retirement, and at most one version of a rule ID is in force at any time.

A prohibited-goods reference is the F18.S01.M02 identity (publisherId, ruleKey) with an optional ruleId for one exact version, a version drafted from a governance decision keeps its governanceRef, and review flags and reference status derived from governance events live in a store-local review table beside the immutable version rows.
Rule input is validated strictly, including ID format, text sizes and allowed action vocabulary.
Publication checks the notice period for restrictive changes only, the changelog and that the rule is the next version, and initial adoption on a new relay takes effect at its stated effective date.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
A change is classified initial, restrictive or non_restrictive by testable rules, and a declared class that the rules contradict is refused.

A governance decision becomes a draft only when it is relay-scope, approved, about platform_policy, published by this relay's operator and its content digest matches, and every draft built from it passes the same rule checks as an operator draft.
Rule versions follow the declared lifecycle and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Publishing a version supersedes the previous in-force version at effectiveAt, and the previous stays readable.
Retiring a rule prevents new citations and leaves all existing citations valid.

The in-force state of a published version moves from scheduled to in_force at effectiveAt and to superseded when a later version takes effect or the rule is retired, and only an in_force version is citable for a decision at that time.

A governance-built draft starts in state draft with governanceRef and is published only by an operator through moderation.policyrule.publish; a conflicted outcome discards the proposal's unpublished drafts and flags a version already published from it without changing that version.
Every command is a relay command; publish also produces a signed policy statement that vaults can fetch.
Publish emits moderation.policy.published in the same transaction as the version row and the statement.
The module consumes relay-scope governance events to create drafts and flag rules for operator review, and never publishes, retires or changes a published version by itself.
moderation.policyrule.check_citable answers in-process whether ruleId@version was in force at a given decision time, and F12.S02.M01 and F12.S01.M03 cite only versions it confirms.

governance.policy_proposal.decided is consumed in relay runtime only with scope relay (a decision this relay stored through F18.S02.M01 relay_upload) and targetType platform_policy: outcome approved creates one draft version per targetRef from proposedChange[targetRef], the canonical platform_policy change record { family, severity, allowedActions, changeType, texts, prohibitedRuleRef?, changelog?, effectiveAt }, with governanceRef { proposalId, publisherId, proposalStatementCid, decisionCid, changeDigest } and without a second lookup (only a payload carrying proposedChangeCid instead reads the proposal statement proposalStatementCid stored on this relay); rejected creates nothing; conflicted discards the proposal's unpublished drafts and flags versions already published from it; vault-scope events are ignored.

governance.prohibited_rule.changed is consumed in relay runtime only with scope relay (the relay's applied pack, emitted by F18.S01.M02 relay_upload): versions whose prohibitedRuleRef has the event's (publisherId, ruleKey) get prohibitedRefStatus retired on change retired or emergency_expired and a review flag, a version pinned to a ruleId that is no longer the active version is flagged, check_citable reports citable false for a version whose reference is retired, and vault-scope events are ignored.
Relay policy: only relay operators draft, publish and retire rules; moderators and members read published rules; the public read capability needs no session.
Vault policy: a vault stores a policy statement only if signed by the relay key it fetched it from and pins the statement it showed the user.
Policy reads are cacheable for 5 minutes and never reveal drafts.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutations require expectedRevision.
Publication writes the version row, signature and event in one transaction.
Concurrent edits to the same rule serialize on version uniqueness.
Rules and statements are P0 public data and contain no personal data; drafts are visible to operators only.
Published versions are retained under RET-EVIDENCE and never deleted while any action cites them.
Policy tampering is prevented by signatures, immutability and audit of every operator action.
Publish and read latency and outcomes are measured per CTR-OBS-001.
Public reads meet the read budget (p95 ≤ 150 ms) and are cache friendly.
In-force index freshness is observable.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check commands, statements and events against the schema registry.
Version immutability is covered by property tests.
Policy export contains all versions with statements and is portable between relays as a starting template, not as authority.
Import verifies statement signatures when keeping them as history, and templates import as drafts under the new relay's keys.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

The expand step turns a v1 prohibitedRuleRef string (an F18 rule version id) into { publisherId, ruleKey, ruleId } through governance.prohibited_rule.get { ruleId }, and a reference that cannot be resolved is flagged for operator review instead of guessed.
A ModerationCase stores subject target and key, source, linked report receipt IDs and snapshot IDs, action IDs, assignee, status and outcome, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

An EnforcementAction stores kind, target, scope, policy rule IDs with versions, facts summary, decider, expiry, statement-of-reasons content id and issue time, and status; actions are never silent and always carry rule IDs.

Cases and actions are P2 between the relay's moderators and the subject, retained under RET-EVIDENCE, and never federated; the only outward statements are the subject's statement of reasons and reversal and the opt-in advisory with its retraction.
A case can carry several actions (for example removal plus a warning) and stays assigned after an action until a moderator closes it, unless the apply asks to close it.

Every action stores targetRef { type, id, cid? } naming exactly the content it concerns (cid is the signed projection's content id when known, for a listing its statementCid), so index and hosting consumers act only on that item, and type account is the only form that concerns every document of the subject key.

A host-policy action recorded for a hosting module is an ordinary relay action with caseSource auction_review, kind remove_from_index, targetRef { type auction, id auctionId }, the seller as subjectKey, in-force ruleRefs, a factsSummary, the confirming moderator as deciderKey and the proposing moderator as proposerKey, so it has a statement of reasons and an appeal route like any other action.
Action input is validated strictly, and rule references, facts summary and expiry are mandatory.
Role limits (moderator versus operator) and last-admin protection are checked before persistence.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Rule references must be versions in force at the decision time, and restricted capabilities may never include the appeal, own-action read, subject evidence read, export or deletion capabilities.

A host-policy record is accepted only for a registered source and kind (auction_review with remove_from_index), with two different moderators whose principals differ from the subject, and is not refused because the target is no longer in the relay index.
Cases and actions follow the declared lifecycles and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.

An action takes effect only after its statement of reasons is transport_acknowledged by the subject's mailbox or 24 hours have passed since apply, except imminent-harm rules where effect is first and notice follows within 24 h.
Revert and expiry restore the relay-side effect, publish the reversal and, when an advisory was published, a signed advisory retraction; they never alter the original statement.

An appeal outcome reduced reverts the contested action with reason appeal_reduced and applies a new linked action with the reduced kind, expiry and capabilities and a new statement of reasons in one relay transaction.
Advisories carry the action's expiresAt, and subscriber vaults drop them at expiry or on the verified retraction.
Every command declares whether it is a relay command or a vault-local intake and which signed statements it produces.

Case opening is driven by consumed events (received reports through moderation.report.received, spam detections, shill suspicions, high risk levels) and by the operator command moderation.case.open, and emits moderation.case.opened in the same transaction as the case.
Apply and revert emit action events in the same transaction, and the statement of reasons is stored before the event is dispatched.

A subject's vault verifies received classrup.moderation.reasons/v1 and reversal/v1 statements and derives local moderation.action.applied and moderation.action.reverted events (EVT-9, actor.kind federated) with the same target fields and without deciderKey.
Action events carry the target, restricted capabilities, rule references, expiry, statement content id and issue time that appeals, limits, signals, index and notification consumers need.

moderation.action.applied and moderation.action.reverted always carry targetRef { type, id, cid? } and caseSource, and the relay-signed reasons/v1 and reversal/v1 statements carry relayId, actionId and targetRef (for a listing, id listingId and cid the projection statementCid), so F06.S01.M01 removes only the targeted document and F01.S01.M03 binds each notice to one delivery.

moderation.action.applied and moderation.action.reverted affect only the acting relay's hosted copy: relay consumers (F06.S01.M01 index, F07.S02.M02 profile hosting, F16.S01.M01 authorization caches) apply them in relay runtime only, and vault-origin copies derived from verified statements are informational and never change vault records.

moderation.action.record_host_policy is the in-process relay command a hosting module calls in its own decision transaction (F04.S02.M03 confirm_void); it opens or reuses the case for the auction with source auction_review, applies the action, optionally closes the case, and returns actionId and caseId, which the hosting module stores to match moderation.appeal.decided.actionId.

governance.prohibited_rule.changed is consumed in relay runtime only with scope relay (the relay's own applied pack after F18.S01.M02 relay_upload; vault-scope copies are ignored): each open or assigned case with an action citing a policy rule version whose F12.S02.M03 prohibitedRuleRef has the event's (publisherId, ruleKey) gets one review flag for moderator review, and the flag never reverts or changes an action by itself.

The action kind enum (warn, remove_from_index, restrict_feature, suspend_relay_access) and the origin enum (relay, vault) of moderation.action.applied and moderation.action.reverted are a stable v1 vocabulary bound by the F18.S02.M02 transparency dimensions and its contract test T22; adding, renaming or removing a value is a breaking change that needs a new major event schema (CTR-SCH-001 SCH-3) coordinated with F18.S02.M02.
Relay policy: relay moderators work cases and apply actions up to their limits, operators open cases, apply permanent suspensions and revert any action, and admins assign roles through F16.S01.M01.
Vault policy: a user's vault accepts a statement of reasons only when signed by the issuing relay key, shows it with the relay name, and never changes local records because of it.
A moderator cannot decide a case in which their own principal, by any linked key, is the subject or a reporter.

Conflict-of-interest checks compare principals, not single keys, using the F07.S02.M01 key set (device keys and seq chain), same-owner attestations and the relay moderator registry, in assignment, apply, close and revert.

Keys suspended or restricted on this relay keep moderation.appeal.receive, moderation.appeal.withdraw, moderation.appeal.read_status_own, moderation.action.read_own and moderation.evidence.read_as_subject, in addition to the CAP-5 read, export and deletion rights.

Host-policy records are accepted only in-process from a hosting module registered for the source (F04.S02.M03 for auction_review) on the relay that hosts the auction, never over HTTP, and the two moderators named in the record pass the same principal conflict checks as any decider.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Apply, statement storage and outbox event commit in one relay transaction; delivery to the subject is at-least-once.
Case intake from events is idempotent via the inbox table so duplicates never create two cases.

A host-policy record is idempotent on (caseSource, hostRef) for as long as the action is retained and commits in the hosting module's transaction, so a retried or crashed confirm never records a second action.

Cases and actions are P2 relay-side data, accessible to relay moderators and the subject, and never leave the relay except as the subject's statement of reasons or reversal and the opt-in public advisory with its retraction.
Retention is RET-EVIDENCE, with legal hold override, and subject deletion leaves a pseudonymized record for the case duration.
Moderator abuse is limited by assignment, rule requirement, principal-level conflict checks, audit logging and operator reversal.

Moderation never issues classrup.federation.tombstone/v1: remove_from_index changes only this relay's index, and other relays and vaults act only on the opt-in advisory under their own policy or subscription (F12.S01.M01).
The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying case and action fields per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.
Relay command latency and outcomes are measured per CTR-OBS-001; logs never contain facts summaries or keys.
Apply meets the write budget (p95 ≤ 300 ms) at 50 req/s.
Queue age and pending-notice counts are alerting metrics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check commands, statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
Race, conflict and no-silent-action cases are covered by deterministic tests.
A subject's vault export contains the statements of reasons they received and appeals, never case notes or reporter data.
Relay admin export of cases and actions requires operator role and omits reporter identities unless under legal hold.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
The module owns no persistent entities; all inputs are signed projections or local records and results are events carrying the evidence values.
The derived fingerprint index stores only hashes and counters, never text, and expires entries after 30 days.
Every result records the heuristic set version and thresholds used so decisions can be reproduced.
Fingerprint and key-observation rows key the subject by a store-salted hash; the subject did:key appears only in the query input and in the store-local P2 event, never in an index row or a log.
Inputs are validated for size and encoding before evaluation, and oversized input is rejected rather than truncated.
Thresholds are configuration with hard minimum and maximum values so an operator cannot disable all heuristics.
Evaluation never throws on hostile text and always returns a bounded result.
Evaluation is a pure function of input, fingerprint index snapshot and configured thresholds, and has no lifecycle.
A throttle recommendation expires after at most 1 hour and is renewed only by new evidence.
A degraded mode with exact-hash checks only is used while the index rebuilds, and results record degraded true.

Velocity counts every first-seen content id by the store's receipt time regardless of its claimed createdAt, and a gap of more than 24 h between claimed createdAt and receipt time adds the backdated_claim heuristic instead of excluding the statement.

The SpamEvaluator port evaluate(input) is exposed in-process as the query moderation.spam.evaluate, returning score, heuristics, throttle?, rulesVersion and degraded, with no side effects except the fingerprint and key-observation indexes and, for relay_intake and vault_filter, the event.
moderation.spam.detected is emitted only when score ≥ 50 in relay_intake or vault_filter mode, never for an author's pre-sign check, with throttle only when the velocity heuristic matched.

The relay index-intake hook passes the projection text before indexing, and the store's own first observation of a key (identity.session.started on a relay, federation.record.accepted in a vault) starts the new-key window; identity.account.created is never used for other keys.

moderation.spam.detected carries the subject did:key (a pseudonymous public key, P2, never leaving the store per EVT-8) so F12.S02.M01, F12.S03.M02 and F12.S03.M03 act on the same key, and hashing is used only inside the indexes and logs.
In author_presign mode the query reads the author's own local publication history, writes nothing and emits nothing, and its output contract is the one F01.S01.M03 tests against (N19).

The mode enum of moderation.spam.detected (relay_intake, vault_filter) is a stable v1 vocabulary bound by the F18.S02.M02 transparency dimension spam_detected (relay_intake only, throttled when a throttle is present) and its contract test T22; author_presign never appears in the event, and adding, renaming or removing a mode is a breaking change that needs a new major event schema (CTR-SCH-001 SCH-3) coordinated with F18.S02.M02.
The evaluator is reachable only in-process through the query moderation.spam.evaluate, which is not routable over HTTP, so it has no member-facing capability.
Configuration changes to thresholds require the relay operator role and are written to the audit log of F16.S01.M01.
Results visible to a member are limited to their own folded items in their own vault.
Evaluation is idempotent for the same input and index snapshot, and events are deduplicated on (targetCid, rulesVersion).
Index updates and the detection event commit in one store transaction.
Index loss degrades to exact-hash mode and recovers automatically without operator action.
Only hashes, counters and heuristic names are stored; text is processed in memory and never logged.
Fingerprint entries are RET-SHORT (30 days) and keyed by a salted key hash so they cannot be joined across relays.
Heuristic gaming and false positives are limited by explainable results, no automatic bans and operator-tunable bounded thresholds.
Evaluation outcomes and timing are measured per CTR-OBS-001 on relays and kept as local diagnostics in the vault.
Evaluation meets p95 ≤ 20 ms for 20000 code points on a relay and ≤ 50 ms on a Moto G-class device.
Degraded mode and index size are observable.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Heuristics are covered by deterministic fixtures with expected scores.
Event payloads are validated against the schema registry.
The fingerprint index is derived data and is excluded from user exports and from backups.
Operator threshold configuration is exported with relay configuration and validated on import against allowed ranges.
Heuristic changes are versioned in rulesVersion and old versions stay readable for audit for 180 days.
An AccountLimit stores key, limit key, tier, base value, risk multiplier, action restriction, override, effective value and the reasons for each adjustment, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Limits are P2 between the member and the relay's moderators and retained under RET-STANDARD with the membership record.
Effective value is 0 while an action restriction is active, otherwise the override when active, otherwise floor(base × multiplier) with a minimum of 1 unless the base is 0.

Limit keys cover only resources the relay itself observes (index writes of public projections it hosts, mailbox puts to new recipient mailboxes, bids on auctions it hosts and governance comments it accepts for a policy proposal), never offers, cycle proposals or other end-to-end encrypted statements.

new_key_comments_per_proposal applies only while the key's firstSeenAt on this relay is less than 7 days ago, with base value 1 per proposal on every tier and a fixed proposal-wide cap of 25 accepted comments from such keys that no per-key override raises; from the 7-day mark the check answers allowed without consuming.
Override input is validated strictly with bounded value, reason and expiry.
Limit checks validate the limit key and treat unknown keys as denied.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
A check never accepts a caller-supplied count; usage comes only from F12.S03.M03 buckets the relay itself consumed for the subject key.

The new-key governance comment cap reports denials as RATE_LIMITED with retryAfterMs, because F18.S02.M01 V15 reports every comment intake limit that way and cannot depend on this module, while the other limit keys report MODERATION_ACCOUNT_LIMIT_REACHED.

Tier derives from relay-clock age since this relay's own first observation of the key and completed dealings counted from voluntarily submitted two-party completion statements, and promotion is evaluated by the daily sweep and by each counted submission.
A risk level change recomputes the multiplier immediately, and recovery to low restores the base value immediately.
Overrides expire automatically at overrideExpiresAt and the recompute emits a limit.changed event.

An active restrict_feature action whose restricted capabilities map to a limit key sets that limit to 0 until the action expires or is reverted, which clears it and emits limit.changed with cause action_expired or action_reverted.
The module exposes override, clear-override and completion-submission relay commands, the member's own limits read, and the in-process check used by the relay bus.
Every effective value change emits moderation.limit.changed in the same transaction as the row.

The module consumes risk level rises and drops, enforcement action applied and reverted events and relay session starts to keep multiplier, restriction and first-seen current, and consumes no vault-local deal or account events.

restrictedCapabilities of moderation.action.applied are mapped to limit keys by the documented capability-to-limit table (federation.record.ingest, comms.mailbox.put to a new recipient, auctions.bid.place), and other capabilities never change limits.
Completion submission verifies every party signature on the deal_completion/v1 body, counts it once per key, and never learns amounts or obligations.

The relay bus calls moderation.accountlimit.check in-process before F18.S02.M01 governance.policy_comment.accept (N18) with limitKey new_key_comments_per_proposal and scopeRef the proposal statement cid; for a key first seen less than 7 days ago the check consumes F12.S03.M03 class governance.policy_comment.new_key (per key and proposal, limitOverride the effective value) and, only when that allows, governance.policy_comment.new_key.proposal (25 per proposal); F18.S02.M01 lists no depends_on edge to this module because the bus injects the check.
Relay policy: moderators set and clear overrides within bounds and members read their own limits; the check capability is for the relay bus only.
Vault policy: not applicable beyond showing the relay's limit statement; the vault never enforces another party's limits.
A moderator cannot override limits on their own key, including any key linked to their principal.
Overrides are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision.
Checks never mutate limit state and flow-limit consumption is atomic through F12.S03.M03.
Recompute and event commit in one transaction.
Limits are P2 relay-side data visible to the member and the relay's moderators and never federated.
Retention is RET-STANDARD with membership, and deletion removes the rows.
Abuse (limit evasion by many keys, moderator favoritism) is limited by per-prefix rate scopes, bounded overrides and audit logs.
Relay limits never depend on counts supplied by the subject's vault, and the relay learns of dealings only from completion statements the parties chose to submit, without amounts.
The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying every AccountLimit field per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.
Check outcomes and tier distribution are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without keys.
Check meets p95 ≤ 5 ms in-process on a relay.
Override counts and denials are observable for abuse review.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Tier tables and multiplier math are covered by deterministic and property tests.
Authorization and non-disclosure are covered by abuse tests.
A member's export includes the limits the relay reports for them as read-only context, without moderator override identity.
Relay import of limits is only from its own backups; imports from other relays are ignored because standing is relay-local.
Tier tables are configuration versioned with the relay policy and validated against bounds on import.

A RateBucket stores key hash, scope, capability class, algorithm state (theoretical arrival time, token count or window sub-counters), penalty factor, salt epoch and update time, and is operational state kept for its policy window plus at most 24 h (RET-EPHEMERAL for windows up to 24 h, RET-SHORT for longer windows up to 30 days).

A RatePolicy stores per-tenant limits per capability class with algorithm, limit, period, burst, allowed scopes, prefix multiplier, fail mode and version, and is retained as configuration under RET-STANDARD.

Raw IP addresses and keys are never stored; they are hashed under a per-class salt whose epoch is at least the policy window, the previous epoch's salt is kept only until its last counter leaves the window, and IP-prefix scopes are limited to windows of at most 24 h so prefix salts are destroyed at most 48 h after creation.
A policy expresses any limit from 1 per 30 days to 100 000 per second as { limit, periodMs, burst }, and GCRA uses the emission interval periodMs / limit.

A RatePolicy may carry one longWindow { limit, periodMs } so one class expresses two limits such as 20 per minute and 200 per hour, records the ownerModule of a class registered through RatePolicyRegistry.register and whether its fail mode is locked, and every tenant has a request.default policy row (the per-tenant default request rate per actor key formerly held as Tenant.limits.requestRatePerMinutePerKey).
Policy input is validated against bounded ranges so an operator cannot set unlimited rates.
The port validates its inputs and never throws; invalid input is treated as a denied request.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Registered classes and the request.default policy are validated against the same bounds as operator policies, a class has exactly one owner, and an owner's locked fail mode cannot be changed by an operator.
Bucket state evolves only by the GCRA, token bucket or window counter arithmetic, and a bucket idle for its full window is equivalent to a new bucket.
Penalties from spam throttles expire after at most 1 hour and never accumulate beyond factor 0.25.
Policy changes take effect for new consume calls within 5 seconds without resetting buckets.

Counting survives salt rotation, because consume looks a key up under the current and the previous epoch salt and sums window counters across both until the previous epoch has left the window, after which the previous salt is destroyed.

A class with a longWindow allows a request only when both windows allow and counts it in both, its salt epoch lasts max(24 h, longWindow periodMs), and for 24 h windows such as read.proximity.center_new the previous salt is kept 24 h after rotation and checked together with the current one.
The port RateLimitPort.consume is in-process and used by the kernel command bus before each handler; it is not an HTTP endpoint.
Operators change policy and reset buckets through two relay commands; the vault changes local thresholds through the same policy command in local scope.
moderation.rate.exceeded is emitted at most once per key per minute with a count, so denial storms do not create event storms.
Consuming moderation.spam.detected derives the bucket key from the payload subjectKey with this module's own HMAC and applies the penalty to that key's write buckets.

For class report.receive, consume uses class report.receive.reduced while the key carries a reduced marker, which this module sets from moderation.signal.recorded of kind report_dismissed_bad_faith (F12.S03.M02) for 30 days from the signal's observedAt, unless the caller marks the request exempt (minor_safety).

Vault scope local provides flow guards (offers and reports per hour) and stock guards (open offers, open cycle proposals) counted from the vault's own records; they are UX confirmations, never security controls, and relays never receive their counts.

RatePolicyRegistry.register({ capabilityClass, ownerModule, algorithm, limit, periodMs, burst?, longWindow?, scopes, failMode, failModeLocked }) is the in-process registration port owner modules call at relay composition (F06.S02.M03 registers read.proximity.query.anonymous, read.proximity.query.token, read.proximity.center_seen and read.proximity.center_new with its own numbers); this module seeds a tenant RatePolicy row from the defaults when none exists, and owners depend on this module, never the reverse.

Every relay-scope consume also charges the actor key's request.default bucket once per request (the first consume carrying the request's correlationId), so the per-tenant default request rate applies to every relay command and query without a second bus call; anonymous requests charge it by IP prefix.

Built-in governance classes for F18 relay intake are charged by the relay bus in-process (N18): governance.policy_comment.accept (10 per hour per key) and governance.policy_comment.accept.prefix (30 per 24 h per /24 or /48 prefix) for F18.S02.M01 governance.policy_comment.accept; governance.policy_comment.new_key and governance.policy_comment.new_key.proposal only through the F12.S03.M04 limits check; governance.prohibited_rule.relay_upload, governance.category.relay_upload and governance.jurisdiction_profile.relay_upload (10 per 24 h per operator key each); governance.transparency.relay_upload (5 per 24 h per operator key, the F18.S02.M02 value); and governance.transparency.relay_counter_snapshot (20 per 24 h per key); all are window_counter classes with failMode closed by default.
Relay policy: only relay operators change policy and reset buckets; any caller can read the status of their own bucket.
Vault policy: only the local principal changes local UX guards, and local guards never apply to or report on other parties.
The consume port runs for every request including anonymous ones, keyed by IP prefix only for anonymous requests.
consume is atomic per key so concurrent requests never exceed the configured burst.
Policy writes are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision.
Store outages follow the policy fail mode, open for reads at half rate, closed for sensitive classes.

No raw IP address, actor key or user identifier is stored; keys are HMAC hashes under per-class salts destroyed once the previous epoch leaves the window (at most 48 h for windows up to 24 h, at most 60 days for 30-day windows), and logs contain at most /24 or /48 truncated prefixes per CTR-OBS-001.
Bucket state is kept for its window plus at most 24 h (RET-EPHEMERAL for windows up to 24 h, RET-SHORT for longer ones up to 30 days) and never exported.
Abuse (distributed low-rate attacks, limit evasion by key rotation, limit-based harassment) is addressed by layered scopes and tenant caps.
Consume outcomes and latency are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with labels limited to tenant, module, code and outcome.
Consume adds at most 1 ms p95 per request on a relay and at most 0.2 ms in a vault.
Persisted snapshots and denial rates are alerting metrics.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
GCRA, token bucket and window counter arithmetic are covered by property tests against a reference model.
Fail modes, privacy of keys and event throttling are covered by integration and abuse tests.
Rate buckets are ephemeral and excluded from exports and backups; policies are exported with relay configuration.
Policy import validates all bounds and locked fail modes before applying.
Policy schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A RiskAssessment stores subject (key, transaction reference or own listing publication), level, score, factors with per-factor points, model version, input digest, frictions, validity window and next threshold crossing, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.
Assessments are derived data, P3 in a vault (owner only) and P2 on a relay (the subject and that relay's moderators), retained 30 days under RET-SHORT, and recomputable from signals.
The sum of factor points equals the score before clamping to 0..100, and every factor names a signal kind and count, never a content item.

Points follow the published table risk/1: per signal kind floor of the summed decayed weights (compensations netted, a kind never below 0); deal credit −2 per unexpired deal_completed signal together with manual_positive weights, never below −20; new_key 10 under 24 h and 5 under 7 days since the relay's first observation (relay opt-in, keys only); amount_bucket small 0, medium 5, large 10 (transactions only); for listing_publication, publication_velocity 3 per publication beyond 5 in 24 h up to 45, new_principal 10 under 7 days and spam_score floor(score / 2).
Inputs are validated strictly, and the model version must be one this build knows.
A transaction assessment requires both party keys and a bucketed amount, never the raw amount.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Assessments have no transitions; a new computation creates a new row only when its inputDigest differs from the latest one.
Level rises are applied immediately and level drops use hysteresis so that borderline scores do not flap.

Recomputation is triggered by moderation.signal.recorded after a 5 second debounce per subject and at the stored nextCrossingAt of decaying signals (at most 24 h after the last computation), so a level drop is detected when it happens.
Every level rise emits moderation.risk.elevated and every level drop that hysteresis allows emits moderation.risk.lowered, each in the same transaction as the new assessment.
The module exposes one recompute command, the N19 query moderation.risk.assess and two read queries; level rises and drops are the only events.
Recompute is vault-local or relay-local and produces no signed statement; levels are never sent to other parties.
The module consumes signal events to recompute, and emits moderation.risk.elevated or moderation.risk.lowered in the same transaction as the new assessment.

moderation.risk.assess is the in-process query named by N19 (it replaces moderation.riskassessment.assess_transaction, kept as an alias for one release) for transaction and listing_publication subjects, and F01.S01.M03 tests against its contract.
Vault policy: only the local principal can read or recompute assessments in its vault.
Relay policy: moderators with an open case, operators and the subject (own key) can read relay assessments; no other member can.
Assessments are never returned to the counterparty and never federated.
Recompute is idempotent by inputDigest and creates at most one assessment per digest.
The assessment row and the level event commit in one transaction.
Debounced recomputes tolerate duplicate and out-of-order signal events.
Assessments are derived data (P3 in a vault, P2 on a relay) kept 30 days and contain only factor kinds and counts, never content or counterparties' identities beyond the subject key.
Consumers receive the minimum, level and factor kinds, not signal sources.
Misuse of levels (as a de facto ban, or to shame) is limited by friction-only semantics, subject visibility and no federation.
Relay recompute outcomes and level distribution are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without keys; the vault keeps local diagnostics only.
Recompute meets p95 ≤ 50 ms for subjects with up to 5 000 signals.
Level changes per hour are observable to detect model anomalies.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Score math, hysteresis and explanation completeness are covered by property tests.
Friction-only semantics are covered by a schema test and abuse tests.
Assessments are derived and excluded from user exports and backups, and are recomputed from signals after import or restore.
The model formula and thresholds are exported with relay configuration and validated on import against allowed ranges.
Model changes are versioned and run in shadow mode for 7 days before activation.

A Signal stores subject key, kind, signed integer weight, half-life in days, source module and event ID, optional source key, evidence reference, observed time from the store clock and expiry, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Signals are P3 in a vault (owner only) and P2 on a relay (the subject and that relay's moderators), retained until expiresAt and at most 365 days under the expiry-bounded class RET-SIGNAL, and are never exported to other users.
Signals are append-only; the only mutable field is none, and corrections are new signals that reference the corrected one.

Each event-derived signal names the key that caused it (reporter, opener or counterparty) as sourceKey when the producer payload carries one, and at most 3 signals per (subject, sourceKey) in 30 days count for scoring.
Manual signal input is validated strictly with bounded weight and a required reason.
Ingestion from events validates the mapping table and ignores events lacking a verified signature in the vault case.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Mappings use only fields present in the producer payload; a mapping whose subject cannot be resolved records nothing, and a vault never records a signal about its own local principal.
A signal has no transitions; it is valid from observedAt until expiresAt and read with decay applied.
Decay is exponential, weight times 0.5 to the power of age over half-life, evaluated at read time in the store clock.
Expired signals are purged by a daily sweep and a rollup keeps only counts per kind for 365 days.
The module exposes a manual record command and three queries; automated ingestion happens through event consumers.
Every recorded signal emits moderation.signal.recorded in the same transaction as the row.
The consumed event table below is fixed per rulesVersion (signals/3), and every mapping names its subject, source key and evidence fields from the producer's payload.

Report outcomes map to relay signals: an applied action records report_actioned by kind, a revert other than expiry records a compensation, and moderation.report.dismissed records report_dismissed_bad_faith only when one reporter key reaches 5 non-exempt dismissals in 30 days.

The in-process summarize read exposes per-kind counts in a window for F12.S03.M01 scoring, and the moderation.signal.recorded event of kind report_dismissed_bad_faith is what F12.S03.M03 uses to select the reduced report class for 30 days.

SignalPort.record is the in-process relay port (command moderation.signal.record_module) through which relay-local modules record signals of the module table without a catalog event: proximity_pattern from F06.S02.M03, weight 10, half-life 7 days, against the caller's did:key; it deduplicates on (kind, sourceRef) and emits moderation.signal.recorded like any other signal.

Claims that the other party has not answered carry no weight: rentals.damage.claimed and a comms.meetup.no_show with contradicted true record nothing, rentals.damage.resolved records damage_agreed only for outcomes accepted, counter_accepted, refund_claimed or return_agreed (F05.S02.M03 applies no automatic penalty), and comms.meetup.no_show_contradicted records a compensation of the weighed no_show signal.
Vault policy: only the local principal can read and add signals in its vault, and signals derive only from events produced by verified local state or verified signed statements.
Relay policy: moderators read signals on that relay for open cases, operators read summaries, and subjects can read category counts about themselves on that relay.
Signals about a subject are never returned to other members or federated.
Ingestion is idempotent through the unique source index and the inbox table of CTR-EVT-001 EVT-3.
A row and its event commit in one transaction.
