Consumer failures retry with CTR-IDM-001 backoff and dead-letter after 8 attempts.
Signals are P3 in a vault and P2 on a relay, contain no content, and are never federated, never shown to other members and never merged across stores.

Retention is bounded by expiry (at most 365 days, class RET-SIGNAL) with a counts-only rollup; in a vault signals are deleted only by the local principal's own deletion or by expiry, never by a counterparty's tombstone or deletion, and relay signals are pseudonymized when the subject's signed deletion request is applied.
Signal poisoning (fake disputes to damage a rival) is limited by small weights, decay, source verification and a per-source cap.
The module meets N6 by registering ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10, classifying every Signal field per F10.S02.M02, and consuming privacy.deletion.completed.
Relay ingestion lag and outcomes are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without subject keys in logs; the vault keeps local diagnostics only.
Summarize meets p95 ≤ 50 ms for subjects with up to 5 000 signals.
Dead-lettered ingestion events are alerting on the relay.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Decay math and cap logic are covered by deterministic and property tests.
Consumer mapping is covered by contract tests per consumed event.
A user's vault export includes the signals recorded in their vault; relay signals about a subject are exported only to relay operators under legal hold.
Imported signals are marked with source import, capped at weight 20 per source and never inflate decay.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A relay EmailAddress service copy stores the normalized address encrypted at rest with a lookup hash, the locale, status, verification token hash and expiry, bounce counters, the creating device key and the registered consent reference; under the CTR-PRV-001 PRV-10 notification channel exception only the channel identifiers (address and locale) reach the single relay named in the granted notify_email consent (F10.S01.M01), which stores them P3-equivalent, uses them only for the verification email and content-free notifications (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-4), never federates or exports them, and erases both within 24 h of removal or a registered withdrawal.

An EmailDelivery stores the delivery kind, the template key from the fixed email registry, status, attempts, the transport Message-ID, the VERP tag and times, never the address in clear, never a notification category and never any user content.

Emails carry a generic subject and body from the fixed email template registry (notify.tpl.email.verify, notify.tpl.email.notice, notify.tpl.email.security_notice, notify.tpl.email.activity and notify.tpl.email.digest, at most 12 templates), a link to the app origin without identifiers, and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe headers whose URL comes from UnsubscribeTokenPort of F13.S02.M03.

The vault email target is the authoritative user-owned record - the cleartext normalized address (P3), locale, relayId, the relay emailAddressId and a status mirror - while the relay copy is a disclosed service copy, sealed to the relay key in transit, never authoritative, and rebuilt from the vault record after a relay loss or a vault import.

The locale in notify.email.add is a copy of F15.S04.M03 LocalSettings.defaultLocale taken by notify.email.enable and sent only inside the sealed add body after privacy.consent.check {purpose notify_email, relayId} returned granted (N6), and every email template declares only the parameters app origin link, verification link and unsubscribe URL, never a parameter carrying user content or Money.
Address input is validated for syntax, length and domain in the vault and again at the relay before storage and before any verification mail.
Sends are validated for registered consent, address status, delivery kind and per-address, per-user, per-IP-prefix and relay-wide limits before the transport port is called.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Bounce and complaint reports are accepted only when authenticated, namely a DSN received at the VERP return address whose HMAC tag matches one delivery and that quotes its Message-ID, or a complaint from a configured feedback-loop source or a signed provider webhook.
An EmailAddress relay copy moves unverified to verified to bouncing to removed; removed is terminal and a returning user adds the address again as a new record.

An EmailDelivery moves queued to sent to settled or bounced, queued to failed, or queued to cancelled; settled, bounced, failed and cancelled are terminal, and a bounce for a settled delivery leaves that row unchanged but still applies the address transition and emits notify.email.bounced.
Removal, a registered email consent withdrawal or the deletion withdrawal registered at the relay erase the address ciphertext within 24 hours and cancel queued deliveries.

When the vault learns from notify.email.get_mine on sync that its address became bouncing, it updates the vault email target and emits vault-local notify.email.bounced, which the inbox routes to the security notice template notify.tpl.security.email_stopped.

Verified to bouncing requires two authenticated hard bounces within 72 hours, three authenticated soft bounces within 7 days, or one signed provider hard-bounce event, so a single forged or stray report cannot cut off security email.

The vault exposes enable, disable and sync_status commands and a local view; the relay exposes the sealed add, remove and get_mine requests signed by an active device key, the public token verify link, and the internal send and report_bounce commands.

Each relay send, bounce and cancellation is recorded and emits its relay-local event in the same SQLite transaction as the status change, and the vault-local notify.email.bounced is emitted in the IndexedDB transaction that updates the email target.

The relay instance consumes relay-local channel consent events to erase addresses and cancel deliveries; the vault instance consumes vault-local channel consent events, privacy.deletion.requested (pause only) and privacy.deletion.completed.

Unsubscribe URLs come from UnsubscribeTokenPort.urlFor(consentId) of F13.S02.M03 at render time, so every email carries a working token without storing it, and a verified complaint calls RelayWithdrawalPort.withdraw(consentId, unsubscribe_link) of the same module.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.email), DeletionPort (purge step) and RetentionPurgePort (kinds notify.email_target and notify.email_delivery) with F10 (N6), annotates every field with its F10.S02.M02 class, calls privacy.consent.check for notify_email before enable, and routes every limit through RateLimitPort of F12.S03.M03 (N18).
Relay policy lets only an active device key of the user add, remove and read its own address, and only with a granted email consent registered at that relay.
Verification is open to the holder of the unguessable token; send and bounce handling are internal to the relay and cannot be called by clients.
Relay operators can access ciphertext of addresses only through the transport adapter at send time; the UI states that the operator can read the address.
Bounce and complaint reports reach report_bounce only from the transport adapter after authentication, so no outside party can mark an address bouncing or withdraw a consent.
Enable, disable, add, verify and remove are idempotent, and send is idempotent per dispatchRef with a 10-minute dedupe window.
Transport failures retry 3 times over 6 hours with the Message-ID unchanged so duplicate submissions collapse at the receiver.
A relay restart resumes queued deliveries from the database and never sends a delivery already marked sent.

Every event consumer of this module is registered with externalSideEffects true, so F15.S03.M03 restore re-delivery excludes it (V11) and no email is sent twice after a relay restore; instead, before the first send after a restore, the relay marks removed and erases every address whose email consent is not granted in the restored registrations and cancels its queued deliveries.

The email address is P3 in the vault and a P3-equivalent service copy at the selected relay under CTR-PRV-001 PRV-10 (sealed in transit, encrypted at rest), never in events, logs, federation or exports to others, and erased at the relay with its locale within 24 hours of removal or a registered consent withdrawal.

Emails contain no listing, message, name or amount content and carry only a generic subject and a link to the app origin; the operator and mail providers still learn that the address received a ClassRup email.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity because email links an identity to a DID at the operator, so consent text says this plainly.

The relay cannot be used to mail arbitrary addresses, because verification mail is limited per (user, address), per user, per IP prefix and relay-wide, and no user can exhaust another user's verification quota.
Forged DSN or ARF reports are refused, so third parties can neither stop a victim's security email nor withdraw the victim's consent.
Sends, bounces and queue depth are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with no addresses in logs.
Send submission p95 ≤ 500 ms to the transport and the relay can submit 50 emails per second.
Bounce rate above 5 percent over 1 hour raises an operator alert.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests use the dev log adapter and a fake SMTP server and verify headers, bodies and bounce handling.
Privacy tests assert that no address appears outside the vault target and encrypted relay storage and no user content appears in any email.
The screens listed under ux meet the listed a11y items, verified by an axe scan with zero serious issues, a keyboard and screen-reader walk-through and a no-JavaScript run of the verification page.
A user's vault export contains the email target with the cleartext address as the user's own P3 data, the relay, locale and status, and never the relay copy.

Relay restore from backup keeps encrypted addresses, fails queued deliveries older than 6 hours and revalidates the registered consent before any send; when the relay lost the copy, the vault re-adds the address from its email target after user confirmation.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new templates are additive keys in the fixed registry.

A Notification stores the recipient DID, category, template key, a content-free reference (type and opaque ID), collapse key, collapsed count, urgency class, read state, source event ID and times, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Notifications are P2 vault records that never contain message text, names or amounts; titles and lines are rendered at display time from the template key and data the vault already holds, and retention is RET-SHORT with a cap of 500 items.
Urgency class is normal or urgent where urgent is allowed only for the security category.
Routing validates event shape, recipient rule and registry membership before a notification is created.
Read operations validate ownership and revision.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
A Notification starts unread and becomes read; collapsing keeps it unread and increments count, and a read notification is never reopened except by a new collapse window starting a new row.
Deletion by cap or retention is not a state; rows are physically removed with a local tombstone count.
Read is terminal for the row, and new matching events after the collapse window create a new unread row.
Creation is a vault-internal command invoked by the routing consumers; mark-read and mark-all-read are vault commands; list and unread-count are vault queries.
Creation and read emit their events in the same IndexedDB transaction as the row change (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-8).
The routing table below is the complete set of routed events; every listed event exists in the module catalog emits.
Vault policy lets only the local principal read and mark its own notifications; routing consumers act as the vault itself.
Notifications are created only from events of statements already verified by their owning modules (signed by an authorized key for the role), never from raw relay data.
No relay or other user can read or create inbox rows.
Routing consumers are idempotent on event ID through the consumer inbox (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-3), so redelivery never creates duplicates.
Collapse and creation happen in one IndexedDB transaction so counts are exact under concurrent events.
If rendering a template fails the row is still created with a generic fallback text, so no alert is lost.
Notifications are vault-local, content-free and P2; they never leave the device except as the separate content-free push or email alerts decided by the gate.
Retention is 30 days with a cap of 500 items, and security rows are the last to be dropped by the cap.
Notification spam from hostile peers is limited by blocking, by collapsing, and by per-source caps.
The PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7) with counters for created, collapsed, dropped and read notifications.
Routing one event and creating a row meets p95 ≤ 30 ms and inbox list of 50 items p95 ≤ 100 ms on a mid-range phone.
Catch-up routing of 1 000 events after being offline completes within 5 s.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
A routing table test asserts every routed event type exists in the catalog emits and has category, template, recipient rule and collapse key.
Contract tests check commands, queries and event payloads against the schema registry.
A user's vault export contains unread notifications and the last 30 days of read ones as references and template keys only.
Import drops rows older than 30 days and rows whose reference type is unknown, keeps counts, and never regenerates alerts for imported rows.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new templates and routing rows are additive and unknown templates render a generic fallback.

A relay PushSubscription service copy stores the user DID, the ID of the device key that created it, the push endpoint URL, the browser public key p256dh (65 bytes) and auth secret (16 bytes), the content encoding aes128gcm, a per-subscription topic key, status, counters and the registered consent reference, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

The relay copy is a disclosed service copy under the CTR-PRV-001 PRV-10 notification channel exception - only the channel identifiers endpoint, p256dh, auth and the per-subscription topic key, held by the single relay named in the granted notify_push consent (F10.S01.M01) and stored there P3-equivalent; the subscribe body is sealed to that relay's published key, endpoint, keys and topic key are encrypted at rest, used only for content-free notifications (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-4), never exported, evented, logged or federated, and erased in the same transaction as the registered withdrawal, unsubscribe or expiry and so within the PRV-10 24 h bound, and the relay copy is never authoritative because the vault record and the browser rebuild it.

Push payloads are content-free JSON of at most 1 024 bytes in exactly one of three forms: sealed {v, urg, s} for vault-originated alerts, whose box s opens only on the target device to {v, tpl, ref, ck}; hook {v, urg, tpl, ref?, ck?} carrying only data the dispatching relay hook already holds; and digest {v, urg, tpl: notify.tpl.system.digest, n}.

The vault push target record is the authoritative user-owned record per device - relayId, deviceKeyId, deviceLabel, enabled, the relay subscriptionId, a status mirror and the consent reference - while the browser PushManager holds the endpoint and keys, so the vault stores neither and rebuilds the relay copy from the record and a fresh browser subscription.

The relay VAPID key pair is owned by this module through RelayKeyStorePort (private key in the relay key file store, mode 0600, never in SQLite, logs, events or exports), and every VAPID public key is registered with purpose vapid in F16.S02.M02, which also records its revocation.
Subscribe input is validated for signer key status, endpoint origin, keys, registered consent and limits before storage.
Send input is validated for payload form, size and Topic derivation before encryption, and the endpoint address is re-resolved, pinned and re-checked on every send.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

The Topic header never carries a collapse key or reference; it is the first 32 characters of base64url(HMAC-SHA256(per-subscription topicKey, collapseTag)), so the push service sees an opaque value that differs between subscriptions and between users even for the same event.
A relay PushSubscription starts active and ends expired or revoked; both are terminal, secrets are erased at the transition, and re-enabling creates a new subscription.

A 404 or 410 from the push service expires the subscription immediately; transient failures and 401 or 403 rejections of that one subscription only increment its counter and expire it after 5 consecutive failures over at least 24 hours.

A push consent withdrawal registered at the relay (relay-local notify.channel.opted_out) and a revocation of the device key that created the subscription revoke it at that relay, and the vault-local notify.channel.opted_out disables the push target on the device.
The vault push target moves from pending to active and ends disabled or expired; the vault learns relay-side expiry from notify.push.list_mine on app open and shows Re-enable push.

The relay exposes the sealed subscribe, unsubscribe and list requests, the internal send command, the public VAPID key query and an operator VAPID rotation command; the vault exposes enable, disable and a local view that drive the browser PushManager and call the relay.

Each send attempt emits exactly one relay-local notify.push.sent or notify.push.failed in the same SQLite transaction as the counter update, without endpoint, collapse key or reference, and without a template key for sealed sends.

The relay instance consumes relay-local channel consent events and key revocations, and the vault instance consumes vault-local channel consent events and privacy.deletion.completed, as labelled per environment under events_consumed.

No signed statement is produced; subscribe, unsubscribe and list are relay requests signed with the F11.S01.M03 RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures profile (tag classrup/relay-request/v1) whose subscribe body is sealed to the relay's published key, and the VAPID public key is registered with F16.S02.M02 purpose vapid.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.push), DeletionPort (purge step) and RetentionPurgePort (kind notify.push_target) with F10 (N6), annotates every field with its F10.S02.M02 class, calls privacy.consent.check for notify_push before enable, and routes every limit through RateLimitPort of F12.S03.M03 (N18).

Relay policy lets only a device key of the user that F16.S02.M02 reports active at the relay receipt time subscribe, unsubscribe and list that user's subscriptions, and only after a granted push consent is registered at that relay.
The internal send command is callable only by the gate of F13.S02.M01 inside the relay; no external client can trigger a send directly.
The VAPID public key is public; the private key never leaves RelayKeyStorePort and is never logged, and rotation is a relay operator action.
A revoked device key loses its subscriptions and every later request it signs is refused with UNAUTHENTICATED, including requests signed after its revocationEffectiveFrom that arrive late.
Subscribe is idempotent on (userDid, endpointHash) and send attempts are idempotent per (subscriptionId, dispatch reference) and collapse at the push service through the opaque Topic header.
Transient failures (429, 5xx, timeouts) retry with backoff and honor Retry-After, up to 3 attempts within 10 minutes; permanent failures never retry.
A relay restart loses no accepted sends because attempts are recorded before transmission and unfinished attempts are retried once on start.

Sending to a push-service origin pauses for 15 minutes only when subscriptions of at least 5 distinct users on that allowlisted origin are rejected with 401 or 403 within 5 minutes, which indicates a VAPID problem; a single subscription's rejection never pauses sends to others.

Every event consumer of this module is registered with externalSideEffects true, so F15.S03.M03 restore re-delivery excludes it (V11) and no push is sent twice after a relay restore; instead, before the first send after a restore, the relay revokes every subscription whose push consent is not granted in the restored registrations or whose createdByKeyId F16.S02.M02 reports revoked, erasing its secret.

Payloads are content-free and RFC 8291 encrypted to the browser, so the push service sees only the endpoint, size, time and an opaque per-subscription Topic, and for vault-originated alerts the relay sees only a sealed box it cannot open.

The push endpoint and keys form a P3-equivalent service copy for the single selected relay under CTR-PRV-001 PRV-10, sealed in transit, encrypted at rest and erased at expiry, revocation or registered withdrawal, always within 24 h; the push service provider can link the endpoint to the browser vendor, which the explainer states.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity because the relay links a DID to a push endpoint, and users choose the relay.

Endpoints must be on the push-service origin allowlist and are re-resolved and re-checked on every send, so a user-chosen endpoint can neither reach internal addresses nor pause sending for other users.
Send outcomes, latencies and expirations are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with no endpoints, topics or payloads in logs.
Send p95 ≤ 500 ms to a healthy push service and the relay can send 200 pushes per second.
Alerts fire on multi-user VAPID rejection patterns, origin pauses and failure ratios.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Protocol tests use a fake push service that decrypts RFC 8291 messages and validates RFC 8030 and RFC 8292 headers.
Contract tests check commands, events and payload shape against the schema registry.
The screens listed under ux meet the listed a11y items, verified by an axe scan with zero serious issues and a keyboard and screen-reader walk-through.
A user's vault export contains the push target records (relay, device key, device label, enabled, status) and never endpoints or keys, which only the browser and the relay copy hold.

On relay restore subscriptions are re-verified by a probe and failing ones expire; on vault import, or when a relay lost its copy, the vault rebuilds the relay copy from the push target record and a fresh browser subscription after user confirmation.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new content encodings are additive behind the contentEncoding field.

A QuietHoursSchedule stores the user DID, an IANA time zone, an enabled flag, up to 4 windows each with days of week 1 to 7 and local start and end as HH:mm, the tzdata version used, and this device's mirror chain position (seq and head cid), with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

The schedule is P2, held in the vault and mirrored to relays only as a rule-equivalent canonical time zone plus windows; it contains no location and no content, the mirrored zone is a region shared by many places covering at least an L1 cell, and the UI states that the relay learns that region and the sleep rhythm.
Evaluation is a pure function of the instant, the schedule and the pinned tzdata; local wall-clock windows are mapped to instants with the rules in the invariants.

Before mirroring, the time zone is replaced by the canonical zone of its rule-equivalence class in the pinned tzdata (identical UTC offsets and transitions from 2020 to 2100, for example Europe/Busingen to Europe/Zurich and America/Indiana/Tell_City to America/Chicago), chosen so that the class covers at least an L1 cell, and isQuiet results are identical for the original and the canonical zone.

The mirror statement classrup.notify.quiet_hours_mirror/v1 has its own schema distinct from the vault record and from the relay copy classrup.notify.quiet_hours_relay/v1; it is a CTR-FED-001 envelope signed by a device key, addressed to one relay, and chained per (author, signing device key, stream notify.quiet_hours) with seq and prev.
Schedules are validated for time zone, window shapes, overlap and size before they are stored or mirrored.
Evaluation inputs are validated so isQuiet is total and never throws for any instant in the supported range 2020 to 2100.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Relay mirror statements are validated for signer key status, audience relay, canonical zone, chain position, forks and the registered channel consent, and a stale or forked statement is never applied.
The schedule is a settings record without lifecycle states; it is replaced as a whole on each save with an incremented revision.
Enabled and disabled are a flag, not a state machine, and disabling never deletes the windows.

Mirror progress to each relay moves through local committed, prepared, transport acknowledged (HTTP 2xx) and peer accepted (relay acceptance signature over this statement's cid as the applied head), and a stale, forked or superseded statement never shows peer accepted.

Saving the schedule is a vault command that emits vault-local notify.quiet_hours.changed in the same IndexedDB transaction and produces a signed mirror statement for each relay that holds a registered push or email consent.

The relay exposes a mirror command that emits relay-local notify.quiet_hours.changed in the same SQLite transaction when the effective mirror changes, and a signed get_mirror query; both environments expose the same pure evaluate query.

The vault instance consumes vault-local channel consent events to mirror the current schedule to a newly consented relay, and the relay instance consumes relay-local notify.channel.opted_out and security.key.revoked to delete or retire its mirror rows.

classrup.notify.quiet_hours_mirror/v1 is registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2) with signer role principal (device key active in the author's portable document and in F16.S02.M02) and audience the relay named in payload relayId.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.quiet_hours), DeletionPort (purge step) and RetentionPurgePort (kind notify.quiet_hours) with F10 (N6), classifies every field with F10.S02.M02, and routes limits through RateLimitPort of F12.S03.M03 (N18).
Vault policy lets only the local principal save its schedule; evaluation is a pure function usable by any local module.
Relay policy lets an active device key mirror its owner's schedule only where the relay holds a registered granted channel consent; the relay-side evaluate function is available to the dispatch gate.
Other users and relay operators cannot edit a schedule; operators can read the mirrored copy of consenting users as part of operating the relay, which is disclosed.
Saving is idempotent on the resulting schedule content and expectedRevision, and mirroring is idempotent on the statement cid.
Evaluation is deterministic and has no I/O, so it can be retried and cached freely.

Each device of the principal is a separate vault with its own mirror chain; the relay keeps the latest verified statement per device chain, the gate uses the one the relay accepted most recently across the user's active devices, and a device whose statement was superseded is shown which device's schedule the relay uses.

The schedule reveals sleep rhythm and a time zone region, so it is P2, mirrored only as the canonical zone to relays where the user holds a registered push or email consent, and deleted there as soon as the last such consent at that relay ends.
No location is read to choose the time zone; the default is the browser setting and the user can change it.
The schedule is never part of notification payloads, and the changed event carries neither the time zone nor the windows.
Relay mirror calls are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7), including tzdata version.
The evaluate function completes in under 1 ms and the relay can evaluate 100 000 users in under 5 s.
Mirror lag and evaluation errors are observable.

A user's vault export contains their schedule including the tzdata version.
Import validates the time zone against the target build's tzdata and refuses unknown zones, asking the user to choose another.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new window fields are additive and old windows keep their meaning.

A NotificationPreference stores user DID, category, the three channel flags, the lock flags, a per-cell revision and the per-channel mirror sequence last sent from this device, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Preferences are P2, held in the vault; a relay holds only the column of each channel consented at that relay (push flags at a push relay, email flags at an email relay) per device chain, and deletes them as soon as the last consent for that channel at that relay ends.

The default matrix is fixed and versioned as defaultsVersion 2 - in-app on for the seven inbox categories, push on for offers, cycles, messages, auctions, bookings, security and activity, push off for moderation, email on only for security, all others off - and the relay applies the same versioned defaults when no mirror exists.

The activity category covers content-free wake-ups for mailbox arrivals; only its push and email cells exist (inApp is fixed false and not editable), and after a wake-up the service worker applies the routed category's push cell and thread mute in the vault.
Unknown categories from a newer app version are stored, with V01 relaxed only for import and app-update merge, under an other bucket with in-app on and push and email off, and are never mirrored.
Matrix changes are validated for category, lock rules and size before they are stored.
Relay mirror statements are validated for signer key status, audience, channel consent, chain position, forks and schema.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Flags for a channel without consent are stored and shown inactive, never silently enabled, and are mirrored only after that channel is consented at a relay.
The matrix is plain settings without a lifecycle; every cell is edited in place with a revision counter and no cell is ever deleted.
The enforced transition rules are the locks, which refuse any change that would turn security in-app off or activity in-app on.

Mirror status per relay and channel moves through local committed, prepared, transport acknowledged (HTTP 2xx) and peer accepted (relay acceptance signature over this statement's cid as the applied head), never claims more than that acceptance, and a stale or superseded statement stays below peer accepted.

Matrix changes and reset are vault commands, check is a vault in-process query for every channel, the mirror is a relay command accepting a signed per-channel statement, and resolve is a relay internal query for hook dispatches.

Each vault command emits vault-local notify.preference.changed in the same IndexedDB transaction as the change, and the relay mirror emits relay-local notify.preference.changed in the same SQLite transaction when the effective cells change.

The vault instance consumes vault-local channel consent events to show channel status and to mirror a newly consented channel, and the relay instance consumes relay-local notify.channel.opted_out and security.key.revoked to delete or retire its mirror rows.

classrup.notify.preference_mirror/v1 is registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2) with signer role principal and audience the relay named in payload relayId, one statement per channel with its own chain stream.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.preferences), DeletionPort (purge step) and RetentionPurgePort (kind notify.preference) with F10 (N6), classifies every field with F10.S02.M02, and routes limits through RateLimitPort of F12.S03.M03 (N18).
Vault policy lets only the local principal edit its matrix and lets local notification modules call check.
Relay policy lets an active device key mirror its owner's column for a channel only where the relay holds a registered granted consent of that user for that channel.
Relay operators and other users cannot read or edit a user's in-app column; the relay-side resolve query is internal to the relay's dispatch gate.
Vault commands commit locally first; mirroring is a retried outbox step with states prepared, transport acknowledged and peer accepted.
Mirror statements are idempotent on cid and applied only when they extend the head of their device chain.

Each device is a separate vault; within one vault concurrent edits of the same cell produce CONFLICT_REVISION, and across devices the relay applies per channel the statement it accepted most recently among the user's active device chains, shows the other devices which device's matrix it uses, and never merges cells.
The in-app column and the other bucket never leave the device, and a relay learns only the eight booleans of each channel consented there, for users who consented to that channel.
Mirror statements are signed and contain no content, no thread or listing identifiers and no schedule.
Preferences are deleted from the relay as soon as the last consent for that channel at that relay ends, including when the deletion sign-step withdrawals are registered.
Relay mirror and resolve calls are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).
Vault set meets p95 ≤ 50 ms and relay mirror p95 ≤ 300 ms at 50 req/s; resolve p95 ≤ 20 ms.
Mirror lag is visible in local diagnostics.

The default matrix is verified against a golden table.

Import validates categories and the locks, keeps unknown categories in the other bucket with defaults and does not mirror to relays without a fresh user action.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new categories are additive and default to in-app on and push and email off.

A vault ChannelConsent stores user DID, relay (canonical self-certifying relayId with the hostname as display hint), channel (push or email), status, the required linked F10 privacy consent ID and purpose, the signed statement CID, grant and withdrawal claims, the withdrawal path and the expiry, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

The consent is P2 evidence held in the vault and registered at the sending relay as a relay registration record, retained under RET-EVIDENCE, and a new grant after withdrawal or expiry creates a new record instead of reviving the old one.

One-click unsubscribe tokens are derived as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(relayUnsubscribeKey, consentId || channel)), recomputed for each email and verified in constant time without being stored, and a redeemed marker is kept for 365 days after withdrawal.

The statements have their own schemas distinct from the record schemas - classrup.notify.channel_consent_statement/v1 and classrup.notify.channel_withdrawal/v1 signed by a device key of the principal and addressed to one relay, and classrup.notify.channel_withdrawal_receipt/v1 signed by the relay key for withdrawals made at the relay (CTR-SCH-001 SCH-1).

The vault record classrup.notify.channel_consent/v1, its statement classrup.notify.channel_consent_statement/v1 and the relay registration all carry the mandatory privacyConsentId and privacyPurpose (the F10 purpose, notify_email or notify_push), so the channel consent statement is the single relay-facing artifact for notification consent and F10.S01.M01 sends no statement of its own for these purposes.
Opt-in statements are validated for signer key status, channel, audience relay key, linked privacy consent and expiry before the relay registers them.
Unsubscribe tokens are validated by recomputing the HMAC and comparing in constant time; an unknown token returns NOTIFY_UNSUBSCRIBE_TOKEN_INVALID and a reused token returns the unchanged result.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

The linked privacy consent is required - privacyPurpose must match the channel (push to notify_push, email to notify_email), relayId must equal the consent scope, and opt_in calls privacy.consent.check for that purpose and relay, while the relay relies only on the registered channel consent because privacy.consent.check is vault in-process only.
The opt-in order is fixed as opt_in, then register at the relay with its acceptance, then notify.push.enable or notify.email.enable, which refuse without a registered granted consent.
A ChannelConsent starts granted when created and ends withdrawn or expired; both are terminal and a new consent needs a new record.

Withdrawal takes effect in the vault immediately and at the relay as soon as the relay registers the withdrawal, which emits the relay-local notify.channel.opted_out that erases the relay copies of push and email.
Expiry happens 365 days after grant and is enforced by the relay sweep independent of the app; the vault applies it from its own clock or from the relay-signed withdrawal receipt with via expired.

Withdrawals made at the relay (unsubscribe link, verified complaint, relay policy, expiry) reach the vault as relay-signed withdrawal receipts fetched with notify.channel.list_changes and applied with notify.channel.apply_relay_change.

During a pending deletion the consent shows paused, derived from privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending with nothing stored, and at execution the DeletionPort sign step signs withdrawals with via account_deletion for every granted consent and queues them to each relay before any key is revoked or destroyed.

The 365-day expiry asks the user to reconfirm the channel only - reconfirmation creates a new ChannelConsent and statement linked to the still-granted F10 consent of the same purpose and relay, never re-asks, re-grants or withdraws that F10 consent, and an expiry (via expired) leaves the F10 consent granted; if that F10 consent was withdrawn meanwhile, the reconfirm control is replaced by the F10 grant flow.

Opt-in, opt-out and apply_relay_change are vault commands; opt-in and opt-out produce signed statements registered at the relay with notify.channel.register; unsubscribe is a public relay command that redeems a token, the expiry sweep is a relay internal command, and list_changes is a signed relay query.

Each vault command emits its event in the same IndexedDB transaction as the state change, and register, unsubscribe, RelayWithdrawalPort and the expiry sweep emit relay-local notify.channel.opted_in or notify.channel.opted_out in the same SQLite transaction (EVT-8 relay side), which the relay instances of push, email, quiet hours, preferences and the gate consume.

The module consumes privacy consent events matched by purpose and scope.relayId, never by consent ID (which changes when F10 supersedes a grant), and privacy.deletion.requested (pause only) and privacy.deletion.completed.

Statements are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2) - channel_consent_statement and channel_withdrawal with signer role principal and audience the relay named in payload relayId, and channel_withdrawal_receipt with signer role relay (key chain pinned through F11.S03.M01), accepted only for consents registered at that same relay.
The relay ports UnsubscribeTokenPort.urlFor(consentId) and RelayWithdrawalPort.withdraw(consentId, via) are provided in-process to F13.S01.M02 for List-Unsubscribe headers and verified complaints.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.channel_consents), DeletionPort (sign, pseudonymize and purge steps) and RetentionPurgePort (kind notify.channel_consent) with F10 (N6), classifies every field with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check, and routes limits through RateLimitPort of F12.S03.M03 (N18).
Vault policy lets only the local principal grant, withdraw or apply relay changes to its own channel consents.
Relay policy lets an active device key of the user register its owner's statements and list its changes; unsubscribe is open to a holder of a valid token and can only withdraw, never grant.
Relay operators cannot create a consent for a user; they can only withdraw it under their hosting policy through RelayWithdrawalPort, recorded with via relay_policy in a relay-signed receipt.

Vault commands commit locally first; relay registration is a retried outbox step whose sync state is transport_acknowledged on HTTP 2xx and peer_accepted only with the relay acceptance signature over the statement cid, issued after signature, consent and chain checks; a duplicate or refused statement never reaches peer_accepted.
Relay register is idempotent on the statement cid, unsubscribe on the consent and token, and apply_relay_change on the receipt cid.
Conflicting states between vault and relay resolve toward withdrawn; a withdrawal is never undone by a late grant statement.
Consent records contain DID, relay and channel only; no address, endpoint or content is part of the consent.
Consent evidence is retained under RET-EVIDENCE, unsubscribe tokens are never stored or logged, and redeemed markers are kept 365 days after withdrawal.
Dark patterns are prevented by defaults of not enabled, plain wording, one-click withdrawal and no re-prompt for 30 days after a refusal.

Consent statements name the relay by its self-certifying key-derived relayId and pinned key, so whoever controls the hostname later cannot inherit consents, and relay acceptances and withdrawal receipts are verified against that relay's key chain.
Relay registration and unsubscribe calls are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without logging tokens; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).
Register and unsubscribe meet p95 ≤ 300 ms at 50 req/s and vault commands p95 ≤ 50 ms.
Expiry sweep lag is observable.

Contract tests check commands, statements and event payloads against the schema registry.
Send-path tests assert that no push or email leaves without a granted registered consent.
The screens listed under ux meet the listed a11y items, verified by an axe scan with zero serious issues, a keyboard and screen-reader walk-through and a no-JavaScript run of the unsubscribe page.
A user's vault export contains their channel consents with the signed statements and applied receipts.
Import re-verifies statements and never re-registers a consent at a relay without a fresh user confirmation.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new channels are additive enum values behind a relay capability flag.

A vault DeferredNotification stores the user DID, channel (os_alert, push or email), category, template key, a content-free reference, collapse key, the linked inbox row, the relay dispatch handle, decision and release times, jitter, attempt, count, status and expiry, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001, and it never leaves the device.

A relay DeferredNotification holds no reference, template key or collapse key for vault-originated items - only the user DID, channel, urgency normal, sealed boxes it cannot open, an opaque collapse tag and the vault's dispatch ID - while hook items hold only the category, template key and reference that the dispatching relay hook already holds; both are P2, contain no content or schedule and live at most 24 hours (RET-EPHEMERAL).
Only urgency normal is stored as deferred; urgent security alerts are never deferred, so no urgent deferred record exists.

The digest template notify.tpl.system.digest is generated only by the gate, carries a count and no reference, uses the template class system that callers cannot submit, and is governed by the matrix cells of the items it replaces rather than by a cell of its own.
Dispatch requests are validated per mode (vault routing decision, sealed relay dispatch, relay hook) for template, category, reference, sealed boxes and urgency before the gate decides.

The gate procedure is deterministic and side-effect free until the decision is applied, and applies one order everywhere - caller authentication, deletion pause for non-security, mute, collapse, channel consent or browser permission, matrix cell, single-producer arrival rule, urgency, quiet hours, rate.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

os_alert needs browser Notification permission and follows the inApp column of the matrix because an OS alert is the local alert of an inbox row; push and email need the channel consent and their own columns; muted items are dropped for all three channels; collapse updates never dispatch again and only raise the count of a deferred item.

Each event has a single alert producer per channel - events that arrived through a relay mailbox are pushed only by the relay mailbox hook (category activity) and the vault never requests push for them, while locally raised and direct-file events are pushed only by the vault path and email for them is requested only by the vault.
A DeferredNotification ends released, dropped or cancelled, all terminal and never reopened; the vault record passes through handed_off while the relay holds its sealed item.

Release happens only when the clock passes releaseAt and a fresh consent, matrix and quiet-hours check still allows sending; a check that cannot be read, or a time still quiet at releaseAt, re-defers with attempt + 1, bounded by expiresAt.

Changing the schedule, consent or matrix re-evaluates all deferred items of the user within 60 seconds - items no longer quiet are released with reason schedule_changed, items no longer allowed are dropped, and relay items are re-evaluated on the relay-local events of the mirror and registration commands.
More than 5 items for one user and channel due in one sweep are replaced by one digest alert carrying the count, and the replaced items are dropped with reason superseded_by_digest.

Dispatch is one command with three modes - the vault mode receives routing decisions through NotificationDispatchPort, the sealed relay mode receives requests signed by a device key of the user, and the hook mode receives in-process calls from relay hooks (mailbox put, auction host, cycle matching, moderation).
Release is an internal sweep in both environments and cancel is a relay command signed by a device key; release emits its event in the same transaction as the record change.

The vault instance consumes vault-local inbox, schedule, consent, preference and deletion events, and the relay instance consumes the relay-local consent, quiet-hours and preference events emitted by the registration and mirror commands, as labelled per environment under events_consumed.

For vault-originated push the gate seals {v, tpl, ref, ck} per target device with an ephemeral X25519 key and XChaCha20-Poly1305 to the X25519 agreement key that F16.S02.M01 agreementPublicKeyOf derives from that device's Ed25519 key listed active in the principal's portable identity document (F07.S02.M01), and sends the relay only {userDid, channel, urgency, dispatchId, notBefore?, collapseTag, boxes}; email requests carry no box and select a generic template by urgency.

When notify.notification.read arrives the vault cancels its local items and calls the relay command notify.notification.cancel for items it handed off, so a deferred push is never sent for a notification already read.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section notify.deferred, counts only), DeletionPort (purge step) and RetentionPurgePort (kind notify.deferred) with F10 (N6), classifies every field with F10.S02.M02, calls privacy.consent.check in the vault, holds non-security decisions while privacy.deletion.assert_not_pending reports a pending deletion, and routes limits through RateLimitPort (N18).

Relay policy lets only in-process relay hooks and active device keys of the target user call dispatch, cancel and list for that user; a valid device key of another principal is refused with FORBIDDEN and an unsigned or revoked-key request with UNAUTHENTICATED.

Vault policy lets the local principal's routing consumers dispatch through NotificationDispatchPort and the vault sweep release local alerts; the gate never reads message content because none is passed.
Users read their own deferred counts; relay operators can see counts, timing and hook categories of consenting users but never the contents of sealed boxes, which is disclosed.

Dispatch is idempotent on dispatchId for sealed requests, on (userDid, channel, templateKey, ref, collapseKey) within 10 minutes for hook calls, and on sourceEventId in the vault, so retries never double-send.
Release is idempotent per deferred item; a crash after the send but before the status update causes at most one repeated send which the push Topic and email Message-ID collapse.

The gate never fails open - if consent, preference or schedule cannot be read, the item is re-deferred for 5 minutes, and after 3 failures it is dropped for push and email and kept in the inbox; when no preference mirror exists the relay applies the versioned default matrix, so urgent security is never dropped for lack of a mirror.

Deferred items carry only template key, reference and timing in the vault and, for vault-originated items, only sealed bytes, an opaque tag and timing at the relay; they never carry content and are erased on release, drop, cancel or after 24 hours.
The quiet-hours mirror is used only for evaluation and is never written into deferred records.
Urgent bypass is limited to the security category so that quiet hours cannot be abused to push promotional content, and the platform sends no promotional content.

The relay can neither read sealed payloads nor link participants of one cycle, thread or booking, because references, template keys and collapse keys of vault-originated alerts never appear in relay records, events, logs or push headers and collapse tags are keyed per dispatching device.
Relay gate decisions and release lag are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the PWA keeps local diagnostics only (OBS-7).

A gate decision completes in p95 ≤ 20 ms excluding the channel send, and each release sweep loops over batches of 500 until no item with releaseAt ≤ now remains, bounded by the push send budget of 200 per second.
The expected release lag is at most 300 s jitter + 30 s sweep granularity + due items ÷ 200 s, and an alert fires when the observed lag exceeds that bound by more than 60 s.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check commands and event payloads against the schema registry.
DST and urgent bypass behaviors are covered with golden fixtures that reuse the F13.S02.M02 schedule fixtures.
The screens listed under ux meet the listed a11y items, verified by an axe scan with zero serious issues and a keyboard and screen-reader walk-through.
Deferred records are operational and short-lived, so a user's vault export contains no deferred items, only the counts since the last export in diagnostics.
Relay restore from backup drops deferred records older than 24 hours and rechecks the registered consent before any release.
Schema changes follow expand and contract; new channels or categories are additive and ignored by older relays.
The module owns no stored entity; its artifacts are CSS tokens, TypeScript primitives and lint rules versioned with the PWA.
Design tokens define --focus-ring-width 2px, --focus-ring-offset 2px, --target-min 44px and --scroll-pad-top and --scroll-pad-bottom computed from the heights of sticky bars.
Primitive components expose a documented keyboard contract (keys and expected behaviour) that tests assert.

Build-time lint and unit checks, plus end-to-end measurements for properties that exist only after the CSS cascade (computed hit area and obscured focus), reject patterns that make keyboard or single-pointer operation impossible.
Each rule failure has one stable code that appears in CI output and in the developer overlay.

Rules are enforced on every pull request and cannot be waived without an expiring entry in tests/a11y/waivers.yaml (schema owned by F14.S01.M03) whose single target is the file glob or component that fails; the lint runner of this module reads that same file.
Focus management is a deterministic function of navigation events and dialog open and close events.
The dialog helper keeps a stack so closing a dialog always restores focus to the element that opened it, or to the nearest focusable ancestor if that element was removed.
There is no persisted lifecycle, so no entity state machine is declared.
The module exposes component APIs and CSS tokens, not vault or relay commands or queries.
Components emit DOM events only (for example close and reorder) and no domain events.
Errors are developer-facing lint and test failures with stable codes and never reach end users.
The library performs no authorization and has no roles; it runs in the browser under the unlocked local principal.
It must not read or store vault data and must not transmit anything over the network; preference values are passed in as parameters by the PWA shell.
Developer overlays are compiled out of production builds.
Focus helpers are idempotent, so calling the route-focus handler twice leaves focus on the same element.
If the intended focus target is missing, the helper falls back in order to the view heading, the main landmark, then the document body and logs a development warning.
Dialog helpers never leave the page inert; unmounting a dialog always removes the inert and aria-hidden state it applied.
The module collects nothing; keyboard events are handled locally and never logged with key values (to avoid capturing typed secrets).
Developer warnings contain element selectors only, never field values.

The PWA sends no telemetry (OBS-7), so accessibility problems found by users are reported by the user through the project issue tracker, optionally attaching the file written by the F15.S03.M01 'Export diagnostics' action; nothing is reported automatically.

Received content cannot move focus, because user-supplied markup is rendered as text, any rich content is sanitised so autofocus, tabindex and on* attributes are removed before it reaches the DOM, and the PWA CSP script-src 'self' without 'unsafe-inline' blocks injected script; the primitives themselves move focus only on user action, route change or dialog open.
CI reports counts of violations per rule and per screen as a build artifact; production builds send no metrics.
Focus moves after route change complete within 100 ms.
Keyboard and target-size checks for all screens finish within 5 minutes in CI.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test, except 09.R04, which is the manual device-session requirement itself and is covered by the recorded manual test.
Keyboard-only Playwright flows cover the core journeys on the Pixel 7 and iPhone 14 profiles with an external keyboard emulation.
Lint rules have positive and negative fixtures proving they fail and pass correctly.

A manual keyboard session on physical Pixel 7 and iPhone 14 devices supplements the automated tests and is recorded per release, with device, date and owner, in the F14.S01.M03 release checklist (V05).
The module stores no user data, so a user export contains nothing from it.

The only user preference that affects these primitives, the reduced-motion override, lives in F15.S04.M03 LocalSettings (optional field a11yMotion system | reduced) and travels with that module's vault export; the PWA shell reads LocalSettings and passes the value to the primitives as a parameter, so 05.R02 holds.
Token and primitive changes are versioned and rollback restores the previous release without migration.
The module owns no stored entity; its artifacts are page shell and form components, the announcer service and spoken-name helpers with typed inputs.

Spoken-name helpers take typed values (Money with its F09.S03.M01 CurrencyDef, the F06.S02.M01 DistanceBucket, Instant, SyncState) and a locale and return Result<string, AppError>; they never take pre-formatted strings.

Alt text belongs to the record that references the photo, as a shared MediaRef { ref, alt?: plain text ≤ 140 characters, decorative?: boolean } in the signed listing projection (F01.S01.M01) and as the attachment altText of F08.S01.M03 with the same 140 limit; this module receives alt and decorative as props and never stores them.

SyncState is 'local_committed' plus the F15.S01.M01 OutboxEntry.state enum (prepared, sending, transport_acknowledged, peer_accepted, completed, conflict, failed, expired, discarded); spokenSync speaks each of the ten values from the shared catalog keys sync.state.<value> that the F15.S01.M01 sync chip also uses, names the transport (relay display name or direct peer) and never claims a stronger state than CONSISTENCY_STATES allows.
Lint and unit checks reject markup that breaks screen reader structure.
Each failure has one stable code printed in CI and in the development overlay.

Rules run on every pull request and waivers require an expiring entry in tests/a11y/waivers.yaml (schema owned by F14.S01.M03) whose single target is the file glob or component that fails; the lint runner of this module reads that same file.

The <Photo> runtime contract is checked in end-to-end tests, not at build time; a received photo without alt text and not marked decorative is announced as 'Photo n of m, no description', the add-description prompt appears only on the user's own listings, and refusing to publish such a photo belongs to the F01.S01.M03 publish rule with that module's error code.
The announcer keeps one bounded queue per region, holding at most 3 messages, with deterministic rules for priority, de-duplication, rate limiting and coalescing.
Polite messages never interrupt assertive messages and an assertive message replaces queued polite ones of the same region.
There is no persisted lifecycle, so no entity state machine is declared.

On overflow the queued polite messages of the region are replaced by one catalog summary tp(summaryKey, count) for the caller-supplied coalesceKey (default key a11y.announce.updates, '{count} updates'), later messages with that key increase the count, and queued polite messages older than 10 s are dropped unannounced.

The PageShell listens for the localechange event that F14.S02.M01 setLocale dispatches after re-rendering and announces 'Language changed to <language>' once, in the new language, through the polite status region, without moving focus.
The module exposes component and helper APIs and no vault or relay commands or queries.
It emits DOM events only and no domain events.
Lint and test failures are developer-facing codes never shown to end users; runtime helper failures are Result errors whose localized text the components render.
The library performs no authorization and has no roles; it runs under the unlocked local principal in the browser.
It never reads vault data on its own; callers pass values in.
Announcements must not contain P3 or P4 data, so callers pass only the same text that is visible on screen.
Announcing the same message twice within 2 s results in one announcement.
If a locale lacks a spoken-name pattern, the helper falls back to English patterns and logs a development warning, never to an empty string.

Helpers are pure and return Result<string, AppError> - Ok for every valid typed input, Err(COMMERCE_MONEY_INVALID) for a malformed amount and Err(COMMERCE_CURRENCY_UNKNOWN) when the caller found no CurrencyDef - and components render the localized error text on Err, so a value is never silent and never spoken as raw minor-unit digits.
Nothing is collected, and announcement text is held in memory only until cleared after 5 s.
Alt text is written by authors, carried in the owning record's MediaRef under that record's privacy class, limited to 140 characters of plain text and rendered by this module as text only.
Live regions never include secrets such as recovery codes or key material.

Remote parties cannot flood screen-reader users, because each region queues at most 3 messages, overflow collapses into one summary per coalesce key, stale polite messages are dropped after 10 s and assertive messages are capped per minute.
CI reports rule violations per screen as artifacts; production builds send no metrics.
Spoken-name helpers run in at most 0.2 ms p95 per call.
The announcer adds no more than 2 KiB gzip to the initial bundle.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test, except 09.R04, which is the manual assistive-technology requirement itself and is covered by the recorded manual test.
Structure rules are tested with positive and negative fixtures and with axe-core rules for landmarks, labels and names.
Spoken names are tested per shipped locale with golden strings reviewed by a native speaker.
Manual VoiceOver (iPhone 14) and TalkBack (Pixel 7) runs of the core flows are recorded per release in the F14.S01.M03 release checklist (V05) with device, date and owner.
The module stores no user data, so a user export contains nothing from it.
Spoken-name patterns live in the locale catalogs of F14.S02.M01 and follow their versioning.
Rollback restores the previous release patterns without data migration.
The module owns no stored entity; its artifacts are route inventory, waiver file, checklist and report in the repository.

The report schema lists for each run the route, state, theme, viewport, locale, rule id, impact, selector and WCAG success criterion, and report.json is validated against the JSON Schema tests/a11y/report.schema.json that requires all nine fields.

Waivers are structured data with an expiry, cannot be open-ended, and each names exactly one target (a route, a file glob or a component), so route-level axe findings and the file- or component-level lint findings of F14.S01.M01 and F14.S01.M02 are waived through the same file.

routes.yaml lists for every route its applicable UX states (by default all six of CTR-UX-001 UX-2) and, for each excluded state, a reason and the reviewer who approved the exclusion; waivers are for rule failures only, never for states a route does not have.
CI fails on any serious or critical axe violation that has no valid waiver.
CI fails on contrast failures, missing route coverage, expired waivers and incomplete manual checklist at release time.
Each failure has one stable code printed in CI output.

CI fails when a passphrase or recovery input on the vault unlock, recovery-kit restore or backup passphrase screens lacks the correct autocomplete value, blocks paste, drop or password-manager autofill, has no show/hide toggle, or when recovery offers transcription as the only path.
The gate runs as a pipeline of install, build, route discovery, axe runs, contrast check, authentication-assistance check, report and gate decision, and any failing step fails the build.
A release candidate cannot be tagged until the manual checklist for that candidate is complete.
There is no persisted lifecycle, so no entity state machine is declared.

Pull requests run the pairwise subset (light + 320 px + en and dark + desktop + ar-XB) over every route and applicable state; the full matrix runs nightly and must pass on the exact commit of a release candidate before it is tagged.
The module exposes command-line tasks and no vault or relay commands, queries or events.
Tasks return exit codes and write machine-readable reports for the release process.
Failures use stable codes so dashboards and triage can group them.
The tooling needs no application authorization and runs only in CI and on developer machines.
Waiver changes require review by two maintainers (CODEOWNERS) because they weaken the gate.
Test fixtures use synthetic vaults and never real user data.
Every task is deterministic and re-runnable, producing the same report for the same commit apart from timestamps.
Flaky browser failures are retried once and reported as flaky if the retry passes, without hiding real findings.
Partial runs never mark a build green; a missing report fails the gate.
Test runs use synthetic data only, so reports contain no user data.
Reports contain selectors and rule ids, never text typed by users, and are kept as CI artifacts for 90 days.
The gate cannot be silently weakened, because waivers expire, require two reviewers and are listed in every report, and state exclusions in routes.yaml carry a reviewer.
CI publishes violation counts by rule, route and impact as artifacts and a trend over the last 30 builds.

The pull-request axe subset completes in 15 minutes or less and the nightly full matrix in 60 minutes or less on the CI runner, assuming at most 60 routes with 4 applicable states on average; above 60 routes the budget and the subset are revisited.
The contrast check completes in 10 seconds or less.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test or documented manual pass.
The gate itself is tested with seeded broken fixtures that must fail it, proving it detects what it claims to.
Manual criteria are recorded per release with device, date and owner.
The module holds no user data; its repository artifacts are versioned with each release tag.
Upgrading axe-core or @axe-core/playwright is done by pinning exact versions after a trial run, and a rollback restores the previous pin and baseline report.
The accessibility statement draft is generated from results and edited by humans, never published automatically.

The module owns no stored entity; its types are Money (CTR-MNY-001, F09.S03.M03), the F09.S03.M01 CurrencyDef { code, kind fiat | crypto, decimals, name } supplied by callers from the registry, and QuoteLabel { source, sourceKind, issuerDisplay?, label?, signatureVerified, asOf, expiresAt, status, pinned? } built by callers from an F09.S03.M02 FxQuote.
Amounts are canonical F09.S03.M03 minor-unit strings (optional leading minus, 1 to 38 digits, no leading zeros, never '-0') or bigint in code, and are never converted to floating point.
Display output is derived data and is never stored or sent as the source of truth for an amount.
Inputs are validated before formatting so the output is either exact or an explicit error, never a silently wrong number.
Parsing refuses ambiguous or lossy input instead of rounding.

Each failure has one stable error code usable in forms and tests; Money and currency errors reuse the F09.S03.M03 and F09.S03.M01 codes (N1) and only input and label errors specific to display or a locale use I18N_ codes.

Group separators in typed text are accepted only when every group after the first has exactly 3 digits and the text also contains the locale decimal separator; text with group separators but no decimal separator is rejected with I18N_MONEY_AMBIGUOUS and the hint 'use 12345 or 12,345' written with the locale's separators.

formatMoney, formatMoneyParts, formatApprox and parseMoneyInput return Err(I18N_MONEY_SPEC_MISMATCH), never a string, when money.currency differs from the CurrencyDef code, and Err(COMMERCE_CURRENCY_UNKNOWN) when the caller found no CurrencyDef for the code.
Formatting is a pure function from (Money, CurrencyDef, locale, options) to a Result of a string and parts.
Parsing is a pure function from (text, locale, CurrencyDef) to a Result of a minor-unit string, normalized to a neutral decimal string and built with F09.S03.M03 parseDecimal.
There is no persisted lifecycle, so no entity state machine is declared.
The module exposes library functions and no vault or relay commands, queries or events.
All public functions return Result values, Ok with the string, parts or minor-unit amount for valid input and an AppError otherwise, never a silently wrong string.
Formatting the same input twice returns identical output, so UI snapshots are stable.
The library performs no authorization and has no roles; it runs in the browser under the unlocked local principal.
It reads no vault data itself; callers pass in the Money, the F09.S03.M01 CurrencyDef, the QuoteLabel and the display preference.
Formatted strings are derived from data the viewer is already allowed to see and add no new disclosure.
Formatting is deterministic and idempotent, and never returns a string for an invalid amount; invalid input yields an explicit error value shown as a localized message.

If the Intl implementation lacks exact decimal-string support, the BigInt part-substitution path produces identical output; a startup self-test verifies the two paths agree on 20 sample values, and on any disagreement the BigInt path is used for the rest of the session and a development warning is logged.

If Intl.NumberFormat cannot format a registered currency code (not in Intl's currency list, such as USDC), the decimal style plus isolated code is used so a price is never blank; a code missing from the registry returns COMMERCE_CURRENCY_UNKNOWN and callers render the explicit 'amount unavailable, unknown currency <code>' state.
The module stores and transmits nothing, and formatted prices are never logged with user identifiers.

Price display must not mislead, so an approximate value is rendered only with its full label (code, provenance wording, time and expired marker); without a source or time the converted amount is not rendered at all and callers show the original-currency price with 'conversion unavailable', and the UI never presents an approximate value as a payment amount.

Quote source display names come from catalog keys for known adapter IDs; other source strings and issuer pseudonyms are rendered as plain text through F14.S02.M01 t() parameters (bidi-isolated, directional controls removed), never as links or markup.

Quote wording reflects provenance, so a manual or unverified quote never borrows a provider's authority; manual quotes read 'manual rate by <issuer>', unverified quotes read 'unverified source', the bare 'quote from <name>' wording is reserved for verified catalog adapters, and 'pinned rate agreed by all parties' appears only when the caller passes pinned.consentCollected true (N16).
CI reports golden-string and property test results; production builds send no metrics.
Formatting one amount takes 0.05 ms or less at p95 after the formatter cache is warm.
The module adds at most 3 KiB gzip to the initial bundle beyond the browser's built-in Intl and the F09.S03.M03 package.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Property tests prove digit-exactness for random bigint amounts up to 38 digits in every shipped locale, for fiat decimals 0 to 18 and crypto decimals 0 to 36.
Golden strings are generated with a pinned Node ICU version and cross-checked in Chromium and WebKit, with CLDR differences reviewed.
The module stores no user data; amounts in exports remain minor-unit strings as defined by CTR-MNY-001 and are never formatted text.

The display preference (symbol, code or name) lives in F15.S04.M03 LocalSettings as the optional field moneyDisplay and travels with that module's vault export; the PWA shell reads it and passes it to formatMoney as the display option.
Upgrades of locale data change only display strings, never stored values, so rollback needs no data migration.

The module owns no stored entity; catalogs are static files and the chosen locale is the defaultLocale field of F15.S04.M03 LocalSettings (P1, device only), which the locale bootstrap reads at runtime through the vault-local query platform.local_settings.get.
A catalog is a flat JSON object from key to string or plural object, with keys named area.screen.name and plural objects holding the CLDR categories.
Placeholders use {name} syntax only, with no code execution or nested formatting, and every locale must have the same parameter set for a key.
CI validates every catalog against the en catalog and the plural rules of its locale.
Runtime negotiation and lookup never throw; invalid input degrades to English.
Each failure has one stable code printed in CI output.

Locale switching is a deterministic sequence of negotiate, load catalog, set lang and dir, re-render and dispatch a localechange DOM event; setLocale resolves after the event, and the announcement is made by the F14.S01.M02 PageShell.
A failed catalog load keeps the previous locale and shows the app in English if none was loaded, so the UI is never blank.
There is no persisted lifecycle, so no entity state machine is declared.
The module exposes library functions and no vault or relay commands, queries or events.
Functions return strings or Result values and never throw for bad input.

Push alert text is rendered on the device by the service worker from the template key of one of the three F13.S01.M01 push payload forms - the tpl inside the opened sealed box {v, tpl, ref, ck} of a sealed payload {v, urg, s}, the tpl of a relay-hook payload {v, urg, tpl, ref?, ck?}, or tp(notify.tpl.system.digest, n) for a digest payload {v, urg, tpl: notify.tpl.system.digest, n}; relays never render push text. Only the generic email templates of F13.S01.M02 (no user content, no amounts) may be rendered by the user-selected email relay.
The library performs no authorization and has no roles; any user may change their own locale.
Catalogs contain no secrets and are public static files shipped in the app bundle.
Locale choice is F15.S04.M03 LocalSettings.defaultLocale, changed only by the unlocked local principal through the vault-local command platform.local_settings.update.
Locale negotiation and catalog lookup are pure and idempotent; switching to the active locale does nothing.
If a catalog fails to load or parse, the app keeps the last good catalog or en and shows a retry control.

Interpolation never fails; a missing param renders as the visible ellipsis marker '…' with a development warning, never as an empty value or an exception, and CI fails when a call site omits a parameter declared in en (V07).

The chosen locale is a mild fingerprinting signal, so it stays in the vault and is sent to a relay only as a copy inside the opted-in email registration of F13.S01.M02 (consent purpose notify_email, F10.S01.M01), to that one user-selected email relay, and never otherwise; the browser's own Accept-Language header is outside the app's control.
User-provided text is inserted into messages as plain text only, preventing injection through parameters.

Missing-key diagnostics are written through the F15.S03.M01 logger into its in-memory ring buffer as P0 entries holding only the catalog key and locale tag; they are cleared on reload and leave the device only when the user explicitly exports diagnostics.

t() and tp() wrap every string parameter in FSI…PDI (U+2068…U+2069) and remove unpaired U+202A–U+202E and U+2066–U+2069 characters, and every U+202D or U+202E override, inside parameters at render time, whatever the sending vault did, because received titles and names come from other vaults that may be adversarial.
CI reports key coverage per locale and the number of fallbacks used in end-to-end runs; production builds send no metrics.
Locale switch completes within 300 ms after the catalog is loaded, and t() takes 0.05 ms or less per call.
Each catalog is at most 30 KiB gzip and loads in 1 s or less on the 4G profile.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Property tests cover plural selection for every shipped locale against CLDR data via Intl.PluralRules.
Pseudolocale end-to-end runs prove no clipping with expansion and correct mirroring in RTL.

The only user data involved is LocalSettings.defaultLocale, which F15.S04.M03 owns, exports and imports; this module owns no user data and registers no ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort or RetentionPurgePort (N6).
Importing a locale that is not shipped in this release selects the negotiated fallback and keeps the imported value so a newer release can honour it.
Catalog changes are additive; removing a key needs a deprecation period of one release.
The module owns no persisted entity; it defines cache namespaces, the build-time precache manifest and the routing table as configuration.

Cache names follow classrup-precache-v{buildId} for the Workbox precache and classrup-img-v1-<partition> for runtime public images, where buildId is the 8-character content hash of the build and partition is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the principal DID and a per-device random salt.
The routing table is data (an ordered list of rules) so it can be unit tested without a browser.

Image cache entries are keyed by content address under the synthetic same-origin URL /__media/sha256-<base64url>, so the same blob fetched from any relay is one entry and the relay that served it is not recorded.
The build fails when the precache manifest exceeds 1.5 MiB uncompressed or contains a URL that is not same-origin, so that budgets and the trust boundary are enforced before release.

A response is cached or handed to the page only when it passes the cacheability checks (status 200, image content type, no private directives, no cookies, at most 5 MiB) and the SHA-256 of its body equals the requested content address.
Violations during build are reported with stable codes; at runtime a cacheability violation means the response is not stored, and a digest mismatch means it is neither stored nor shown.
Control messages are accepted only from controlled same-origin window clients, and SKIP_WAITING only with the one-time nonce that the waiting worker issued in its GET_VERSION reply.

The build fails unless the precache manifest holds every shipped production locale catalog (en, de, fr, es) together within 120 KiB gzip, so the catalogs are installed in one step and no catalog is ever fetched per locale at runtime.
The worker follows the browser lifecycle installing, installed (waiting), activating, activated, redundant, and does not skip waiting on its own.

Activation only happens after the user consents (SKIP_WAITING with a valid nonce), when no client of the previous worker is open, or when the kill file retires the active build and the known-good build named there takes its place.
Activation deletes every classrup- cache not on the allowlist before the new worker handles fetches.

When the kill file names the active build (buildId in killedBuilds or releaseSeq below minReleaseSeq), the worker deletes all classrup- caches of that build within one update check and is replaced by the knownGood build, or unregisters itself when none can be installed; IndexedDB is never touched.

The module exposes no vault commands, relay commands or queries; its interface is the fetch event routing table and the postMessage messages SKIP_WAITING {nonce}, GET_VERSION, BIND_PARTITION {partition, relayOrigins} and CLEAR_USER_CACHES {reason, partition}.
Messages are accepted only from same-origin window clients, SKIP_WAITING only with a valid nonce, and unknown message types are ignored.
The module produces no domain events and consumes none; version and cache status are available to the page through GET_VERSION.

Public media is read only from the F15.S02.M01 route GET /media/v1/sha256-<base64url>, which serves P0 F15.S02.M03 blobs with Cache-Control public, max-age=31536000, immutable, Access-Control-Allow-Origin for allowlisted PWA origins and no Set-Cookie, outside the command bus's no-store policy.
The worker holds no credentials and attaches none; relay access tokens are added only by page code to relay commands and pass through NetworkOnly untouched, and vault data never enters Cache Storage.
