The module defines no capabilities because it performs no vault commands or relay operations; access to user data is governed by vault policy (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-8), and relays authorize only their own resources using relay access tokens (CAP-8 to CAP-10).

Only same-origin controlled windows may send control messages; vault lock, principal switch and Erase vault each send CLEAR_USER_CACHES, which unbinds the principal's image partition (lock, principal switch) or deletes it (Erase vault).
A failed install never replaces a working worker, and a failed runtime cache write never fails the response.
Fetch handlers are stateless; repeating a request has the same effect as a single request.
Offline navigation always resolves to the precached shell, and relay failures are surfaced as network errors to the page for the outbox and UI to handle.

No personal data, relay access token, vault record, P1 or higher content, or exact location is ever stored in Cache Storage; only build assets and verified public P0 images in per-principal partitions are cached.

Cached public images are limited to 200 entries and 30 days per partition, are unbound on vault lock and principal switch, are deleted on Erase vault, and are deleted on version change of the cache name.
The worker scope is limited to the application path and refuses to cache cross-origin opaque responses.

A relay cannot substitute or alter a cached or displayed image, because bytes are verified against the content address before caching and before display, and the cache is keyed by content address independent of the relay.

Catalog loads never reveal the chosen locale, because every production catalog is precached together at install and served from the precache, so neither the static host nor a relay sees a per-locale request (F14.S02.M01 T03 and T10).
Cache effectiveness and update adoption are measured only locally in the vault diagnostics view (the PWA sends no telemetry, CTR-OBS-001 OBS-7) and in CI runs.
Cached shell navigation meets the PWA budgets of CTR-OBS-001 OBS-5 (LCP ≤ 2.5 s on Moto G-class with 4G profile).
Precache size and entry count are tracked in CI per commit and fail the build on budget violations.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Routing, cacheability and verification logic is unit tested as pure functions, and lifecycle and offline behavior is tested in real browsers with Playwright.
Tests assert the negative property that no relay command, vault or private response ever reaches Cache Storage and no unverified image is ever shown.
Caches are derived data and are excluded from export, import and backup.
Rolling back a release deletes the cache versions of the newer release on the next activation and keeps users' data untouched.

A kill file lets the static host retire a bad build within one update check (at most 1 hour) by replacing it with a named known-good build, or by unregistering the worker when none can be installed, without touching IndexedDB.

The module owns no persisted entity; install state, local session and action counters, dismissal counters, the last session in which the card was shown, update deferral and the unverified-build flag are per-device preferences stored in localStorage under the key classrup.install.v1.
The manifest is a build artifact validated against fixed field rules; its id is stable forever so reinstalls keep the same app identity.
Preferences contain no personal data and are safe to lose; the module renders correctly when storage is unavailable.
The build fails if the manifest violates installability rules, so a broken app is never published.
The install prompt is shown only when its gating rules hold, so it never interrupts first-time use and appears at most once per session.
Update activation is allowed only at a safe point.

An update is offered only for a waiting build whose signed release manifest verifies under the release key pinned in the running build, and activation requires a live user gesture checked in the page (navigator.userActivation.isActive) plus the waiting worker's one-time nonce.

Before an update is offered and again immediately before activation, the module checks for a release hold that verifies through F16.S02.M03 under context classrup/release-hold/v1 and the release key pinned in the running build, and refuses activation of a covered build while the hold is valid.
Install and update each follow explicit states and the UI shows only the state reached.

While a client of the running build is open, a waiting worker is activated only after consent with a live user gesture, never by automatic skipWaiting; once every client is closed the browser activates a waiting worker at the next cold start, so consent covers live tabs only and the spec does not claim more.
Deferral is time-boxed so the user is asked again after 24 hours but never forced.

A waiting build whose release manifest fails V07 is never offered for update; the unverified-build warning is shown and persisted so that the next start, if the browser activated that build anyway, still shows the warning.

While a valid release hold covers the waiting build (V08) the attempt is held - Update is hidden, the paused notice names the reason and expiresAt, consent cannot override it, and the hold ends only at expiresAt - and, as with an unverified build, the browser may still activate the waiting build at a cold start once every client is closed, which the notice tells the user to avoid.
The module has no vault commands, relay commands, queries or events; its interface is UI components, the manifest and a small local API (install(), applyUpdate(), getInstallState()).
Nothing in the module calls a relay or any network origin other than the app's own static files, including the waiting build's /release-manifest.json.
Local state is exposed to other modules only through getInstallState(), a pure read.
The module performs only local UI actions by the person holding the device and defines no relay capabilities.
Installing or updating changes code, never vault data, and requires an explicit user gesture checked in the page.

No relay or remote party can trigger install or update; the update source is only the app's own origin, which the user chose by opening it, and an update is offered only when signed by the pinned release key; a compromised origin can still run its code at the next cold start, which the warning and published checksums expose.
Repeated install() or applyUpdate() calls are safe and have the effect of one call.
A failed activation leaves the previous version running and the banner available.
Everything works with no connectivity; update checks simply fail silently and retry at the next trigger.
The module collects no analytics and sends nothing to any server (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-7); install and update counters remain on the device.

The persistent-storage explanation says that data lives on this device, that clearing site data or browser eviction can delete it, and that export is the backup, with a reminder after 30 days, or after 7 days when persistent storage is denied (F15.S01.M01 exportOverdueThresholdDays).
The install prompt must not nag or dark-pattern the user.
Install and update outcomes and the local session and action counters are counted locally and viewable in the diagnostics panel; no telemetry is sent.
The install card and update banner must not worsen CLS (≤ 0.1) or INP (≤ 200 ms) per CTR-OBS-001 OBS-5.
The module adds at most 6 KiB gzip to the initial bundle.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Manifest and gating logic are unit tested; the install and update flows are tested end to end in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox where each supports them.
A Lighthouse installability check runs in CI on the built app.
Install state and dismissal counters are device preferences and are excluded from the vault export.
Reinstalling the app on the same origin keeps the vault in IndexedDB; uninstalling or clearing site data deletes it, which the install explanation states before the first export reminder.
Rolling back to an earlier build is a static redeploy and needs no data migration in this module.

An OutboxEntry stores the canonical destination, kind (statement or relay_command), the prepared payload, the dedupe identity (statement cid or Idempotency-Key), optional expectedRevision or deterministic resourceId, the acknowledger role, principal, a monotonic sequence number, sync state, attempt counter, firstAttemptAt, receipts and timestamps, with ids and the vault tenantId per CTR-ID-001.

Entries are P2 device-local data held only in the principal's vault and never uploaded as a record; expiresAt is capped at createdAt + 30 days in every state, the payload is erased at expiry, and the payload-free expired stub is deleted 24 h later, so no payload outlives 30 days (RET-SHORT) and no row outlives createdAt + 30 days + 24 h.

The signed payload and cid of an entry are immutable after preparation; only sync bookkeeping changes, and a rebase or reroute discards the old entry (reason superseded or rerouted) and creates a new entry with a new id and seq (and, for a rebase, a new cid) instead of editing the old one.

OutboxEntry rows are the vault's only sync outbox and are written through the F15.S02.M03 transaction(fn) in the vault's single IndexedDB database, so a domain record and its outbox entry always commit or roll back together; this module publishes the one OutboxEntry state machine that every sender uses.

A federation statement entry also stores the F11.S02.M01 destination descriptor, {kind selected_relay, relayId} or {kind recipient_mailbox, recipientDid, mailboxId, relayId}, from which its canonical destination string is derived, and needsPeerAck (acknowledger counterparty) is true exactly for recipient_mailbox entries of participants statements.

Enqueue validates destination, delivery eligibility, size, quota, privacy class and signature presence before writing, inside the caller's storage.transaction(fn); on a violation nothing is stored and the domain record rolls back with it.

Delivery classifies every relay response into receipt, retryable, conflict, relay rejection or failed using only the code, status and retryable flag from CTR-ERR-001, and accepts a receipt only after it verifies against the destination relay's published key set.

A peer acknowledgement is accepted only when it is a verified signed statement over exactly this entry's cid, signed by the recipient DID that the statement registry names as acknowledger, with a key authorized for that DID at verification time; otherwise it is refused with PLATFORM_OUTBOX_ACK_MISMATCH.

Statements registered at class P2 or higher are accepted for a relay destination only as end-to-end encrypted envelopes addressed to the recipients' mailbox keys, and schemas or fields classified P3 or P4 are never queued (CTR-PRV-001 PRV-5).
Every deliveryEligible relay command declares its replay safety, and a relay command first attempted more than 23 h ago is resent only when that replay safety holds; otherwise it moves to conflict.

Relay key revocations, rotations and restore announcements are used only after their signatures verify against the relay's key history, and a relay whose key history equivocates is frozen for delivery.

A destination descriptor must match the registry audience of the statement (public to selected_relay, participants to recipient_mailbox), its canonical string must equal the entry destination and recipientDid, and a caller-supplied needsPeerAck that disagrees with the registry is refused.
Entries follow the declared lifecycle and any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.

transport_acknowledged is recorded only after a relay receipt verifies (V14) and peer_accepted only after a verified acknowledgement of the exact cid (V09), which is accepted from prepared, sending, failed or transport_acknowledged; a network failure or a missing reply never advances the state, a direct transfer stays prepared (export prepared) after its bytes are produced, and the UI shows the state reached.

Conflict and failed entries block only later entries with the same destination and aggregateKey, are never auto-merged or auto-retried, and forked conflicting promises freeze the affected coordination instead of choosing a winner.

A rebase or reroute never edits an entry; the old entry moves to discarded with reason superseded or rerouted and supersededBy, and the replacement is a new entry with a new id and seq, re-validated by V04, V05, V10 and V11.

A verified restore announcement of the destination relay that covers an entry's receipt returns the entry from transport_acknowledged to prepared, and it is resent with the same cid or Idempotency-Key.

An entry that needs no peer acknowledgement (a public statement on a selected relay or a relay command) moves to completed when its relay receipt verifies; completed is its final sync state, claims only relay receipt (the transport acknowledged row of CONSISTENCY_STATES, never peer acceptance), is kept until createdAt + 30 days and is reopened to prepared only by a verified restore announcement covering its receipt.

A transport_acknowledged entry that reaches its expiry without a verified acknowledgement ends in expired with expiredOutcome unconfirmed, a terminal unconfirmed outcome shown with the transport_acknowledged text (delivered to the relay, peer has not confirmed), never as failed and never as not sent.

An entry for which the FederationTransportPort reports a hold (the retryable F11.S02.M01 FEDERATION_RECIPIENT_UNRESOLVED) stays prepared with heldReason recipient_unresolved, consumes no attempt and is not sent until F11.S02.M01 re-routes it, which discards it as rerouted and prepares a new entry with the same payload and cid for the recipient's new mailbox; the 7-day unsent expiry still applies.

Every command here is a vault-local command with actor = unlocked local principal; none is a relay command and none produces a signed statement itself, although the entries it manages carry statements produced by other modules.
The module produces no domain events leaving the device and emits only local UI notifications over the BroadcastChannel classrup-outbox (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-8).
Relay responses are interpreted only through CTR-ERR-001 fields so that new error codes need no code change here.

Destination strings, relayId, relay receipts (classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1), key history and restore announcements use the formats defined by F15.S02.M01 and F15.S03.M03; this module verifies them and never issues them.

The acknowledger role and privacy class of every queued statement schema come from the F11.S01.M01 statement registry (N2); this module acts only on acknowledgements that the receiving path verified and that pass V09.

Enqueue is available to other modules only as OutboxPort.enqueue(tx, entry) inside their own F15.S02.M03 transaction, and the vault-local command platform.outbox.enqueue wraps the same call in a transaction of its own for entries without a domain record.

platform.storage.get_status reports persistence, quota, eviction risk and export age, with exportOverdue = exportAgeDays > exportOverdueThresholdDays, where the threshold is 30 days when storage is persisted and 7 days otherwise (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-6; used by F15.S01.M03).

Federation statements are delivered only through the FederationTransportPort that F11.S02.M01 registers in the kernel port registry at vault composition (inverted registration, because F11.S02.M01 depends on this module), called with the entry's destination descriptor and needsPeerAck, and this module is the only vault-side outbox for them; relay commands use the relay transport of F15.S02.M01 destinations.

The sync chip, its accessible name and the outbox sheet derive one SyncState per item through syncStateOf(entry) - local_committed for a committed record without an entry, otherwise the entry state, except that an expired entry with expiredOutcome unconfirmed shows transport_acknowledged - and render it only from the shared catalog keys sync.state.<value> with {transport} naming the relay display name or the peer's device directly, so the visual text equals the F14.S01.M02 spokenSync text.
Vault policy applies, meaning only the unlocked local principal may run any command or query here, and every entry is bound to the principal that created it.

The outbox stores no session token, relay access token or private key; each delivery obtains a relay access token by challenge-response at send time (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-10), so a relay that revoked access cannot be sent to.

Relay policy decides at send time whether the relay accepts the write or mailbox delivery; a FORBIDDEN or BLOCKED_PARTY response or a relay-signed rejection marks the entry failed with failureReason relay_rejected and never changes local data.

Every relay command is sent with its stored Idempotency-Key and every statement carries its cid, so deliveries inside the relay's 24 h idempotency window take effect at most once; after 23 h from firstAttemptAt a relay command is resent only with expectedRevision, a deterministic resourceId with create-if-absent semantics or a read-back showing no effect, and otherwise moves to conflict with "may already have been applied" (CTR-IDM-001 IDM-1, CTR-FED-001 FED-7).
Retry timing follows IDM-4 exactly; only retryable errors and network failures are retried, at most 6 attempts per entry.
A crash between send and receipt leaves the entry recoverable, and a lost peer acknowledgement leaves it in transport_acknowledged rather than claiming acceptance.

Receipts that a verified restore announcement of the destination relay declares lost return the entry to prepared, and it is resent with the same cid or Idempotency-Key, so data a restored relay lost is delivered again.

Queued payloads are signed statements or relay commands that can contain P2 content; they stay in the vault, and enqueue enforces PRV-5 by rule V10 (P2 to a relay only as an end-to-end encrypted envelope for the recipient's mailbox keys) and V11 (P3/P4 never queued), using the statement registry and F10.S02.M02 field classes.

Unsent entries expire after 7 days with a prompt and entries awaiting an acknowledgement at createdAt + 30 days; the payload is erased at expiry, expired entries are never sent, and no row outlives createdAt + 30 days + 24 h.
A hostile page script or another principal on a shared browser profile must not be able to read or send a principal's entries, and the PWA sends no telemetry (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-7).

The module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort for F10.S01.M03, F10.S01.M04 and F10.S01.M02 through the kernel port registry (inverted dependency, because F10.S01.M01 and F10.S01.M04 depend on this module), annotates every OutboxEntry field with its F10.S02.M02 class, and consumes privacy.deletion.completed (N6).
The PWA sends no telemetry; outbox and storage diagnostics stay in the vault, are shown in the Storage status panel and can be exported by the user (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-7).
Enqueue completes fast enough to feel instant on a Moto G-class device (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-5).
Delivery of 200 entries never blocks the main thread for more than 50 ms per task.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Logic is tested with fake-indexeddb through the F15.S02.M03 IndexedDB adapter, and the Web Locks, reconnect and UI flows with a real browser (Playwright, offline emulation).

Conformance with CTR-IDM-001 IDM-1, IDM-4, IDM-5 and IDM-7 is tested with a stub relay that injects network failures, 429 and 409 responses, signed relay receipts, key rotations, restore announcements and peer acknowledgements.

The outbox is device-local transient state; its ExportSectionPort contributes section platform.outbox with counts per state and destination and no payloads (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-1, IOX-6), and the export contains the signed statements already committed in the domain records.
Outbox entries are never imported; after an import the user sees imported records only, and unsent statements must be re-created from the records.
Storage schema upgrades are forward-only through F15.S02.M03 migrations with data kept, and a downgrade of the app leaves the database untouched and ignores entries it cannot read.
An IdempotencyRecord stores tenantId, actor, command name, idempotency key, requestHash (SHA-256 of canonical JSON of the raw input), response status, response JSON body, createdAt and expiresAt.

All identifiers are lowercase canonical UUIDv7 values generated from WebCrypto randomness with a monotonic counter inside one millisecond; IDs more than 24 h ahead of the receiver clock are rejected with ID_TIMESTAMP_SKEW.
IdempotencyRecord rows expire 24 h after creation; lookups ignore expired rows and a purge removes them.
Command and query input is parsed strictly with zod; unknown keys, missing fields and type errors return VALIDATION_FAILED with fields [{path, code}] using stable UPPER_SNAKE codes.
Shared validators exist for UUIDv7, RFC 3339 UTC millisecond timestamps, strings bounded in code points and the Money shape {amount integer string, currency 3 to 10 uppercase}.
Idempotent commands require an Idempotency-Key that is a UUIDv7; a missing or malformed key returns VALIDATION_FAILED on field idempotencyKey and a key from the future returns ID_TIMESTAMP_SKEW.
defineMachine rejects at definition time any terminal state with an outgoing transition, any ambiguous (from, event) pair and an initial state that does not occur in the table.
next(state, event) returns the declared target state or CONFLICT_STATE with params.state and params.event, and can(state, event) agrees with next.
Each machine exports its transition table (from, to, on and edges()) so module tests compare it with the module.spec.yaml rows.

Commands and queries are declared with defineCommand and defineQuery (name, module, capability, strict zod input, idempotent flag, surface vault, relay or both, deliveryEligible, handler) and registered once; duplicates are rejected at startup.

The dispatch pipeline runs flag, authn, rate limit, validation, authorize, idempotency, handler in one transaction, outbox, idempotent response and audit in that order, and each stage short-circuits with its CTR-ERR-001 code.

Events are CTR-EVT-001 envelopes built from defineEvent(type, version, privacy, payload schema); payloads are validated strictly, written to the local outbox in the handler transaction and published to the EventSink only after commit.

The bus runs in-process in the vault without any network, and the Node HTTP adapter exposes only relay-surface definitions at POST /api/v1/cmd/<name> and POST /api/v1/query/<name> with problem+json errors.
The module provides three relay commands for access tokens; none of them is a vault command and none produces a signed statement.

The bus calls AuthzPort.authorize(actor, capability, resource, context) before the handler and denies by default; the vault composition passes the local principal with vault policy, the relay composition passes the relay actor with relay policy.
FORBIDDEN is mapped to NOT_FOUND when a definition sets hideForbidden (ERR-4), and vault-surface definitions are not reachable from a remote transport.
Every allow and deny decision for a state-changing command is recorded through AuditPort with actor, capability, operation, resource reference, decision and code, never payload content (CAP-7).
A missing session on a definition that requires authentication, or an invalid relay access token, yields UNAUTHENTICATED before rate limiting and validation.

The same key with the same request hash within 24 h replays the stored status and body (Idempotent-Replay true over HTTP); the same key with a different hash returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; failed commands store nothing.
A handler error result or exception rolls back records, outbox events, sync-outbox entries and the idempotency record together; exceptions map to INTERNAL and are logged with the correlation ID.
Concurrent dispatches with the same key are serialized by the storage transaction so the handler runs at most once.
Only RATE_LIMITED, DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and INTERNAL are retryable; RATE_LIMITED carries retryAfterMs and the HTTP Retry-After header.
Problem responses expose only type, title, status, code, retryable, messageKey, params, fields, correlationId and retryAfterMs; never stack traces, SQL, internal messages or another user's data.
IdempotencyRecord rows are scoped to (tenantId, actor, command, key), may hold P2 response bodies, never leave the vault or relay that stored them and are purged after 24 h.
The HTTP adapter enforces 256 KiB JSON bodies, sends Cache-Control no-store, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and a deny-all CSP, and never logs the Authorization header, tokens or request bodies.

Every command records classrup_command_duration_ms and classrup_command_total{module, outcome, code} and every query records classrup_query_total and classrup_query_duration_ms when a metrics registry is wired (OBS-3).
Bus overhead keeps relay writes within OBS-4; 500 sequential sample commands on SQLite WAL complete with p95 at or below 50 ms.
Each command and query logs exactly one line with correlationId, module, code, durationMs and operation and no input or output values.
Every requirement of PS-117 is covered by a test whose title starts with its TEST-PS-117-09 identifier.
The kernel core is isomorphic; no file outside the Node adapter entry imports a module with the node scheme, which a static test enforces.
Property tests (fast-check, at least 200 runs) cover UUIDv7 monotonicity and state machine transitions.
IdempotencyRecord rows are operational data excluded from the user export (IOX-1); rows restored from an older backup are ignored once expired.
Error codes, the problem shape and the event envelope are versioned contracts; changes within v1 are additive and removed codes are never reused.
HTTP routes are versioned under /api/v1; unknown versions or paths return NOT_FOUND so N-1 clients fail explicitly during a rollback.

A RelayIdentity record stores the stable relayId, the keyId and seq, public key, status (active, retired or revoked), the previous keyId, the signed rotation and revocation statements and timestamps for each signing key; the private seed is never stored in the database or logged.

The relayId is derived once from the genesis public key and stays stable across rotations signed by the previous key, so vaults keep their relay selection and can verify the chain; any key not reachable through that chain (after a revocation of the active key, a lost key file or --new-identity) always yields a new relayId.

Rotated-out keys remain published with status retired for at least 400 days so older receipts stay verifiable, and revoked keys remain published with their signed revocation for as long as the relay exists; a receipt signed by a revoked key is valid only in a vault that stored it before revokedAt.

The canonical identifiers are defined here and referenced by F15.S01.M01, F15.S02.M03, F11.S02.M01 and F01.S01.M03 - relayId 'relay:' plus the first 26 characters of lowercase RFC 4648 base32 (no padding) of SHA-256 of the genesis public key; keyId '<relayId>#k<seq>'; destination '<relayId>', '<relayId>/mailbox/<mailboxId>', '<relayId>/index/<indexName>', '<relayId>/auction/<auctionId>' or 'direct:<did>'.

A revocation with reason compromised signed by the revoked key itself names successorRelayId, the relayId of the successor genesis key generated in the same CLI run, and the successor identity records predecessorRelayId and publishes, as its first statement, a relay-signed restore announcement naming the predecessor.
Configuration is validated strictly at startup against a typed schema with defaults and ranges; unknown RELAY_* variables are warned about, invalid ones abort startup.
Every HTTP request is bounded by size and time limits for its route class before it reaches the command bus or the media store.
Violations map to stable codes; configuration failures use exit code 78 (EX_CONFIG).
Identity changes are checked for revision, rate and signing authority before any statement is signed, and the media route serves only public unencrypted blobs.

The relay key file is checked with F16.S01.M02 checkSecretFile before it is read and the seed is held only in the Secret wrapper, and the secrets owned by F16.S01.M02 use RELAY_SECRET_<NAME> or RELAY_SECRET_<NAME>_FILE and are never read, printed or validated by this module's configuration loader.
The process follows starting, ready, draining, stopped, and /readyz is true only in ready.

Shutdown is ordered, meaning stop accepting, drain in-flight requests for up to 10 s, stop the dispatcher after its current batch, run the registered pre-checkpoint hooks (the F15.S03.M02 final WAL archive), checkpoint with TRUNCATE only if every hook succeeded, and close the database.

A RelayIdentity key moves from active to retired only through a rotation that it signs itself, from active or retired to revoked only through revocation from the local CLI with filesystem access (no prior-key authorization required), and never back.

relay identity init --new-identity activates the pending successor key named by a compromise revocation (or a fresh genesis key), and before the port opens it calls the NewIdentityHook that F15.S03.M03 registers with the relay process to sign and publish a classrup.platform.relay_restore/v1 announcement from the new identity naming predecessorRelayId; the relay does not become ready without that announcement.

The module registers relay commands and queries for identity (rotate, revoke) and status through the shared command bus, plus the HTTP routes /.well-known/classrup-relay.json and /media/v1/*; vault commands are not defined here.
Rotation and revocation are the only relay commands that change identity, and each emits platform.relay_identity.rotated for relay-local consumers.
The dispatcher consumes no domain events; it delivers events produced by other modules to their consumers.

Every relay route that accepts bytes for storage or forwarding (mailbox put of F08.S01.M01, index and publication intake of F06.S01.M01 and F11.S01.M02, federation inbox POST /fed/v1/inbox, media upload PUT /media/v1, auction bid intake of F04.S01.M02) returns in its response field receipt a classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1 from ReceiptPort.issue - the RFC 8785 JCS body { relayId, keyId, destination, digest, cid?, receivedAt, epoch, seq } signed with Ed25519 over the bytes of context 'classrup-relay-receipt:v1', a 0x0A byte and the JCS body, where digest is sha256- plus base64url SHA-256 of the exact request bytes received (the ciphertext for mailbox puts) and cid is present only for P0 public statements; vaults verify it against the published key set including retired keys.

Statements signed by this module and their signer role relay_identity are registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2) - classrup.platform.relay_receipt/v1, classrup.platform.relay_rotation/v1 and classrup.platform.relay_key_revocation/v1; the restore announcements classrup.platform.relay_restore/v1 written by F15.S03.M03 are served here unchanged.

The public media route GET /media/v1/sha256-<base64url> is handled before the command bus and sends Cache-Control public, max-age=31536000, immutable, ETag equal to the content address, Content-Type of the blob, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy cross-origin, Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing an allowlisted PWA origin with Vary Origin, and never Set-Cookie (exempt from the bus's no-store policy).

Every non-genesis key is published at /.well-known/classrup-relay.json only together with its rotation statement signed by the previous key under classrup-relay-rotate:v1, so a vault that pinned the relay's key set when the user selected the relay follows only signed rotations (F01.S01.M03 V16, F15.S01.M01 V15) and treats any key outside the chain as a different relay.

Relay policy applies, so identity reads are public, status reads and rotation need the relay-scope role relay_operator or admin, and revocation needs local CLI access; the roles are F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment records of scope relay that govern nothing beyond this relay (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-9), and tenant-scoped operator roles never grant these capabilities.

The relay holds no user credentials; operator actions are authorized by signed requests from a device key holding an active F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment, or by the local CLI with filesystem access to the key file, never by entries in the relay configuration.
Receipts and announcements are signed with the relay key under context strings, so a relay signature never authorizes any action on a vault.
Startup is repeatable, so migrations, identity creation and lease acquisition are idempotent, and a crash during startup leaves a state from which the next start succeeds.
Event delivery is at least once and consumers are idempotent through the inbox (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-3); the dispatcher can be killed at any point without losing events.
The relay is stateless toward vaults beyond the data it hosts; losing it never loses user-owned private data.

The relay stores only signed public projections, encrypted envelopes, P0 public media and relay-local operational data; it sees ciphertext plus minimal routing metadata for P2 data (CTR-PRV-001 PRV-5) and never plaintext P2 or higher.

Logs omit tokens, bodies and personal data, record only registered route templates without path parameters, query strings, mailbox ids or listing ids, truncate IPs to /24 or /48 and omit the IP prefix entirely on mailbox routes, and are kept 1 year as RET-AUDIT then deleted (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-1).
Operators can read only what the relay holds; seizure of a relay reveals no vault private records, keys or plaintext messages, and its logs do not link client addresses to mailboxes.
A receipt for a mailbox put signs only the digest of the ciphertext and the mailbox destination, never the plaintext statement cid, so receipts disclose nothing beyond PRV-5 routing metadata.
The relay exports logs and metrics per CTR-OBS-001 OBS-1 to OBS-4 and OBS-6 through the observability module, including dispatcher lag and drain duration.
The relay meets the reference budget on 2 vCPU / 4 GB with read p95 ≤ 150 ms and write p95 ≤ 300 ms at 50 req/s.
Startup and shutdown times are bounded and measured.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Configuration, identity, shutdown and dispatcher behavior are tested against a real node:http server and a real node:sqlite database in CI.
A canary suite runs the node:sqlite adapter on the pinned Node version and on the latest 22.x to detect behavior changes in the stability 1.1 API early.

Production relay builds expose no test-only route or hook (clock, seed); end-to-end and chaos suites start the relay through the separate in-process e2e entry that injects the FakeClock and seeding, and F17.S01.M04 V07 and T21 probe and scan the production build.
RelayIdentity public records are included in the relay's operational export; the private seed and revocation certificates are excluded and backed up only by the operator in a separate secret store.

A restored relay must present the same relayId and active key, otherwise members' vaults treat it as a different relay and show a fingerprint warning; a restore with --new-identity always yields a new relayId.
Application rollback redeploys the previous release (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-4); schema changes are expand/contract so N-1 starts.

A StoredRecord holds the key (tenantId, type, id), a revision starting at 1 and incremented by exactly 1 per accepted write, JSON data, up to four indexed text values and createdAt and updatedAt timestamps.
An OutboxEvent stores the CTR-EVT-001 envelope with a strictly increasing sequence, and an InboxEntry records the delivery status, attempts and next attempt time per (consumer, eventId).
The memory, IndexedDB and SQLite adapters share one row model so data round-trips identically, including JSON normalization and UTF-8 binary ordering of index values.
A MediaBlob is stored by content address blob:sha256-<base64url> with size, content type, privacy class and encryption flag, and its holders are the records that reference it.
A put whose expectedRevision differs from the stored revision returns CONFLICT_REVISION with params.currentRevision; expectedRevision 0 creates and fails when the record exists.

Updating or removing a missing record returns NOT_FOUND; repository definitions declare a type named <slug>.<entity> and at most four indexes, and queries accept limit 1 to 500 and only declared index names.
Acquiring a lease held by another holder until expiresAt returns PRECONDITION_FAILED, and renewing an expired lease returns EXPIRED.
A blob larger than 5 MiB returns PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, a malformed content type or ref returns VALIDATION_FAILED, and relay storage rejects non-P0 plaintext blobs.
Outbox delivery per consumer follows the InboxEntry machine; a failure schedules a retry after random(0, min(30 s, 500 ms × 2^(attempt-1))) and the eighth failure moves the event to dead_letter.
Sync-outbox entries follow prepared, transport_acknowledged and peer_accepted with failed reachable from prepared and user retry back to prepared (IDM-7); no state implies more than was observed.
Leases follow acquire by compare-and-set, renew by the holder, release by the holder and automatic expiry at expiresAt, with a fencing counter that increases on every new acquisition (IDM-3, IDM-8).

Storage exposes transaction(fn) that commits records, outbox events, inbox entries, idempotency records, leases, sync-outbox entries and blob references atomically when fn returns ok and rolls back on err or exception.
Repo<T> per type offers get, require, put with expectedRevision, remove, restore and query by up to four indexed fields with equality and range filters, ordering and opaque cursors.
The outbox dispatcher delivers to subscribers registered per event type in (aggregate, revision) order per aggregate and deduplicates by (consumer, eventId) in the inbox.

The sync sender delivers signed statements per destination in creation order through a SyncTransport port and exposes recordPeerAck, the primitive behind platform.outbox.record_peer_ack (F15.S01.M01).
Blob storage offers put, get, info, attach and detach, and repositories that declare blob refs keep reference counts in step with record writes.
Storage performs no authorization itself and is reached only through the bus, the dispatcher or the sync sender, which scope every repository, lease, blob and sync entry to the context tenantId.
A repository, lease or sync scope bound to one tenant cannot read or write another tenant's rows.
Lease holders are proposal, cycle or auction IDs, never session tokens, and release or renewal by a non-holder returns PRECONDITION_FAILED.
Writes are serialized per vault or relay (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE with WAL and busy_timeout 5000; IndexedDB one readwrite transaction per commit), and a busy database maps to DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.
A failed IndexedDB commit restores the in-memory working set so the vault state equals the last committed state.
Consumer failures are retried with backoff and dead-lettered after 8 attempts, and a duplicate delivery is acknowledged without re-running side effects.
Storage copies record data only into its own row; logs, metrics labels, inbox rows and dead-letter rows carry IDs, types and error codes, never record data beyond the event envelope itself.
Outbox rows are pruned after 7 days and idempotency rows after 24 h; dead letters are kept 30 days (RET-SHORT) for replay.
Dead letters and inbox rows store the error code only, never exception messages with payload content.
Relay blob storage accepts only P0 plaintext or ciphertext, and a blob is deleted with its last reference so removed listings do not leave photos behind.
The dispatcher records classrup_outbox_lag_ms per consumer module and classrup_outbox_deliveries_total{module, outcome}, and the sync sender records classrup_sync_sends_total{outcome, code}.
On SQLite with 5 000 records a get-and-put transaction has p95 at or below 5 ms and a 50-item index query has p95 at or below 20 ms.
Dead-lettering logs one warn line with consumer, eventId, type and code and nothing from the payload.
One storage contract suite runs unchanged against the memory, SQLite and IndexedDB (fake-indexeddb) adapters.
Outbox ordering, inbox dedupe, backoff, dead letters and lease expiry are covered by deterministic tests with an injected clock and random source.
Every requirement of PS-119 is covered by a test whose title starts with its TEST-PS-119-09 identifier.

Records are exported by their owning modules (IOX-5); storage provides an ordered cursor scan per tenant and type and a restore that keeps IDs, revisions and timestamps and rejects conflicting copies.
Relay SQLite schema changes are forward-only kernel migrations recorded in schema_migrations, and data migrations run once each in their own transaction.
Rollback to N-1 is safe because kernel schema changes are additive, and drift between code and recorded kernel migrations stops startup with PLATFORM_STORE_MIGRATION_DRIFT.

A BackupRecord stores kind (full, wal, outbox_archive or tombstone_ledger), tier, timing, consistency point, WAL position or frame range, size, checksums, schema version, encryption parameters (salt, key fingerprint) and the manifest chain hash, but never key material.

A manifest JSON file next to every artifact holds the same facts so that restore works without a readable database, authenticated by an HMAC under a key derived from the backup key and chained to the previous manifest, so relabelled or out-of-chain manifests are refused.

Records are relay-local operational data (P1) retained under RET-AUDIT rules for 1 year, longer than the artifacts they describe, except tombstone ledger records which live as long as their 546-day artifacts.

A full BackupRecord records consistentAt and walPosition {salt1, salt2, mxFrame} at the true consistency point of the snapshot, and a WAL record the salts and frame range it covers, so the restore point and the data-loss window can be computed from records and manifests alone.

A full snapshot covers schema main only and records excludedBlobs, the number of encrypted MediaBlobs left out, so backups hold the F08.S01.M03 attachment rows and blob metadata but never attachment ciphertext.
Backup configuration is validated at startup, and a run refuses to start when preconditions fail.
Verification checks every integrity property before a snapshot may be marked verified.
Every violation maps to one stable error code with a messageKey for the operator tool.
Manifests and artifacts are accepted for verification, catalog import and restore planning only when their MAC verifies and they link into the chain.
A run refuses to start when encrypted MediaBlob bytes would be inside the backed-up database, and verification fails when a snapshot contains any.
A backup moves from running to completed only after the encrypted artifact and manifest are fsynced and renamed into place.

completed becomes verified only through a passing verification; a failed verification never deletes the artifact before its tier retention ends, and a verification attempted with a wrong or missing key leaves the record completed with errorCode PLATFORM_BACKUP_DECRYPT_FAILED and raises an alert.

Expiry is the only way an artifact is removed - a completed or verified artifact only when its retention elapsed and a newer verified snapshot covers the tier, a failed artifact when its tier retention elapsed - and the record is always kept.
The module exposes relay commands for an on-demand run and a verification, and queries for listing and status, all for the relay_operator or admin role of the relay hosting them.
Scheduled runs use the same code path as the manual run command and emit the same events.
platform.backup.completed and platform.backup.failed are emitted in the same transaction as the BackupRecord status change.

The platform.backup.completed payload carries consistentAt and walPosition so the restore point is known; WAL segments and ledger appends emit no event, and F15.S03.M03 builds its recovery plan from BackupRecords and authenticated manifests rather than from events.

Relay policy applies, and only a key holding the relay-scope relay_operator or admin role of this relay (an F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment) may run, verify or read backups; tenant-scoped operator roles grant nothing here.
The module has no vault access and handles no user credentials; requests are signed by a device key with an active F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment, or come from the local CLI with filesystem access.
Backup artifacts are readable only with the operator-supplied key, and the key never passes through the API.
A scheduled run that crashes leaves no partial artifact visible and is retried at the next slot; a manual rerun after failure starts a new record.
Backups never block relay writes beyond 50 ms and never run concurrently with each other.
A missing or failing backup is loud, with failure events, an alert after 7 h without a verified snapshot, and an extra snapshot after any integrity failure.

Backups contain only data the relay holds (signed public projections, ciphertext envelopes, P0 media, operational records) and are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM under per-artifact keys; plaintext P2 or higher and vault keys never exist on the relay and so never in backups.
Retention is 8 six-hourly, 30 daily, 12 monthly snapshots, 7 days of WAL segments and 546 days of tombstone ledger, and expired artifacts, including those of failed records, are deleted from disk.

Signed tombstones (CTR-PRV-001 PRV-6, CTR-FED-001 FED-4) survive restore - every tombstone the relay received is in the ledger, kept at least the maximum snapshot age plus 180 days and written by every run, and restore re-applies the newest ledger in its replaying phase - so restoring any retained snapshot, including a 12-month-old monthly one, never resurrects deleted public content.

Nonces never repeat under one key, chunks cannot be moved between artifacts, and manifests are authenticated and chained, so someone with write access to the backup directory cannot splice artifacts or relabel an older authentic backup as the latest.

Encrypted attachment MediaBlobs of F08.S01.M03 are never in a backup artifact, only their attachment rows and blob metadata are, so a deleted attachment cannot be recovered from this module's backups, and after a restore F08.S01.M03 marks the rows without ciphertext expired.
Backup health is exposed as metrics and events per CTR-OBS-001 with alerting thresholds that map to the RPO of 6 h and the typical data loss of 5 min.
Backups must not degrade relay latency beyond the OBS-4 budget while running.
Verification time and restore time are measured so that the RTO of 4 h is evidenced by drills.
WAL gaps are an anomaly that must stay at zero under the reference load, and WAL size and archive lag are observable.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Encryption, rotation and verification are tested with real node:sqlite databases and the real backup API in CI.
A restore drill test restores a generated database with 100 000 rows and proves equality of content hashes.
The operator export is the list of BackupRecords and manifests, not user data; user exports are produced by vaults (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-6) and never by this module.
A snapshot restores only into a new relay instance (IOX-4) and the identity key file must be provided separately, otherwise the instance has a different identity.
Backup schema changes follow expand/contract and manifests stay readable for at least 400 days.
A log line is one JSON object with ts, level and msg first, then correlationId, module, code and durationMs when present, then the remaining redacted fields.
Metrics are counters, gauges and histograms named classrup_<slug>_<name>_<unit> with labels limited to tenant, module, code and outcome.
A readiness report contains booleans for storage, migrations and outboxLag plus lagMs, and ready is true only when all three hold.
Metric names must match classrup_<slug>_<name>_<unit> without reserved suffixes and label names must be in the allowlist; violations throw at registration as programmer errors.
Series per metric are capped (default 1 000); extra label combinations are dropped and counted in classrup_metrics_dropped_series_total.
Log levels below the configured level are discarded and unknown levels are rejected when the logger is created.
GET /healthz returns 200 with status ok while the process serves requests and performs no dependency checks.
GET /readyz returns 200 only when storage is writable, migrations are current and outbox lag is below 60 s, otherwise 503 with the per-check booleans.
During graceful shutdown readiness turns unready before connections close so load balancers drain traffic.
The kernel core exports createLogger, createRingBufferSink, consoleSink, redact, truncateIp, createMetricsRegistry and createReadiness, and all of them are isomorphic.
GET /metrics renders Prometheus text format 0.0.4 and is reachable only by actors granted platform.metrics.read on that relay.
The vault uses the in-memory ring-buffer sink and no metrics export, so nothing is sent off-device (OBS-7).
GET /metrics requires a relay access token whose actor is granted platform.metrics.read by relay policy; others get UNAUTHENTICATED without a token or NOT_FOUND with one.
/healthz and /readyz are unauthenticated and reveal only status booleans and lag, never versions, hostnames or per-tenant counts.
Metric labels never contain actor, user or device identifiers; tenant is the only identity-bearing label and is relay-local.
A throwing log sink never fails the caller; the line is dropped and counted.
Metrics rendering is a pure read of in-memory state and histogram bucket counts, sums and counts stay consistent.
A readiness probe that throws reports unready for that check instead of failing the endpoint.

Redaction drops keys token, secret, password, privateKey, recoveryCode, email, address, lat, lon, note, body and ciphertext case-insensitively, plus authorization, cookie, passphrase and names ending in token, secret, password, email, address, note or body, at any depth.
IP addresses are truncated to /24 for IPv4 and /48 for IPv6 in logs, under IP keys and as bare values, including IPv4-mapped and compressed IPv6 forms.
The PWA sends no telemetry; vault log lines stay in a bounded ring buffer until the user exports them as JSON Lines.
Child loggers carry module and correlationId bindings so one request can be traced across modules by correlation ID.
Observability overhead is small; 10 000 redacted log lines and 100 000 metric updates complete in under 1 s.
Histograms use default millisecond buckets aligned with the OBS-4 budgets (including 150 and 300 ms) so budget compliance is visible.
Redaction and IP truncation have unit tests covering nested objects, arrays, errors, suffix variants and compressed IPv6 forms.
Prometheus rendering is tested against exact expected text including escaping and cumulative histogram buckets.
Every requirement of PS-121 is covered by a test whose title starts with its TEST-PS-121-09 identifier.
The vault diagnostics buffer exports as JSON Lines of already-redacted records on explicit user request only.
The log line format is versioned by field names; additions are additive and ts, level and msg always come first so N-1 parsers keep working.
Metric registration is idempotent for identical definitions so restarts and hot reloads do not duplicate series, and conflicting re-definitions fail fast.
The module owns no persisted entity; restore progress and results live in a restore-report.json file in the target directory.

Dead letters are rows of the dead_letter table owned by the storage module, which keeps replay_count and last_replayed_at across requeue and re-dead-lettering; this module only reads and re-queues them.

The restore report records timing, selected artifacts, checks, the data-loss window, events re-delivered and lost, excluded consumers, the restore announcement and frozen auctions so that drills are evidenced.
Restore refuses to run unless the target, the artifacts, the manifests, the ledger and the keys pass all preconditions.
Replay is bounded by count, repetition and consumer state so that it cannot cause event storms.
Every refusal returns one stable error code with a messageKey for the operator tool.
A restore follows ordered phases and any failure leaves the target directory unusable but the live system untouched.
The restored relay opens its port only after all phases pass and the operator confirms.

A dead letter moves back to pending delivery only through the replay command, each replay is counted in replay_count, and every non-terminal state has an exit - requeued events return to dead_lettered when the consumer is disabled or not delivered within 7 days, and dead letters are purged 30 days after deadLetteredAt.

Restore re-delivers only events with occurredAt ≤ reachedTimestamp whose aggregate revision exists in the restored records, never to consumers with external side effects, and reports later events as lost in rpoAchievedMs and lostEvents.
Before the port opens, the restore writes the relay-signed restore announcement, increments the receipt epoch and freezes relay-hosted auctions with activity in the lost window.

The module exposes relay commands for dead-letter replay and read-only queries for the recovery plan and dead letters, all for relay_operator or admin; the restore itself is an offline CLI that does not use the HTTP API.
Replay emits one summary event per call and never changes event payloads or order guarantees.

The module consumes backup events only to refresh the restore-readiness alert; the recovery plan is computed from BackupRecords and authenticated manifests, including WAL segments, which emit no event.

The restore announcement classrup.platform.relay_restore/v1 is a statement signed by the relay key under context classrup-relay-restore:v1 with signer role relay_identity, registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2), served unchanged by F15.S02.M01 and verified by F15.S01.M01 (V16).

For a new identity (relay identity init --new-identity of F15.S02.M01, or relay restore --new-identity) the NewIdentityHook signs the first restore announcement with the new genesis key, naming predecessorRelayId, with epoch 0, lastReceiptSeq 0, restoredTo the newest data the instance holds (announcedAt when it starts empty) and lostWindow from the predecessor's revokedAt (or restoredTo) to announcedAt; vaults apply it only to the new relayId and reroute to it only after the user confirms the new fingerprint.

Relay policy applies, so only a key holding the relay-scope relay_operator or admin role of this relay (F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment) may replay dead letters or read the plan, tenant-scoped operators may not, and restore requires filesystem access to the backup directory and the backup key.
Dead-letter listing returns metadata only; payloads are never shown through the API because they may contain P1 data.
The restore tool never needs vault keys or user credentials, and the relay identity key is read only from the operator-supplied key file.
Restore is safe to repeat because it only writes into an empty new directory and never touches the live database.
Replay is idempotent at the consumer level through the inbox (CTR-EVT-001 EVT-3), so duplicate delivery has no duplicate effect, and replay writes only dead_letter and inbox rows.
A failed restore phase is resumable from the report or restartable from scratch within the RTO budget.

Data the relay had receipted inside the lost window is recovered from its senders - the signed restore announcement lets vault outboxes return covered entries to prepared and resend them with the same cid or Idempotency-Key - and relay-hosted auctions with activity in that window are frozen for renegotiation rather than contradicting bid orders or results already signed.
Restore handles only encrypted relay data and the operator's keys, produces a report without payload content, and leaves no plaintext snapshot outside the target directory.
Temporary decrypted files are written only inside the restore target, mode 0600, and the target must be on encrypted or access-restricted storage per the runbook.

Every tombstone in the authenticated ledger is re-applied before the restored relay serves public projections, so deleted content is not resurrected on this relay whatever the age of the base snapshot.
Recovery readiness is measured continuously as restore-point age and dead-letter count per CTR-OBS-001.
Drills measure real restore time and compare it with the 4 h RTO and the achieved data-loss window with the 6 h RPO.
Replay throughput and failure counts are visible while running.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The restore path is exercised in CI against generated backups with WAL segments, including corrupted and missing inputs.
A quarterly manual drill on a clean machine is recorded with timings against the RPO and RTO.
The restore report is exportable and contains no content; user data export remains the vault's responsibility (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-6).
Restore is the only data rollback path and always produces a new instance with event replay, never an in-place downgrade (IOX-4).
Application rollback uses the previous release and requires N-1 compatible schemas, verified by opening restored data with the previous binary.
The registry is a generated, immutable data structure (not a stored entity) with one record per feature and per module, and a content hash over canonical JSON (RFC 8785).

Each module record holds id, title, feature id, slug, scope, surface (vault, relay or both), defaultState, registered flag, core flag, dependsOn (module IDs only), dependsOnKnown and dependents (derived).
The registry file is part of the build and versioned with the application, so vault and relay of the same release agree.
Generation validates structure, graph and defaults and fails the build on any violation with a stable code.
The same input always produces byte-identical output so that staleness is detectable by comparison.
Registry queries validate keys against the registry and never accept free-form patterns.
A module whose spec is missing is never treated as a module without dependencies; it stays off and unregistered, and strict generation fails.
The registry has no runtime lifecycle; it is regenerated per build and replaced as a whole.
Generation is an ordered pipeline of parse, merge, validate, order and write steps, and any failing step prevents writing.
The build never publishes a registry that failed validation.
The module exposes four read-only queries that run in the vault (local) and on a relay (relay query), with identical results for the same release.
There are no commands, statements or events because the registry never changes at runtime.
Query results are small enough to be served from memory in under 5 ms.
Settings > Features in the vault lists only modules with surface vault or both, and the operator console lists only relay or both, using the surface field of the registry.
Registry data is public information about the application, so queries are available to every local principal and to anonymous relay clients without authentication.
Vault policy applies locally and relay policy applies on a relay; neither can alter the registry because it is read-only and compiled in.
No capability exists to modify the registry at runtime, which prevents an operator or remote party from rewriting the dependency graph.
Generation and queries are pure functions of their inputs and are idempotent by construction.
A failed generation leaves the previous generated file untouched and fails the build.
A vault and a relay of different releases compare hashes and treat a mismatch as informational, not as an error that blocks work.
The registry contains no personal data and no per-user information, only public module metadata.
Querying the registry reveals nothing about a user's configuration, which lives in F15.S04.M02.
A tampered registry in a modified client cannot enable server-side features on a relay because relays evaluate their own flags (F15.S04.M02).
Generation reports counts and duration in CI and fails when budgets are exceeded.
Registry queries meet read budgets on the PWA and on a relay (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-4, OBS-5).
The PWA sends no telemetry; any usage counters stay local (OBS-7).
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Graph validation is tested with property tests over random graphs and with fixtures of every failure code.
The generated file for the real catalog is checked in CI and compared with a fresh generation.
The registry is application code and data, not user data, and is excluded from every export and backup.
Rolling back a release restores that release's registry together with its code, so no migration is needed.
Imports of vault data from a release with unknown modules keep those records read-only and listed, never dropped.
A FlagSetting stores scope, tenantId, key, value, beta roles, reason, actor and revision, with unique (scope, tenantId, key).

Vault-scope settings live only in the user's vault and are P3 (device-only configuration that could fingerprint a user and is never transmitted); relay-scope settings live in the relay database and are P0 because they describe hosting policy visible to clients.
Settings are never deleted when a module is turned off; resetting a key removes the row so the registry default applies.
The vault-scope tenantId is the vaultId of the vault (F15.S04.M03), taken from the dispatch context tenantId, and never a constant; the relay-scope tenantId is the relay tenant of F15.S04.M03.
Every write is validated against the registry, the dependency rule, the lock list and role names before any change.
Evaluation never throws; unknown keys evaluate to off and are logged locally.
Each violation maps to one stable error code with params that list the modules involved.
A flag key has three values and any change goes through the same validated transition.
A change and its cascade are atomic, so all dependents change or none.
Evaluation always reflects the committed state after at most 30 s of caching, and immediately in the writing process.

The module has two vault-local commands (set and reset, vault scope only) and two relay commands (set_relay and reset_relay, relay scope only, each with tenantId and Idempotency-Key), plus queries for evaluation and listing, all with the signatures below.
A vault-local change produces no signed statement and never leaves the device; a relay change is a relay command that emits a relay-local event.
The module consumes platform.tenant.created to prepare evaluation for a new community, and privacy.deletion.completed to confirm that the deleted principal's vault-scope settings are gone (N6).
Vault policy applies, so only the unlocked local principal can change or reset vault-scope flags, and no remote party can change them.

Relay policy applies, so only a key holding an active F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment of role operator for scope tenant:<tenantId>, or admin, on that relay can change or reset relay-scope flags, and that changes only what that relay hosts for that community (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-9).
Effective values may be read by any local principal, and by any relay client for the community they use, because clients need them to hide entry points.
Writes are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision, so retries and concurrent edits are safe.
A cascade is a single transaction; a failure leaves no partial change.

When settings cannot be read, evaluation fails closed - it uses the last committed values kept in memory or in the mirror row, and when none are available every switchable non-core module evaluates off, the UI shows "settings unavailable" and the relay answers DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE for relay commands of affected modules; FUTURE modules and relay-hosted features that need a host are always off without a value.
Vault flag settings are the user's own configuration and never leave the device except in the user's own export; relay flag settings are public hosting policy of that relay.
Changes record who and why for operators (relay scope) without recording content, and audit entries for relay changes are kept 1 year (RET-AUDIT).
A relay cannot learn a user's vault flags and a user's flags are never sent to a relay, which prevents fingerprinting by configuration.

Vault-scope settings are classified P3 field by field (F10.S02.M02), and the module registers ExportSectionPort (section platform.flags), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort with F10.S01.M03, F10.S01.M04 and F10.S01.M02 and consumes privacy.deletion.completed (N6).
Relay-scope evaluation and change outcomes are measured per CTR-OBS-001; the vault sends no telemetry and keeps local counters only (OBS-7).
Evaluation is fast enough to run on every command and render without measurable cost.
Cache hit ratio and stale reads are observable on the relay.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
The dependency rule is covered by property tests over random registries and settings, running the same code for vault and relay adapters.
Contract tests check command and event payloads against the schema registry.
The vault export includes vault-scope FlagSetting records as the section platform.flags, so a restored vault keeps its configuration (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-1, IOX-6).
Relay-scope settings are part of the relay database and its backups (IOX-3, IOX-7), and an operator may export them as relay configuration.
Import validates keys against the registry and the dependency rule; violating or unknown entries are skipped and reported in the dry-run.

A Tenant stores slug, display name, status, allowed currencies, jurisdiction profile reference (ProfileRef), default locale, limits and revision with the base record fields of CTR-ID-001 (id is the tenantId); its operator keys are not stored but derived from F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment records of scope tenant:<id>.
Tenant data is public hosting information (P0), including the derived operator public keys, and is retained as RET-STANDARD while the community exists.

LocalSettings is the vault's own preference record (P3, stored only on the device and exported with the vault) and holds the vaultId, a UUIDv7 created once at vault initialisation that is the CTR-ID-001 ID-6 tenantId of every record in that vault; the vault has no relay tenant record.

Every limit is capped by the platform maximums (maxUploadBytes and maxLocalAttachmentBytes ≤ 5242880 per N9, maxEnvelopeBytes ≤ 262144 per CTR-SCH-001 SCH-6) and names the module that enforces it; a limit without an enforcer is not part of the record.

Tenant limits hold the relay discovery settings read by F06.S02.M03 - anonymousAllowed (default true), anonymousMinRadiusKm (25, 50 or 100, default 25), anonymousCenterLevel (L1, the only public level coarse enough for anonymous callers) and maxDepth (1..500, default 500) - and they appear in every signed configuration statement.

LocalSettings holds the optional display preferences a11yMotion (system or reduced, default system) and moneyDisplay (symbol, code or name, default symbol), returned with their defaults by platform.local_settings.get and changed only through platform.local_settings.update.

The tenant jurisdictionProfile is a ProfileRef {publisherId?, code} of F18.S01.M01 - code matching ^[a-z0-9_-]{2,40}$, publisherId an optional did:key Ed25519 publisher key - with default code generic and no publisherId, which resolves to the bundled generic profile of F18.S01.M01; it appears in the Tenant, in every signed configuration statement and in the platform.tenant.created and platform.tenant.configured payloads, and this module never resolves it.
Tenant input is validated strictly; unknown fields are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED and each violation lists its field path.
Currency, locale and profile values are validated for format here and for registry membership by their owning modules at use time.
Operator assignment rules protect the community from becoming unmanageable, and operators can be added only by an admin with an expiry.

Bootstrap passes admin keys only through RoleBootstrapPort from the local CLI, which refuses an admin key while an active relay admin exists unless a break-glass reason of 20 to 500 code points is given, and admin grants on a bootstrapped relay go only through security.roleassignment.propose and approve.
Discovery settings and the LocalSettings display preferences are validated against their enums and ranges, and an import replaces an invalid display preference with its default instead of failing.

A tenant is created directly in active within one transaction that also creates its first operator and admin role assignments through F16 RoleBootstrapPort.bootstrap({ adminKey?, operatorKeys, tenantId, breakGlassReason?, osUser }) and its first signed configuration statement, so no partially provisioned tenant exists (a SECURITY_BOOTSTRAP_REFUSED answer rolls everything back), and any transition not listed is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
Suspension is reversible; archiving is final and is allowed only from suspended to prevent accidents.
Status changes are written with their event and the new signed configuration statement in one transaction.

Tenant commands are relay commands with Idempotency-Key; LocalSettings commands are vault-local; every tenant revision produces one relay-signed classrup.platform.tenant_config/v1 statement, signed through F15.S02.M01 under context classrup-tenant-config:v1 with signer role relay_identity and registered with F11.S01.M01 (N2).

Every tenant command emits its events in the same transaction as the state change, and platform.tenant.configured carries the full configuration snapshot (it is also emitted at creation and on operator changes), so consumers such as F10.S01.M02 never need to read the tenant.

The module consumes security.role.assigned and security.role.revoked for tenant-scoped roles to re-issue the configuration with the derived operator keys, and privacy.deletion.completed for LocalSettings.

TenantPort is registered with the F15.S02.M02 bus as a stage after authentication that returns PLATFORM_TENANT_SUSPENDED for writes to a suspended or archived tenant, and with the F15.S02.M01 relay process; it offers limits(tenantId) to the enforcers named per limit (F06.S01.M01, F06.S02.M03, F11.S01.M02, F08.S01.M01, F02.S02.M03 depend on this module; the bus, the relay process and the vault blob store receive it by inverted registration because they are upstream of it).

The vault keeps the last verified configuration statement per selected relay in LocalSettings.knownRelayConfigs and shows what changed; two different statements for one (tenantId, revision) are proof of equivocation and shown as a warning.

Every classrup.platform.tenant_config/v1 statement carries jurisdictionProfile as ProfileRef {publisherId?, code} and the derived operatorKeys; the vault registers an operatorKeys resolver with F11.S01.M01 at composition (inverted registration, no depends_on edge) that answers operatorKeys(relayId) from the verified statement in LocalSettings.knownRelayConfigs and answers none when the vault holds no verified statement for that relay, so F18.S02.M02 transparency drafts and reports resolve the relay operator role only from a relay-signed operator list.

Relay policy applies; operator and admin roles are F16.S01.M01 RoleAssignment records - an operator scoped tenant:<id> manages only that tenant's configuration and status, a relay admin manages the tenant list and operator assignments, relay-wide capabilities (identity, backups, recovery, dead letters) need the distinct relay_operator role, and no role has any effect on a vault or on other relays (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-9).
Operators authenticate with signed requests or relay access tokens obtained by challenge-response; the relay stores no passwords and the tenant record stores no operator list of its own.
Vault policy applies to LocalSettings, so only the unlocked local principal reads or changes them, and no relay can read or write them.
All relay commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and use expectedRevision, so concurrent operator edits never overwrite each other.
Bootstrap is safe to run repeatedly and never creates duplicate tenants or duplicate role assignments.
Vault-local settings changes work offline and have no distributed effect.
Tenant configuration is public hosting information and contains no personal data beyond operator public keys, which are pseudonymous identifiers and not proof of anonymity.

LocalSettings are P3, stay on the device, are not telemetry and are never uploaded as a record; they can reveal a user's language, currencies and chosen relays, so they are excluded from federation and from any relay request, with one exception - a copy of defaultLocale is sent only in the F13.S01.M02 notify.email.add registration after notify_email consent, sealed to that one user-selected email relay.
Archived tenants are purged after 90 days and their exported configuration remains with the operator.

The module registers ExportSectionPort (section platform.local_settings), DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort for F10.S01.M03, F10.S01.M04 and F10.S01.M02 through the kernel port registry (inverted dependency, because F10.S01.M04 depends on F15.S01.M01, which depends on this module), classifies every field with F10.S02.M02 and consumes privacy.deletion.completed (N6).
Relay tenant operations are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with the tenant label limited to a hashed short id, never names.
Configuration reads are served from cache and meet the read budget; the vault sends no telemetry (OBS-7).
Event delivery lag for tenant events is observable so that consumers apply configuration promptly.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests check command inputs, outputs and event payloads against the schema registry for both relay and vault commands.
A privacy test proves LocalSettings never leave the device, except the consented defaultLocale copy in the F13.S01.M02 email registration.
The vault export includes LocalSettings as the section platform.local_settings (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-1, IOX-6); tenants are relay data and are not part of any user export.
Relay tenant records and their signed configuration statements are covered by relay backups (IOX-3, IOX-7) and by an operator configuration export.

Import of LocalSettings validates the schema, clamps limits to platform maximums, replaces an invalid a11yMotion or moneyDisplay with its default and keeps the importing vault's own vaultId; operator import of tenants rejects conflicting slugs.

A RoleAssignment stores relay, subject principal DID, role, scope (relay or tenant:<uuidv7>), status, grant path, grantor, optional approver with the cid of the approver's signed approval, grant time, expiry and revocation, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

An AuditEntry stores sequence, HMAC-pseudonymized actor, capability, resource ID, decision, deny code or reason, correlation ID, idempotency key hash, coalesced count and chain hashes, and never payload content, retained under RET-AUDIT.
Roles exist per relay only; assignments are published as relay-signed role statements (classrup.security.role_statement/v1) and are P1 within the relay's members.

Valid role and scope pairs are fixed - admin and relay_operator only at scope relay, operator only at scope tenant:<id> of a tenant on this relay, moderator at scope relay or tenant:<id> - and authorize matches a relay-scope role for every resource on that relay and a tenant-scope role only for resources whose tenantId equals the scope's id.

The subject of an assignment is a principal DID (the account root did:key), never a device key, and a request exercises the role only when signed by a device key that the principal's portable identity document lists as active at the relay's receipt time (F07.S02.M01 KeyStatusPort).
Role commands are validated strictly, including role and scope vocabulary, expiry bounds, the signed two-person rule for admin and the bootstrap preconditions.
authorize() inputs are validated structurally and any malformed input returns Deny without throwing.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Revocation keeps at least one active admin per relay and at least one active operator per tenant scope, counting only active operator assignments of that same tenant:<id> scope.
Role assignments follow the declared lifecycle and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE; requested is the initial pseudostate of a validated command and is never stored.
Expiry, revocation and device-key revocation take effect on the next request, and no role grant or key status is cached for more than 60 seconds (CAP-6).

Audit entries have no lifecycle; entries for state-changing commands are appended inside the same transaction as the command, and buffered read-only denials are appended once when their 60 second window closes.
Admin assignments never expire, so expiry can never remove the last admin, and an admin proposal not approved within 24 hours expires without granting anything.

Bootstrap and break-glass are the only paths that create an admin without an existing admin's signature, and break-glass use emits security.role.assigned with breakGlass true so that F16.S03.M02 opens a SEV1 incident.

Last-operator protection is per tenant scope - an admin revoke that would leave tenant:<id> without an active operator is refused, an automatic revocation by expiry or subject_contested proceeds and emits lastOperator true, and RoleBootstrapPort.archiveTenant revokes every live assignment of scope tenant:<id> with reason tenant_archived inside the F15.S04.M03 archive transaction.

authorize and authorizeStatement are in-process pure functions, evaluated by the command bus before every handler (authorize) and by F11.S01.M02 intake before a statement is acted on (authorizeStatement), with the required signer role resolved only through RoleResolverPort and key status only through KeyStatusPort.
Role assign, propose, approve, activate_import, bootstrap and revoke are relay commands that produce relay-signed role statements and emit security.role.assigned and security.role.revoked.
The module consumes session, identity document, suspension and legal-hold events only to invalidate caches, revoke the roles of contested identities or protect audit rows.

RoleBootstrapPort.bootstrapTenant(tx, tenantId, operatorKeys, adminKey?, cli?: { osUser, breakGlassReason? }) runs inside the F15.S04.M03 tenant-creation transaction tx and creates the tenant's first operator assignments (scope tenant:<tenantId>, expiry 365 days) and, with adminKey, the relay's first admin or a break-glass admin, so a refusal rolls back the whole tenant creation; bootstrap({ adminKey?, operatorKeys?, tenantId?, breakGlassReason?, osUser }) is the in-process form of security.roleassignment.bootstrap and delegates to bootstrapTenant when tenantId is given.
