Statements and signer roles (N2) are registered with F11.S01.M01 - classrup.security.role_statement/v1 and classrup.security.audit_anchor/v1 are CTR-FED-001 envelopes with author = relay did:key signed by the relay key, and classrup.security.role_approval/v1 is a CTR-FED-001 envelope with author = the approving admin principal and ext.signerKey = one of its active device keys.

Vault policy: the vault accepts local commands only from the unlocked local principal, and authorizeStatement accepts an incoming statement only when its signer holds the role the F11.S01.M01 registry requires and its key is active per F07.S02.M01; F11.S01.M02 stores and shows the quarantined ones.

Relay policy: relay roles apply only to the relay that assigned them and only within their scope; admins assign roles, relay_operators run relay-wide operations, tenant operators configure their tenant, moderators act on moderation capabilities, and members use own-resource capabilities.
Reading the audit log requires relay_operator or admin on that relay, and the vault owner may read the local audit log.
Bootstrap and break-glass are authorized only by filesystem access to the relay data directory through the local CLI, never over HTTP, and the OS user and reason are recorded in the audit entry.

Relay-wide operational capabilities - platform.relay_identity.rotate and revoke, platform.relay.read_status, platform.backup.run, verify and read, platform.recovery.read_plan, platform.deadletter.replay and read, security.containment.*, security.incident.*, security.keyrecord.register and revoke - are granted to relay_operator and admin at scope relay only, and a tenant operator, whose capabilities match only resources of its own tenant, never holds them.
authorize is pure and deterministic, so retries and replays give the same decision for the same inputs and clock.
Role commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands carry expectedRevision.
The audit append and the command's state change commit in one transaction, and a failed append aborts the command for state-changing capabilities.

Audit entries contain IDs, hashes and reason codes only and never payloads, tokens or P2+ values; on relays actors are stored as HMAC-SHA256 with a relay pepper loaded through F16.S01.M02, so a copied audit table cannot be joined to public DIDs without the pepper.
Audit entries and role assignments are retained under RET-AUDIT (1 year), except entries under legal hold which are kept until release.

Privilege escalation and log tampering are limited by default deny, signed two-person admin approvals, expiry on non-admin roles, hash chaining and anchors published off-host every 1 000 entries or 5 minutes.

Tampering is detectable only for entries covered by the last externally published anchor; entries appended since then (at most 1 000 entries or 5 minutes plus the fetch interval of the vaults or peers holding anchors) are the stated residual window.
Authorization outcomes and latency are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with labels limited to module, code and outcome and no keys.
authorize adds at most 0.2 ms p95 in a vault and 0.5 ms p95 on a relay, excluding fact lookups.
Audit append lag, anchor publication lag and chain verification time are observable.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Default deny and purity are covered by property tests over generated capability, role and scope matrices.
Audit integrity is covered by tamper tests.
Relay operators can export role assignments and the audit log with its anchors as JSON lines, and the vault owner can export the local audit log.
Import of roles from another relay is never active; it creates imported_inactive records until an admin of the new relay activates them, which re-signs them with the new relay's key.
Audit schema changes follow expand/contract, keep v1 readable for 180 days and never break chain verification.
The module owns no persistent entities and never writes secret values to the database, to logs or to exports.
Token hashes use SHA-256 over 256-bit random tokens, which is sufficient because the input has full entropy; low-entropy secrets are never accepted as tokens.

Secret names follow RELAY_SECRET_[A-Z0-9_]+ and each has a declared purpose, kind (comparison or data-wrapping), minimum length and rotation period in the secret manifest - DATA_KEY (data-wrapping), AUDIT_PEPPER, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY and SMTP_PASSWORD (comparison or signing) - and the relay signing key is not in the manifest because F15.S02.M01 owns its key file.
Startup validates that every secret in the manifest is present exactly once with correct size and permissions, and that every data-key version still wrapping stored objects is loaded.
Token and secret formats are validated before use, and failures return generic errors that do not reveal which character differed.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Startup is all-or-nothing, so if any required secret fails validation the relay does not open its listener.

Reload on SIGHUP loads new values atomically and keeps the previous value of a comparison secret valid for the configured overlap of at most 300 seconds; data-wrapping keys are exempt from this overlap.

Rotation of the relay data key re-wraps stored per-object keys in batches of 1 000 and records progress so it is resumable, and the previous data-key version stays loaded until a verify pass reports zero objects left on it.

A data-key version may be removed only after the verify pass reports zero objects on it, re-wrapping must finish within 30 days of rotation (after which startup warns daily), and startup refuses with SECURITY_SECRET_MISSING if a version still in use was removed early.
loadSecret returns a Secret or a typed error and never returns the raw string to callers outside reveal().
equalConstantTime compares byte arrays of equal length in time independent of content and returns false immediately only for length mismatch.
The scanner CLI exits 0 with no findings and 1 with findings, printing rule ID, path and line but not the matched value.
The verify-rewrap CLI reports the number of objects per data-key version and exits non-zero while any object remains on a version marked for removal.
Only the relay process user can read secret files, and the library enforces owner and mode checks at load time.
Operators access secrets through the hosting environment, never through the product's API.
The CI scan runs with read-only repository access and cannot publish artifacts on failure.
loadSecret is idempotent and side-effect free apart from caching the loaded value in memory.
Reload is atomic; a failed reload keeps the previous values and logs SECURITY_SECRET_MISSING or PERMISSIONS without values.
Data-key rotation is resumable and idempotent per object.
Secret values are P4 and are never logged, never serialized, never in metrics labels, never in error messages, and never in crash reports.
Secret metadata (name, source, length, loaded time, objects per data-key version) is not secret and may be logged.
Leak attempts through logs, errors, process listings, core dumps and repository history are addressed by redaction, file loading, disabled core dumps and scanning.
Startup and reload emit one log line per secret with name, source and status but no values, per CTR-OBS-001 OBS-1.
equalConstantTime and hashToken add at most 0.05 ms p95 per call and the redaction scanner adds at most 0.2 ms per log line under 4 KiB.
The CI scan completes within 60 seconds for a diff and 10 minutes for full history of 10 000 commits.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Redaction is covered by property tests that inject random secrets into every logging path.
The CI scanner has a corpus of positive and negative samples with expected findings.
Operator configuration exports contain secret names, sources and rotation dates but never values, and backups never contain secret files.
Restoring a relay from backup requires the operator to provide secrets again, including every data-key version that still wraps restored objects, and the relay refuses to start without them.
Scanner rules and the secret manifest are versioned; rule changes keep the previous rule set available for 180 days for comparison.
The stored wrapped key blob contains version, key role (root or device), KDF name and parameters (N, r, p), salt, nonce, ciphertext, key ID and algorithm, all authenticated as associated data.
Private keys exist unwrapped only in memory while unlocked, and the library exposes separate root and device key handles with sign and agree operations, never key bytes, to application code.

Key IDs are the SHA-256 thumbprint of the raw public key in base64url (used inside envelopes), the principal is the did:key encoding of the root Ed25519 public key, and every displayed fingerprint is F07.S01.M01 fingerprintOf (16 base58btc characters with the 8-word spoken form).

Each device's X25519 agreement key is derived deterministically from that device's Ed25519 key (RFC 7748 birational map of the public key, clamped SHA-512 scalar of the seed), so the root-signed portable identity document that lists the Ed25519 device key binds the agreement key, and no separate agreement key is generated, stored or published.
Passphrases are validated for minimum length and a bundled common-passphrase list before any key is created or wrapped.
KDF parameters read from a stored blob are validated against allowed minimums before use, so a tampered blob cannot lower the cost.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Passphrase inputs on create, unlock, change-passphrase and backup export and import accept paste, drop and password-manager autofill - no handler cancels paste, drop or input events - keep autocomplete current-password or new-password and a show/hide toggle, and validation runs only on the entered value (CTR-UX-001 UX-5, checked by F14.S01.M03 V07).
The in-memory lock state moves locked to unlocked only after successful AEAD verification, and unlocked to locked on idle timeout, explicit lock, tab hide for 5 minutes or browser discard.

Device rotation proceeds generate, possession-sign, root-signed device link through F07.S01.M01 identity.device_key.add, overlap, then identity.device_key.revoke of the old key with reason superseded and a new portable identity document, with one overlap bound of 0 to 7 days (default 7) unless the user marks the old key compromised, in which case the revocation is immediate.
After 3 consecutive failed unlocks the library enforces a local delay of 1 s, doubling per failure, capped at 60 s, and resets after one success.
The account root key is never rotated in MVP; a lost or compromised root key is handled by recovery (F07.S01.M03), and rotation applies only to device keys.
createVault(passphrase) generates the root key and the first device key, wraps them, and returns the principal and fingerprint without returning key bytes.

sign(keyRole, context, payload) and agree(peerDevicePublicKey) operate on the unlocked handle and fail with SECURITY_VAULT_LOCKED when locked, and agree derives the peer's agreement key from its Ed25519 device key itself.

rotateDeviceKey generates a new device key and its possession signature, obtains the root-signed device link through F07.S01.M01 identity.device_key.add, waits the overlap, revokes the old key with reason superseded through identity.device_key.revoke, and queues the statements and the new portable identity document through the F15.S01.M01 sync outbox.
Fingerprints returned or shown by this library come from F07.S01.M01 fingerprintOf and never from a separate encoding.
Only code running in the vault's origin can call the library, and sign requests from any other context are impossible.
The library never exposes raw private key bytes to callers, including the application code, and exposes only sign and agree on separate root and device handles.
Auto-lock and unlock lockouts are enforced by the library regardless of caller.
createVault is atomic, so the wrapped blobs and public metadata are written in one IndexedDB transaction or nothing is written.
Unlock is repeatable and has no side effects besides in-memory state; failed attempts only advance the local backoff counter.
Rotation is resumable from persisted progress and never leaves the vault without a usable key.
Private keys and passphrases are P4 and never leave the device except inside the user's own passphrase-encrypted export, and they are never logged or sent in telemetry (OBS-7).
The wrapped blob is retained until the user deletes the vault, and deletion overwrites the IndexedDB records and removes the blob.
Offline brute force against a stolen wrapped blob is slowed by scrypt N=2^17 (about 128 MiB per attempt) and the passphrase minimum, and the user is told the limits.

Device-rotation progress, device link and revocation records for own keys are retained under RET-EVIDENCE and extended while any retained record references a signature by that key, so evidence signed by a rotated key still verifies through its link chain.
The PWA sends no telemetry; the library records local diagnostics (unlock duration, failures count, lock reason) in the vault, exportable by the user per OBS-7.
Unlock completes within 3 s p95 on a desktop-class device and within 8 s p95 on a Moto G-class device, running in a worker so the main thread stays responsive (INP ≤ 200 ms).
Sign and agree complete within 5 ms p95 desktop and 25 ms p95 Moto G.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Cryptographic primitives are covered by known-answer tests from the standards and by round-trip property tests.
Tamper and downgrade attempts are covered by abuse tests.
The encrypted backup file contains the wrapped blobs and public metadata only, uses the same KDF and cipher, and is the user's primary key backup alongside the recovery kit under the user's control.
Import decrypts with the passphrase, validates parameters and refuses unknown or downgraded versions.
Blob format changes follow versioned parsers, keep v1 readable for 180 days and re-wrap to the newest version only after a successful unlock.

A KeyRecord stores public key, algorithm, purpose, owner principal, relationship, authority (the module whose statement or record is the source of truth), status, validity window, revocation details, the identity document sequence it was taken from, provenance and the revocation freshness, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001.

Key records are P1 public data once published; local notes on counterparty keys are P3 in the vault, and KeyRecords are retained under RET-EVIDENCE because signatures are verified against historical status.

Key IDs are unique per public key, and every revoked key is also written to a permanent minimal revoked-key set (key hash, revokedAt, revocationStatementCid) that survives purging of its KeyRecord, so a revoked key is never registered or reactivated again.

For user device keys F07.S02.M01 is the single source of validity; KeyRecords with relationship own, counterparty or relay_hosted are an ingest-only cache of its KeyStatusPort and identity documents, and native records exist only for relay_owned keys (relay transport, VAPID) and peer_relay keys.
Agreement keys are never registered or stored; callers derive a device's X25519 key from its listed Ed25519 key with F16.S02.M01, so no relay or statement can introduce one.

classrup.security.keyrevocation/v1 is the single revocation statement for device keys, with payload { keyId, publicKey, ownerPrincipal, reason, effectiveFrom?, revokedByKey, finalCids? }, where finalCids (reason account_deleted only, at most 120 distinct cids) names the final statements signed in the F10.S01.M04 DeletionPort sign step that verifiers keep accepting after the revocation.

Every key this module shows is displayed with the F07.S01.M01 fingerprint - 16 base58btc characters of SHA-256 over the raw public key, or its 8-word form - and never with keyId or the did:key prefix.

Revocation statements, list heads and relay-owned key registrations are validated for schema, signatures, signer authority and limits before storage, and user device keys are accepted only as F07.S02.M01 reports them.
Revocation effective times are clamped so that a signer cannot reach back more than 30 days before the earliest evidence of the statement, and a revocation is never dropped because it arrives late.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Key records follow the declared lifecycle, revoked and expired are final, and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.

A revocation by another device key waits 7 days as revocation_pending, ending in revoked at the timeout or on root confirmation and in contested on a counter-revocation, and a contested key leaves only by a decision of the account root key (the recovery-key role, from the root device or the recovery kit).
Expiry is evaluated at verification time as well as by the sweep, so a missed sweep never extends a key.

Transitions of cached user keys follow F07 events and identity documents only and never run ahead of or against them; native records follow this module's own commands and mirrored relay and peer events.
Every command declares whether it is vault-local, a signed statement or a relay command, and the signatures below do so.
Register, revoke, record_revocation and the event ingestion emit security.key.registered and security.key.revoked in the same transaction as the record.
The module consumes own-key identity events, received identity documents, peer events and relay identity events to keep records current, and never decides user-key validity itself.

security.keyrecord.get returns publicKey, algorithm and purpose for a keyId, and get_status for a user key is one call to F07.S02.M01 KeyStatusPort.keyStatus(did, publicKey, at) with this module's freshness added; F16.S02.M03 callers pass that result to verify.

Relay revocation lists are a signed head { relayId, listSeq, issuedAt, nextUpdateBy, headHash, entryCount } under classrup/revocation-list/v1 plus entries that point to root-signed identity documents or relay-signed revocations, and a relay's signature is never the authority for a user key.

security.key.registered and security.key.revoked carry keyId, purpose and relationship, so consumers such as F13.S01.M01 match VAPID keys (purpose vapid) and device keys without calling security.keyrecord.get_status.

get_status called with the statementCid of a statement signed by a key revoked with reason account_deleted returns status revoked with finalListed true only when that cid is in the revocation's finalCids, and F16.S02.M03 verify accepts a revoked key only for such a listed statement.

Vault policy: user device keys enter only through F07 identity events and verified identity documents, counterparty status is F07.S02.M01's and is cached here with freshness, and no command of this module revokes a user key; the principal uses identity.device_key.revoke (F07.S01.M01).
Relay policy: relay_operators and admins of the relay register and revoke relay_owned keys, which are signed by the relay key; peer keys come only from F11.S03.M01 pins; revocation lists are public.
Status and public-key queries are read-only and public for published keys, and revocation and list ingestion need no session because they are authorized by signatures.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and ingestion dedupes by statement content ID.
Registration and revocation commit the record, the event, the revoked-key set entry and the revocation list entry in one transaction.
A revocation received before its key is written to the revoked-key set at once and applied when the key is seen, so ordering never loses a revocation.

Public keys, status and revocations are P1 or P0 once published and contain no personal data beyond public DIDs, and the revocation list reveals only key hashes, DIDs of published identity documents, document references, reasons and times.

KeyRecords are retained under RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after the last status change or verification that used them), and the permanent revoked-key set (key hash, revokedAt, revocationStatementCid) is kept as long as the store exists, recorded as an exception to CTR-PRV-001 because it holds no personal data and stops key resurrection.

Abuse (false revocations, registry flooding, revocation suppression, list replay, rollback of revocation, agreement-key substitution) is limited by F07 signer rules, limits, signed monotonic list heads from at least two sources and the permanent revoked-key set.
Relay registry operations and list polls are measured per CTR-OBS-001 without key material labels; the vault keeps local diagnostics only.
get_status meets p95 ≤ 5 ms in a vault and ≤ 10 ms on a relay at 1 000 queries per second, including the KeyStatusPort call for user keys.
Freshness age distribution and detected list replays are observable to spot stale or misbehaving revocation sources.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Revocation ordering, freshness and contested-key behavior are covered by property and chaos tests.
Contract tests check statements and events against the schema registry.

Vault export contains own and counterparty key records with revocation statements, freshness and the revoked-key set, and the relay export contains relay-owned and peer keys, the revoked-key set and the signed revocation list.

Import re-verifies every statement signature, re-derives user-key status from the imported identity documents through F07.S02.M01, and resets freshness of imported counterparty keys to unknown so stale knowledge is never trusted.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
The envelope contains v 1, ctx, the signer key ID kid, alg ed25519, the signedAt claim, payloadHash, an optional inline payload (canonical JSON) and the base64url 64-byte signature.

The signed bytes are the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the header object { v, ctx, kid, alg, signedAt, payloadHash }, with payloadHash the CTR-ID-001 ID-3 form sha256-<base64url> of SHA-256 over the JCS bytes of the payload, so context, key, version, algorithm, signing-time claim and payload are covered by every signature.

Contexts follow classrup/<purpose>/v<major>, and the inventory maps each context to its owner module, signer, payload schema ID, maximum size and binding fields, and lists every other signing prefix and format in the system with its owner module.

Challenge and request prefixes bind an audience (relayId or the request's target authority), a single-use nonce and an expiry (expiresAt inside the signed bytes, the RFC 9421 expires parameter, or a challenge expiry of at most 120 s recorded by the issuer), and an inventory entry without all three is refused.

No two inventory entries are prefix-ambiguous, and the F16 header bytes, CTR-FED-001 envelope bytes, RFC 9421 signature bases and classrup-<purpose>:v<n> strings begin with different leading bytes, so no signature made in one format can verify in another.
Envelopes are validated strictly for size, version, algorithm and context before any cryptographic operation.
Verification is strict Ed25519 (RFC 8032, canonical S, no small-order keys) through F11.S01.M03 and recomputes the header bytes and payloadHash rather than trusting transmitted bytes.
Every violation maps to one stable error code, and results never reveal secret-dependent details.

A revoked signer key passes the key-status check only for a statement that the caller-supplied status marks finalListed (listed in the finalCids of the key's account_deleted revocation, F16.S02.M02), and the result then carries flag finalStatement.
Verification is a pure function of the envelope, the payload, the expectations, the caller-supplied key status and the verifier receipt time, and has no side effects.
The verifier's own first-seen time is the only time used for revocation decisions, and the signedAt claim never extends or shortens a key's validity.
A result with freshness stale or unknown is returned to the caller and never upgraded to fresh by the library.
sign returns a complete envelope and refuses contexts outside the inventory, payloads that fail their schema and key handles whose role may not sign the context.

verify returns { accepted, reason?, signatureValid, contextOk, bindingOk, payloadHashOk, keyStatus, freshnessClass, flags[] }, where accepted is true only when signature, context, binding, payload hash and key status all pass, and it never throws on hostile input.

The module has no JCS, Ed25519 or did:key implementation and no request-signing scheme of its own; it calls F11.S01.M03, and device-to-relay HTTP requests use the F11.S01.M03 RFC 9421 profile with tag classrup/relay-request/v1, created, expires (at most created + 300 s), nonce and @target-uri.
Key status is an input and the module never calls the key registry, so F16.S02.M02 depends on this module without a cycle.
Only vault code holding an unlocked key handle can sign, and the helper never accepts raw key bytes from callers.
Verification is available to every module in vault and relay and requires no secret.
Inventory changes are code changes reviewed in the repository, not runtime configuration.
sign and verify are deterministic and idempotent, since Ed25519 signatures are deterministic for the same key and bytes.
A missing or failed key status input produces keyStatus unknown and accepted false, never an accepted result.
Canonicalization errors from F11.S01.M03 are returned as error values and verify never throws on hostile input.
Envelopes contain only the payload or payload hash the signer chose to sign and key IDs; contexts and verification results never include secrets or P4 values.
Retention follows the embedding record (consents and receipts are RET-EVIDENCE) and the library stores nothing itself.
Replay, cross-protocol and substitution attacks are addressed by domain separation, the prefix inventory, revision binding, header-covered payload hashes and strict verification.
Relay verification outcomes are counted per CTR-OBS-001 with codes as labels and no key IDs; the vault keeps local diagnostics only.
sign and verify meet p95 ≤ 5 ms on desktop-class and ≤ 25 ms on a Moto G-class device for 4 KiB payloads.
Verification failure spikes are visible to the incident detection hooks of F16.S03.M02.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Ed25519 behavior is covered by RFC 8032 known-answer vectors including malleability cases, and domain separation by cross-context property tests.
Canonicalization is covered by the RFC 8785 test vectors.
Exports embed envelopes verbatim with their canonical payloads so they can be re-verified by anyone with the signer's public key.
Import re-verifies every envelope under its recorded context, marks failures as unverified and never silently drops or upgrades them.
Envelope and context changes are versioned, with old contexts verifiable for at least 5 years and new major versions introduced alongside.

An Incident stores category, severity with its history, status, scope, key milestone times, notification decision, notice delivery counts, postmortem link and linked reference IDs, with tenant and revision per CTR-ID-001; its timeline lives in the security_incident_timeline table.
Incident records are P3 relay-operational data readable by relay_operators and admins of that relay, retained under RET-EVIDENCE (2 years), and contain no secrets, tokens, keys or user content.
Severity follows the matrix SEV1 critical, SEV2 high, SEV3 medium and SEV4 low, and changes are recorded with reason and actor.

The timeline is stored in its own append-only table keyed by (incident_id, seq) whose triggers refuse every update except one redaction per row (text set to NULL and redacted_hash set) and refuse deletion while the incident exists.
Incident input is validated strictly, and text fields are scanned for secret patterns with the library of F16.S01.M02 before storage.
Severity, category and status transitions are validated against the matrix and lifecycle.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Incidents follow the declared lifecycle and any other transition is refused with CONFLICT_STATE.
A resolved incident can return to triaged when a regression is found, and closing is final.
SLA targets are tracked per severity and breaches are recorded as timeline entries and metrics without changing status.
Detection hooks never cap SEV1 or SEV2 detections, and SEV3 and SEV4 detections beyond 20 per hour per relay are appended to one open detection_overflow SEV2 incident instead of being dropped.
Commands are relay commands for relay-scope roles; detection hooks call open internally as actor kind system.
Open and close emit security.incident.opened and security.incident.closed in the same transaction as the record.
The module consumes security, platform, moderation, identity and federation events as detection hooks with fixed, tested thresholds.
security.incident.redact_entry clears one timeline row's text, stores its hash and writes an audit entry (F16.S01.M01), and nothing else can change a timeline row.
Incident events are P3, relay-local, never federated and never used to trigger notifications; users receive only the signed incident notice.

Incident notices are classrup.security.incident_notice/v1 CTR-FED-001 envelopes with author = relay did:key, registered with signer role relay in F11.S01.M01 (N2), signed through F16.S02.M03 and F11.S01.M03 and sealed to affected mailboxes through F08.S01.M01.

security.incident.open, for an incident whose affectedDataClasses include a class above P1, calls governance.jurisdiction_profile.resolve of F18.S01.M01 on the relay, where profileRefs defaults to the relay's hosting profile named by ProfileRef {publisherId, code} (applied through relay_upload), and in the same transaction sets notificationDueAt = detectedAt + effective.breachNotificationHours (24..720; 72 from the bundled generic profile with fallback true when no hosting profile or value resolves) and stores breachNoticeBasis from the resolve sources; profiles are never referenced by profileId and later profile activations do not move a stored due time.

Relay policy: relay_operators and admins of the relay (relay-scope F16.S01.M01 roles) open, triage, contain, resolve and close incidents, admins notify and redact timeline entries, moderators and tenant operators have no access, and members never read incident records.

Vault policy: a vault accepts an incident notice only when signed by the key of a relay it uses, shows it with the relay name and never changes local data because of it; a notice from a successor relayId that the old relay's key revocation or restore announcement names is shown as 'unverified until confirmed out of band', never silently quarantined and never acted on.
Detection hooks run as actor kind system with a restricted capability to open incidents only.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and mutating commands require expectedRevision.
Detection hooks are idempotent through the inbox table and the open-incident unique index, so duplicate events never create a second incident.
A timeline append and its revision bump are one transaction and the timeline never loses entries.
Incident records contain IDs, counts and data classes only, never user content, tokens or keys, and text is scanned for secret patterns before storage.
Records and their timeline rows are retained under RET-EVIDENCE (2 years after closure), with legal hold override, and are readable only by relay_operators and admins.

Misuse (incident records used to profile users, forged incidents to trigger panic, concealment of breaches, flooding to bury a critical alert) is limited by content rules, hook thresholds, uncapped SEV1 and SEV2, audit logging and the mandatory notification decision.
Incident counts, durations and SLA breaches are measured per CTR-OBS-001 with labels limited to category and severity.
Open and annotate meet the write budget (p95 ≤ 300 ms) at 50 req/s.
SLA sweep lag is observable and alerting.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test.
Detection hook thresholds are covered by deterministic event-stream tests with an injected clock.
Notification and closure gates are covered by integration tests.
Operators can export incidents with timelines as JSON lines for auditors, excluding any redacted text.
Import is allowed only for relay migration and re-validates all text for secrets and all references.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

Each runbook has ID RB-NN, title, trigger conditions, severity mapping, roles, numbered steps each with an owner role and a time target, verification checks, rollback, communication text and last drill date.

The read-only contract is the sentinel file <RELAY_DATA_DIR>/containment/read_only, read every second by the relay process without the database (the environment value RELAY_CONTAINMENT_READ_ONLY=1 is read only at start and creates the sentinel), and the federation kill contract is the relay-scope sentinel <RELAY_DATA_DIR>/containment/federation_off that gates only relay-to-relay traffic; it is not a CTR-FLG-001 flag, so the FLG-2 dependency rule and FLG-3 module disabling do not apply.

Notice templates contain relay name, plain description, the data classes the breached relay actually held (from the generated relay inventory), user actions, contact route and the relay-signed time, and never include speculation or claims that no data was accessed without evidence.

The read-only exemption list is fixed in code by exact command ID - security.containment.set, identity.login_challenge.issue, identity.session.start, identity.session.revoke, security.roleassignment.revoke, security.roleassignment.bootstrap, security.keyrecord.revoke, security.keyrecord.record_revocation, security.keyrecord.ingest_list, platform.relay_identity.revoke, identity.portable_doc.publish (only documents that newly revoke keys), federation.peer.suspend and every security.incident command - and queries are never blocked.
The documentation linter validates runbook structure, step time targets and references to capabilities, commands, error codes and modules.
Switch commands validate reason text and the relay-scope role before applying, and never accept empty reasons.
Every violation maps to one stable lint or runtime error code.
The linter compares the RB-02 notice inventory with the relay storage declarations of the module specs and the relay secret manifest, so a notice can never understate what a relay held.

RB-01 key compromise. User device key - from another device or the root device the user runs identity.device_key.revoke (F07.S01.M01; the key itself or the root key revoke at once, another device key starts a 7-day pending period), then rotates with the F16.S02.M01 device rotation, and the new root-signed identity document carries the revocation to contacts as they sync; consents received in the clamped claimed-compromise window are labelled, and a lost root key goes through recovery (F07.S01.M03). Relay identity key - within 15 minutes of confirmation run platform.relay_identity.revoke (relay identity revoke --reason compromised) from the relay CLI; while the compromised key file is still readable and passes checkSecretFile, revoke with that live key (useCertificate absent), so the CLI first writes the pending successor genesis key and the revocation signed by the compromised key itself names successorRelayId; only when the key file is missing or unreadable revoke with the pre-signed revocation certificate (useCertificate true), which predates any successor and carries no successorRelayId, so the link then rests on the new identity's classrup.platform.relay_restore/v1 announcement naming predecessorRelayId plus the out-of-band fingerprint check; then run relay identity init --new-identity, which activates that successor (or a fresh genesis key on the certificate path) as a new relayId whose first statements are the restore announcement and the incident notice naming the old relayId, re-sign the active role statements and the tenant configuration with the new key, within 60 minutes confirm the new fingerprint through at least two out-of-band channels on either path, and within 24 hours review the audit log chain for the exposure window; the compromised key signs only its own revocation, never a rotation. Relay-owned VAPID keys - security.keyrecord.revoke and register a new one.

RB-02 relay breach. Within 15 minutes open a SEV1 or SEV2 incident (F16.S03.M02), within 30 minutes apply the read-only switch (RB-04), preserve disk and logs as read-only copies, rotate all relay secrets (F16.S01.M02) and follow RB-01 for the relay identity key within 4 hours, rebuild from a clean image and restore data from the last verified backup within 24 hours, then verify audit chain anchors; users are told that vault data was never on the relay, and the notice lists each data class this relay held according to the generated inventory - for example public projections and media (P0), role and key records (P1), bids and results of hosted auctions, push subscriptions, email addresses, mailbox ciphertext with routing metadata and moderation reports and cases (P2), audit, incident and rate records (P3), session token hashes and login challenges (P4) - plus the relay secrets.

RB-03 data leak notification. Within 24 hours determine data classes and the approximate number of affected users from the audit log and relay storage; record the notification decision in the incident; where personal-data breach notification may apply, prepare the regulator notice within the jurisdiction due time (default target 72 hours after awareness, F18.S01.M01) and send the signed user notice through mailboxes within 24 hours of the decision; the notice lists data classes, actions (rotate keys if keys could be affected, treat reports and metadata as exposed) and a contact route.

RB-04 relay-wide read-only switch. Run classrup-relay containment read-only on --reason (security.containment.set by a relay_operator or admin, or --local from the host when the database is down); within 5 seconds the command bus rejects non-exempt mutating relay commands with SECURITY_READ_ONLY_MODE and Retry-After 300, using the exemption list by exact command ID; vault outboxes keep statements prepared and the UI shows the relay as read-only; to lift, run containment read-only off, verify with the readiness check and drain outboxes at a rate of at most 50 statements per second per key.

RB-05 federation kill switch. Run classrup-relay containment federation off --reason; within 60 seconds POST /fed/v1/inbox requests signed by peer relay keys receive FEATURE_DISABLED with params.reason federation_killed, F11.S02.M01 outbound delivery to peers pauses, in-flight batches abort or finish, and queued deliveries remain in the outbox up to 7 days; requests from vaults hosted on this relay, mailboxes, consent and publishing keep working because only relay-to-relay traffic is gated and no feature flag changes; peers may also be suspended one by one (federation.peer.suspend, F11.S03.M01); to restore, turn it on, verify peer signatures on the first 100 inbound envelopes and re-enable peers one at a time.

RB-06 distributor or release key compromise. Publish a hold statement signed by the release key under context classrup/release-hold/v1 (F16.S02.M03) if that key is still trusted, otherwise a relay-signed incident notice as advice only, instructing users not to activate updates; compare served bundle hashes with the signed release manifest; rotate the release signing key held offline, publish the new key fingerprint through at least three independent channels, release a rebuilt version with published reproducible hashes, and tell users how to verify the build hash shown in the app; users who updated during the window are advised to rotate their device key.

RB-07 postmortem. Blameless, due 7 days after resolution for SEV1 and SEV2: timeline, impact, detection, what went well and badly, root causes, contributing factors, action items each with owner and due date within 30 days, and threat register updates (F16.S03.M01); the summary is published to affected users in plain language.

The relay CLI exposes classrup-relay containment read-only on|off --reason and classrup-relay containment federation on|off --reason, which call security.containment.set with a request signed by the operator's device key, or with --local write the sentinel directly when the database is unavailable; both write an audit entry (F16.S01.M01), the local path at the next start.

The command bus honors the read-only sentinel by returning SECURITY_READ_ONLY_MODE for non-exempt mutating commands (implemented by F15.S02.M02), and the federation sentinel is honored by the F11.S01.M02 inbox for peer relay requests and by F11.S02.M01 outbound delivery.
The linter pnpm security:runbooks:check validates structure, references, drill dates, forbidden claims, template fields and the RB-02 inventory, and exits non-zero on any error.
security.containment.get_status reports both switches with since-time, actor and the last propagation check.

Only relay_operators and admins of the relay (relay-scope F16.S01.M01 roles) apply the read-only and federation switches through signed requests, the host-only --local path is limited to a relay whose database is unavailable and records the OS user, and every change is written to the audit log with the reason.
Documentation edits require two maintainer approvals like the threat register.

Read-only and federation switch states, change counts and propagation times are metrics on the relay per CTR-OBS-001.
Read-only takes effect within 5 seconds and federation kill within 60 seconds, measured by the propagation check.

A broken reference is reported with enough context to fix it in one edit.

Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated or documented review test.

The module owns no persisted entities; each worker gets a fresh browser context whose vault (IndexedDB) starts empty, plus an optional throwaway test relay for the with-relay profile.

Test principals are generated pseudonyms whose did:key identities and device keys are created locally in the browser context, each with its own vault; there are no accounts or logins (ADR-0016, CTR-UX-001 UX-5).
Artifacts (traces, screenshots on failure) are written under test-results/ and git-ignored.
Each e2e test title starts with a valid TEST-PS-NNN-PP.Tnn ID per CTR-TST-001.
A test fails if axe reports any violation with impact serious or critical on a visited screen, or any console error not on an allow list.
Playwright config validation rejects a run when the Chromium path is missing, versions differ from the pinned 1.63.0 or when fewer than the two device projects are configured.

Identity screens meet CTR-UX-001 UX-5: vault unlock uses autocomplete current-password, new passphrase uses autocomplete new-password, paste and password managers are never blocked, a show/hide toggle exists, and a recovery kit can be imported by file; no screen shows sign-up, sign-in, log-in or account wording (N20).
There is no entity lifecycle for the module; each journey exercises lifecycles owned by other modules.

A journey passes only if the UI state of each participant matches that participant's own vault state, and the vaults agree on the signed statements they exchanged (same cid and revision, verified signer). For an offer, the buyer and seller vaults in separate browser contexts hold the same accepted offer cid and revision and the Deal, and the buyer's OutboxEntry reaches peer_accepted bound to that cid; in the no-relay profile the envelopes travel as direct file transfers. Relay checks cover only relay-held artifacts (the receipt for an opaque envelope, index presence of a P0 projection), and no relay query returns offer plaintext (P2, CTR-PRV-001 PRV-5).

Offline journeys walk the F15.S01.M01 sync states: the offer is local committed at once; its OutboxEntry is prepared while offline (Saved on this device), then sending, then transport_acknowledged after a verified relay receipt (Delivered to relay, peer has not confirmed), then peer_accepted when the seller's signed acknowledgement arrives (Confirmed by peer); conflict, failed and expired are driven by injected relay responses and page.clock; each state is visible and announced and the UI never shows more than the reached state.

A no-relay journey runs with all network requests aborted: first-run identity creation, local listing publish, local search, vault export and restore, and sync status displayed as Saved on this device (local committed, OutboxEntry prepared) without claiming delivery.

The module exposes pnpm test:e2e, pnpm test:e2e --project=pixel7, pnpm test:e2e --grep <TEST ID>, pnpm test:e2e:a11y and pnpm test:e2e:budgets, which writes reports/pwa-budgets.json (classrup-pwa-budget-report/v1 with commitSha, profile, lcpMs, inpMs, cls, initialJsGzipBytes) for the release gates.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 test failure, 2 accessibility violation, 3 configuration failure.
The suite consumes the PWA build artifact path from env PWA_DIST and fails when the directory is missing.
E2E tests unlock the local vault with a generated passphrase; relay access, when selected, uses the challenge-response token flow (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-10) with generated device keys.

Authorization is tested at the UI level: a correctly signed statement from a non-author injected into a vault is shown in the quarantine list with its reason and never as accepted, a non-owner sees no accept or reject controls and a direct URL returns the not-found screen.
Test principals, their vaults and the relay are discarded after the run; no relay access tokens are written to traces (traces redact Authorization headers).

Offline replay is verified: an offer created offline keeps exactly one OutboxEntry with its original cid across a page reload during the outage, and after reconnect the seller vault applies it exactly once (statements dedupe by cid; relay commands keep their Idempotency-Key).
Parallel workers are fully isolated by browser context, vault and relay tenant; no shared state exists between tests.

A failed test is retried at most once in CI; the report marks flaky tests, appends each run to the stored history artifact reports/e2e-history.json, and the job fails if any single test needed a retry in more than 3 of the last 20 CI runs read from that history.
Traces and screenshots are retained 14 days in CI and are scrubbed of Authorization headers and request bodies for P2–P4 endpoints.
Test data are synthetic and locations are rendered at coarse L2.
The suite asserts no P3 value (exact address) appears in the DOM of public pages or in page URLs.

No test-only route or hook (relay clock, seeding) exists in a production relay build; the relay FakeClock is injected in-process through the e2e relay entry and the PWA clock through Playwright page.clock.

The suite records per-test duration and Web Vitals measured in Chromium (LCP, INP, CLS) on the 4G Moto G-class profile for the home and listing pages, and writes them with the initial JS size and commit SHA to reports/pwa-budgets.json for the release gates.
Smoke subset (5 tests) finishes in at most 90 s; full suite in at most 8 min on 2 vCPU.

PWA budgets from CTR-OBS-001 OBS-5 are asserted: LCP at most 2.5 s, INP at most 200 ms measured over a scripted interaction (open a listing, tap Make offer), CLS at most 0.1, initial JS at most 150 KiB gzip.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Self-tests plant a missing label and a failing console error to prove the gate fails.
Both device projects must run every test tagged smoke; the report lists project coverage.
The HTML report and JUnit XML are exportable CI artifacts; no user data is included.
Playwright and axe versions are pinned in the lockfile (1.63.0, 4.14.0); upgrades are separate reviewed pull requests.
Rollback is a git revert; there is no persistent state.
The module owns no persisted entities; it creates throwaway in-memory vaults (one per participant), an optional in-memory relay database and destroys them on exit.
Seed data is built through public commands where possible and through fixtures only for actors and listings, never by writing rows directly in flow suites.
Flow reports store step names, event types and IDs only; no payload content of P2–P4 data is written to the report.
Each flow suite must assert the final state, the ordered list of emitted event types and that no unexpected event types appear.
The harness rejects a flow that makes a real network call, writes outside the temp directory or uses a real clock with QUALITY_IT_ISOLATION.
Contract validation fails with a typed code when a command, event or error does not match its registered schema or CTR-ERR-001 shape.

Trust-fault suites are mandatory and this module owns their single oracle: relay_down (local records intact, the OutboxEntry stays prepared until a verified receipt, the flow completes after direct exchange or relay restart); fork_conflict (fork detected, coordination frozen, no last-writer-wins); revocation_lag (receipt-time cases of the revocation edge case, F11.S01.M02 and F16.S02.M02); relay_tamper (FED_SIGNATURE_INVALID, quarantined with provenance, no state change); signer_role_mismatch (quarantined with reason signer_role_invalid, no state change); relay_replay (one effect by cid; other context or after expiresAt rejected); relay_withhold_equivocate (gap detected, chainGap after 24 h, dropped tombstone applied once fetched from the author). In every suite no sync state or label exceeds the state reached.

Statement contract checks run per F11.S01.M01 registry entry: required signer role, payload schema classrup.<slug>.<entity>/vN, cid per FED-7, ext at most 4 KiB with unknown payload keys outside ext rejected (SCH-2), and a negative case signed by the wrong role that must be quarantined.

Flow reports and UI-facing statuses never use verified or paid as a state; payment steps use only CTR-COM-001 COM-3 states and catalog payment events, and a report that contains either word as a state fails the lint.
There is no entity lifecycle for the module; each flow drives the lifecycles of the entities it exercises (Offer, Proposal, Cycle, Deal, Receipt).
A flow is complete only when its terminal state is reached or its documented timeout fires on the FakeClock.
Every flow ends by asserting outbox drained: zero undelivered events and zero stuck inbox entries.
The module exposes pnpm test:integration, pnpm test:integration --flow <name> and pnpm test:contract.

The 12 flows are named listing_paid, sale_local, barter_two, cycle_three, cycle_four, cycle_n, barter_mixed, dispute_cancel, fraud_moderation, messages_private, payments_claims, federation_io (two steps, federation and portability), each runnable with --mode relay or --mode direct.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 assertion failure, 2 contract mismatch, 3 isolation violation.

Flow mode table (FLOW id, suite, mode, reason): FLOW-01 listing_paid relay-only (promotion fee and the Promoted label are relay R hosting policy); FLOW-02 sale_local both; FLOW-03 barter_two both; FLOW-04 cycle_three both; FLOW-05 cycle_four both; FLOW-06 cycle_n both (direct is O(N^2) envelopes, relay is O(N) mailbox fan-out); FLOW-07 barter_mixed both; FLOW-08 dispute_cancel both (the mediator outcome is a signed statement that travels either way); FLOW-09 fraud_moderation relay-only (report review and index removal are relay R hosting policy); FLOW-10 messages_private both (relay mailbox, or a sealed envelope file in direct mode); FLOW-11 payments_claims both (chain verifiers are per-vault ports); FLOW-12 federation_io federation step relay-only (relay-to-relay federation by definition) and portability step both (vault A to vault A' with no relay contacted in either mode).

Flows act through each vault's command bus as its local principal; incoming statements are accepted only when signed by a key authorized for the role (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-8, N2 registry), a correctly signed statement from a key without that role is quarantined with its reason and changes nothing, and relay requests use signed requests or relay access tokens.
Each flow includes at least one negative authorization step (wrong actor gets FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND per CTR-ERR-001 ERR-4).
Fake ports have no capabilities of their own and cannot be reached from production code paths.
Idempotency is tested in every flow by replaying the first mutating command with the same key and asserting identical response and no new events.
Concurrent steps use deterministic scheduling (explicit awaits on a controlled executor) so the same interleaving runs on every execution.
After a simulated consumer crash, redelivery produces a single net effect (CTR-EVT-001 at-least-once with idempotent consumers).

After a relay outage or tampering, each domain record is local committed and its OutboxEntry moves only along the F15.S01.M01 states prepared, sending, transport_acknowledged, peer_accepted (or conflict, failed, expired) per CTR-IDM-001 IDM-7, and the harness asserts after every step that the UI-facing label never exceeds the state reached.

Integration data is synthetic and actors are generated pseudonyms; public locations are L2 cells, and synthetic L3 cells and L4 points marked P3 (meetup point, home address) are seeded into participant vaults so canary-leak checks prove they never reach public views, search documents, federation envelopes, relay storage or logs.
The suite asserts that private-message payloads and P3 fields never appear in public views, federation exports or event payloads marked P0.
Logs from the relay in tests are captured and scanned: a canary P3 value must never appear.
The harness reports per-flow duration and event counts in reports/integration.json.
Each flow completes in at most 5 s and the whole integration suite in at most 120 s on 2 vCPU.
Relay startup in the harness takes at most 2 s per test file.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Each of the 12 flows has at least one dedicated test row and the flow list is asserted against the reference list in this spec.
Contract tests are generated from the schema registry so a new registered command or event is covered automatically.
The flow report reports/integration.json is the only export; it contains no user data.

The federation_io flow proves two different things in two steps: federation (a vault publishes P0/L2 envelopes to relay R1, R1 federates signed batches of at most 100 to R2, and R2 holds read-only mirrors with provenance, CTR-FED-001) and vault portability (a classrup-export/v1 bundle exported from memory vault A is imported into a fresh memory vault A' on another simulated device under the IOX-2 dry-run and collision rules, CTR-IOX-001); no relay ever receives an IOX-1 bundle.
Rollback is a git revert; harness changes never alter production code.
The module owns no persisted entities; fixed regression cases are stored as JSON files in tests/property/regressions/ versioned in git, and open cases exist only as CI artifacts and issues.

Each regression file (classrup-regression/v1) records property ID, generator ID and version, fast-check version, seed, path, the shrunk concrete value, status open or fixed, and the expectation that the property holds for that value, so it replays as a plain expected-pass example.
Arbitraries are derived from production schemas and never construct invalid Money (non-integer or negative amount strings) unless an invalid-input arbitrary is named explicitly.

Envelope properties are included: JCS canonical bytes are stable under object key reordering, any single-byte mutation of a signed envelope fails verification, and two conflicting signed promises on the same subject are detected as a fork regardless of delivery order and never resolved by last-writer-wins.

Statement-trust properties are included: for any generated (statement type, signer role) pair that the F11.S01.M01 statement registry (N2) does not allow, the receiving vault quarantines the statement with reason signer_role_invalid and its state is unchanged; re-delivering any accepted envelope any number of times and in any order yields the same vault state as one delivery (dedupe by cid, CTR-FED-001 FED-7).
Every property declares numRuns and a seed; the pr profile requires numRuns of at least 200 and the nightly profile exactly 10 000.
A property title must be a valid TEST-PS-NNN-PP.Tnn ID matching CTR-TST-001, plus a short human name after a space.
Each property must finish within 10 s per property in the pr profile and 120 s in nightly, otherwise it fails with a timeout code.

Geoprivacy properties generate raw L4 latitude and longitude and cells of precision 6 to 9, and assert for any input: every public, search or federated output is a cell of precision 5 or coarser equal to the F06.S02.M01 snap of the input (assertPublicCell, N8; CTR-PRV-001 PRV-1, PRV-3); every shown distance is one of the PRV-2 buckets computed cell to cell with a search radius of at least 5 km; and repeated queries from origins shifted inside one cell return identical results.
There is no entity lifecycle; a property run is a stateless process with exit code 0 or 1.
A failing property is shrunk by fast-check to a minimal counterexample and the run always exits 1, never retries with a different seed to turn red green.

A nightly counterexample is never committed automatically: the nightly report job uploads it as a classrup-regression/v1 file with status open as an artifact and opens or updates one issue per counterexample hash (issues: write on that schedule-only job, F17.S03.M01). The fix pull request adds the file with status fixed, and CI in that pull request runs the case once on the parent commit, where it must fail, to prove the fail-before-fix condition.

The module exposes pnpm test:property (pr profile) and pnpm test:property:nightly (10 000 runs) and pnpm test:property --seed --path

for replay.
No relay commands or events exist; outputs are reports/property.json and JUnit XML.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 counterexample found, 2 timeout, 3 profile misconfiguration.
The module needs no capabilities and runs without relay sessions.
Properties for authorization (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-2) call the pure authorize() function with generated actor and resource combinations and assert default deny.
Property code cannot import secrets or network clients; the dependency rule from F17.S01.M01 applies.
Replaying the same seed and path reproduces the same counterexample deterministically on the pinned fast-check and Node 22 versions.
Property runs are pure, write only to reports/ (open regression cases go to reports/regressions/), never modify tests/property/regressions/, and are safe to re-run any number of times.
A property that mutates shared state in a test double resets it in a beforeEach hook; the lint rule forbids module-level mutable state in property files.

Generated data is synthetic and comes only from the shared generators under tests/property/arbitraries; geoprivacy generators deliberately produce raw L4 coordinates and precision-6+ cells as P3 inputs, so a leak of finer precision into a public, search or federated output can fail a property.
Reports contain generated values only for failures, retained 30 days as CI artifacts, and never contain real data.
Seeds are not secret; they are printed in logs and PR comments.
The runner records numRuns, duration and shrink count per property in reports/property.json.
PR profile completes the whole property suite in at most 60 s on 2 vCPU; nightly in at most 20 min.

Self-tests prove that planted bugs (an off-by-one money split, a broken cycle checker, a state machine with a missing guard) are found within 200 runs.
The nightly profile is verified by a dry-run with numRuns 10 000 on a small property set in CI weekly.
Regression files are the only exported artifact; they are plain JSON and portable, open ones as CI artifacts and fixed ones in git.
Upgrading fast-check changes value generation, so the version is pinned at 4.10.2 and upgrades require a full nightly run with zero new counterexamples before merge.
