The module owns no persisted entities; the only artifacts are vitest.config.ts (test.projects node and browser-like, pool forks, isolate true, testTimeout 5000), shared setup files, the code-owned tests/quarantine.yaml and generated coverage reports under coverage/ which are git-ignored.
Fixtures define data shapes by importing the production schemas, so a schema change breaks fixtures at compile time rather than silently diverging.

Fixture data is synthetic only: no real names, emails, phone numbers or coordinates. Public fixtures use geohash cells of precision 5 or coarser; synthetic L3 cells (precision 6) and L4 exact coordinates exist only as fixtures marked P3 so leak tests can prove that public, search and federated outputs hold only the F06.S02.M01 snap of the input at precision 5 or coarser (CTR-PRV-001 PRV-1, PRV-3; N8 assertPublicCell).

Fixtures include MemoryVault (the storage/memory adapter), a seeded Ed25519 keypair factory and builders for CTR-FED-001 signed envelopes, so vault commands and statement verification run with no relay and no network.
A custom lint rule validates that every test title in packages with a module.spec.yaml starts with TEST-PS-NNN-PP.Tnn where NN is two digits.
The global setup rejects nondeterminism sources (Math.random, Date.now, argument-less new Date, global fetch, process.env reads not on an allow list) with a typed error.
Coverage thresholds are evaluated per package after the run and violations map to exactly one error code per package.

Unit suites of isomorphic packages run twice, in Node 22 and in a browser-like environment with fake-indexeddb and WebCrypto, and fail with QUALITY_UNIT_NODE_IMPORT_IN_CORE when core code imports node: modules.
There is no entity lifecycle; a unit run is a stateless process with exit code 0 on pass and 1 on any failure.
A run never mutates the working tree outside coverage/ and .vitest-cache/.
Test isolation is per file (isolate: true, pool: forks) so no test observes state from another file.
The module exposes the scripts pnpm test:unit, pnpm test:unit --coverage, and pnpm test:unit --changed for local use.
The interface emits no relay events; run results are JUnit XML at reports/unit.xml and JSON at reports/unit.json.
Exit codes are documented: 0 pass, 1 test failure, 2 coverage threshold failure, 3 configuration or lint failure.
The module requires no capabilities and must not import relay session code, so unit tests cannot call authorize() against a live session.
Unit tests of authorization logic use pure authorize() with constructed actors from fixtures (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-2).
Test files and fixtures are excluded from production build outputs by the package files allow list.
Re-running a unit suite with the same seed and FakeClock start time produces byte-identical JSON reports apart from durations.
Failures print the seed, fixed clock start time and sequence ID generator offset so any failure replays locally with one command.

Retries are disabled (retry: 0) so intermittent failures are never masked. A test that fails at least once in 100 CI runs is quarantined within 24 h by an entry in the code-owned tests/quarantine.yaml {testId, issueUrl, owner, createdAt, expiresAt at most 14 days later}; the runner moves listed tests into a non-blocking quarantine project that still runs and reports them, F17.S03.M02 treats an active entry as a waiver under its V08 rules, an expired entry fails the release gate, and the lint allows skips only through that file.
Fixtures contain only synthetic data and the lint rule fails on strings matching real email or phone patterns outside the reserved example.com and 555-01xx ranges.
Coverage and JUnit artifacts are retained 14 days in CI and contain no secrets because tests run without environment secrets.
Tests run with an empty environment allow list so credentials in the developer shell never leak into snapshots.
The module records suite duration, test count and coverage per package as run metrics in the JSON report.
Unit suite wall time on the 2 vCPU CI runner stays under 60 s for the whole workspace and under 5 s per package.
Slowest 10 tests are listed in each CI summary and any test over 500 ms is flagged for review.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test, using the mapping in section 09.
Tool self-tests run the lint rule and the nondeterminism guard against crafted fixtures to prove rejection.
The coverage gate itself is tested with a synthetic package below and above threshold.
Configuration is plain TypeScript in the repository; there is no user data to export or import.
Fixture factories are versioned with the production schemas; upgrading vitest or fast-check versions is a reviewed change to the pinned lockfile.
Rollback is a git revert of the configuration commit; thresholds are only ever raised in a separate commit from feature work.
The module owns no persisted entities; faults are described in a scenario file (YAML) and results in reports/chaos.json.
A scenario lists fault type, injection point, duration, seed, and the invariants to assert; the schema is validated before the run.

Fault injectors wrap ports and the clock in the test relay and in test vaults (the F15.S02.M03 storage/indexeddb adapter over fake-indexeddb aborts a transaction on the Nth write; each vault clock is skewable on its own); production code contains no chaos hooks and a build check of both the relay bundle and the vault (PWA) bundles proves it.
Every scenario must assert the full invariant set after recovery, not only that the process stays alive.
Fault parameters are bounded: BUSY duration at most 30 s, clock skew at most 24 h, peer outage at most 10 min, crashes at most 5 per scenario.
A scenario without a seed or without recovery step is rejected with a typed error.
There is no entity lifecycle; a scenario runs phases arrange, inject, observe, recover, assert.

Recovery is time-boxed per scenario on the FakeClock (06.R04): 60 s for local faults (db_busy, idb_abort, consumer_crash, duplicate_delivery, combined_busy_crash); for peer_outage the next scheduled F11.S02.M01 round plus one IDM-4 cycle (about 16 min of fake time) or 60 s after federation.peer.reinstated; otherwise the scenario fails.
Scenarios are independent: each starts from a fresh relay and database.

Trust-fault scenarios are mandatory reruns of the F17.S01.M03 suites with the same names and that module's oracle, which owns the expected outcomes: relay_down, fork_conflict, revocation_lag, relay_tamper, signer_role_mismatch, relay_replay and relay_withhold_equivocate, each with 3 seeds in the PR profile and 30 seeds nightly of randomised fault timing.
The module exposes pnpm test:chaos (smoke profile), pnpm test:chaos:nightly and pnpm test:chaos --scenario <name> --seed <n>.

Scenarios are db_busy, idb_abort, consumer_crash, duplicate_delivery, clock_skew, peer_outage, vault_outbox_outage, combined_busy_crash and the reruns of the F17.S01.M03 trust-fault suites relay_down, fork_conflict, revocation_lag, relay_tamper, signer_role_mismatch, relay_replay and relay_withhold_equivocate.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 invariant violated, 2 recovery timeout, 3 scenario invalid.
Chaos runs use only the test relay and fake ports; no real peers, hosts or credentials are touched.
Fault injection endpoints exist only in the test harness process, not exposed over HTTP.
Authorization checks keep working under fault: a denied command still denies after recovery, and audit entries are not lost.
Idempotency is verified under each fault: replaying a command whose response was lost returns the stored result with no duplicate effect (CTR-IDM-001).
Consumers dedupe by event ID, so duplicate or reordered deliveries are safe (CTR-EVT-001).

After any single injected fault, a sweep with nothing else running covers every participant vault (reservation store: no classrup.bazaar.reservation/v1 hold past expiresAt; saga state: no saga stuck outside a documented state; sync outbox: every OutboxEntry in a documented F15.S01.M01 state) and, on the relay, only the relay-hosted leases (auction close) and the mailbox and federation queues.

Recovery bounds are per scenario and derived from the owner's schedule on the FakeClock: 60 s for local faults (db_busy, idb_abort, consumer_crash, duplicate_delivery, combined_busy_crash); for peer_outage the next scheduled F11.S02.M01 round (1 min, then 15 min after the previous round) plus one IDM-4 cycle, about 16 min of fake time, or 60 s after federation.peer.reinstated; for vault_outbox_outage the F15.S01.M01 behavior is asserted instead of auto-drain - after 6 IDM-4 attempts (each delay uniform in [0, min(30 s, 500 ms x 2^(n-1))], retryAfterMs honoured) the entry is failed with failureReason retry_exhausted, and after Retry now it reaches transport_acknowledged.

Clock skew invariants are checkable without trusted time (ADR-0016 section 5): (1) ordering by seq, revision and outbox order never depends on wall time; (2) an entity that has expired never comes back when the clock moves backwards and its expiry event fires exactly once; (3) a vault whose clock is +24 h expires its own reservations and cycles by its own clock and the other vaults see a signed withdrawal or expiry rather than silent divergence; (4) relay-hosted leases (IDM-3, auction close) use only the relay clock.
Chaos data are synthetic; reports contain scenario names, seeds and invariant results only.
Logs from the relay during chaos are scanned for P2–P4 canaries; faults must not cause sensitive data to be logged in error paths.
Reports retained 30 days.
The harness records classrup_quality_chaos_* metrics and scrapes the relay's own outbox lag gauge (classrup_outbox_lag_ms).
Smoke profile finishes in at most 2 min; nightly profile with 30 seeds per scenario in at most 30 min.
Recovery time per scenario is measured; a trend regression above 2x the baseline is flagged.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
A planted bug (consumer applies effect twice on redelivery) must be caught by the duplicate_delivery scenario.
A planted bug (an expired reservation is resurrected after the clock moves back) must be caught by clock_skew.
Scenario files and reports are the exports; a failed run exports its seed and fault schedule for replay.
Scenario schema is versioned (classrup-chaos-scenario/v1) and the runner reads v1 only.
Rollback is a git revert; no state outside git and CI artifacts exists.
The module owns no persisted entities; it produces reports/load.json (schema classrup-load-report/v1) with scenario results and environment details.
The report records relay commit SHA, Node version, CPU model, memory, disk type, seed and profile so runs are comparable.
Seed datasets are synthetic and deterministic from seed 20261104; no production data is ever loaded.
Each scenario has a declared target (rate, duration, p95 budget) and the verdict is pass only when measured p95 is at most the budget and error rate at most 0.1 %.
The driver rejects runs that are invalid: generator CPU above 70 %, achieved rate below 95 % of target, or less than the profile duration.
The load script refuses to run against any host not on the explicit allow list (localhost and the CI relay) with a typed error.

The load script targets relay services only: signed public-projection index reads and writes (write_index through federation.record.ingest with signature verification), mailbox put and get of opaque encrypted envelopes with the content-free push enqueue that a mailbox put triggers (N17), matching over public projections and auction hosting (auction_bid through auctions.bid.place at the host relay); the relay never receives plaintext P2+ data in the test.
There is no entity lifecycle; a load run goes through phases seed, warm-up (30 s, discarded), measure and report.
A run ends with exit 0 only if every scenario passes; otherwise exit 1; invalid runs exit 2.
A soak run additionally checks that memory growth stays under 10 % between minute 10 and minute 60.
The module exposes pnpm load:smoke, pnpm load:standard, pnpm load:soak and pnpm load --scenario <name>.
Scenarios are read_index, write_index, write_mailbox, search_text, search_geo, cycle_search, auction_bid and mixed_70_30.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 budget failure, 2 invalid run, 3 configuration or seed failure.

The load driver authenticates its traffic to the test relay with relay access tokens from the challenge–response flow (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-10) using generated device keys, and the traffic never uses a relay operator or admin role; only the setup step (RatePolicy) and the metrics scraper hold a separate operator token of the throwaway test relay, minted per run and revoked at the end.

Rate limits are not disabled; the setup step raises the load tenant's limits through an F12.S03.M03 RatePolicy (moderation.ratepolicy.set on the test relay) and the report records the policy revision and values.
Load never runs against production hosts; the host allow list is enforced in code and by CI network rules.
Runs are repeatable: a fresh relay and database are created per run and the seed is deterministic.
Write scenarios use unique Idempotency-Keys per request (signed index writes dedupe by cid) and also replay 1 % of requests with the same key or cid to verify idempotency under load.
If the relay crashes mid-run, the run is invalid, exit 2, and the relay log tail is saved.
Load data are synthetic P0; the report contains no listing text or IDs of real users.
Relay logs captured during load are scanned for P2–P4 canaries.
Reports are retained 90 days as CI artifacts to allow trend comparisons.
The driver exports the metrics it measures: classrup_quality_load_latency_ms by scenario and percentile, error rate and achieved rate.

The relay's own metrics (CTR-OBS-001 OBS-2, operator-only /metrics) are scraped every 5 s during the run by the separate scraper with its per-run operator token for the test relay, never by the load driver, and stored in the report.
Smoke profile completes in at most 3 min including seeding; standard in at most 15 min including seeding of 100 000 listings.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Self-tests run the driver against a stub server with known latencies to prove percentile computation within 2 %.
A planted slowdown of 400 ms in write handling must turn the write scenario red.
Reports are exported as JSON and Markdown; the gates module (F17.S03.M02) reads reports/load.json.
Report schema is versioned; the gates module accepts v1 and ignores unknown fields.
Rollback is a git revert; budgets are defined in CTR-OBS-001 and are never edited in this module without a contract change.
The module owns no persisted entities; it reads the OutboxEntry shape owned by F15.S01.M01 through the public API and never defines its own copy.
Test fixtures create outbox entries through the production enqueue function so the schema is exercised as shipped.
Network scenarios are described as data (sequence of online, offline, latency, loss steps) in tests/offline/scenarios/.

The core must work with no relay configured: create, edit and search local records and sign statements offline; the sync status shows Saved on this device (local committed, OutboxEntry prepared) and never a relay or peer label without a verified receipt or acknowledgement.
Every offline test must assert exactly-once effect: the receiving vault applies each statement once, identified by its cid, and a relay command takes effect once under its Idempotency-Key.

Conflict tests must assert that CONFLICT_REVISION or a peer rejection never produces a silent overwrite, that the dialog offers exactly Prepare a new version on theirs (a new entry with a new cid and expectedRevision = currentRevision) and Discard mine, that no option overwrites the peer's signed revision, and that a fork freezes the coordination with no resolve option.
An unsent entry triggers the expiry prompt from day 6 and at 7 days moves to expired with its payload erased; it is never sent afterwards and a send attempt is refused with EXPIRED.

The UI label for an entry is never stronger than the F15.S01.M01 label for its reached state, ranked by CONSISTENCY_STATES (Saved on this device, then Delivered to relay, peer has not confirmed, then Confirmed by peer); an overclaim is for example Confirmed by peer before peer_accepted, or any delivered wording at transport_acknowledged that does not say to relay, and fails with QUALITY_OFFLINE_OVERCLAIM.

Outbox limits are asserted as F15.S01.M01 defines them, at most min(200, the local limit) entries and 5 MiB of payload per principal, and the next enqueue is refused with PLATFORM_OUTBOX_FULL and a visible message, never a silent drop.

There is no entity lifecycle for the module; tests walk the F15.S01.M01 OutboxEntry states prepared, sending, transport_acknowledged, peer_accepted, conflict, failed, expired and discarded with that module's state-to-label table (the domain record itself is local committed; quarantine is a receiver-side status of F11.S01.M02, not an outbox state; CTR-IDM-001 IDM-7).
Transitions are asserted in both unit tests with the fake network and a browser run with Playwright network emulation.
A test ends only after the outbox is empty or in an explicit expected terminal state.
The module exposes pnpm test:offline (fake network, no browser, under 30 s) and pnpm test:offline:browser (Playwright, Pixel 7 profile).
The scenarios are offline_queue, flaky_replay, conflict_prompt, fork_freeze, expiry_prompt, retry_exhausted, outbox_full, cache_shell, quota_full, vault_lock and reload_during_replay.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 assertion failure, 2 configuration failure.

Offline tests use real authorization: a queued statement signed by a key revoked while offline is refused or quarantined by the receiving vault (F11.S01.M02), and the sender's entry shows the reported rejection as Needs attention with its reason; quarantine is the receiver's status, not an outbox state.

On vault lock (F07.S01.M02) and principal switch, the suite asserts: in-memory keys are dropped; the vault in IndexedDB stays encrypted and unreadable until unlock; OutboxEntry rows are kept but not sent; relay access tokens are dropped; the principal's image partition is unbound (CLEAR_USER_CACHES reason lock or principal switch, F15.S01.M02); a second principal on the device gets a separate vault; and only an explicit Erase vault (F10.S01.M04 deletion flow) after an export prompt may delete IndexedDB data.
No test uses an elevated relay role (operator, moderator); test principals are locally created identities.

Retry follows CTR-IDM-001 IDM-4 as F15.S01.M01 specifies it - each delay for attempt n is uniform in [0, min(30 s, 500 ms x 2^(n-1))], retryAfterMs is honoured when larger, after 6 attempts the entry moves to failed with failureReason retry_exhausted, and Retry now resets attempts; tests assert the bounds with a fake clock and a seeded jitter source.
Resend is idempotent by construction (the same cid for statements, the same Idempotency-Key for relay commands); the test resends 1, 3 and 10 times across resets with identical results.
A command that fails with a non-retryable error is not retried and is surfaced to the user.

Cached and queued data are synthetic; outbox entries for relay destinations contain only ciphertext for P2 and no P3 field, and an enqueue of plaintext P2 or of P3 is refused (F15.S01.M01, CTR-PRV-001 PRV-5), proven by a planted-leak test.

Vault lock and principal switch keep the previous principal's vault encrypted and its outbox entries kept but neither shown nor sent; a locked vault's records are unreadable without unlock, unlocking restores them intact with zero entries lost, and only Erase vault after an export prompt deletes them.
Browser traces from offline tests redact Authorization headers.
The suite records resend latency after reconnect: first entry sent at most 2 s after connectivity returns on the fake network.
OBS-5 offline budget is asserted: the app shell loads offline after the first visit in at most 2.5 s on the 4G profile.
Fake network tests finish in at most 30 s; browser tests in at most 3 min on 2 vCPU.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Planted bugs (resend with a new key, relay-authenticated response cached, a label stronger than the reached state, a third merge option, plaintext P2 queued for a relay) must fail the suite.

pnpm test:offline runs in the F17.S03.M01 fast gate on every pull request, and pnpm test:offline:browser runs after build-pwa whenever the changes job reports apps/pwa changes; both report into gate-summary.
Reports are JUnit XML and reports/offline.json; no user data.
Scenarios are plain data files and can be reused by the e2e module.
Rollback is a git revert; no persistent state.
The module owns no persisted entities; its files are workflow YAML under .github/workflows and a lint script tools/ci-lint.

Workflow artifacts are named pwa-dist, reports-fast, reports-nightly, reports-weekly and reports-release with defined retention: 7, 14, 30, 30 days and, for reports-release, attached to the release and kept 1 year.
Environment pins are declared once as env at workflow level: NODE_VERSION 22, PNPM_VERSION 10.28.0, with actions pinned to a full commit SHA or an exact major tag.

The workflow lint rejects: any uses: outside actions/*, missing permissions block, permissions broader than contents: read except the per-job allowlist (issues: write only on the nightly-report job of nightly.yml; contents: write only on the release-publish job of release.yml, which needs the gates job; never a write permission on a job reachable from pull_request), pull_request_target triggers, workflow-level paths-ignore or paths filters on ci.yml, missing concurrency cancel-in-progress, and missing timeout-minutes.

The fast gate must contain jobs changes, install, spec-check, typecheck, test (unit, property, integration), offline (pnpm test:offline, fake network, under 30 s, on every pull request), build-pwa, offline-browser (pnpm test:offline:browser after build-pwa when pwa_changed), e2e-smoke and gate-summary, where every job after changes depends on changes and install.

Branch protection requires the single check gate-summary, which runs with if: always() and passes only when every job succeeded or was skipped because of a changes output; it fails if any job failed, was cancelled or was skipped for any other reason.
A workflow run moves through queued, in progress, then success, failure or cancelled; cancelled by newer push is a normal outcome.

The nightly-report job, the only job holding issues: write, opens or updates one issue labelled nightly-failure when a long run fails and closes it when the next run passes; it also files property counterexamples and flake quarantine proposals as issues and never commits or opens pull requests.

Job dependency graph: changes, then install, then parallel spec-check, typecheck, unit-property-integration, offline and build-pwa, then e2e-smoke and offline-browser (if pwa_changed) after build-pwa, then gate-summary with if: always().

Release job graph on the tagged commit: install, then parallel fast suites, property-nightly, load (smoke then standard), chaos-smoke, compat (data, schema diff, browser matrix), e2e-full (with axe and test:e2e:budgets) and spec-report (specgen check --strict --report), then collect (download all reports into reports/ and run pnpm gates:release), then release-publish only when collect returned GO.
The module exposes workflow triggers: push, pull_request (opened, synchronize, reopened), workflow_dispatch, schedule for nightly and weekly, and push of a v* tag for release.
Reusable scripts are pnpm ci:fast, pnpm ci:nightly, pnpm ci:weekly and pnpm ci:release so that developers can reproduce a gate locally; the YAML only calls these scripts.

The release workflow first regenerates all evidence on the release commit (fast suites, property nightly profile, load smoke and standard, chaos smoke, compatibility data, schema diff and browser matrix, e2e full with axe and test:e2e:budgets, specgen check --strict --report), downloads every report into one reports/ directory, then calls pnpm gates:release from F17.S03.M02 and fails on a non-zero exit; release-publish runs only after GO.

Workflows default to permissions contents: read and no secrets on pull requests; the per-job allowlist grants issues: write only to the schedule-triggered nightly-report job and contents: write only to release-publish in release.yml after gates:release returns GO; no job reachable from pull_request holds any write permission, and no workflow opens pull requests (one created with GITHUB_TOKEN would not trigger CI, so nightly findings become issues and artifacts).
No workflow uses long-lived credentials or deploys; the PWA is static and relays are operated by their hosts.
Secret scanning (F16.S01.M02) runs in the fast gate on the diff computed by the changes job against the fetched base commit and fails on a finding.
Re-running a failed job is safe because every job is a pure function of the commit; artifacts are overwritten by name.
Cache and artifact steps use continue-on-error false for artifacts and true for cache restore, so cache outages slow the build but do not fail it.
Infrastructure failures (runner lost, cache service error) are retried once automatically by re-run; assertion failures are never retried.
Fork pull requests run with read-only tokens and no secrets; logs are scanned for token patterns by the secrets step before upload.
Artifacts contain test reports and the static build only, with no user data (the PWA sends no telemetry per OBS-7).
Retention: PWA artifact 7 days, fast reports 14 days, nightly reports 30 days.
The fast gate completes in at most 10 min p95 on ubuntu-24.04 (2 vCPU) with a warm cache; install at most 60 s warm; PWA build at most 90 s.
Each workflow writes a job summary with per-job durations and the cache hit ratio; a cache hit ratio under 80 percent over 20 runs is flagged.
Initial JS size of the built PWA is reported (budget 150 KiB gzip) and fails the build job when exceeded.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
The workflow lint is unit-tested with good and bad workflow fixtures, and dry-run in CI on every change to .github.
A canary pull request fixture proves that docs-only changes skip tests and spec YAML changes run spec:check.
Workflow files and the lint script are the only exports; there is no user data.
A new workflow is introduced by pull request and validated by the lint before merge; branch protection settings are documented in the repository settings file.
Rollback is a git revert of the workflow change; in-flight runs finish with their previous definition.
The module owns no persisted entities; N-1 fixtures live in tests/compat/fixtures/<version>/ and are regenerated by a script at each release.
Each fixture set contains a vault snapshot, an export bundle (CTR-IOX-001), signed statements (CTR-FED-001) and relay API recordings with the producing version recorded.
Fixtures are synthetic and contain generated keys that are never used elsewhere.
The current release must read every N-1 fixture and, after upgrade, every record validates against its current schema and every N-1 signature still verifies.
Schemas follow expand and contract: removed required fields or changed meanings of a field fail the schema diff check with QUALITY_COMPAT_BREAKING_CHANGE.

Readers follow CTR-SCH-001 SCH-2 - an unknown key in a statement payload outside ext is rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED; ext keys are preserved byte-exact so cid and signature still verify and ext is at most 4 KiB; an unknown key listed in ext.crit is refused; unknown major versions are refused with UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION.
Vault upgrade runs through states N-1, upgrading and N; interruption in upgrading must resume or roll back on next start with zero lost or duplicated records.

Automated browser matrix cells move through queued, running and pass, fail or unsupported, and manual cells through pending checklist, then signed pass or signed fail; a cell marked unsupported needs an entry in the support policy.

A release is blocked when any automated cell fails its smoke journey, and when any manual cell (Firefox stable N and N-1, Safari desktop and iOS Safari last 2, iOS 16.4+ installed-PWA push) has a missing or failed signed checklist; F17.S03.M02 reads both from reports/compat.json.

The module exposes pnpm test:compat (N-1 data and API), pnpm test:compat:browsers (automated matrix, nightly and release), pnpm compat:schema-diff and pnpm compat:checklist <version>, which merges the signed manual cells from gates/manual/<version>/ into reports/compat.json.
Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 compatibility failure, 2 matrix cell failure, 3 configuration failure.
The OpenAPI diff compares the generated relay spec of the previous release tag with the working tree and fails on removed paths, removed fields or changed types.
Compat tests run as unit and integration tests with no relay credentials; relay API recordings are replayed against the in-process relay with relay access tokens from fixtures.
Vault upgrade tests use locally generated keys; no secret leaves the test process.
Statements from N-1 signed by a key authorized in N-1 remain accepted when the role mapping is unchanged (CTR-CAP-001 CAP-8).
The vault upgrade is idempotent: running it twice leaves identical data, and an interrupted upgrade resumes without duplicating records.

Rollback of the app to N-1 follows one explicit rule: the IndexedDB database version is bumped only for object-store or index changes, and record-level additive changes go through lazy SCH-4 migrations without a bump, so the N-1 read test (N-1 code opens and reads N vault data) applies to releases without a bump; for a release with a bump, N keeps a pre-upgrade export or snapshot, N-1 code catches VersionError and offers restore from it, and the test asserts zero record loss and no partial open (CTR-IOX-001 IOX-4, never a destructive in-place downgrade).
The matrix runner retries a cell once for infrastructure failure only.
Fixtures and reports contain no real data; keys are synthetic.
Browser matrix runs use clean profiles with no extensions and no signed-in browser profile; manual checklists record device, OS and browser version but no personal data beyond the approver handle.
Reports are retained 30 days in CI.
The runner records pass or fail per cell, durations and the browser version tested.
N-1 data tests finish in at most 60 s; schema and OpenAPI diff in at most 20 s; browser matrix in at most 25 min nightly.

Automated runs only feature-detect Web Push and check the content-free push payload format (reference and template key only) on the WebKit engine build; real push delivery to an installed iOS 16.4+ PWA is a manual checklist cell recorded with device, iOS version and approver.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Planted breaking changes (field removed, type changed, required field added) must be caught by the schema diff.
The support matrix in documentation is compared with the matrix actually run in CI to prevent drift.
Compat reports and the support matrix table are exports; fixtures are the N-1 export bundles.
Importing an N export into N-1 must fail clearly (UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION) rather than partially; importing N-1 into N must succeed fully.
Rollback of this module is a git revert; fixtures for a new release are generated at the release tag before changes to schemas are merged.
The module owns no persisted entities; reports/gates.json (schema classrup-gates-report/v1) records each gate verdict, evidence and timestamp.
The trace matrix reports/trace.json maps each requirement ID to test IDs and results, covering all modules with a module.spec.yaml.
Evidence references are file paths and counts; reports contain no user data.

Traceability is 100 percent: every requirement PS-NNN-PP.Rnn is covered by at least one passing test whose title starts with TEST-PS-NNN-PP.Tnn and whose spec row lists the requirement (for level manual rows, a signed checklist entry instead of a JUnit result), or by an active waiver or quarantine entry, or has a documented untested reason (CTR-TST-001 TST-4).
The audit gate fails on any critical or high production vulnerability reported by pnpm audit --prod and fails closed when the audit cannot run.
The a11y, budget and compat gates fail when any report is missing, older than 24 hours, from another commit SHA, or shows a violation, exceeded budget or compatibility failure.

The spec gate runs node tools/specgen/specgen.mjs check --strict --report for this commit and passes only with 0 errors and GO; the compat gate reads reports/compat.json for this commit and passes only when no QUALITY_COMPAT_* failure is present and every browser cell passes or is policy-unsupported, including the manual Safari and iOS checklist cells.

Manual tests count only through a signed checklist file gates/manual/<version>/<testId>.yaml with result pass, approver handle, date, device, OS and engine version, and the release commit SHA, committed with code-owner approval; it replaces JUnit only for rows with level manual, and waiver and checklist commits print their approver from git metadata.

Mapping relevance: each covers entry counts only when the test text (scenario and expected cells of the spec row plus the code test title after its ID) and the requirement text share at least one key term, where key terms are the lowercase tokens split on characters other than letters, digits and underscore, at least 4 characters long, not in the fixed stopword list tools/gates/stopwords.txt, with a trailing s, es, ed or ing removed; otherwise it counts only through an entry in gates/mapping-reviews.yaml with testId, requirementId, reviewer handle, date and the SHA-256 of both normalized texts, committed with code-owner approval; a review whose hash no longer matches is stale, and a mapping without overlap or a valid review fails with QUALITY_GATE_TRACE_MAPPING.

Governance bundles: gates/governance-bundles.yaml holds projectPublisherDid (the release-pinned project publisher did:key) and, per release version, one review entry for each of the three required bundled packs (taxonomy pack core-1, the bundled rule pack, the generic jurisdiction profile) with statement type, file path in the release commit, packCid, reviewer handle and date, committed with code-owner approval; the gate passes only when every required pack has an entry, its file exists, the recomputed cid equals the reviewed packCid, the Ed25519 signature over JCS bytes verifies (CTR-FED-001 FED-2, FED-7), and author and payload.publisherId equal projectPublisherDid; a missing manifest, entry or file fails closed.
There is no entity lifecycle; the release process is a sequence of gates, each pass or fail, with the final verdict GO only when all pass.
Gates run in the order spec, traceability, audit, a11y, budgets, compat, governance, changelog and all run even after a failure so the report is complete.

A waiver is a documented entry in gates/waivers.yaml with ID, reason, owner and expiry date at most 14 days away, and an active tests/quarantine.yaml entry of F17.S01.M01 is treated as a waiver under the same rules; expired waivers fail.
The module exposes pnpm gates:release, pnpm gates:trace, pnpm gates:audit and pnpm gates:report.
Exit codes: 0 GO, 1 at least one gate failed, 2 evidence missing or stale, 3 configuration failure.

The release workflow of F17.S03.M01 calls gates:release in its collect job after downloading every report of the release commit into one reports/ directory; its separate release-publish job (contents: write) attaches reports/gates.md only after GO, and the gates themselves never write to the repository.

Gates are read-only against the repository and run with contents: read; no token or secret is needed. Attaching reports/gates.md is done after GO by the separate release-publish job, the only job allowed contents: write by the F17.S03.M01 per-job allowlist.

Waivers, quarantine entries, manual checklists, mapping reviews and the governance bundle manifest (projectPublisherDid and release review entries) require a code-owner approved commit; the gate prints the approver from git metadata and fails an unapproved commit with QUALITY_GATE_WAIVER_UNAPPROVED.
Audit calls use the public registry endpoint only and send no repository content.
Gates are idempotent and side-effect free apart from writing reports; re-running yields the same verdict for the same inputs.
Stale evidence (older than 24 h or from a different commit SHA) is rejected so a green result from another commit cannot be reused.
If a gate crashes it is reported as failed with the error message and the other gates still run.
Reports contain package names and advisory IDs from the audit and test IDs; no user data.
Waivers are public in the repository and carry no personal data beyond a GitHub handle.
Gate reports are retained with the release artifacts for 1 year.
The module records gate durations and the trace coverage ratio in reports/gates.json.
The complete gate run finishes in at most 60 s (excluding the audit network call, at most 30 s).
Trace coverage ratio is reported per module and in total; the release requires 1.0.
Every requirement of this module is covered by at least one automated test using the mapping in section 09.
Gate logic is tested with synthetic repositories: full coverage, one missing test, one skipped test, a duplicate ID, an expired waiver.
The audit gate is tested with recorded audit JSON for critical, high, moderate and unavailable cases.
reports/gates.json, reports/trace.json and reports/gates.md are the exports and are attached to the release.

Gate input formats are JUnit XML, load report v1 (reports/load.json), PWA budget report v1 (reports/pwa-budgets.json), axe JSON, compat report v1 (reports/compat.json), the specgen check --strict --report output (SPEC_COMPLETENESS_REPORT.md), signed manual checklists (gates/manual/<version>/), tests/quarantine.yaml, gates/waivers.yaml, gates/mapping-reviews.yaml, gates/governance-bundles.yaml with the bundled governance pack envelopes (CTR-FED-001) and the audit JSON; unknown fields are ignored and unknown major versions are rejected.
Rollback is a git revert of tools/gates; the release workflow then fails closed on a missing command.

A Category has a stable uuidv7 id, a key unique per publisher, a parent, a depth between 1 and 4, localized names and a status; ids are never reused and never shared with another publisher in a vault.
Categories are P0 public configuration; a vault stores a verified mirror with provenance and only the publisher vault may change the origin copy.
A restricted flag marks categories that need extra notices or review under a jurisdiction profile; it does not itself prohibit anything.

Every category change that needs approval (a restricted-flag change or a retirement) carries the proposalId of the approving decision, and the pack carries the cited decision envelopes with receipts or their cids so receiving vaults can verify them.
Authoring commands validate names, depth, uniqueness and limits before a change is staged.

Applying a pack validates the entire pack atomically: one structurally invalid category rejects the whole pack, while a change whose required decision does not verify keeps that record at its previous state, held with GOVERNANCE_CATEGORY_PROPOSAL_REQUIRED.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Receiving vaults verify through F18.S02.M01 every restricted-flag change and retirement that differs from their applied snapshot, at the anchored activation time, so a publisher cannot skip the proposal requirement.
Category ids are unique across publishers in a vault, and a category may be retired only after it was deprecated for at least 30 days.
Category follows the declared machine in the publisher vault; user vaults mirror the status from verified packs only.
Retired is terminal and requires a merge target so listings referencing the category can be resolved.
Applying a pack is atomic: the resulting snapshot, with applied changes and changes held for a missing decision, is stored in one transaction or not at all.
A category is retired only after at least 30 days of deprecation; there is no direct active to retired transition, in the publisher vault or in apply_pack.

create, update, move and set_status are authoring commands that run in the publisher's vault and stage a change set; release_pack signs the full taxonomy as classrup.governance.taxonomy_pack/v1 with its approvals and queues it to the publisher's relays.

apply_pack is a vault command available in every vault: it verifies the pack, the publisher's trust and every required decision, applies the result atomically and emits one governance.category.changed event per changed category; in a user vault packs from untrusted or paused publishers, and packs that change restricted flags or retire categories, are held in the F18.S02.M01 pending inbox for the owner.

A relay serves the latest pack with its receipt publicly and read-only through relay_latest; relay_upload, accepted only from the relay's operator key, verifies the pack, applies it as the relay's hosting taxonomy and emits governance.category.changed relay-locally.

The bundled seed pack ships signed by the release-pinned project publisher key; it is approved by the release review (F17 release gates), applied without decisions on first start with provenance bundled, and later changes to it follow the normal proposal path.
Statement types of this module are registered in the F11.S01.M01 registry with audience, signer role, role resolution and maxAge (N2).

Vault policy: authoring and release require the vault's principal to hold a publisher key; apply is available to every vault owner for packs from publishers trusted for scope taxonomy in F18.S02.M01, and the apply command never grants trust.
There is no global taxonomy role; relay operator and moderator roles apply only to what that relay hosts (CAP-9), and a relay cannot change a user's mirror.
Relay policy: a relay serves the pack read-only to anonymous clients and accepts a pack upload only from a registered operator device key.
Authoring commands and apply_pack are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; packs are deduplicated by packCid.
apply_pack writes all category changes, held changes, the pack record and the outbox events in one IndexedDB transaction.
Offline vaults keep working on the last applied pack; release_pack shows prepared until a relay receipt exists.
Taxonomy data is P0 and contains no personal data; the only personal link is the publisher key fingerprint, which is public by design.
Packs are retained RET-STANDARD; the last 3 applied versions are kept locally for diff and rollback.

A relay or publisher cannot silently change a user's mirror: every change arrives as a signed pack, and packs that change restricted flags or retire categories wait in the pending inbox until the owner applies or refuses them after seeing the diff.

A compromised or malicious publisher key is contained: packs signed by a revoked device key are quarantined through F07 key status, and the owner can pause trust in F18.S02.M01 so new packs wait in the pending inbox.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); pack outcomes are local diagnostics.
Tree queries and pack application meet local budgets on Moto G-class hardware.
The relay serving packs follows OBS-1 to OBS-4.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate pack statements, commands and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Tree invariants are covered by property tests with at least 200 runs, 10 000 nightly.

The user export contains the applied Category mirror with provenance and held changes; the trusted-publisher list is exported by F18.S02.M01; publisher vaults also export staged changes and their signing history.
Import re-verifies the pack signature, tree invariants and recorded decisions; categories failing verification are not applied.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days; the last 3 packs allow reverting by applying an older signed snapshot re-released with a higher version.

A JurisdictionProfile has a code, a version, covered countries, bounded retention overrides, a minimum age with an age gate, required notices, restricted category references, an optional cash limit and a breach-notification period, and is identified across versions by ProfileRef (publisherId, code).
Profiles are public signed configuration (P0); the user's selection is a P3 local preference that is never sent anywhere.
Profile bounds protect privacy floors: location precision, home address secrecy and evidence retention limits cannot be loosened by any profile.
A bundled generic profile (publisher = the release-pinned project key, code generic) carries the CTR-PRV-001 defaults and is the fallback whenever nothing is selected or a reference is unknown.
Profile content is validated against bounds and privacy floors before it is staged, released or applied.
Selection and resolution validate trust in the publisher and the profile status.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Receiving vaults verify the approved decision for every version whose governed fields differ from the previous verified version, or from the generic profile for a new code, so the publisher's own client is not the only check.
Merge directions are fixed per field by one merge table that resolve, the Compare view, the upgrade check and the tests all use.
JurisdictionProfile follows the declared machine in the publisher vault; vaults mirror status from verified statements.
Retired is terminal; a changed profile is a new version that supersedes the previous active one atomically.
A user's local selection is separate from profile status and can be changed at any time.

A selection follows its ProfileRef to newer versions: a new version applies automatically only if no governed field becomes Looser by the merge table; otherwise the selection stays upgrade_pending on the current version until the owner confirms, and Looser retention values then apply only to records created after effectiveFrom.

draft, release and retire are publisher commands in the publisher's vault; release and retire produce signed statements (classrup.governance.jurisdiction_profile/v1 and classrup.governance.jurisdiction_profile_retirement/v1) with relay destinations and syncState prepared.

receive and select are vault commands in every user's vault; select is a local preference that produces no statement but emits governance.jurisdiction_profile.activated with change selected or deselected so local consumers refresh.

resolve and get are queries used by F01.S01.M03 (publish and age gate), F10.S01.M02 (retention), F09.S01.M02 (cash limit), F16.S03.M02 (breach notice) and the UI; resolve accepts explicit profileRefs and returns the merged values with their sources.

Relays apply their operator's profile through the relay command relay_upload, which verifies the operator key and emits governance.jurisdiction_profile.activated relay-locally with scope relay, and serve it through relay_latest.
Profiles are referenced everywhere by ProfileRef (publisherId, code) with the version resolved at evaluation time, and every statement type is registered in the F11.S01.M01 registry (N2).
governance.jurisdiction_profile.activated distinguishes released, retired, selected, deselected, upgrade_pending and upgraded so consumers know when to refresh.

Vault policy: authoring and releasing require the publisher key; receiving, selecting and reading are available to the vault owner for publishers trusted for scope profiles in F18.S02.M01, and no command here grants trust.
Relay policy (CAP-9): a relay applies its own profile to what it hosts and accepts profile uploads only from its operator key; a relay role has no effect on a user's local selection.
The age declaration and the selection are P3 local preferences and are never transmitted.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; statements are deduplicated by cid and version.
Release, supersession of the previous version and the outbox entry commit in one transaction.
Offline use is complete locally; publication state is prepared until a relay receipt exists.
Profiles contain no personal data; the user's selection and age declaration are P3 local data and never leave the vault.
Profile versions are retained RET-STANDARD, with the last 3 versions of each code kept locally.
The UI states that profiles are configuration, not legal advice, and that the platform cannot verify age.

A signed change from a trusted but compromised or malicious publisher never removes records by itself: Looser retention waits for the owner's confirmation and applies only to records created after effectiveFrom, revoked signer keys are quarantined, and trust can be paused in F18.S02.M01.

The selection and age declaration are user data: the module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort through the composition root and classifies them P3 through F10.S02.M02 (N6).
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Resolve is called on every publish and must be fast on Moto G-class hardware.
Relay profile serving follows OBS-1 to OBS-4.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate statements, commands and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Privacy-floor tests fail the build if any profile field can loosen CTR-PRV-001.
The user export contains stored profiles with provenance and the local selection; the trusted-publisher list is exported by F18.S02.M01.
Import re-verifies signatures, bounds, privacy floors and recorded decisions; failing profiles are stored as read-only history.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
A ProhibitedRule is an immutable version of a rule identified by a stable (publisherId, ruleKey); activating a new version retires the previous version of the same key.

Keywords are stored normalized (NFKC, case-folded, diacritics folded) and bounded: at most 50 phrases per rule, each 2 to 60 code points, at most 2 000 active rules per pack; sensitive rules carry in the signed pack only salted hashes of whole-word phrases of at most 5 tokens.
Rules are public configuration (P0) so sellers can see what is not allowed; evaluation results are local P3 and never leave the vault.

A rule pack declares the taxonomy its category scopes refer to and expresses jurisdiction scopes as ProfileRefs; scopes that do not resolve are stored as scope_unresolved with one defined fallback, never skipped silently.

Each rule version records the pack version that first activated it and its proposalId, and the pack embeds the decision envelopes with receipts for rule versions first activated in that pack version and cites older ones by decisionCid.
Rule content is validated for size, normalization, scope and action before staging or applying.
Evaluation input is bounded and validated before matching so evaluation time stays predictable.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.

Receiving vaults verify decisions only for rule versions that are new or changed against their applied snapshot, at the anchored activation time of the pack version that first activated them and never at the receiver's clock, so full snapshots with long-approved rules stay applicable for new and long-offline vaults.
Emergency rules are limited per (publisherId, ruleKey) over any 30-day window, and receivers enforce the limit from their stored pack history.
ProhibitedRule follows the declared machine; retired is terminal and a rule is changed only by activating a new version.
Activating a version retires the previous active version of the same key in the same transaction and increases the ruleset version.
Emergency rules retire automatically at their effective expiry, min(emergencyUntil, firstSeenAt + 7 days); the sweep and the evaluation both honour it.

When an applied pack gives a block verdict for an already active publication, the publication is held for its owner (policy_attention in F01.S01.M03): the owner is notified, renewals and re-publication of unchanged content stop until the owner resolves it by an edit that clears the verdict or by confirming Unpublish, and nothing is unpublished or tombstoned before that confirmation.

draft, retire and release_pack run in the publisher's vault; retire only stages a retirement, and release_pack signs the full rule set with its taxonomyRef, salted hashes for sensitive rules and the cited decisions as classrup.governance.rule_pack/v1 and queues it to the publisher's relays.

apply_pack runs in every vault: it verifies the pack, the publisher's trust, decisions for new or changed versions and emergency limits, applies it atomically and emits one governance.prohibited_rule.changed event per changed rule key; packs from untrusted or paused publishers wait in the F18.S02.M01 pending inbox.

evaluate is a pure query run locally and by relays against their own packs; its result contains rule keys with their publisherId, reason keys, notices and the list of evaluated packs, never matched text.

Relays apply their operator's pack through the relay command relay_upload, which verifies the operator key, applies the pack as the relay's hosting policy and emits governance.prohibited_rule.changed relay-locally, serve it unchanged through relay_latest, and evaluate index submissions against it.
governance.prohibited_rule.changed carries ruleId (the version id) besides publisherId, ruleKey and version; cross-module references use (publisherId, ruleKey), and ruleId names an exact version.
Statement types of this module are registered in the F11.S01.M01 registry with audience, signer role, role resolution and maxAge (N2).

Vault policy: authoring and releasing require the publisher key; apply is available to the vault owner for publishers trusted for scope rules in F18.S02.M01 and never grants trust; evaluate is callable by the owner and internal callers F01.S01.M02 and F01.S01.M03.

Relay policy (CAP-9): a relay evaluates its own rule pack on index submissions and may refuse or remove content from its index with a signed statement of reasons; this has no effect on other relays or on the author's vault.
There is no global rule authority; each user chooses which publishers to trust.
Authoring and apply commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; packs are deduplicated by packCid.
apply_pack replaces the active rule set atomically; evaluation always sees a complete pack, never a partial one.
Offline vaults evaluate with the last applied pack; relay unavailability never blocks local evaluation.
Evaluated listing text is processed only in memory in the user's vault; the module stores no copy and logs no matched text.

Rule packs are public signed configuration; sensitive keyword lists are published only as salted hashes, which hides them from casual reading but does not resist dictionary search, and anyone can test text against the pack; the UI says so.
Rule versions are retained RET-STANDARD with the last 3 packs kept locally; decisions that created them are RET-EVIDENCE in F18.S02.M01.

A signed change from a trusted but compromised or malicious publisher never removes a user's publications by itself: block verdicts caused by a pack change hold the publication for its owner with a grace of at least 7 days before a reminder, and a tombstone is signed only after the owner confirms.
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); verdict counts are local diagnostics and contain no text.
Evaluation latency is budgeted because it runs on every publish and edit.
Relay evaluation follows OBS-1 to OBS-4.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate pack statements, commands, evaluate results and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Evaluation determinism is covered by property tests with at least 200 runs, 10 000 nightly.

The user export contains the applied rule mirror with provenance; the trusted-publisher list is exported by F18.S02.M01; publisher vaults also export drafts, the plaintext of their own sensitive keywords and signing history.
Import re-verifies pack signatures, publisher trust, size limits and recorded decisions; failing packs are stored as pending or rejected.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days; the last 3 packs allow review of what changed.

A PolicyProposal records publisher, target type and references, a structured proposed change keyed by target reference (at most 16 KiB), summary, a comment period anchored to a relay receipt, status, decision and changelog entry.
Proposals, decisions, co-signatures and authority lists are public signed statements (P0) and comments are P1 statements visible to members of the hosting relay; every receiving vault verifies them.

Decisions bind the proposal statement cid and the digest of the approved change for exact targets, may activate a target only within 30 days after the decision's anchored time, and are evidence retained under RET-EVIDENCE.

The module owns the vault's trusted-publisher list (TrustedPublisher with scopes taxonomy, rules, profiles, proposals and transparency) and the pending-statement inbox (PendingStatement) used by all F18 modules; both are P3 local records.

A publisher's authority list (classrup.governance.authority_list/v1) names the decider and co-signer keys it delegates to, and each key's listing time is anchored to the relay receipt of the list version that first named it.
Proposals are validated for length, target references, comment period and signer roles before publication.
Comments and decisions are validated against the proposal state and signer keys on the relay and again in every receiving vault.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Receivers enforce the comment period from relay receipts, never from publisher or decider timestamps, and verify that the activated content equals the approved content.

PolicyProposal follows the declared machine; conflicted is terminal, and approved, rejected and withdrawn are final for their signers and change only to conflicted when a validly signed contradicting statement is verified.

The comment period starts at the relay-signed receipt of the proposal statement and ends commentPeriodHours later on that relay's clock; publisher and decider timestamps are claims and are shown as such.
A decision cannot be reversed; a new proposal is required to change policy again.

Vaults other than the authoring vault move their mirror only on verified received statements, and a verified withdrawal plus a verified decision, or two verified decisions with different outcomes, for the same proposal cid make it conflicted in every vault that sees both.

PendingStatement follows its own machine: pending items are applied when the publisher becomes trusted for the scope or the owner applies them, and are discarded after 30 days or refused by the owner.

Publisher commands (draft, request_cosign, open, withdraw, authority_list draft and release) run in the publisher's vault, decide runs in the decider's own vault and cosign in the co-signer's vault; every command that signs a statement takes relayIds[] and returns syncState prepared.

post_comment and withdraw_comment are vault commands in the member's vault producing classrup.governance.policy_comment/v1 and an author-signed classrup.federation.tombstone/v1; accept, relay_withdraw and hide are relay commands and relay_list is a relay query on the publisher's relay; vaults ingest comments only through governance.policy_comment.receive.

receive is a vault command in any vault that verifies and stores proposal, decision, withdrawal and co-sign statements from trusted publishers; verify is a pure query used by F18.S01.* and F18.S02.M02 that checks publisher, content digest, anchored period and validity at the activation time asOf.

governance.policy_proposal.decided carries the approved proposedChange (or its cid when larger than 16 KiB), proposalStatementCid, decisionCid and changeDigest, so consumers such as F12.S02.M03 need no second lookup; targetType platform_policy maps to an F12 PolicyRule.

Trusted publishers and pending statements change only through explicit owner commands (trusted_publisher add, remove, pause and resume; pending_statement apply and refuse); sync ingestion can never add trust, and other F18 modules hold untrusted statements through pending_statement.hold.

Every statement type of this module is registered in the F11.S01.M01 statement registry with audience, signer role, role resolution and maxAge (N2), and the vault acts only on statements its receiving path accepted.

Vault policy: authoring and publishing require the publisher key; deciding and co-signing require a key delegated in the publisher's verified authority list and different from the publisher; commenting requires any local principal; receiving verifies signer roles (CAP-8).

Relay policy (CAP-9): the publisher's relay accepts comments from registered device keys within its quota, serves comments only to holders of a valid relay access token (CAP-8, CAP-10) because they are P1, honours author tombstones and lets its own moderator hide comments; a relay role has no power over other relays or vaults.
There is no global governance role; trust is per publisher and chosen by each user.
A delegated decider or co-signer shows that a different key acted, not that a different person did; the UI, threat model and changelog say so.
All commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001 and statements are deduplicated by cid.
State change, signed statement and outbox entry commit in one IndexedDB transaction of the signing vault only; transport is retried separately and no guarantee spans two vaults.

Contradicting signed statements (two decisions with different outcomes or content, or a decision and a withdrawal, for one proposal cid) are detected in any receiving vault, marked conflicted and never resolved by last writer or by timestamps.

Comment delivery states follow IDM-7: the relay's signed acceptance is transport_acknowledged and labelled 'accepted for hosting by relay R', and peer_accepted is shown only when a verified decision by the publisher's delegated decider lists the comment cid in acknowledgedCommentCids.
Proposals and decisions are public signed statements; comments are visible to the relay's community and are linkable to pseudonyms; the UI says pseudonymity is not anonymity.
Decisions and proposals are retained as evidence (RET-EVIDENCE); comments follow RET-STANDARD and hidden comments keep their signed statement for audit.
No comment or proposal content is sent through notification channels beyond a reference and a template key.

PolicyComment is user content: the module registers ExportSectionPort, DeletionPort and RetentionPurgePort, classifies comment fields through F10.S02.M02, signs comment tombstones in the DeletionPort sign step (N6a), and reacts to privacy.deletion.requested and cancelled with reversible actions only.

Comment display filters blocked authors through F07.S02.M02 filterBlocked, and relay intake is rate limited per key and per network prefix with a per-proposal cap for keys registered less than 7 days ago (N7, N18).
No telemetry leaves the device (OBS-7); counters are local diagnostics.
Relay comment acceptance follows OBS-1 to OBS-4.
Verification must be fast because other modules call it before applying changes.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate statements, commands and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Time-based behaviour is tested with injected clocks for vault and relay separately.

The user export contains proposals, decisions and authority lists from trusted publishers, own comments, the trusted-publisher list, pending statements and, for publishers, their drafts and signing history.
Import re-verifies every signature, role, anchored receipt and the conflict check; failing statements are quarantined.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.

A TransparencyReport is an immutable computed report identified by relayId, periodKey and version, with suppressed aggregate tables, a content digest, the snapshot it was computed from and a publication status; corrections are new versions.
TransparencyCounter rows hold only period key, metric, dimension value and count; they never reference users, cases, listings or free text.

Reports are public P0; counters are relay-local operational data (IOX-7) of class P2 for that relay's operator role, stored only on the relay, and leave it only as a relay-signed snapshot sealed to an operator key.

Dimension vocabularies are bound to the producer enums: reason codes of the relay-side moderation.report.received of F12.S01.M01 (the vault-local moderation.report.filed is never counted), action kinds of F12.S02.M01, appeal outcomes upheld, overturned and reduced of moderation.appeal.decided of F12.S01.M03 (moot closures emit no event and are not counted) and spam detections of F12.S02.M02 relay intake.
Inputs are validated against closed vocabularies so counters can never carry identifying text.
Computation and publication validate suppression, coverage, reviewer separation and period state.
Every violation maps to one stable error code.
Receivers verify two distinct operator signatures, compiler on the draft and reviewer on the report, against the relay's signed operator list and refuse self-reviewed reports.
Differencing is prevented across periods and versions: one period granularity per relay and suppression of small changes between a correction and the version it supersedes.
TransparencyReport follows the declared machine; superseded, discarded and conflicted are terminal.
Publication needs a compiler-signed draft and a reviewer countersignature by a different operator key of the same relay; there is no single-key publication path.
A published report is never edited; corrections create a new version that supersedes it.
Counters of a period freeze 24 hours after periodEnd on the relay's clock, so every snapshot of a frozen period is byte-identical and both operators can obtain the same snapshotCid.

import_snapshot, compute, request_review and discard are vault commands in the compiler's vault and publish runs in the reviewer's vault; request_review sends a compiler-signed classrup.governance.transparency_draft/v1 sealed to the reviewer, and publish signs classrup.governance.transparency_report/v1 embedding that draft and queues it to the relay.

Counters accumulate on the relay in a relay-side consumer of relay-local moderation events and relay-scope policy decisions, idempotent by event id and by proposalId and statementCid; legal request tallies are operator-signed relay commands; relay_counter_snapshot returns a relay-signed snapshot sealed to the requesting operator key.

receive is a vault command in any vault that verifies and stores reports from publishers trusted for scope transparency and drafts addressed to the local operator key; get_published and list_published are public reads on the relay and local reads in vaults; relay_upload accepts only two-key reports from the relay's operators.
Every statement type of this module is registered in the F11.S01.M01 registry with audience, signer role, role resolution and maxAge (N2).

Vault policy: compiling, importing snapshots and discarding require an operator key of the relay; publishing requires a different operator key of the same relay; applying a received report is open to the vault owner for publishers trusted for scope transparency.

Relay policy (CAP-9): the relay serves published reports to anonymous readers, and serves counter snapshots and accepts legal tallies and report uploads only on requests signed by its operator keys; a relay role has no power over other relays.
Counter data is operator-private and is not readable by members or by other relays.
Commands are idempotent per CTR-IDM-001; counter consumers are idempotent by event id (EVT-3).
Compute is deterministic: the same snapshot and parameters give the same contentCid.
Coverage is measured, not declared: counters accumulate on the relay while its consumers run, the snapshot's coverage comes from the relay's hourly processing checkpoints, and the report states it.
Reports reveal only suppressed aggregate counts and contain no user, listing, case or request identities and no free text.

Counters are kept under RET-AUDIT and purged exactly 90 days after the period's report is published through RetentionPurgePort; published reports are kept as public record (RET-STANDARD) and as evidence in the operator vault.
Small-number suppression and complementary suppression prevent inference of individual cases from differences between rows, totals or periods.

Differencing across periods and versions is blocked by one period granularity per relay, by withholding totals of metrics with suppressed cells and by suppressing every cell whose change from the superseded version is 1 to 9.
No telemetry leaves user devices (OBS-7); operator-side jobs are measured under OBS-1 to OBS-4 on the relay.
Compute and publish are batch operations with explicit time budgets.
Overdue publication is a visible alert for operators.
Every requirement is covered by at least one automated test.
Contract tests validate the report statement, commands and events against the registry and verify signatures.
Suppression is covered by property tests with at least 200 runs, 10 000 nightly, including differencing attacks.

The operator export contains reports (all versions) and imported snapshots of unpublished periods; counters stay on the relay; a user export contains reports from trusted publishers that the user stored.
Import re-verifies both signatures, operator-list membership, suppression and reviewer separation; failing reports are quarantined.
Schema changes follow expand/contract and keep v1 readable for 180 days.
Store one current PrivateIntent under the unlocked principal with a random UUIDv4 key and no historical revision table.
Keep owner, criteria, state and expiry inside existing encrypted vault storage without public projection.
Use StoredRecord revision and canonical intentId binding; the cancellation epoch is ephemeral only.
Validate closed criteria, canonical UTC expiry and safe positive expected revisions before mutation.
Bound query to 120 characters, canonical nonnegative amounts to 78 digits and live intents to 50.
Reject unknown authority fields, identifier collisions and expired creation or activation without partial writes.
Create as draft; activation requires explicit owner action against the current revision and unexpired content.
Edits reset state to draft; pause stops matching and erase removes the row instead of storing erased state.
Invalidate the ephemeral epoch before mutations and permanently revoke the store instance after session loss.
Expose create, read, list, revise, setState and erase as an owner-bound library with structured Result errors.
Register no command-bus operation and emit no events, idempotency hashes, outbox records or audit entries.
Return detached validated rows without raw exception details or remote operations.
Bind storage, principal and current-session guard at composition; operation bodies cannot choose the owner.
Require literal enabled true for creation, revision and activation while retaining inspection, pause and erase cleanup.
Check the session before admission, inside the transaction and after asynchronous settlement; ended sessions receive no data.
Use optimistic revisions and atomic storage transactions; a rejected storage transaction rolls back, while session loss after commit can conceal a successful mutation behind FORBIDDEN.
Retain no replay cache or deleted-object registry; repeated erasure reports absence without history.
Conceal late results after session loss and require explicit fresh owner action after state inspection.
Keep private criteria, identifiers and amounts out of logs, network requests, URLs, notifications and public projections.
Erase the local intent immediately without retaining an identifying deletion event, hash or tombstone.
Limit erasure to local intents and ephemeral results; independent backups, peer copies and physical remnants remain outside scope.
Logging, audit and metrics collection are absent from the local API and remain off by default.
Reject capacity overflow explicitly without silently truncating live intents or hard criteria.
Qualify encrypted storage and target-device resource behavior before activation; host tests are not mobile evidence.
Assert owner isolation, revisions, expiry, cancellation and rollback independently rather than checking source presence.
Exercise encrypted-vault codecs and signed public fixtures, with native browser qualification recorded separately.
Report actual outcomes and remaining activation gates without treating mocks or documents as production readiness.
Register the explicit codec and bind imported owner and stored key to validated content.
Restore intents as draft, preserve the live source during export and require fresh action before matching resumes.
Keep legacy archives compatible and reject unknown or malformed records; old external backups restore content only through explicit import.
Own no persistent entity; consume authenticated public-candidate snapshots and owner-private criteria.
Return only ownerId, listingId, revision and cid references without criteria, private amounts, scores or negative reasons.
Revalidate closed metadata and projection identity bindings without claiming structural checks verify signatures.
Accept at most 128 dense candidates with bounded fields and a valid safe clock; reject malformed or oversized input.
Apply every hard criterion and exact same-currency price bounds without FX or inferred negotiated prices.
Reject duplicate owner/listing identities and inconsistent evidence references instead of choosing an input-order winner.
Keep pure results deterministic and sorted independently of input candidate order.
Permit one ephemeral job; newer calls supersede older calls and cancellation settles stalled reads or loaders.
Recheck owner, session, epoch, revision, active state, expiry and blocks after the final awaited read before release.
Expose matchLocalCandidates and createLocalMatchSession as libraries without bus commands, events or provider fallback.
Pass only signal and limit to the authenticated local loader, never private criteria or intent identifiers.
Reject nonlocal modes before loading candidates and return fixed errors without input echoes.
Default matching to disabled and enable only for configuration that is literal true.
Use the owning discovery adapter after signature admission, never another domain private tables or a verified boolean.
Exclude blocked, own, conflicted, withdrawn, unavailable and expired records without implying disclosure or trade consent.
Keep jobs and results ephemeral; late completion cannot revive cancelled or superseded operations.
Read durable intent revision after loading to detect changes by another owner-bound controller.
Handle loader errors without network fallback or automatic retry; reopening resumes no job.
Keep private criteria inside unlocked local computation and require a network-free candidate loader.
Persist no results, query logs, negative explanations, deletion markers or private fingerprints.
Describe public-record comparison as local filtering, not confidential cross-user computation or anonymity.
The matcher and session have no logging, telemetry, event sink or metrics dependency.
Bound candidates and references to 128 with explicit overflow rejection and no constraint truncation.
Keep real mobile, accessibility and native-browser qualification separate from host unit timing.
Compare exact price boundaries and synthetic eligible sets against an independent deterministic oracle.
Exercise malformed input, every asynchronous cancellation stage, late session changes and minimal-output privacy.
Preserve existing gates and report unavailable browser runs honestly; absent or skipped execution establishes no acceptance.
Export no matching job or result because this module owns no persistent row.
Recovered intents are draft and require a new explicit match action after backup import.
Preserve signed public formats and discovery provenance; remote confidential protocols require independent qualification.
